Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Custom Text Grip Fidget Ring – Print-in-Place Spinner This is not just another fidget ring with text on it. This is a fully parametric print-in-place spinner ring where the custom text becomes the actual tactile grip of the rotating outer ring. Instead of using standard grooves, ribs or generic knurling, the external grip is generated directly from your own text, name, brand, nickname, date or message. Your text is not decoration. Your text is the grip. A Personal Message You Can Wear, Touch and Spin Because the grip is generated from custom text, this ring can become much more than a simple fidget toy. It can be a name, a romantic message, a special date, a couple nickname, an inside joke, a maker signature or a short phrase wrapped around a rotating ring. This makes it perfect as a unique personalized gift for someone special. A small object, but with a message built directly into its function. You can turn a name, a date or a love message into a tactile spinning ring. Examples: I LOVE YOU FOREVER YOU & ME MY LOVE ALWAYS LUCA ❤️ SARA SINCE 2024 SPIN MY HEART The message is not hidden inside the model. It is the part you touch, feel and spin. The Key Idea Most fidget rings use a standard external pattern for grip. This model does something different. The outer rotating ring uses raised custom text wrapped around the side surface as the tactile texture. The letters create: the grip the feel the visual identity the personalization So every ring can be different. Minimal, romantic, funny, branded, personal or completely weird: it depends only on the text you choose. Custom Text Becomes Functional Grip The text is placed on the outside of the rotating ring and follows the circular shape of the model. It is not simply stamped on a flat face. It is not just decorative branding. It becomes the surface your fingers touch while spinning the ring. Short texts are automatically repeated around the ring. Longer phrases are repeated only when they fit completely. No broken words. No interrupted messages. Only complete readable text patterns. Main Features Custom text used as tactile grip Print-in-place spinner ring Two-piece rotating structure No assembly required No external knurling Raised side text replaces the grip texture Automatic full-word text repetition No interrupted words or broken phrases Parametric inner diameter Adjustable ring width Adjustable text spacing Adjustable character width Adjustable text relief Adjustable print-in-place clearances Comfort-fit internal profile Chamfered inner edges for easier wearing Supportless design Designed for MakerWorld Customizer Multicolor-ready design What Makes It Different This model combines three things in one object: custom text + functional tactile grip + print-in-place rotating fidget ring The result is a small, simple object with a very clear identity: a personalized spinner ring where the message itself becomes the texture. It is not a ring with a label. It is a ring where the label becomes the grip. Text Ideas You can use names, brands, nicknames, short messages, romantic phrases or maker signatures. Examples: Made by CiCAdesign SPIN YOUR WORDS YOUR TEXT HERE FOCUS RELAX MAKER CREATE CUSTOM I LOVE YOU FOREVER ALWAYS YOU & ME Short words will repeat several times around the ring. Longer phrases will appear only as complete repetitions. Print-in-Place Mechanism The model is made of two separate functional parts printed together: an inner ring that stays fixed an outer ring that rotates around it Both parts rest on the build plate, making the model easier to print without supports. After printing, gently free the outer ring and rotate it gradually until the mechanism becomes smooth. Clearance parameters are available to adapt the model to different printers, materials and calibration levels. Multicolor Printing This model can be printed in two different ways. Single Color Print For a standard single-color print, simply export and print the STL as it is. No extra steps are required. Export STL Import into slicer Print normally This is the simplest option and works like a normal print-in-place fidget ring. Multicolor Print For multicolor printing, import the STL into Bambu Studio and split it into parts. The model is designed to be divided into separate printable parts: inner ring outer rotating ring text grip Recommended workflow in Bambu Studio: 1. Import the STL 2. Right click on the model 3. Select Split 4. Choose Split to Parts 5. Assign a different filament/color to each part 6. Disable Arachne wall generator 7. Use Classic wall generator 8. Slice and print This allows you to create 2-color or 3-color versions. Examples: outer ring: blue inner ring: light gray text grip: white or: outer ring: black inner ring: gold text grip: ivory or: outer ring: white inner ring: teal text grip: coral For a clean multicolor result, the raised text is separated as its own printable part, so the custom text becomes a clearly visible tactile grip. Important Multicolor Note When the model is split into parts, you may see very thin construction lines connecting the raised letters. These lines are intentional. They are used only to keep the custom text connected as a single selectable text-grip part inside the slicer, instead of having every letter detected as a separate object. These construction lines are necessary for multicolor part detection. They are not intended as visible design details. Do not use Arachne wall generator for multicolor printing. Use Classic wall generator instead. With Arachne enabled, the slicer may try to print these thin construction lines. With Classic wall generator, they should remain non-printable construction geometry and disappear from the final toolpath. So, when using multicolor mode: inner ring = one part outer rotating ring = one part text grip = one connected part This makes it much easier to assign colors in Bambu Studio without selecting every single letter manually. Final practical note: For single-color printing, print the STL normally. For multicolor printing, split the STL into parts and assign colors. For multicolor printing, use Classic wall generator instead of Arachne. The thin connection lines help the slicer treat the text as one text-grip part. Comfort Fit The inner surface is shaped for better comfort. It includes: a slightly curved internal profile chamfered upper and lower inner edges smoother finger insertion improved wearing feel This makes the ring more comfortable to wear, hold and spin. Recommended Print Settings Orientation: flat on the build plate Supports: no Layer height: 0.16 – 0.20 mm Walls: 3 Top/bottom layers: 4 – 5 Infill: 15 – 25% Brim: optional For best rotation: Use a clean first layer Avoid excessive elephant foot Do not over-squish the print Free the outer ring gently after printing Rotate gradually until smooth Customizer Parameters The model is intentionally simple to customize. Main parameters: inner diameter ring width custom side text text spacing character width text relief radial clearance axial clearance The advanced geometry is already tuned, so the user can focus on the fun part: writing the text and printing a unique ring. model_name: Capsule Radar — Live Flight Radar Desk Gadget
description: See real aircraft flying around you — live, on a round touch AMOLED. Open-source, and you flash it from your browser. Overview Capsule Radar is a 3D-printed desk gadget that shows live air traffic around your location . It pulls nearby aircraft from a free online ADS-B feed over Wi-Fi and plots them on a glowing round radar scope, rotated by heading and colour-coded by altitude, with an animated sweep and fading trails. Tap any aircraft to see its full details — even where it's flying from and to . It's a finished, polished build: a capacitive touch UI, four selectable themes, a boot splash, audible alerts, battery and real-time-clock support, idle auto-dim, and a built-in web page to configure everything. No coding required — flash it straight from Chrome or Edge, then enter your Wi-Fi from your phone. The enclosure is a round "scope-orb / pocket-watch" form factor: a matte shell with a knurled tactile ring, a crown on top, a side USB-C port, an integrated speaker, and an engraved logo. No soldering — the Waveshare board carries all the electronics. 💡 Already have this board? It can do more! The same Waveshare ESP32-S3 AMOLED screen can also become a Pokémon Tamagotchi inside a Pokéball https://makerworld.com/es/models/2937822-tamapoke-a-pokemon-pokeball-tamagotchi Same screen, completely different gadget. AMOLED screen can also become a marine ships radar. https://makerworld.com/es/models/2972002-capsule-radar-marine-live-ais-ship-radar Same screen, a ship's radar Functions (what it does) Live air traffic Real aircraft from a free ADS-B feed ( airplanes.live , with adsb.lol as a fallback), refreshed every couple of seconds. Aircraft are drawn as glyphs rotated by their heading and colour-coded by altitude , with fading trails and an animated radar sweep. Out-of-range traffic appears as edge markers pointing in its direction . A memory-safe streaming parser caps the number of aircraft so busy areas never overload the device. Touch & details Tap an aircraft to open a detail card: callsign, type, altitude, vertical speed, ground speed, distance, bearing, squawk, and the origin → destination route (looked up online and cached so the same flight isn't re-queried). Swipe between three circular views: Radar , List , and Stats . On-screen zoom button cycles the display range (10 / 20 / 30 / 50 / 100 km) and shows the current value. Long-press the screen to cycle the visual theme. Four themes (remembered across reboots) Phosphor — classic green-on-black radar scope: rings, sweep, altitude colours. Capsule / Orb radar — green grid with glowing "ball" blips emitting sonar-style rings and edge arrows for distant traffic. Amber CRT — warm amber monochrome scope. Military — night-vision green scope. Status HUD Wi-Fi indicator (turns amber if the data feed is failing), in-range aircraft count, clock, battery % (charging bolt; turns red when low), and the date. Sound (built-in speaker) A soft ping when a new aircraft enters range, and an urgent double-beep for emergency / military contacts. Volume, mute and a test button are on the web page. Power & time Battery aware (optional LiPo): on-screen charge %, low-battery warning, and a slower polling rate on battery to save power. Real-time clock : keeps the time and date across power loss, so the clock is right even before/without Wi-Fi; it re-syncs from the internet (NTP) when online. GPS auto-location (optional — "‑G" board variant) If you use the GPS version of the board (Waveshare ESP32‑S3‑Touch‑AMOLED‑1.75**‑G**, with an onboard LC76G GNSS + antenna), the radar can set its own centre point — no need to type coordinates. Tick "Use GPS for location" on the web page and a satellite icon appears in the status bar ( amber while acquiring, green once it has a fix); the radar then auto‑centres on your real position, with a GPS line on the Stats view too. The standard (non‑GPS) board works exactly the same — you just enter your location manually, which is also used as the fallback until a fix is acquired. Tip: plug the antenna into the GPS u.FL connector (the board has a separate one for Wi‑Fi), white patch facing the sky, and allow a few minutes outdoors for the first cold‑start fix. Smart dimming Idle auto-dim after a configurable time with no touch. Face-down sleep : flip the device over to turn the screen off (motion sensor). Configuration & updates A built-in web page at http://capsuleradar.local/ to set the centre point (pick it on an interactive map) , display range, theme, brightness, sound, idle-dim timeout, reset Wi-Fi, and update the firmware over Wi-Fi . All settings persist on the device. First boot opens a Wi-Fi setup hotspot. What you need (Bill of Materials) Qty Item Notes 1 Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75 All the electronics in one board: round 466×466 CO5300 AMOLED, capacitive touch, ESP32-S3R8 (8 MB PSRAM / 16 MB flash), motion sensor, real-time clock, power-management/charger, audio codec. Pick the Standard version (no case) or the -G (GPS, also fits). Avoid the "-B" — it comes with a protective case that won't fit; you'd have to remove it. (The separate "1.75C" is a different board — not this one.) 1 Speaker (small 8 Ω, with the board's JST connector, optional) For the alert pings. Optional but recommended. 1 USB-C cable (data) To flash and power the device. 1 LiPo battery (3.7 V, JST, optional) For cordless use; the board charges it from USB-C. — Printed enclosure 4 parts, see below. Optional "‑G" board variant The same board with an onboard GPS (LC76G) + antenna for automatic location. Not required: the standard board is fully functional; you just set your location on the web page. The Waveshare board is the only electronics you need to buy. No soldering. Installation — flash the firmware You don't need any toolchain. Option A — flash from your browser (easiest) Open the web flasher : https://socquique.github.io/capsule-radar/ (Chrome or Edge on desktop). Plug the board into your computer with a USB-C data cable. Click Install , choose the serial port, and pick Erase + Install the first time. Option B — download the binary Grab CapsuleRadar-esp32s3.bin from the GitHub releases and flash it to offset 0x0: esptool.py --chip esp32s3 write_flash 0x0 CapsuleRadar-esp32s3.bin Option C — build from source with PlatformIO: pio run -e esp32-s3-amoled-175 -t upload Tip: if the board isn't detected, hold BOOT , tap RESET , then release BOOT , and try again. First-time setup After flashing, power the device. On first boot it creates a Wi-Fi hotspot named CapsuleRadar-Setup . Join that hotspot from your phone; a setup page opens. Enter your home Wi-Fi. The radar connects and real aircraft appear within seconds. Open http://capsuleradar.local/ on any device on the same network to fine-tune: Centre point — tap the interactive map or drag the pin (or type lat/lon). Display range , theme , brightness , sound (volume / mute / test), dim-screen-after timeout. Reset Wi-Fi to move it to a new network. Updating over Wi-Fi (no cable) Once it's running, you can update wirelessly: Open http://capsuleradar.local/update (also linked from the config page). Upload CapsuleRadar-ota.bin (the app image from the GitHub release — not the merged flash image). A progress bar runs and the device reboots into the new firmware. (Builders can also use PlatformIO: pio run -e esp32-s3-amoled-175-ota -t upload.) Using it (quick reference) Action Gesture Inspect an aircraft Tap it → detail card with route Switch view Swipe left/right (Radar ↔ List ↔ Stats) Change zoom range Tap the range button (⟳ … km) Change theme Long-press the screen Turn the screen off Flip it face-down Find the config page See the Stats view footer (shows capsuleradar.local + IP) Troubleshooting No aircraft showing — check Wi-Fi (the HUD Wi-Fi icon is red if disconnected, amber if the feed is failing) and that your centre point is set near you. Quiet areas/times simply have little traffic. Can't reach capsuleradar.local — use the IP shown on the Stats view instead. No sound — check Volume isn't 0 / Mute is off on the web page, and that the speaker is connected. Use the Test ping button. Lost/changed Wi-Fi — open the web page → Reset Wi-Fi , then rejoin CapsuleRadar-Setup. GPS not locking — GPS is only on the "‑G" board. Make sure the antenna is on the GPS u.FL connector (not the Wi‑Fi one), with a clear view of the sky; the first cold‑start fix can take several minutes.

description: 適用於6374/6384推進器 M4*16mm 螺絲 4ea 一體打印 2026/06/20 增加B rev 免除馬達軸心支撐 增加插銷環洞 2026/06/22 update 6374 CCW/CW propeller 2026/6/24 Update SUP 6437 US FIN BOX Here are the components I bought from a local shop: Motor: 6374 Brushless Motor (waterproofed both the inner and outer rotors of the brushless motor using epoxy) ESC (Speed Controller): 60A ESC Receiver: 433MHz Receiver with a watch-style remote controller Wires: 12 AWG silicone wire Sealant: Epoxy resin (Note: I'm not entirely sure if these exact brands/models are available in your area, but these are the general specs.) The seal process for the 6437 brushless motor is divided into two main parts: the stator and the rotor. For the rotor: I used a small brush to apply a very thin, even layer of epoxy resin. Keeping this layer thin is crucial to prevent throwing off the rotor's dynamic balance. For the stator: I made a custom mold to fit around the entire coil and magnet assembly. First, I sealed the wire connections using 706 RTV silicone glue for flexible strain relief, and then I potted the entire component with epoxy. Just a quick tip: make sure to seal or mask off the bearing area beforehand to prevent any epoxy from seeping in and ruining the bearings.

TamaPoke — A Pokéball Tamagotchi (ESP32-S3 round AMOLED) Raise a Gen-1 Pokémon inside a real Pokéball. TamaPoke turns a Waveshare round AMOLED board into a pixel-art virtual pet: it hatches from an egg, you choose a starter, then you feed it, play with it, keep it clean and watch it grow, evolve and — one day — say goodbye. Everything happens on a glowing round screen set into a 3D-printed Pokéball that sits on your desk and tilts the display toward you. This model is the 3D-printed enclosure that houses the electronics. The game firmware is open source (links at the bottom). 🙏 Based on / Credits — please read This enclosure is a remix built on top of the excellent "Pokeball" model by yoyothechicken on MakerWorld: 👉 https://makerworld.com/es/models/839922-pokeball I build on its clever closing system — the front magnets , alignment pins and button — and its print-in-place hinge ring . I modified the lid (dome) to embed the round screen and hold the electronics, and added a few small parts (screen mount, two ring variants, and a power-button cover). All credit for the original Pokéball shape and the whole opening/closing system goes to yoyothechicken — if you build this, please go like and follow their model first. ❤️ License note: the original is licensed CC BY-NC-SA (Attribution – NonCommercial – ShareAlike), so this remix is shared under the same license . Pokémon is © Nintendo / Game Freak. This is a personal, non-commercial fan project — not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. 💡 Already have this board? It can do more! The same Waveshare ESP32-S3 AMOLED screen can also become a Live ADS-B aircraft https://makerworld.com/es/models/2907695-capsule-radar-live-flight-radar-desk-gadget AMOLED screen can also become a marine ships radar. https://makerworld.com/es/models/2972002-capsule-radar-marine-live-ais-ship-radar Same screen, a ship's radar. ✨ What it does Round AMOLED screen embedded in the dome, tilted toward you like a tiny desk pet Full life cycle: egg → pick a starter → growth → evolution → farewell 6 languages (English default, plus ES / FR / DE / IT / PT) Touch controls, sound effects , battery + night-sleep handling A Progress page (XP to next level, levels to evolution, care mistakes) Classic Pokéball look: red top, white bottom, black band, front button 🎮 How to play (quick version) Pick a starter (Bulbasaur / Charmander / Squirtle), then raise what hatches from each egg . Four needs — food, joy, energy, hygiene — drain over time; feed, play, bathe, pet and let it sleep. Levels up by the hour (real time, even while off). Each egg rolls a rarity : ~ 70 % common · ~27 % rare · ~3 % legendary (legendaries after you've registered 25+; better odds with a daily care streak ). Shiny ≈ 1/48 (better with care). Evolution needs the right level and good care at that moment — every slip-up delays it. It never evolves by itself : a button appears and you tap to watch it . Three endings, all by your choice and witnessed on screen: 💛 farewell (a final form that lived its 3 days — blesses your next egg) · 💔 run-away (total neglect — curses the next egg) · 👋 release . Then a new egg begins. Catch & evolve them all: 151 + shinies , a Pokédex, medals, bonds and streaks. 6 languages (EN default + ES/FR/DE/IT/PT). Full game manual with the exact numbers: see the project README . 🧰 Bill of Materials (BOM) Electronics Item Notes Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75 The brain + screen. Round 1.75" AMOLED (466×466), capacitive touch, AXP2101 PMU, ES8311 audio, RTC, 6-axis IMU, microSD, USB-C. Board ≈ Ø46 mm. Pick the Standard version (no case) or the -G (GPS, also fits). Avoid the "-B" — it comes with a protective case that won't fit; you'd have to remove it. (The separate "1.75C" is a different board — not this one.) 3× M2 × 4 mm screws Mount the board/screen to the top dome. 1S LiPo battery (optional) The one I use: 3.7 V 1100 mAh LiPo (Amazon.es) — model 102540, with protection board. ≈ 42 × 25.5 × 11 mm , micro JST 1.25 connector matching the board's BAT port. Without it the Pokéball just runs while plugged into USB. Small speaker (optional) Rectangular ≈ 30.5 × 20.5 × 6.7 mm , MX1.25 connector matching the board's SPK port. Without it there's simply no sound. USB-C cable Any straight cable — a slot in the case lets you plug it directly into the board to charge (no right-angle adapter needed). Also used for flashing. microSD card Holds the sprite set (recommended for the full 151-mon library). Any small card works. 4× disc magnets 6 × 2 mm Snap-shut closure. 6 × 1.75 mm (6×2 nominal) discs in the counterbores. Mind the polarity! Printed parts Top dome (modified lid) — holds the board, with the screen window + 3 screw bosses Bottom dome (base model lid) — holds the optional battery + speaker Power-button cover — a small cover with a button that presses the board's PWR switch from the outside Hinge ring — two variants (pick one): Self-assembling (print-in-place) — easiest, but may not move freely if your printer's tolerances are tight Filament-hinge — a separate ring that uses a short piece of filament as the hinge pin ; more reliable if the print-in-place one seizes From the base model #839922 : button (inner + outer), alignment pins (4×: two 8 mm + two 6 mm) Filament 🔴 Red — top dome ⚪ White — bottom dome ⚫ Black — equator band + button Tools A computer with Chrome or Edge (to flash the firmware via the browser) A USB-C cable (also used for flashing) A small M2 Phillips screwdriver No soldering required — everything connects through the board's connectors 🖨️ Printing — no AMS needed You do NOT need an AMS / multi-color setup. Each part is a single color , so just load the matching filament and print each part on its own: Top dome → red Bottom dome → white Band + button → black Suggested settings (tune to your printer): Layer height 0.2 mm , walls 2–3 , infill 15 % (matches the base model's profiles) Supports: the top dome needs supports under the screen window / board seat. The bottom part prints with little or no support. Print the domes rim-down (flat side on the plate) for the cleanest curved surface. Hinge ring — print ONE of the two: Self-assembling (print-in-place): set your elephant-foot compensation correctly or it can seize. If it doesn't move freely once printed, use the other ring instead. Filament-hinge: print it, then push a short piece of 1.75 mm filament through as the hinge pin — works even if your tolerances aren't perfect. PLA/PETG both work; no brim usually needed. 🔩 Assembly (overview) Flash the firmware first (browser installer — see below) while the board is still easy to reach. Load the sprites (one click in the installer, ~10 min) onto the microSD card. Mount the screen: drop the board into the top dome so the screen faces out through the window , and fix it with the 3× M2 × 4 mm screws . Power-button cover: fit the printed cover over the board's PWR switch so you can power it on/off from the outside. (Optional) Bottom dome: place the battery and speaker in their pockets and plug them into the board's BAT and SPK connectors. (Skip either if you're not using it.) To charge, plug a straight USB-C cable through the side slot — no need to open the ball. Pins: insert the 4 alignment pins into the lid holes — 8 mm pins in the back, 6 mm pins in the front (as in the base model). Magnets: press the 4 magnets into the counterbores . Test polarity so the halves attract — don't glue anything until you've verified the ball snaps shut! Hinge: clip each dome onto your chosen ring (self-assembling, or filament-hinge with a 1.75 mm filament pin); the ball now opens/closes like a clamshell, held shut by the front magnets. Button: push the inner button into the outer button and glue the assembly to one hemisphere of your choice. Done — power on and meet your Pokémon. 🎉 ⚠️ Handle the screen ribbon with care. The AMOLED flex cable is delicate; seat the board gently and never flex or pull the display ribbon, or you can kill the panel. 🔋 Battery & power — make it last - Short-press the PWR button = screen on/off. Long-press (~4 s) = full power-off. - The trick for battery life: when you're done playing, long-press to power it off completely — the AMOLED and the chip then draw almost nothing, so a single charge lasts far longer. - You don't lose any progress: a real-time clock keeps running on microamps while it's off, so your Pokémon keeps "aging" in the background (hunger, level, evolution…) and catches up the moment you switch it back on (up to ~2 weeks). - So treat it like a phone: power it off when you're not playing, top up the battery now and then, and your pet lives on. 🔋 💾 Firmware & sprites The game firmware is open source and flashes straight from your browser — no Arduino IDE, no toolchain, no drivers to hunt down. How to install (≈ 10–15 min, mostly waiting) Plug the board into your PC and open the web installer in Chrome or Edge : https://socquique.github.io/TamaPoke/web/ Click Install firmware and pick the board's serial port → it flashes in seconds. Click Load sprites to stream the bundled sprite pack onto the microSD card over USB (this is the slow part, ~10 min for all 151). Unplug, screw it together, close the ball, and play. What the game includes The 151 Gen-1 Pokémon (shinies too), pixel-art animated from the microSD Hatch from an egg → choose your starter → feed / play / clean / sleep → grow → evolve → say goodbye (evolution, release and run-away endings, each with its own animation) Touch UI, sound effects (with the optional speaker), real-time clock with a night-sleep cycle, and battery monitoring A Pokédex and a Progress page (XP to next level, levels left to evolve, care mistakes), plus a mini-game to train your Pokémon 6 languages — EN (default), ES, FR, DE, IT, PT — switchable in Settings Factory-reset to start a brand-new Pokémon whenever you like The firmware ships with a small set of built-in sprites, so it still boots and plays even without an SD card — the SD just unlocks the full animated library. Source code & docs: https://github.com/socquique/TamaPoke 📜 License & attribution Enclosure: remix of "Pokeball" by yoyothechicken ( #839922 ), licensed CC BY-NC-SA . This remix keeps the same CC BY-NC-SA license (ShareAlike). Firmware / source code: MIT — see the repo. Sprites: Pokémon © Nintendo / Game Freak; pixel art from community sources (e.g. PMD SpriteCollab, CC BY-NC). Personal, non-commercial use only. Built with way too much love for a 1.75-inch Pokémon. Have fun and tag your builds!

description: A fork of ESP32 C3 Plane Radar by the matixovi — modified for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28 Touch board. A round 1.28 inch GC9A01 screen on a Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28 Touch that shows live aircraft near your location. Sonar-style grid, callsigns and altitude. It connects to your home WiFi and pulls live flight data from adsb.fi. Set your lat/lng and choose km or miles on the setup page. The built-in boot button cycles through range options (5 / 10 / 15 / 25 km). Distant aircraft are shown as red dots on the rim. This variant takes advantage of the Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28's integrated GC9A01 display - no wiring required. The display, touch controller, and screen are all on-board. Parts Part What to look for Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28 Round 1.28" GC9A01 display, touch USB-C cable Must be a data cable. No breadboard, no jumper wires. The display is already on the board. No wiring needed The Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28 has the GC9A01 display, CST816S touch controller. This fork remaps the firmware to use the board's native SPI pinout. Function GPIO MOSI (SDA) GPIO 11 SCLK (SCL) GPIO 10 CS GPIO 9 DC GPIO 8 RST GPIO 12 BL (backlight) GPIO 40 These are handled in firmware. Flash the firmware Download the release .bin from my forked repo GitHub Releases. Put the board in download mode: unplug USB, hold BOOT, plug USB in, wait 2 seconds, release BOOT. If that doesn't work: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT. Open https://web.esphome.io/ in Chrome or Edge. Choose Install (no need to set up a new ESPHome device). Select your serial port and the downloaded .bin. When complete, unplug, wait a few seconds, plug back in without holding BOOT. WiFi setup Connect to PlaneRadar-Setup , then open http://plane-radar.local or http://192.168.4.1. Enter your home WiFi SSID, password, and latitude/longitude. Save and wait for reboot. The ESP32-S3 supports both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz WiFi. Credits Original design and firmware by matixovi — ESP32 C3 Plane Radar . This is a hardware fork only, adapting the enclosure and pin mapping for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-1.28 Touch board.

description: Turn your 140mm USB-powered PC fan into a simple and effective ventilation solution for roof top tents, campers, vans, or any setup with a mosquito net or fly screen. HydroLink Pump Station Bring your HydroLink waterway to life! The HydroLink Pump Station adds a completely new way to interact with the system. Instead of simply pouring water into the channels, children can now generate their own water flow by turning a large hand crank. At the heart of the module is a working Archimedean screw pump. As the crank is turned, water is lifted from the one side and discharged into the other HydroLink channels. The open frame makes the pumping process fully visible and turns a simple mechanical principle into a fun hands-on experience. Safety Feature The Pump Station is designed with a simple built-in overload protection mechanism. If excessive resistance occurs – for example due to a foreign object entering the pump or an attempt to force the mechanism – the gear assembly can move upward and disengage from the drive. This allows the crank to slip instead of transmitting excessive force to the pump components. As a result, damage to the mechanism is unlikely and the risk of trapped fingers is significantly reduced. Designed specifically for HydroLink, the Pump Station connects directly to existing channels and expands the system with an active, player-driven element. It works particularly well as the starting point of larger layouts, creating a continuous flow that can power waterfalls, race boats, vortex modules, and future HydroLink expansions. Features Functional Archimedean screw pump Hand-powered operation Direct HydroLink compatibility No batteries required Designed for outdoor water play Whether used as the heart of a small setup or as the source of a large HydroLink network, the Pump Station transforms the waterway from a passive track into an interactive water playground. description: This is my take on a motorized shade solution for automating existing roller-style shades. This works with traditional cordless roller shades (the spring loaded type that you pull down). Its based around a relatively cheap aliexpress geared brushless motor with an encoder driven by an esp32 for use with ESPHome and HomeAssistant. The finished product is capable of accurate positional control and uses a reed switch at the full open position to re-home the system each time the shade is fully opened. They are relatively quiet, very reliable and operate on 12v DC power. You will have to attach a small magnet to the shade (with tape or something). Here is the Bill of Materials: Item Qty Links Socket head cap M3x6 5 Socket head cap M2x4 7 Small Neodymium Magnet 1 CHR-GM25-BL2418 DC12V i34 (130rpm variant) 1 Link Alibaba (cheaper for bulk) MKA17101 Reed Switch NO 1 Link 5v Buck Converter 1 Link 3x7cm Protoboards 1 Link ESP32 1 Link 608 2RS Ball Bearing 1 Link The more of these you build the cheaper they are per unit because you end up buying the smaller components in bulk anyways. If you make 5 of them they end up being around $25 each. Use Alibaba for the motors if ordering more than one or two. In theory you probably don't need a protoboard if you really want to cut costs. There are two versions of the printed files, one with holes sized for heat-set inserts and one with holes meant to be directly threaded into. Here is a diagram of the wiring: Push the reed switch as much towards the esp32 (into the page) as possible to get it closest to the magnet that you will attach to the shade. When attaching the magnet to the shade, it works best if it is mounted sideways rather than flat. Here is a picture of how I did it, and so far it has never failed to home properly after a month of use. Wherever you place it will determine the stopping point of the shade. The bottom endpoint is configurable inside home assistant. The only issue I have run into is drift over many cycles if the shade isn't homed for a while (eg. 50% →0% → 50%) over and over without fully opening. After around 20 ish cycles it will drift downwards about an inch. As long as they are opened fully periodically, this will never be a problem. Assembly should be pretty straightforward if you follow the exploded view diagram. The gear shroud needs to be snapped on and might require some force, Its not meant to come off again without breaking. I've also included a version of the wall plate with different mounting points for shallower window frames and the hangar I used for the other end of the shade. You may also need to make a different size shade insert to fit in your particular tube. If you leave a comment with the inner diameter of your tube i can add more variants. That's it! Happy printing!

description: Description This is my replica of the legendary Rapala Original Floating 11 cm , designed and modeled directly from a precise 3D scan of an original Rapala F11 lure. The Original Floating is world-renowned for its iconic, wounded-minnow action and its ability to trigger strikes at the surface or mid-water. This 3D-printed version brings that exact legendary presentation to your tackle box, making it an incredible weapon when targeting big perch, trout, pike, and zander. A massive amount of thought, engineering, and testing went into the physics of this design to respect the delicate balance of a true floating lure. Despite the challenges of replicating a balsa wood classic in 3D-printed plastic, this model achieves the exact characteristic swimming action and buoyant floatability that makes the original so famous. Design Notes 3D Scanned Precision: Modeled directly from a physical 3D scan of a real Rapala Original Floating 11 cm to ensure perfect proportions, a sleek profile, and flawless hydrodynamics. Optimized Weight & Physics: The original balsa lure weighs 6 grams. Due to the physical limitations of plastic and internal hardware structures, this fully assembled 3D-printed version weights 7 grams . This slight increase does not negatively impact the lure; in fact, it enhances casting distance, allowing you to cover more water while keeping the iconic swimming action and floating buoyancy completely uncompromised. (Note: Slight weight variations may occur depending on the thickness of your clear coat). True-to-Original Action: Carefully engineered and weighted to replicate the legendary, subtle, and lifelike triggering action of the original F11 model. Reinforced Lip Design (Printed Flat): The diving lip is printed as a separate piece alongside the body to ensure the absolute strongest layer orientation. By printing it flat, the lip gets superior durability, ensuring it won't easily snap off when repeatedly hitting underwater obstacles like large branches, rocks, or heavy submerged weeds and water plants. Advanced Print Stability Block: To guarantee a perfect print and maximize your success rate, I have engineered a custom support stability block system. This system securely locks the slender body in place during the print, completely eliminating wobble so you can print seamlessly without failures. Strength & Testing 6.8 kg+ Load Capacity: This lure uses the exact same robust internal connection system as my other models, which has been thoroughly tested to lift at least 6.8 kg with absolutely no issues. The internal structure and hardware anchor points are rock-solid and built to handle heavy, hard-fighting predators. Strength & Finishing (Crucial Step) To match the ultra-lightweight profile of the original floating lure, this model is engineered with relatively thin walls. Therefore, I highly recommend on the strongest terms that you treat the finished lure with a clear coat to provide essential structural strength and ensure it is 100% waterproof. My Personal Finishing Method: I personally use Nova3D High Transparency Clear UV Resin (intended for resin printers) paired with a handheld UV flashlight to cure it. Dip: Dip the entire printed model directly into the clear UV resin. Drip: Let the excess resin drip off cleanly. Cure: Blast it with the UV flashlight to quickly snap-cure the resin. Repeat: Dip and cure a second time for an ultra-durable, glass-like finish. This process is incredibly fast. When production-lining multiple lures at once, I use my standard resin curing station. Alternatively, a high-quality, traditional 2-component epoxy clear coat also works beautifully. Assembly The lure consists of two printed parts: the main body and the separate diving lip. Remove Support Block: Once printed, simply "rock" the custom stability block back and forth to snap it off the body. Clean & Sand: Use a deburring tool or small snippers/flush cutters to remove any tiny remaining bumps from the connection points. Give it a quick, light sand with 400-grit sandpaper to make it perfectly flush. It takes almost no time at all! Glue the Lip: Secure the diving lip into the body slot using a strong 5-minute epoxy or superglue. Prepare the Holes & Install Hardware: Install the 4 screw eyes into the prepared pilot holes. To make this step incredibly easy, I have uploaded a "Handdrill Handle" model on my MakerWorld profile . You can print it, glue a 1mm HSS drill bit inside, and use it to effortlessly pre-drill the holes before screwing the eyes firmly into place! Alternatively, you can gently heat the screw eyes with a lighter before pressing them into the plastic. Clear the Eyes: If using UV resin or epoxy, remember to clear away any excess clear coat from the screw eyes before curing so they stay completely open for your split rings. Rig the Hooks: Attach your split rings and hooks to the designated screw eyes. Hardware Requirements To fully assemble the lure and match its intended buoyancy and balance, you will need the following hardware: 3x Screw Eyes: Stainless steel. 1.3 mm thread thickness, 12 mm full length, 5 mm outer eye diameter, 8 mm shaft length. (Available on sites, like Temu, for very cheap). 2x Split Rings: Size 5 mm. 2x Treble Hooks: Size #6 is standard, but I recommend size #8 (which I use on my personal builds) to perfectly compensate for the extra 1 gram of body weight and maintain flawless balance. Important For the best balance, the correct swimming action, and optimal floating performance, it is highly recommended to use my included print profile. The internal layout, wall count, and infill distribution are specifically calculated to achieve the target 7g weight and correct center of mass. Changing these settings can heavily affect the lure's unique performance in the water. Tight lines!!

description: Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast bud vases with a smooth design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final vase size of 6.5cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier.

The seal process for the 6437 brushless motor is divided into two main parts: the stator and the rotor. For the rotor: I used a small brush to apply a very thin, even layer of epoxy resin. First, I sealed the wire connections using 706 RTV silicone glue for flexible strain relief, and then I potted the entire component with epoxy. Just a quick tip: make sure to seal or mask off the bearing area beforehand to prevent any epoxy from seeping in and ruining the bearings. As for the ESC (Electronic Speed Controller) : Using an ESC with a higher current rating is absolutely fine and actually gives you a nice safety margin. description: Description This is my replica of the legendary Rapala Mini Fat Rap 3 cm , designed and modeled directly from a precise 3D scan of an original Mini Fat Rap. Famous for its compact profile and tight, aggressive swimming action, the Fat Rap is a classic killer for perch, trout, chub, and other light-tackle predators. This 3D-printed version brings that exact tight wiggling presentation directly to your tackle box! A massive amount of thought, engineering, and testing went into the physics of this ultra-compact design. Because it is so small, replicating the exact action required meticulous balancing. Through fine-tuning the internal structure, this model achieves the exact same characteristic swimming action as the original, creating a lifelike motion that predators simply cannot resist. Design Notes 3D Scanned Precision: Modeled directly from a physical 3D scan of a real Rapala Mini Fat Rap 3 cm to ensure perfect proportions, a fat profile, and flawless hydrodynamics. Lead-Free / Component-Free Weighting: The original balsa lure weighs 4.2 grams. To make this project accessible to everyone, I wanted to design a lure that does not require adding external lead weights , which can be hard to source in the right sizes. Instead, through smart internal geometry, this replica achieves the iconic swimming action at a finished weight of 3.3 grams . It casts incredibly well on light gear and behaves perfectly in the water! Perfected Center of Mass: To match the original's physics without lead, a custom infill modifier has been integrated into a very precise area inside the body. This modifier is set to 20% infill and must not be changed , as it is the secret to the lure's unique balance and stability in the water. Integrated Brimplate Stability: Because of its tiny footprint, I have engineered a custom integrated brimplate as a support system. It completely locks the body in place during fast prints, eliminating any risk of wobble or detachment. Once the print is complete, you can easily "rock" the lure right off the plate cleanly— leaving no annoying connection points or bumps that need to be snipped or sanded off! Crucial Support-Free Lip Design: The diving lip has been carefully oriented so it can be printed entirely without supports, despite its organic, curved shapes. To achieve this successfully, it is pretty much a must to print the lip at a 0.08 mm layer height . This ultra-fine layer height is required to handle the steep overhangs without any flaws or print failures. Strength & Testing 6.8 kg+ Load Capacity: Despite its tiny 3 cm size, this lure uses the exact same robust internal connection system as my larger models. It has been thoroughly tested to lift at least 6.8 kg with absolutely no issues. The internal structure and hardware anchor points are rock-solid and built to handle surprisingly large, hard-fighting fish. Strength & Finishing While this compact model has great structural integrity right off the print bed, applying a high-quality clear coat (like a 2-component epoxy or clear UV resin) will make it 100% waterproof, heavily increase its durability against sharp teeth, and give it a beautiful glass-like professional finish. Assembly The lure consists of two printed parts: the main body and the separate diving lip. Remove Stability Plate: Simply rock the lure off the integrated brimplate. Glue the Lip: Secure the diving lip into the body slot using a strong 5-minute epoxy or superglue. Prepare the Holes & Install Hardware: Install the 3 screw eyes into the prepared pilot holes. To make this step incredibly easy, I have uploaded a "Handdrill Handle" model on my MakerWorld profile . You can print it, glue a 1mm HSS drill bit inside, and use it to effortlessly pre-drill the holes before screwing the eyes firmly into place! Alternatively, you can gently heat the screw eyes with a lighter before pressing them into the plastic. Crucial Step - Front Screw Eye Orientation: When installing the front nose screw eye, it must be screwed in at an upward angle . The internal pilot hole is engineered to point diagonally upwards so the screw shaft completely clears and stays above the diving lip. Please check my uploaded cross-section image of the model to see exactly how the internal channel runs before you begin screwing it in! Clear the Eyes: Clear away any excess resin or epoxy from the screw eyes before curing so they stay completely open for your split rings. Rig the Hooks: Attach your split rings and hooks to the designated screw eyes. Hardware Requirements To fully assemble the lure and match its intended action, you will need the following hardware: 3x Screw Eyes: Stainless steel. 1.3 mm thread thickness, 12 mm full length, 5 mm outer eye diameter, 8 mm shaft length. (Can be bought very cheaply on sites like Temu or AliExpress). 2x Split Rings: Size 5 mm. 2x Treble Hooks: Size #12. Important Print Profile Notice To achieve the absolute best performance, I have uploaded two different print profiles depending on your printer and build plate size: Profile 1 (Recommended - Print by Object): This profile uses Print by Object enabled. This allows the printer to create the diving lip at the required 0.08 mm layer height to successfully handle the overhangs without supports, and the main body at a standard 0.2 mm layer height —all in the very same print job! You get the perfect finish on both parts without starting the printer twice. Profile 2 (Multi-Plate): If you have a very small build plate where Print by Object isn't ideal, use this profile. It splits the main body and the diving lip onto two separate plates so you can print them in two quick, individual runs. Changing the internal infill modifier or wall settings will ruin the delicate balance of this ultra-light lure, so please stick to the profiles for the best results! Tight lines!!

model_name: Twist Bud Vase - 3 Part Slipcasting Mould
description: Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast bud vases with a twisted design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final vase size of 6.5cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier.

model_name: Parametric Rugged Box Gridfinity-Ready No Hardware
description: Parametric Rugged Case, Gridfinity-Ready, Multi Lid Style Your size. Your grid. Your style. A rugged case you print to the exact size you need and optionally Gridfinity-ready. Pick one of the three ready-made sizes if you just want to print and go, or type in your own internal dimensions and the box builds itself around them. Latch and screws are all printed. There’s no hardware to buy . What you get 📦 Fully parametric. You give it the inside dimensions , the usable cavity, and the outside is worked out for you (wall, latch and hinges all live outside the usable volume). Most boxes make you fight the outside to get the inside right. Here you ask for the inside and forget the rest. Three pre-set sizes. S, M and L, dialled in and tested. If you don’t want to touch a parameter, just grab the size you need. No hardware. Latch and screws are printed, no metal anywhere, and the hinge is part of the body. They’re also identical on every size , so one printed set covers all your boxes, and a broken part is just a reprint. Gridfinity-ready, not gridfinity-only. An optional gridfinity baseplate is built into the floor (42 mm pitch), so standard bins drop straight in. Not into gridfinity? Grab the custom model and it’s a plain case. Three interchangeable lids. Two with sci-fi engraving (radial and circuit) and one plain, which you can leave bare or run in multicolour with an AMS. Using it with gridfinity 🧩 The baseplate is molded into the floor at the standard 42 mm pitch, so any standard gridfinity bin sits in it. I’m not shipping a bin generator, there are already good ones out there, so make the bins you need with whatever generator you already trust. Gidfinity Generator Gridfinity Rebuilt Two things worth knowing. Height. In gridfinity mode you set the inside height in U. The catch is that “U” gets measured differently by different generators: the bin’s stacking lip (roughly 4.4 mm) is counted inside the N×7 by some and added on top by others. So measure the bin you actually have in your hand and use that number. One U is 7 mm . When in doubt, trust your calipers. Tall bins. If a bin is as tall as the whole case , shave its front edge at an angle. The lid swings on a hinge, and a full-height bin sitting right at the front lip will catch the lid as it closes. A small diagonal cut on the front face of the bin clears it. Check picture below. Printing and assembly 🛠️ Material : It depends on your use, generally speaking I would use PETG, but PLA would work too. Orientation : the lid prints upside down, top face on the plate, so the engraving comes out crisp. Screws: yes, they print vertically, and yes, I know that usually means fragile. I've printed and used dozens of them and not one has broken. The trick is simple: don't overtighten. They don't need it, hand-snug is enough. Supports : the only support you need is a small one under the lid catch pin. Everything else prints support-free. Warping : on big sizes you could get warping (edges lift up while printing). I solved it using a plate with glue, but a brim or an elephant-foot setting should work too. Keep this in mind if you print big boxes. Assembly : simple. Put the lid on and close it, insert the two screws in the back hinges and tighten them (by hand is enough, don’t force them). Take the latch and push it into the front hinges. Ready. Tolerances : the XY clearance is parametric, set to 0.4 mm total by default (0.2 per side). If your printer runs tight or loose you can adjust it. If you are printing from parametric check setup below. Pre-set sizes 📐 Inside cavity (X × Y) External (X × Y) Default height Small 84 × 42 mm (GF: 2x1) 99.0 × 66.5 mm base 28 / lid 14 mm (4U/2U) Medium 126 × 84 mm (GF: 3x2) 141.0 × 108.5 mm base 28 / lid 14 mm (4U/2U) Large 168 × 126 mm (GF: 4x3) 183.0 × 150.5 mm base 35 / lid 14 mm (5U/2U) Remember the external size is an output. You set the inside , and the wall, the latch, the hinge and the hook add up to the outside on their own. Depth is free in mm in both modes, so the table is a starting point, not a limit. Customizing your own box ⚙️ There are six ready-made versions to pick from: two ways to size the box (gridfinity or custom) times the three lids. Pick the row that matches how you think. Version Sizing Lid You set Gridfinity – Radial gridfinity radial sci-fi engraving grid cells X × Y, box & lid height in U, tolerances Gridfinity – Circuit gridfinity circuit sci-fi engraving grid cells X × Y, box & lid height in U, tolerances Gridfinity – Plain gridfinity plain (or your own with an AMS) grid cells X × Y, box & lid height in U, tolerances Custom – Radial custom radial sci-fi engraving inside X × Y in mm, box & lid height in mm, tolerances Custom – Circuit custom circuit sci-fi engraving inside X × Y in mm, box & lid height in mm, tolerances Custom – Plain custom plain (or your own with an AMS) inside X × Y in mm, box & lid height in mm, tolerances The gridfinity versions have the baseplate active, good if you’re building around bins you already have. The custom versions have no baseplate (but you could add it as standalone part like the bins), good if you just want a case of a specific size. One U is 7 mm, so in the gridfinity versions the height steps in 7 mm units, while in the custom versions you set it freely in mm. Every parameter has a safe min/max already set. You'll see the limits in the customize panel, stay within them and it'll generate fine. Once you’ve got your size, you download a single 3mf with everything in it. To print: Open the 3mf in Bambu Studio. Right-click the model. Split → To Objects. Arrange the parts on the plate and set up the slicer (see Printing and assembly above). Printing from the parametric source (no preset profile) 🧩 If you download the print profile, everything is already set and you can ignore this. This is only for people slicing the parametric model from scratch. Global settings: Enable "slow down for overhangs". Layer height 0.20mm. You can go lower for a finer finish, but 0.20mm is enough for everything except the threaded hardware (see below). Per-object settings: Lid: place it top face down on the plate (engraving against the plate). Add a small support under the front catch pin only (should be added by default when support is enabled). Bolt and cap nut: print these at 0.12mm . The finer layers are what let the threads come out clean and turn properly. The closure, and the honest bit about water 💧 The latch is a snap. I went through a couple dozen prototypes first. An over-center toggle looked great on paper but it’s too fragile to print tolerances, so the snap won: it held better and took the cycling without complaining. About water, straight talk: this is splash and dust resistant, not waterproof. FDM parts are porous along the layer lines, and TPU isn’t soft enough to spread and seal, so no printed gasket holds up well, I've tested a lot. I’d rather say that than have you find out in a river. There’s a tongue-and-groove channel around the rim: leave it empty (the labyrinth alone stops splashes, dust and pocket lint) or press in a soft TPU cord, a silicone cord or a rubber elastic to push it further. For real watertightness this article on closable prints is the best reference, short version being that an O-ring with silicone grease beats any printed seal . If you try something in that channel and it works, tell me. I’d like to collect what people find. Notes 📝 If you liked my older Travel Box , this is a different take on the same idea, rebuilt from scratch. Not a successor, just the same itch scratched a different way. Print it, post a make, drop a comment. I read them, the feedback on the last one shaped half the decisions here. Credits: Gridfinity by Zack Freedman, licensed CC-BY. The baseplate follows the standard gridfinity spec.

Tired of fighting with the stock xTool M2 hold-down feet every time you need to remove and reposition a project? This magnetic alignment jig was designed to provide repeatable material registration for the xTool M2 laser cutter. The jig uses magnetic corner fixtures that reference the plywood edges rather than the corner itself. A built-in corner relief allows chipped, rounded, or imperfect plywood corners to sit correctly against the locating surfaces without affecting alignment. This makes it ideal for projects that require multiple operations, such as paint filling, resin filling, sanding, staining, or multi-pass engraving. The design was created as a fully parametric Onshape model, allowing dimensions such as material size, wall thickness, magnet size, and corner relief dimensions to be easily customized for your own workflow. Why I Made This I originally designed this because I got tired of fighting with the stock xTool M2 hold-down feet. The factory feet work fine for keeping material from moving, but they don't provide reliable registration. If you remove a project for painting, resin filling, sanding, or inspection, you often have to spend time getting everything lined back up. This jig solves that problem. Place your material against the locating faces, remove it when needed, and drop it back into the exact same position later. Features Magnetic mounting system Repeatable material registration Edge-referenced positioning Corner relief for imperfect corners Embedded magnet pockets Easy customization through Onshape will work with any Laser engraver that has a metal bed. Embedded Magnet Installation The magnet pockets are designed to capture magnets during the print. Add a pause in your slicer at the layer immediately before the magnet cavities are covered. When the printer pauses: Insert the magnets into the cavities. Verify the polarity is correct. Resume printing. The remaining layers will seal the magnets inside the part. No glue required. 🏖️ GRAB Ground Retention Anchor Block Stop chasing your umbrella. Let physics do the work. We've all seen it. A sudden gust of wind, a beach umbrella taking off like a kite, and someone sprinting across the beach trying to catch it. GRAB was designed to solve that problem with an incredibly simple principle: Use the sand as the anchor. Simply bury GRAB, wrap a rope around its central groove, and connect it to your umbrella. Once buried and covered with sand, it acts as a deadman anchor , using the weight and resistance of the surrounding sand to keep everything firmly in place. 🔧 How to use Use GRAB to dig a hole about 15–20 cm deep . Wrap your rope around the central groove. Bury GRAB completely and compact the sand. Connect the rope to your umbrella. Relax. ⚠️ Disclaimer GRAB is designed to improve umbrella stability in sand but cannot guarantee protection against extreme weather conditions . Always remove your umbrella in strong winds or stormy weather.

model_name: Rubber Band Powered Toy Plane THAT FLIES
description: Description This is my second iteration of a rubber-band-powered 3D printed plane. The fuselage has been redesigned around a NACA 0012 aerofoil profile. The model also uses an adjustable flat wing. The front propeller is a 3D printed 3 blade propeller driven by a rubber band. The materials and assembly approach are pretty similar, but this version was printed using Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament. This model is intended as a toy and a simple educational aircraft. Materials Required 3D printer duh Rubber band (40 to 50 cm) Super glue Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament or any other suitable filament. Optional: sandpaper or small file for cleaning tight printed joints Assembly Instructions Step 1: Print all parts Print all the model parts. For best results, keep the parts lightweight. A heavy fuselage or propeller will reduce flight performance. After printing, remove any stringing, rough edges or small blobs from the parts. Step 2: Adjust the adjustable wing The wing should sit straight and level when viewed from the front. Small changes to the wing position or angle can be used later to trim the flight path. Step 3: Insert the rod hook and attach the small nub Insert the rod, as shown in the pictures, and then add the nub on the outside of the nose of the plane. Do not glue anything as off yet. Step 4: Install the propeller Then insert the propeller after the nub and glue only the front of the propeller to the rod, make sure to not glue the nub to the nose or rod. Allow the glue to dry fully before installing the rubber band or testing the propeller. Check that the propeller can rotate freely, which then inturn should also now turn the hook and thus wind the rubber band. The nub should be abe to rotate independently to the propeller and hook. If the propeller is stiff, lightly clean or sand the contact area until it spins smoothly. Step 5: Attach the rubber band Attach one end of the rubber band to the rear hook on the fuselage. Attach the other end to the propeller hook. The rubber band should sit along the fuselage centreline. It should be tight enough to drive the propeller, but not so tight that it bends the fuselage or pulls the propeller out of alignment. Step 6: Check alignment Before winding the rubber band, check the full model alignment. The fuselage should be straight, the wing should be level or adjusted, and the propeller should spin freely. The rubber band should not rub heavily against the printed body. If the model turns too much during testing, adjust the wing position slightly and test again. Step 7: First test wind Wind the propeller gently by hand for the first test. Do not fully wind the rubber band immediately. Start with a low number of turns to check that the propeller works and that the rubber band stays attached. Release the propeller carefully and check that it spins smoothly. Step 8: Flight trimming Test the plane in a clear open area. If the nose drops or rises quickly, increase throw speed or try a different wing angle. (CoG sits below the wings so the issue can be fixed with just how you throw it). If the plane rolls or turns sharply, check that the wing is symmetrically bent or is flat and that the propeller is aligned with the fuselage centreline. Notes This model is designed for simple educational testing and is a toy, not long-distance powered flight (a motorised version would be cool). Lightweight printing improves performance. The propeller must spin freely for the rubber band mechanism to work properly. The adjustable wing is useful for experimenting with stability and trim. Test indoors only if there is enough space, or outdoors in calm conditions. Do not aim the plane at people, animals, windows or fragile objects. Print Material Used Printed using Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament.

Plate 6 (56x36mm Oval Frame): Sized for pools with a medium 56mm x 36mm oval frame tube. Plate 7 (61x41mm Oval Frame): Sized for pools with a large 61mm x 41mm oval frame tube. Dieses rechteckige Lüftungsgitter ist voll anpassbar, d.h. die meisten Parameter können eingestellt werden. Optional kann auch ein sehr feines passendes Insektenschutzgitter ergänzt werden, das hinten in das Lüftungsgitter gesteckt wird. Mögliche Einstellungen für das Lüftungsgitter Breite, Höhe, Tiefe und Dicke des Rahmens, der in die Öffnung (Wand, Schrank) eingesteckt wird. Breite der vorderen Blende - wie viel soll über die Wand nach außen ragen und wie viel soll nach innen überlappen Lamellen: Länge, Winkel, Dicke. Und ein Faktor, der bestimmt, ob sie genau die Sicht verdecken (Faktor=1) oder größere Lücken lassen (Faktor > 1) oder dichter sind (Faktor < 1) Querstreben: Die Querstreben dienen der Stabilisierung und lassen das Gitter auch “professioneller” aussehen. Einstellbar sind Anzahl, Dicke und Tiefe. Außerdem kann man wählen, ob sie 5 mm nach hinten versetzt werden sollen. Das sieht noch sauberer aus, erfordert aber das Drucken mit Stützstrukturen. Das von mir eingestellte Druckprofil hat bereits die entsprechenden Einstellungen. Hilfreiches Es gibt eine englische und eine deutsche Version der Einstellungs-Datei. Du brauchst ein rundes Lüftungsgitter? Das findest du hier . Insektenschutz Das Insektenschutzgitter ist optional und kann hinten in das Lüftungsgitter eingelegt werden, um selbst sehr kleine Insekten fernzuhalten. Ich habe es in ein separates Projekt ausgelagert, um es auch für andere Lüftungsgitter-Modelle verfügbar zu machen: Insektenschutz für Lüftungsgitter Die Maße müssen passend zum Lüftungsgitter eingestellt werden. Dabei muss die Wandstärke berücksichtigt werden: X: Breite - 2 * Wandstärke Y: Höhe - 2 * Wandstärke Z: nicht ändern, auf 1 mm lassen Beispiel: Maße des Teils, das in die Wandöffnung gesteckt wird: 100 x 200 mm. Wandstärke 3 mm Dann muss das Insektenschutzgitter die Größe 94 x 194 haben, denn X=100-2*3=94 und Y=200-2*3=194 Wie immer freue ich mich über Kommentare und Feedback, Verbesserungsvorschläge oder Wünsche. description: NOVA MEG-X — Magnetic Levitation Future Car What can you build when gravity is no longer a limitation? THE DESIGN: NOVA MEG-X was born from MakerWorld's Kit Challenge Round 3: Magnetic Levitation DIY. I joined the contest, won it, and everything started from there: a futuristic car, designed from scratch to float steadily above its RGB base. Every line was shaped to suggest speed and a "next-generation" feel, but the real challenge was weight: the levitation kit holds up to 200 g, and NOVA MEG-X comes in at just 184 g (magnet included). A balance chased millimeter by millimeter, to float with margin and stay perfectly stable. FROM 3D DESIGN TO REAL MODEL: Everything was modeled in Fusion 360, with careful attention to every section and detail before printing. Below you'll find some images of the project: 3D views of the car, internal cross-sections, and the various components that make up the system. THE COMPONENTS: Everything you need to build it: Filaments (Bambu Lab PLA) - Black — PLA Basic 10101 - Blue — PLA Basic 10604 - Gray — PLA Basic 10104 - Translucent — PLA Translucent 13612 (to let the LED light shine through) Hardware - Maker's Supply Magnetic Levitation Kit — ZC008 - S Shape LED Strip Light — KA2 - 2× BT3x6 screws — AA170 (car) - 4× M3x8 SHCS screws — AA037 (levitation kit) THE CLEVER BITS: This is where NOVA MEG-X becomes more than just a model sitting on a kit. Multicolor car with a glowing logo. The car prints in multicolor (4 colors) and uses translucent material in key spots: an LED inside shines through and lights up the logo on top of the car, creating a glowing effect along the sides. Fully integrated LED system — no glue. I designed: - a slot built directly into the print to house the LED strip; - a custom clip that bends and locks the LED, keeping it low and in place; - a second clip that holds the touch button. Hidden touch button. To change the lighting, just tap (don't press!) a spot on the top cover with your finger. No visible buttons, no cables sticking out. Linear effect on the base. The base's top cover features a linear pattern that creates a beautiful play of light along the sides. INCLUDED FILES: Files are cleaned up and ready to go: Car (NOVA MAG-X) - 3mf Nova Mag-X → complete pre-assembled file, multicolor - Separate parts: Front Fascia, Rear Fascia, Insert, Magnet Cover Levitation Base - 3mf Base → complete pre-assembled file - Separate parts: Base, Bezel, Top Cover, Led Retainer, Pcb Retainer, Nameplate COMING SOON: This is just the beginning. If you like NOVA MEG-X, more versions of the series are coming! Let me know in the comments which one you'd like to see. Doppel TinyWhoop Case Übersicht Da es häufiger Anfragen gab, ob ich ein Case entwickeln kann, welches zwei TinyWhoops gleichzeitig unterbringen kann, habe ich dieses Doppel TinyWhoop Case entworfen. Das Case ist die Weiterentwicklung meines bekannten BetaFPV-Cases für einen Copter und bietet nun Platz für bis zu zwei TinyWhoops, zahlreiche Akkus, ein 1S-Ladegerät sowie Ersatzteile und Werkzeug. Features Platz für 2 TinyWhoops In der Standardausführung können folgende Modelle direkt verwendet werden: 2 × BetaFPV Meteor 75 Pro Kompatible Copter Mit optionalen Einsätzen BetaFPV Air65 (mit Air65-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air65 II (mit Air65 II-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air75 (mit Air75-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air75 II (mit Air75 II-Einsatz) BetaFPV Meteor 65 Pro (mit Meteor 65 Pro-Einsatz) Mobula 6 (mit Air65-Einsatz) Ohne zusätzlichen Einsatz HDZero M8 Freestyle Für weitere Modelle können zukünftig zusätzliche Einsätze veröffentlicht werden. Ladegerät-Kompatibilität Im Case ist Platz für das beliebte WhoopStor 3 1S Ladegerät . Zusätzlich ist ein optionaler Einsatz erhältlich, mit dem auch das BetaFPV Hexa 1S Ladegerät sicher im Case untergebracht werden kann. Akku-Aufbewahrung Im Deckel des Cases können bis zu 29 Stück 1S LiPos sicher verstaut werden. Wichtiger Hinweis: Die Halteklammern für die Akkus müssen gegebenenfalls mit etwas Sekundenkleber fixiert werden, damit sie dauerhaft sicher sitzen und sich nicht verschieben. Parts- & Tool-Fach Das Case verfügt über eine integrierte Ablage für: Ersatzteile Werkzeug Propeller Schrauben weiteres Zubehör Die Ablage wird durch ein verschiebbares Rollo verschlossen und schützt den Inhalt während des Transports. Verbesserte Verschlüsse Da das Doppel-Case größer als das ursprüngliche Einzel-Case ist, wurde es mit zwei Verschlüssen ausgestattet. Dadurch wird gewährleistet, dass das Case auch bei voller Beladung sicher verschlossen bleibt. Wichtiger Hinweis zur finalen Version Die auf den Bildern gezeigte Version ist gespiegelt. Nach dem ersten Testdruck ist mir aufgefallen, dass das Ladegerät in der ursprünglichen Anordnung auf dem Kopf stehen würde. Deshalb wurden die Positionen des Ladegeräts und der Tool-Ablage in der finalen Version miteinander getauscht. Die veröffentlichten Dateien enthalten bereits diese überarbeitete Version. Benötigte Hardware Für den Zusammenbau werden zusätzlich folgende Schrauben benötigt: Scharniere 3 × M3x20 mm Schrauben Verschlüsse 4 × M3x30 mm Schrauben Für jeden Verschluss werden zwei Schrauben benötigt. Montage der Scharniere Deckel und Unterteil so ausrichten, dass die Scharnierhälften ineinandergreifen. Die Scharnierhälften zusammenschieben. Anschließend jeweils eine M3x20 mm Schraube durch das Scharnier führen. Die Schraube dient dabei als Achse und ermöglicht die Drehbewegung des Deckels. Montage der Verschlüsse Die beiden Verschlussklemmen mit insgesamt vier M3x30 mm Schrauben montieren. Anschließend prüfen, ob die Verschlüsse leichtgängig arbeiten und das Case sicher schließen. Montage der Tool-Ablage Schritt 1 Zunächst die linke und rechte Seitenwand mit dem Boden zusammenstecken. Gegebenenfalls muss der Boden leicht nachbearbeitet werden, damit er mit etwas Druck in die beiden Seitenwände passt. Schritt 2 Die vormontierte Baugruppe in die dafür vorgesehene Aussparung im Case einschieben. Dabei zunächst etwa 1 cm vor der endgültigen Position stoppen. Schritt 3 Nun das Rollo von der Frontseite aus in die Führungsschienen einschieben. Tipp: Ein kleiner Tropfen Öl in den Führungen erleichtert das Einschieben und verbessert die Leichtgängigkeit des Rollos. Schritt 4 Sobald das Rollo vollständig eingeschoben wurde, kann die komplette Baugruppe bis zur Endposition in das Case geschoben werden. Schritt 5 Falls der Rahmen etwas locker sitzt, kann dieser mit einem kleinen Tropfen Sekundenkleber fixiert werden. Viel Spaß mit dem Doppel TinyWhoop Case!
