description: Description This is the Inch Preset Version of a fully parametric straight barbed hose-to-thread adapter with automatic engraved identification and an adjustable external thread fit . A dedicated THREAD_FIT parameter allows the user to compensate for printer, filament and slicer tolerances without changing the selected nominal UNC thread. For example, a 1/2-13 UNC fitting remains a 1/2-13 UNC fitting, while the generated male thread can be reduced slightly for smoother assembly with the real mating component. This is especially useful because printed male threads can become too tight due to: extrusion width slight overextrusion filament dimensional variation material shrinkage outer-wall flow printer calibration mating-thread tolerance Each generated fitting also includes automatic identification engraved directly on the hexagonal body: the selected nominal UNC thread diameter on one face, for example 3/4" the selected hose diameter on an adjacent face, for example Ø1/2" The full thread designation, including TPI and UNC series, remains selected in the Customizer. The shorter engraved labels remain readable even on smaller hexagonal bodies. The labels update automatically whenever the Customizer parameters are changed. This makes every printed fitting immediately identifiable, even after it has been removed from its storage box or mixed with other adapters. There is no need to manually add text, rename the model or measure the fitting after printing. The model is designed to connect a flexible rubber, silicone or soft PVC hose to a male UNC threaded port. It combines five main functional features: a parametric barbed hose connection an imperial hexagonal wrench section an external UNC male thread adjustable printed thread clearance through THREAD_FIT automatic engraved size identification All main dimensions are selected through practical fractional-inch presets. The user does not need to manually convert fractions into decimal inches or millimeters. The model can be customized directly in OpenSCAD / MakerWorld Customizer by selecting only seven essential parameters. The remaining technical dimensions are calculated automatically, including: barb height number of barbs thread diameter thread pitch from TPI thread length internal passage minimum wall thickness minimum hexagonal size engraved thread label engraved hose diameter label external thread clearance compensation The geometry is generated internally in millimeters, while the Customizer displays familiar fractional-inch values. The complete adapter maintains a minimum radial wall thickness of 1.8 mm beneath the barb roots, around the thread root and across the hexagonal faces. Airform Lamp v2 This project is a complete rework of my original Airform Lamp . The Airform Lamp was one of my first FDM 3D printing projects . At the time, limited experience led to some design flaws, particularly in the lamp’s shape and printability. This new version was developed to eliminate those issues . Airform Lamp V2 improves upon the original by featuring a reworked internal and outer structure , using only easily printable angles for more consistent and reliable results. The new version also uses the Lamp Kit 001 instead of the previous E14 bulb setup . The new Lamp uses way less Supports and is much more clean and consistent with newly made print profiles (see below for more info) If you prefer the proportions and build of the original Airform Lamp , the project is still available and can be found here, althoug i do not recommend printing the old settings : Airform Lamp Print Settings To achieve the best possible surface quality when printing the lampshade, I added a sacrificial (dummy) object to the build plate. This object helps even out the layer printing time , which significantly reduces visible layer lines on certain areas of the lampshade. Without it, uneven cooling can cause noticeable artifacts. For the smoothest results , the following settings were enabled: Ironing on the top layers Variable layer height Arachne wall mode Reduced wall speed for improved surface quality These adjustments help achieve a clean, consistent finish on the lampshade. Step 4: Insert the bottom cap into the underside of the lamp base. The cap should hold in place by tension . Step 5: Attach the lamp shade to the threaded part of the lamp base. Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast round ornaments with a smooth design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 6.5cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier.

description: Description This is my replica of the famous Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm , designed and modeled directly from a precise 3D scan of an original 4-gram Rapala Jointed lure. Known for its broken-back design and unmistakable, hyper-active swimming action, the Jointed Floating is a legendary choice when fish are finicky or biting short. This 3D-printed version brings that exact lively, snake-like presentation directly to your tackle box, making it perfect for targeting perch, trout, pike, and zander. A massive amount of engineering and testing went into recreating the physics of a two-part jointed balsa lure in 3D-printed plastic. Because the action depends entirely on the freedom of movement between the two sections, the internal balance has been meticulously tuned to achieve the exact same characteristic swimming motion as the original classic. Design Notes 3D Scanned Precision: Modeled directly from a physical 3D scan of a real Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm to ensure perfect proportions and flawless hydrodynamics. True-to-Original Weight: Engineered to match the compact 4-gram profile of the original, providing excellent buoyancy and a highly responsive action on light tackle gear. Finetuned Slicer Modifiers: The lively and chaotic swimming action of this lure relies heavily on custom internal weight distribution. I have integrated multiple precise slicer modifiers inside the model to perfect the center of mass for both sections. It is crucial that you do not change these settings , as they have been heavily tested and tuned across numerous prototypes. Crucial Support-Free Lip Design: The diving lip is oriented to print completely flat on its own separate plate. To handle the steep overhangs successfully without supports, it is highly recommended to print the lip at a 0.08 mm layer height . Printing it at a standard 0.2 mm layer height will cause print flaws on the curved edges. Strength & Testing 6.8 kg+ Load Capacity: Despite the jointed design, this lure uses the exact same robust internal hardware connection system as my other models. It has been thoroughly tested to lift at least 6.8 kg with absolutely no issues. The internal structure is rock-solid and fully prepared to handle heavy, hard-fighting predators. Strength & Finishing (Crucial Step) Applying a clear coat is highly recommended to ensure the model is 100% waterproof and to add structural strength. ⚠️ IMPORTANT FINISHING NOTE: Unlike my other models, do not dip this lure in your clear coat! Instead, I highly recommend applying your UV resin or epoxy clear coat with a brush . It is extremely important that you keep the central joint connection completely clean. If resin or epoxy gets inside the "link" where the two screw eyes connect, it will lock up the joint and ruin the lure's unique swimming action. Assembly The lure consists of three printed parts: the front body, the rear tail section, and the separate diving lip. Prep the Parts: Clean up any print lines or imperfections. Secure the diving lip into the front body slot using a strong 5-minute epoxy or superglue. Assemble the Joint (The Link): To create the jointed action, take two stainless steel screw eyes. Gently bend one of the eyelets slightly open with a pair of pliers, loop the second screw eye into it, and bend it completely shut again. Install the Joint: Screw the ends of this connected pair into the pre-modeled holes linking the front body and tail section together. Make sure the joint moves freely and smoothly. Install Remaining Hardware: Install the remaining 3 screw eyes (nose, front belly, and tail) into their pilot holes. (Tip: Use my 1mm Handdrill Handle tool from my profile to pre-drill the holes, or gently heat the screw eyes with a lighter before screwing them in for maximum strength). Rig the Hooks: Attach your split rings and size #8 treble hooks to the designated belly and tail screw eyes. Hardware Requirements To fully assemble the lure, you will need the following hardware: 5x Screw Eyes: Stainless steel. 1.3 mm thread thickness, 12 mm full length, 5 mm outer eye diameter, 8 mm shaft length. (Can be bought very cheaply on sites like Temu or AliExpress). 2x Split Rings: Size 5 mm. 2x Treble Hooks: Size #8. Important Print Profile Notice To make printing as easy as possible, the included print profile is split onto two plates : Plate 1: Contains the main body parts set to a standard 0.2 mm layer height . Plate 2: Contains the diving lip set to the required 0.08 mm layer height to handle the steep overhangs perfectly. (Note: If your printplate is big enough, you can easily combine these onto a single plate and utilize "Print by Object" to print both parts in a single run). Tight lines!!

description: Powered Pottery Handle and Coil Extruder 2.0 New Design is all 3D printed to use with Powered Caulk Gun This is a powered pottery extruder. It has a 47mm (1.85 in) inside diameter. Can support extruding shapes of about 1.5". There are three separate Print Profiles for all the pieces. The extruder main body is printed from Transparent PETG, the Accessories for the plunger and adapter to the caulk gun, and a wide variety of handle and coil dies printed in PLA. IMPORTANT - The Extruder Body should be printed so it has solid walls, the profile is setup to print very slow to allow better transparency and better layer adhesion. If you change print settings be careful, the powered caulk gun can put enough force to separate the layer lines on the printed body. The setting for transparent PETG were tested with Sunlu Clear PETG and held up to the forces. Other plastics and settings may need to be experimented with. With a 0.4mm nozzle the body takes a bit of time to print. Using a 0.6mm nozzle can speed this up. SEE NOTE BELOW ON USING VARIABLE LAYER HEIGHT FOR THREADS. THE DEFAULT LAYER HEIGHT IS 0.24mm AND THE THREADS ARE AT 0.08MM. IF YOU CHANGE NOZZLES THIS WILL NEED TO BE RESET. Assembly Instructions Assembly is pretty easy, print the extruder body and cap in the first profile and the p;unger and adapter in the second profile. Print one or more of the extruder dies in the third profile 1) The plunger adaptor replaces the black plastic part on the caulk gun and the plunger screws into the adapter. 2) Then add one of the extruder dies onto the extruder body and screw on the top fitting. 3) Load clay, it takes about 700g of clay. Don't overfill need to leave about 1.5" of free space to allow room to screw the extruder to the caulk gun. A plunger handle is included to help pack down the clay. 4) Then attach the extruder body to the caulk gun. Use caution when running, the extruder body should be strong enough but best to stop the plunger before it goes all the way to the end. Addition Parts Needed Extruder Gun - Ryobi Caulk Gun - https://www.ryobitools.com/products/33287195169 Notes: Can usually find it around $50 on sale without battery, if you already have Ryobi one tools. Full kit is usually $130.00-$200.00 Other options may work, the harbor freight version looks like its the same interface for the caulk tube ($39 without battery). I have not tested to see if this works: https://www.harborfreight.com/20v-caulk-and-adhesive-gun-tool-only-59793.html European versions use a different tube style so not sure they work. Tested by user @wbarringer42 with the Dewalt DCE560 as well as the Ryobi. There are now over 16 coil and handle dies! NOTE: IF YOU CHANGE NOZZLE (or possibly other changes), THE ADJUSTABLE LAYER HEIGHT FOR THE THREADS WILL NOT BE SET. ITS ONLY SET FOR THE 0.4MM NOZZLE. For the threads make sure the layer height is at 0.08mm not the default 0.24mm or the threads will not be as good. The threads on the original 3mf file have 0.08 layer height using the Variable Layer Height option for both the top and bottom threads. Same for the matting cap. Also with the PETG print slow to get good layer adhesion. At 0.24 layer height the threads are not great and maybe hard to get started. Also print the PETG slow both for the translucent to be more clear (its never clear without alot of post processing) and for strength. SkyOrb — Live Flight Radar & Clock (ESP32) Watch real aircraft fly overhead in real time, right on your desk. SkyOrb is a desk gadget built around an ESP32 and two round 1.28" displays. One screen is a live flight radar with an animated sweep that makes nearby aircraft glow as it passes over them; the second screen is a clean digital clock with the day and date. This model is the 3D-printed enclosure that holds it all together — and the firmware is free and flashes straight from your web browser, no coding required. ✨ What it does Live flight tracking — shows real aircraft around your location using free ADS-B data (no account, no API key, no subscription). Animated radar sweep — planes light up as the sweep passes, just like a real radar scope. Callsigns and altitudes show right on the display. Airport markers — nearby airports appear on the radar; the portal can auto-find commercial airports near you. Digital clock — the second round display shows the time, day, and date. It auto-detects your time zone (with daylight saving) once you set your location, and supports both 12-hour and 24-hour formats. Set up from your phone — a built-in web page lets you set your location, search radius, airports, clock format, and even the portal's accent color. No computer needed after flashing. Tap to track — tap any flight in the web portal to open it on FlightRadar24. 🛠️ What you need (electronics) These are inexpensive, widely available parts: ESP32 dev board (30-pin ESP-WROOM-32) Two GC9A01 round 1.28" displays (240×240 SPI, 7-pin) — one for the radar, one for the clock 30-pin ESP32 GPIO breakout board with screw terminals — lets you wire everything up with no soldering A USB cable for power (Exact links to the parts I used are in the firmware project — see the link at the bottom.) 🖨️ About this print This model is the SkyOrb enclosure. It's designed to hold the ESP32, the breakout board, and both round displays in a clean desk-friendly housing. Print settings (suggested): Material: PLA Layer height: 0.2 mm Infill: 15–20% Supports: No Supports Needed No brim needed Print orientation and any part-specific notes are shown in the preview images. The display bezels are sized for standard GC9A01 round modules. ⚡ Flashing the firmware (no coding!) The firmware installs straight from your web browser using ESP Web Tools — there's nothing to download or compile. Wire up the two displays to the ESP32 using the breakout board (wiring diagram is included on the install page). Open the SkyOrb installer page in Chrome or Edge on a computer, plug in your ESP32, and click Install . After flashing, connect your phone to the SKYORB-Setup WiFi hotspot, pick your home network, and enter your password. Switch your phone back to your home WiFi, then open skyorb.local in a browser to set your location. Done — planes appear within seconds. The radar display even shows the setup address on screen at startup, so you never need a serial monitor or any developer tools. 💡 Why I built it I wanted something that made the invisible traffic in the sky above me feel real and tangible — a little window into what's flying overhead at any moment. SkyOrb turns live flight data into a calm, glanceable desk object, and pairing it with a clock made it something I actually keep next to my monitor all day. The whole thing is open and free so anyone can build their own. 📦 What's included 3D-printable enclosure files (this model) Link to the free firmware + browser-based installer Full wiring guide and step-by-step setup instructions 🔗 Firmware & full build guide The firmware, browser installer, wiring tables, and parts list are all free and open source here: https://gulfcoastmaker.github.io/SkyOrb/ Licensed under the MIT License — free to build, modify, and share. Flight data by airplanes.live · Airport & address lookup by OpenStreetMap · Browser flashing by ESP Web Tools. Built it? I'd love to see your SkyOrb — post a Make and share a photo!

model_name: 3U 10" Rack Case - Mini-ITX + SFX PSU + GPU
description: A proper SFX-powered Mini-ITX rack case — finally! I run a 10" rack homelab and wanted to run local AI workloads in the rack — that meant fitting a real GPU alongside an SFX PSU and a Mini-ITX motherboard in the same enclosure. So I designed this enclosure that mounts the GPU directly into the PCIe slot, combining everything into a single 3U unit. Compatibility 10" rack Side panels and SSD-bay is compatible with “ NAS ” variation! What fits in this enclosure Mini-itx motherboard SFX Power Supply GPU (Thickness up to 42-43mm) 2x 60x60x20mm fans 1x 92x92x15mm fan Max CPU cooler height: ~80mm (measured from motherboard PCB to top panel interior — not confirmed, verify your cooler fits before building) Models used in renders: Mini-ITX motherboard , SFX Power Supply , GPU — sourced from GrabCAD. Structural Integrity Total weight of the enclosure with all hardware installed is around 3.5kg, so structural integrity has been a real concern and top priority since day one. Unlike the storage version, this enclosure doesn't have an HDD tray to help distribute load — instead the main stress point is the GPU, which is supported directly by the PCIe slot without a riser cable. The front panel uses 4mm thickness, 25% infill, and 6 walls, fixed with 3 screws on the left side and 5 on the right due to space constraints. I also did some stress testing by shaking the case from the rack ears and it feels solid. The one thing I haven't tested is long-term behavior — I can't guarantee how it holds up under stress over months or years, but deformation shouldn't be an issue under normal use. The enclosure is printed in PETG, and if you want even more rigidity you can use ASA or ASA-CF. Thermals Tested with an AMD Ryzen 5 5600G (Thermalright X47 cooler) and an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB under full load (GPU burn-in and s-tui stress testing). CPU stabilized around 80°C and GPU around 70°C — both within acceptable range for an enclosed rack build. Hardware requirements Heatset inserts M3 OD - 5mm / L - 4-5mm Aliexpress M3 x 6mm Aliexpress Motherboard standoff M3 - Length 6mm Aliexpress Motherboard screw M3 Aliexpress 6-32x6mm (GPU bracket screws) Aliexpress Power Button - 12mm Aliexpress Hardware Total M3x6 36 Inserts 27 Motherboard standoff 4 Motherboard screws 4 6-32x6mm 2 Power Button - 12mm 1 Print settings Some panels use Grid or Honeycomb infill with 0 top/bottom layers to allow airflow through the walls and to speed up printing compared to modelled honeycomb or grid patterns. Settings are included in the .3mf file, but if issues occur or you are using an incompatible slicer, see the instructions below. These instructions apply specifically to BambuStudio/OrcaSlicer but same idea works with all slicers I believe and I will provide .step files so model data for slicing stays intact. Object specific settings can be found in “Objects” view. Under objects menu choose objects/object which you want to change settings with. Set global settings first and after that set per object settings otherwise global settings are gonna override some per object settings. Global settings for all parts Infill gyroid 25% Wall loops 6 - Top shell layers 6 - Bottom shell layers 4 Material: PETG Nozzle size: 0.4mm Layer height: 0.2mm Front panel/rear panel/fan grill mesh settings Infill grid 50% Wall loops 0 - Top shell layers 0 - Bottom shell layers 0 Honeycomb settings for left and right side panel. Infill honeycomb 20% Wall loops 1 - Top shell layers 0 - Bottom shell layers 0 Front panel should look like that after slicing. Right and left side panels should have this type of honeycomb ventilation after slicing. In case you want to experiment with sidepanel patterns, feel free to choose different infill or even tinker with .step models. Notes Some images have been AI-enhanced, but all photos show the real printed model. This model is designed around KWS rack dimensions. It should also fit LabRax racks by dimension, but note it extends ~7mm past the rear. Panels with grid/honeycomb patterns cannot be printed via Bambu Handy — per-object infill settings are not supported in the app.

I really like the design of BeamCase and I wanted a smaller version of it. So what I have created is basically that. I have based some of the design on the BeamCase (designed from scratch) - mainly the truss on the mobo tray. The case is not modular, there is only one 5.5L version - and I won't be making any other versions of it. Specs: 5.5L volume (not accounting for panels) Max 47mm cooler height Max 2 slot 200mm GPU Flex ATX PSU 90mm fans at the top - brackets are made for Noctua NF-A9x14 which are 14.5mm thick Filament: Frame - I've used Bambu Labs PETG-HF, but according to the internet It would be best if you used ABS or ASA for the internal parts, although you will need to take the shrinkage into the account Panels - Does not really matter, PLA is fine. I used Polymer Panchroma PLA Matte Lime Green Note on seams: If you want to use raw STLs, make sure the seams for the brackets that go into the T-Slots are NOT anywhere near the T-Slots. I have manually painted seams in the included profile to avoid that. Note on panels: Panels are in a separate print profile and have an internal infill-based pattern - which means you can control it in the slicer. I am partial to triangles but you can set it up however you want :) You will get better results using thicker nozzles, I've used 0.6mm - 0.4mm works ok too but the panels are a bit less rigid. Parts needed: 200mm double reverse PCI-E riser - Specifically this one (4.0) from Aliexpress Bracket is made to fit only this riser but I've included step file so you can modify it to fit yours 16mm push button for power button - you can buy it pre-made, I soldered my own, cable length should be ~20cm Hardware needed: 1010 T-Slot Makerbeam 200mm extrusion profiles T-Slot M3 Nuts from Makerbeam Countersunk M3 screws, just buy a whole bag of each, you can use them in different projects :) 6mm 8mm 12mm 16mm PSU - #6-32 x 3/8" UNC screws - I bought these M3 nuts Note: I take no responsibility for you breaking your potentially expensive PC parts. You are building this case at your own risk, so double-check clearances, whether you are using the correct length of screws, support heavy components, and proceed carefully. I only tested it with my own components and I cannot guarantee it will fit your exact configuration. Components I have used for my build: Mobo - Asrock B550M-ITX/ac Cooler - Thermalright AXP90-X47 Full Copper CPU Fan - NF-A12x15 with this bracket that I've slightly modified PSU - Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT GPU - Powercolor Radeon 9060XT Reaper Assembly Instructions: Here are all the 3D printed parts that you will need: (apart from the gpu bracket locker which I realised I forgot to print, it's present in subsequent pics) Tools that you will need: M3 driver - hex key is fine too but you will need more elbow grease Electric screwdriver with M3 bit (H2) - technically not necessary, but it will make it much easier Prepping the parts Insert hex nuts in correct places and press them in. 2 on the front of the mobo tray 4 on the back of the mobo tray 2 in the back of the case (power button) 2 in the gpu bracket locker 2 in the back of the pcie riser You should prepare the beams (inserting Makerbeam T-Slot nuts on the sides) before you start putting the case together. It will be really annoying to do afterwards - so my suggestion is to triple check everything and try to imagine how it will go together (feel free to scroll down to use the pics to help your imagination). The holes for panels are lined up exactly with the T-Slot nuts - on end positions. Note: The parts (brackets) that you insert into the beams have the T-Slot shaped in a way where you will be essentially “shaving” off a sliver of plastic when inserting them. That's by design, I found it gives the best fit. So if they do not “go in” all the way, take it out, flip them out, clear out the plastic shavings and try again. Top beams Insert fan brackets and push them towards the center Insert end brackets, holes should be facing outwards Insert T-Slot nuts in places where you will be mounting the panels - so, 2 on the top, 2 on each sides Push the fans into the brackets Bottom beams Insert end bracket - I am using a custom one made for Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT PSU (included in the files), so if you will be using the generic one, it will look slightly different. Frame Screw the back of the case to the mobo tray using 16mm screws Note: You will be screwing into the plastic and essentially threading it, so electric screwdriver with M3 bit is recommended. Don't screw them in fully with the electric screwdriver though or you'll risk stripping the threads. Use a normal M3 driver for that. Stop when you encounter too much resistance. Motherboard I would suggest prepping the motherboard first (cpu, cooler, ram, storage). I've also inserted the pcie riser and power cables cause I found it annoying to do it after the case is put together. Note: The case itself is held together by 4 screws at this point, so I would suggest laying it on the corner of a desk/table so that you do not put unnecessary stress on the plastic parts at this point. Insert the IO shield for the motherboard Put the motherboard on the motherboard posts Put 4 x 16mm screws through the spacers that you have printed Screw the motherboard into the tray PCI-E Riser Bracket Install the PCIE riser bracket with 12mm screws to the back of the mobo tray PSU You can put your PSU in and secure it to the back of the case with #6-32 x 3/8" screws This will allow to put the case vertically and the weight of the mobo tray will rest on the PSU for now Make sure your pcie riser was inserted and routed by this point and it goes above the PSU Bottom Beams You can now slide the bottom beams with brace installed and screw them in from the back of the case with 16mm screws If you are using Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT PSU then you can screw it to the custom brace using #6-32 x 3/8" screws Power button Unscrew the nut from your 16mm power button, put it through the power button plate, screw the nut in Put the cable through the back of the case and screw the plate into the back of the case with 6mm screws GPU Connect the GPU to the riser Put the GPU into the case Line up the holes from the pcie riser to the ones on the pcie riser bracket Screw the pcie riser into the pcie riser bracket using 8mm screws - leave it a bit loose for now, as in don't screw it in fully - this will make it easier to line up everything properly Insert the gpu bracket that "plugs" the hole on the back of the case - you might need to push the gpu upwards a little bit Screw in 12mm screws from the top to secure the gpu - you might need to push the gpu towards the mobo tray to wiggle them in - hold your finger underneath the nuts, they might pop out Front Line it up to the mobo tray Install the front of the frame to the mobo tray using 16mm screws It might help if you temporarily screw in the front to the bottom beams to line it up better. Put the top beams on and route fan cables accordingly Secure all the braces with 12mm (not 16mm!!) screws from the outside. Done, you've built the frame :) Panels Now the only thing remaining is to put on the panels. Mount side, top and bottom panels with 6mm screws Mount the front panel with 16mm screws

description: Update: The model was updated with wider holes, and a center hole for more diverse mounting. A lightweight, no-nonsense bracket set for mounting a 200mm fan into a 10" server rack. Why I made this Most existing fan mounts for 10" racks didn't accommodate 200mm fans at all - and the few that did ate up a lot of filament and print time. Since a 200mm fan is plenty rigid on its own, there's no need for a bulky full-frame mount. This design uses two identical brackets that bolt directly onto the fan, which then mounts straight into the rack. Less plastic, less time, same job done. Design notes Two identical brackets - print two of the same part, no mirrored versions to keep track of. Designed around the Noctua NF-A20, but it should fit any standard 200mm fan. The fan itself provides the structural rigidity, so the brackets stay minimal. Printing The print profile includes the two brackets needed. No supports required. I recommend printing using PETG, since server racks can run warm and PETG holds up better to heat. If heat isn't a concern in your setup, PLA works perfectly fine. Warning This is a beta project . That means things will break, some geometry is still being refined, and the documentation, while thorough, is still a work in progress. Don’t expect a plug-and-play kit that works perfectly out of the box. Do not build this project unless you: Enjoy Hobby RC Enjoy 3D Printing Have built RC kits before Have a drawer (or two) of spare RC parts lying around Are comfortable with reprinting parts, tweaking parts, and troubleshooting What is Oscar SCT? Oscar is my attempt at creating a hobby-grade style 1:10 Scale, 2WD Short Course Truck. It is compatible with most off-the-shelf Short Course Truck bodies and wheels. It is designed to use standard RC electronics for the motor, battery, and steering servo. Build your own keypad Annoyed with doing the same things with your mouse over and over and wasting time or there are too many keybindings to remember? This might be right for you: A simple and small keypad with 25 keys boosts your efficiency by executing different actions just by clicking a key. It is cheap to build and you can even customize it the way you want. I use it for designing my 3D models I love it. What you need: 1x KB2040 Microcontroller 1x 40percent club “25” PCB (www.40percent.club/2017/09/25.html - Download .zip file and order the board from some PCB manufacturer ) 25x MX style switches 25x 1N4148 Diodes some pin headers and female pin headers USB type C cable the printed parts How to build it Cut two (male) pin headers to a length of 12 pins and solder them to the board (use a breadboard to hold them in place) Warning: Align both headers so all the pins but D+ and D- have a header pin soldered to them, as shown below: (My soldering joints are awful) Go to https://config.qmk.fm/#/40percentclub/25/LAYOUT_ortho_5x5 (make sure “LAYOUT_ortho5x5” is selected), name your keymap and configure your keymap horizontally mirrored (actions you want to be placed on the right side of your board should be placed on the left on the website). Download it as a JSON File. There is also an example keymap for a Fusion 360 macropad at the bottom of this page. Install QMK MSYS, run it with administrator privileges and enter the command qmk setup (you will want to answer with y in most cases) ! Make sure no USB devices are connected to your computer before continuing ! Now connect the KB2040 Microcontroller to your computer with the USB type C cable. Copy the path to your file and then run: qmk flash -c /Path/to/your/keymap.json -e CONVERT_TO=kb2040 (Make sure to paste your path instead of the example) When “Waiting for drive to deploy” is shown, press the RST button on your controller while holding BOOT. If the command finished, disconnect your controller. Place your circuit board on the table so the holes where the microcontroller is placed are on the left side of the board and place the diodes in the corresponding holes. Make sure the side with the black stripe of the diode points to the right side of your PCB, otherwise your keypad will not work. Here is an image of how it should look: Solder the diodes to the board from the other side. Cut two female pin headers to the size of 12 pins, place them in the holes for the microcontroller and solder them to the board from the other side again. It should look like on the image below: Turn the board around, place your switches and solder them to the PCB from the other side again: You have finished soldering! Push the microcontroller into the female headers, … slide the PCB into the case, … slide the bottom cover on and press it in: Now, you can finally install your keycaps (in the 3mf, there are also example keycaps for a CAD Keypad that match the example configuration)! Your keypad is ready - You just need to connect it to your PC and it should work like a charm! If something doesn't fit well, just scale the problematic part in BambuStudio. I hope you liked this project. If you want to support my work, feel free to leave a comment, a like or a boost. If you have suggestions, problems or feedback, don't hesitate to reach out! model_name: Double hose for Siguro air conditioner home
description: Because single-hose portable air conditioners create negative pressure when exhausting hot air, warm outside air is drawn into the room through gaps and openings. I designed an adapter that allows a second hose to be connected to draw intake air directly from outside. This eliminates the negative pressure and significantly improves the air conditioner's efficiency. The cooled air is then recirculated within the room, instead of continuously pulling in warm outdoor air. The adapter features a threadless opening for a 140 mm (14 cm) hose and is compatible with the Siguro SGR-AC-C140W . Added several more models. Elbow adapters for the inlet and outlet hoses (to attach at the end for directing the airflow). Added a simple front panel that allows an outlet hose to be connected to the cold-air outlet (for directing cool air into another room), as well as a new similar panel that allows the airflow direction to be changed either directly from the air conditioner or into the cold-air outlet hose, plus sliding shutters to close the openings. description: Airbus A320 ENG Panel als USB-Controller Dieses Modell stellt das ENG Panel des Airbus A320 dar. Im Original befindet es sich hinter den Schubhebeln auf dem Mittelkonsolenbereich und dient zur Steuerung sowie Überwachung der Triebwerke. Das Panel kann als USB-Controller für Flugsimulatoren wie den Microsoft Flight Simulator verwendet werden und sorgt durch die beleuchteten Anzeigen und Schalter für ein deutlich immersiveres Flugerlebnis. Funktionen Das Panel verfügt über: 2 Triebwerksschalter (ENG 1 / ENG 2) 1 Drehschalter für die Betriebsmodi 2 Druckknöpfe 4 beleuchtbare Anzeigen (FIRE / FAULT für jedes Triebwerk) Die FIRE- und FAULT-Anzeigen können unabhängig voneinander angesteuert werden und eignen sich hervorragend zur Darstellung von Warnungen, Fehlern oder Statusinformationen. Benötigte Komponenten Für den Nachbau werden benötigt: 1× Arduino Pro Micro LINK 2× Schalter mit ca. 7 mm Gewindedurchmesser LINK 1× Drehschalter LINK 2× Taster LINK Standoffs / Abstandshalter LEDs für die Beleuchtung Kabel und Lötzubehör Anpassung der Dateien Auf zwei Teilen der Main.3mf befinden sich negative Objekte, welches auch je nach situation skalliert werden muss . Es ist auch eine .f3d datei enthalten, wo du es fallst gemocht noch genauer machen kannst. Diese dienen als Platzhalter für: den Ausgang des Arduino Pro Micro zusätzliche Schalter zum manuellen Schalten der LEDs Die entsprechenden Aussparungen wurden bewusst nicht fest in das Modell integriert, da deren Position je nach verwendeten Abstandshaltern, Schaltern und individueller Verkabelung variieren kann. Vor dem Druck sollten die negativen Objekte daher an die eigenen Komponenten angepasst werden. Verkabelung Für den Betrieb ist eine selbst gelötete Platine erforderlich. Als Orientierung kann die beigefügte Fritzing-Skizze verwendet werden. Die von mir verwendete Platine besitzt die auf dem zweiten Bild angegebenen Abmessungen und wurde lediglich an den beiden markierten Befestigungspunkten verschraubt. Je nach verwendeten Komponenten kann die Verkabelung selbstverständlich angepasst oder erweitert werden. Rot=5V Schwarz=GND Blau=Signalkabel Grün=Nur zur Ansicht Weitere Druckprofile Die beiden zusätzlichen Druckprofile enthalten: Knopfkappen Schalteraufsätze für ENG 1 und ENG 2 Drehschalteraufsatz Diese Teile werden nach dem Druck auf die jeweiligen Schalter aufgesteckt und vervollständigen das Erscheinungsbild des Panels. Entwicklung Dieses Modell wurde für einen Freund von mir entworfen, der sein Flugsimulator-Setup um ein eigenes A320 ENG Panel erweitern wollte. Auch wenn dies nicht mein erstes Elektronikprojekt ist – ich arbeite beispielsweise bereits an einem eigenen F/A-18 Homecockpit – hat dieses Projekt in den letzten Wochen einen großen Teil meiner Zeit in Anspruch genommen. Zwischen CAD-Konstruktion, Testdrucken, Verkabelung und der Anpassung an die verwendete Hardware sind viele Stunden Entwicklungsarbeit in dieses Panel geflossen. Falls ihr euch also gefragt habt, warum in letzter Zeit etwas weniger neue Modelle erschienen sind: Dieses Projekt ist der Hauptgrund dafür 😄 Jetzt, da das ENG Panel fertig ist, wird es aber wieder mehr Modelle, Bewaffnungen und andere Projekte geben. description: Da ich für mein Dachfenster keine passende Lösung gefunden habe, habe ich diesen Adapter selbst konstruiert. Der Adapter ermöglicht es, den Abluftschlauch einer mobilen Klimaanlage durch ein Dachfenster zu führen, während das Fenster nahezu vollständig geschlossen bleiben kann. Dadurch wird der Luftaustausch mit der warmen Außenluft reduziert und die Kühlleistung verbessert. Eigenschaften Passend für 125 mm, 130 mm und 150 mm Abluftschläuche Integrierte Aussparung für den Fenstergriff Große Auslassfläche für einen möglichst geringen Strömungswiderstand Mehrteilige Bauweise für eine einfache Herstellung auf handelsüblichen 3D-Druckern Für verschiedene Schlauchdurchmesser stehen passende Anschlussstücke zur Verfügung Version 2 Ich habe bereits eine V2 des Modells erstellt. Hier wurden zusätzlich 6 Verstärkungsrippen ergänzt, die nach dem Druck eingeklebt werden. Hintergrund ist, dass der Adapter während eines längeren Betriebs der Klimaanlage durch die warme Abluft leicht erwärmt wird. Je nach Material kann sich der Auslassbereich mit der Zeit minimal verformen. Die Verstärkungsrippen erhöhen die Stabilität deutlich und halten den Auslass dauerhaft in Form. Zusammenbau Der Adapter besteht aus: 2 Auslassteilen 1 Schlauchadapter 6 Verstärkungsrippen (V2) Alle Teile habe ich mit einem hochwertigen Sekundenkleber verklebt. Durch die mehrteilige Bauweise lassen sich sämtliche Komponenten auch auf Druckern mit normaler Baugröße problemlos herstellen. Druckempfehlung Bei mir wurde das Modell erfolgreich mit Bambu PETG HF und dem Standard-Bambu-Profil gedruckt. Ein Druck mit normalem PETG hat ebenfalls gut funktioniert. Da es sich jedoch um einen langen Druck handelt und PETG zu leichter Tropfenbildung neigt, verwende ich zusätzlich einen selbst eingebauten Nozzle-Cleaning-G-Code , der die Düse regelmäßig reinigt. Dadurch konnte ich die Druckqualität nochmals verbessern. Natürlich kann der Adapter auch aus anderen temperaturbeständigen Materialien gedruckt werden. Hinweise Da Dachfenster und mobile Klimaanlagen sehr unterschiedlich sind, kann ich keine universelle Passgenauigkeit garantieren. Bitte prüft vor dem Druck die angegebenen Maße und wählt den passenden Schlauchdurchmesser (125 mm, 130 mm oder 150 mm). Dieses Modell wurde ursprünglich für meinen eigenen Anwendungsfall entwickelt und anschließend so aufbereitet, dass möglichst viele Nutzer davon profitieren können. Feedback Ich freue mich über jedes Feedback! Solltet ihr Verbesserungsvorschläge, Ideen oder Anpassungswünsche haben, schreibt diese gerne in die Kommentare. Ich bin jederzeit offen für konstruktive Kritik und werde sinnvolle Verbesserungen gerne in zukünftige Versionen einfließen lassen. Viel Spaß beim Drucken – und ich hoffe, der Adapter hilft euch dabei, auch an heißen Sommertagen einen kühlen Kopf zu bewahren! 😊

SmartLid - Smart Sourdough Starter Lid for WECK-jars is a wireless, battery-powered smart sensor lid for monitoring sourdough starter rise, temperature, humidity, and battery status. It is a complete DIY solution designed to monitor the most important parameters of your starter, helping you identify the perfect time for feeding, baking, or refrigeration. Take the guesswork out of your baking and leverage peak yeast activity for consistently better bread! The device operates fully wireless, powered by a rechargeable LiPo battery, and transmits measurements via Wi-Fi using MQTT to your smart home setup. Features Growth Tracking : Measure and understand the rise of your starter (in mm and %). Climate Monitoring : Track temperature and humidity inside the jar environment. Battery Powered : Fully wireless operation with battery voltage logging and status monitoring. Smart Home Integration : Data transmission via Wi-Fi (MQTT) for easy tracking over time. Low-Power Design : Utilizes ESP32 deep sleep to maximize battery life. Required Components Printed Parts Main Sensor Body (Lid) Upper Electronics Cover Upper & Lower Mounting Rings Electronics Microcontroller: DFRobot Beetle ESP32-C6 Mini (DFR1117) Climate Sensor: Compact 4-pin BME280 Distance Sensor: VL53L1X ToF (Time-of-Flight) sensor Battery: 3.7 V LiPo battery (Type 503040) Power/Charging: USB-C female breakout board + USB-C plug Switch: SS-12F15 slide switch (handle length: min. 3 mm) (as there are several variants of some parts, ensure that you chose the correct parts. Please see github for detailed information) Fasteners 5 x M2.5 x 6 mm screws 6 × M2.5 × 16 mm screws Compatible Glass Jars The design is specifically tailored for WECK Rundrand 100 (RR100) jars, including: WECK tapered jar 500/580 ml (WECK 742) WECK tapered jar 750/850 ml (WECK 743) WECK tulip jar 950/1062 ml (WECK 745) WECK tapered jar 900/1000 ml (WECK 908) Using a different jar? Let me know in the comments! (including inner and outer diameter at the top of the jar) If there is enough demand, I will design and upload matching adapter rings. Note: Other WECK jars using the RR100 lid size should fit as well. A sufficiently tall jar is highly recommended so the starter never touches the lid or electronics, even at peak rise! Software & Integration The complete firmware and setup documentation are available on GitHub: sourdough-smartlid The firmware is optimized for the DFRobot Beetle ESP32-C6 and publishes all sensor data natively via MQTT. Data Collection & Visualization To use this project, an MQTT broker is required. Popular solutions include: Brokers: Home Assistant + Mosquitto, ioBroker, Node-RED, OpenHAB, or standalone Mosquitto on a Raspberry Pi/NAS. Dashboards: Home Assistant Dashboards, ioBroker VIS, InfluxDB + Grafana, or custom MQTT dashboards. example of measurement graph (with grafana): How It Works & Configuration The SmartLid replaces the standard glass lid of your WECK jar. The VL53L1X Time-of-Flight sensor measures the exact distance to the starter's surface to calculate the growth percentage. Simultaneously, the BME280 tracks the microclimate. To save power, the ESP32 remains in deep sleep, wakes up at your defined interval, reads the sensors, transmits the data via Wi-Fi, and instantly goes back to sleep. Fully Configurable: Via the firmware, you can easily adjust the measuring intervals, jar height, sensor calibration offsets, and Wi-Fi/MQTT credentials. Battery-Powered Operation The device is designed to operate wirelessly from a rechargeable LiPo battery. During normal use, the ESP32 wakes up only for a short time, reads all sensors, publishes the data via MQTT, and then returns to deep sleep. This greatly reduces power consumption compared to continuous operation. Estimated runtime with 10-minute measurement intervals: at least one week. Printing & Assembly Notes Print Profile: It is highly recommended to use the provided print profile. Material Recommendation: PLA or PETG is recommended. model_name: Support pour bouteille d'eau pour ventilateur
description: Ce modèle 3D permet de fabriquer un support de bouteilles pour ventilateur , conçu pour créer un rafraîchisseur d'air artisanal (ou climatiseur d'appoint) très simple et économique. Comment ça marche ? Le principe : Vous remplissez deux bouteilles de soda (de 500 ml) avec de l'air ou de l'eau additionnée de sel (pour que la glace tienne plus longtemps), puis vous les mettez au congélateur. L'installation : Une fois imprimés, les supports s'emboîtent et s'accrochent directement sur la grille de votre ventilateur. Il suffit d'y glisser les bouteilles congelées : l'air propulsé par les pales se refroidit instantanément au contact de la glace. Détails et astuces de conception Impression facile : Le design est pensé pour s'imprimer sans aucun support. Les pièces se clipsent simplement entre elles. Fixation modulable : Le créateur a intégré des fentes sur le modèle. Si l'accroche d'origine ne suffit pas ou si vous voulez bloquer le système, vous pouvez utiliser des serre-câbles ( zip ties ) pour le fixer solidement à la grille. Astuce pratique : N'oubliez pas de placer une petite serviette ou un récipient sous le ventilateur pour récupérer l'eau de condensation qui va perler le long des bouteilles.

Diese modulare Halterung ist die professionelle Lösung für das saubere Trocknen Ihrer bemalten oder mit Airbrush besprühten Modellteile. Das System basiert auf quadratischen und rechteckigen Platten, die mit speziellen, im Lieferumfang enthaltenen Verbindern (Connectors) beliebig erweitert werden können. Ob Sie eine lange Linie, eine T-Form oder sogar um die Ecke bauen möchten – diese Station passt sich Ihrem Arbeitsplatz und Ihren Projekten an. Ein weiterer großer Pluspunkt: Wenn die Halterung gerade nicht benötigt wird, lässt sie sich mit wenigen Handgriffen komplett auseinanderbauen. Die flachen Platten und kleinen Verbinder nehmen im Gegensatz zu klobigen Styroporblöcken so gut wie keinen Platz im Regal oder der Schublade weg. Ein wesentlicher Vorteil ist zudem die Doppelfunktion der Verbinder: 1. Platten verbinden: Um die Station beliebig zu erweitern. 2. Stabilisieren: Wenn keine weitere Platte angeschlossen wird, können die Verbinder als seitliche "Stützbeine" eingesteckt werden. Dies verhindert effektiv, dass die Platte kippt, falls Sie sehr schwere oder große Teile an der gegenüberliegenden Seite zum Trocknen platzieren. Haupteigenschaften: Maximale Modularität: Kombinieren Sie Platten und erweitern Sie diese in absolut jede Richtung. Kompakt & Platzsparend: Nach dem Projekt einfach zerlegen und mühelos verstauen. 4mm System: Kompatibel mit weit verbreiteten 4mm-Stäben (z.B. mit Alligator-Clip-Aufsätzen) oder einfachen Holzspießen. Dichte Lochmatrix: Für maximale Kapazität auf kleinem Raum. Clevere Stabilität: Integrierte Stabilisierungsfunktion durch Connectoren verhindert das Umkippen bei ungleicher Gewichtsverteilung. Druckanweisungen: Material: PLA oder PETG (PETG empfiehlt sich für etwas mehr Flexibilität bei den Verbindern). Infill: min. 8% (Ein höheres Infill sorgt für mehr Eigengewicht und somit für einen noch sichereren Stand). Düsendurchmesser: 0,4mm (Standard). Schichthöhe: 0,2mm. Support: JA, erforderlich.

Firstly - Apologies for the Blue Filament, its all I had for printing the test parts :D So I've done a version one, but it told me nothing about the aircraft near me! So a friend suggested the Cheap Yellow Display or CYD. So I Amazon'd one and got to work. Similarly to V1 it uses the OpenSky Network API based on a free account. It means that it rechecks for aircraft every 20seconds or so but this gives you time to look at them before they move on. Especially in a busy area. Parts List 3D Printed Case - Right Here Cheap Yellow Display (CYD) - Amazon UK - These can be got cheaper on AliExpress I just needed one quickly for the build. Connecting & Building: Print the case whilst waiting for the parts to arrive. Place the CYD into the mount to the part called "Cradle" Slide 'Cradle' in the 'Main Body' Place 'Bezel' into 'Outer Shell' This is a tight fit and should properly click. The flat uprights of the 'Main Body' should be used to guide the 'Outer Shell' its been design this way to keep as little a gap as possible from the screenwithout causing accidental damage Webflasher Caution By Flashing your ESP32 it will wipe any other app you currently have running - I would advice unplugging any other ESP's you may have plugged in just incase you select the wrong COM Port. Connect the ESP32 to your PC with a USB-C cable and head to LINK this will open up a webflasher - Flash your ESP32 and wait for it to complete. Initial Setup Once the ESP32 boots up for the first time, it will create a Wifi Access Point called RandumbRadar, connect to this on your phone/laptop. Head to 192.168.77.1 on your browser and enter your home WIFI details. You'll get a confirmation page and the device will reboot. First Setup The Screen should now be displaying a local IP address, so back on your home WIFI you should be able to go to that address and start the first set up. The First thing you need to do is go to opensky and create an account, once done, on your account page you'll see an option to create an API key. Click this and it will download a file to your PC, there you'll find the ID and Secret. Now head to that IP address you seen on your Radar Screen and click settings. Paste your Client ID and Client Secret into the corresponding boxes (without the speech marks or any other formatting) and click Save. The system will take a few minutes and then start the next scan. The long/lat defaults are Heathrow Airport at a 200km range so expect to see alot of dots first time round! Customisation Now is the fun stuff. Head back to the Dashboard, Click Customisations and go crazy! Update your Lon/Lat and range to suit and I've included a couple of customisations options within the app. I hope to add more in the future. description: Howdy all! As you can tell by now, I like baseball. I also like baseball standings. So here is a little alteration on my baseball standings boards. This standings board is perfect for those who want to put it on their desk at work (or at home) and show off to your coworkers (or your cat if you work from home). The board itself contains 30 magnets, one for each team slot. Then 1 magnet for each of the 30 team's “coin”. So that makes 60! Congrats you passed 1st grade! No glue required anywhere in this set so you don't need worry about glue residue coming into contact with your fridge and leaving a glue stains that cant come off (don't ask me how I know about this, lets just say, “experience”). My only warning is that since the team coins are slightly larger than a quarter, I would recommend you keep this set away from young children, because children find small things delicious and can put them in their mouth. Magnets + Children = Not fun times at the hospital. This set will work with pretty much any printer bed that is the size of an A1 Mini and larger. Design Philosophy This airless TPU soccer ball is generated from a custom four-panel spherical shell system rather than a standard stitched football pattern. The base form starts from a tetrahedral layout: one master panel is created, then rotated into four matching positions around the sphere so the panels meet cleanly with shared curved boundaries. The panel shape is built from smooth two-lobe circular arc curves projected onto the sphere, giving the ball a more organic sports-ball appearance while still keeping the geometry repeatable and balanced. The honeycomb reduces material, improves flexibility, and gives the ball a spring-like response when compressed. Each panel also includes three curved inset strap patterns. Material and Printing Notes For the most functional version, I recommend TPU 95A HF . It gives a good balance of flexibility, durability, and printability. It is soft enough to deform slightly and bounce, while still firm enough to preserve the honeycomb ribs and raised panel details. For supports, I had the best results using PLA as support interface/support material with TPU 95A HF. TPU support can work, but PLA is usually easier to remove and helps keep the honeycomb openings cleaner. I also tested a four-color version using TPU for AMS. The multicolor version looks very cool and shows that the inset strap system works well for color changes. However, TPU for AMS is much harder than regular 95A TPU, so the finished ball feels too stiff for real kicking and can break apart easily. I recommend that version mainly as a display model, color sample, or decorative football. If you want to try print with TPU for AMS, you have to dry them before printing. My TPU for AMS is not dried fully and I have to use a hairdries to give it a cleaner look after printing. Notes: Please read the print file instruction carefully to setup the support z distance correctly for PLA Support (0 mm) and TPU Support (~0.2mm) . Otherwise, it can be very diffcult to remove the support.

description: This is a kumihimo wheel, a thing to help weave friendship braclets, regular braclets or keychains. Works best printed in TPU, but works in PLA too. How to weave? First, grab 4 strings about the same lenght and tie a knot in the middle as shown, then you will have 8 strings in total. Pull the knot through the middle of the wheel, through the biggest hole. Then, put the strings on the wheel in a cross pattern, as shown in the picture below. Now, the weaving begins. put the top left string to the bottom left. description: Soporte de Tubos de dosificacion con Rosca para Cristal de 6mm – 6 Vías para Tubos de Dosificación Mantener el orden en el sump o en el borde del acuario es clave para evitar accidentes, aditamentos cruzados o tubos sueltos que terminen vaciando líquido fuera del sistema. Este Soporte de 6 Vías para Bomba Dosificadora ha sido diseñado específicamente para urnas o sumps con cristal de 6 mm de grosor , permitiendo organizar de forma impecable hasta 6 líneas de adición (Kh, Ca, Mg, elementos traza, etc.) en un espacio mínimo y con una estética totalmente profesional. Como se puede ver en la imagen , el diseño cuenta con una ranura a medida para encajar en el borde del vidrio y se asegura firmemente mediante un sistema de rosca posterior que aprieta contra el cristal para que no se mueva ni un milímetro. Además, incluye 6 tornillos de presión texturizados en la parte frontal para asegurar cada tubo individualmente sin chafarlo, garantizando que ninguno se desplace. 🛠️ Piezas Requeridas Para montar este soporte completo, necesitarás imprimir los siguientes componentes incluidos en el proyecto: Componentes Impresos en 3D: Cuerpo Principal de 6 Vías: Soporte con la ranura de acople para cristal de 6 mm y los 6 orificios pasantes para los tubos. Tornillo de Sujeción al Cristal (x2): Tornillo de rosca ancha trasera para fijar el soporte de forma segura al borde del acuario. Tornillos de Ajuste de Tubos (x6): Tornillos con cabeza moleteada/texturizada para retener los tubos cómodamente a mano. 💡 Parámetros de Impresión Recomendados: Material: PETG . Al igual que con el resto de accesorios marinos, evita por completo el PLA, ya que la humedad constante y la salinidad terminarán por debilitarlo estructuralmente. 📐 Instrucciones de Montaje y Uso Limpieza de roscas: Tras retirar las piezas de la base de impresión, realiza un pre-atornillado manual de todos los tornillos (tanto el trasero de sujeción como los 6 frontales) en el cuerpo principal. Esto ayudará a suavizar las roscas impresas en 3D antes de la instalación. Colocación en el acuario: Encaja el soporte en el borde del cristal de 6 mm de tu sump o urna. Gira el tornillo de sujeción trasero hasta que haga contacto con el vidrio y quede firmemente fijado (aprieta a mano, no te pases de fuerza para no dañar la rosca plástica). Paso de tubos: Introduce los tubos de tu bomba dosificadora a través de los orificios superiores. Deja la longitud necesaria para que el líquido caiga limpiamente al agua sin que el tubo llegue a tocar la superficie (evitando el efecto sifón o la acumulación de costras de sal). Fijación de líneas: Aprieta suavemente los tornillos moleteados frontales a mano hasta que notes que cada tubo queda bien retenido. ☕ Apoya mis Diseños DIY de Acuarismo El diseño de accesorios funcionales para acuarios marinos requiere tiempo de modelado, pruebas de tolerancia en las roscas y gasto de material en prototipos para asegurar que encajen perfectamente en vuestros sistemas. Overview The Modular Dive Marker is a fully 3D printable diving marker designed for pools, swimming practice and underwater games. The system consists of a weighted anchor and a floating buoy connected by a rope. Once placed in the water, the anchor sinks to the bottom while the buoy remains visible at the surface, creating a fixed underwater reference point. The anchor can also be used without the buoy as a simple diving target. The design is intentionally modular and easy to customize. An editable STEP file is included, allowing you to modify the model in your preferred CAD software. Features Fully 3D printable Editable STEP file included Modular design User-fillable anchor User-fillable buoy Adjustable rope length (simply tie a new knot) No special hardware required Easy to customize Designed for remixing Anchor The anchor consists of two printed parts. The rope is inserted through the top opening and secured inside the housing with a simple knot that can be accessed through the side opening. The bottom cap unscrews and can be filled with almost any ballast material, for example: Gravel Small stones Stainless steel nuts Screws Fishing weights Aquarium gravel Adjust the ballast amount to match your pool depth and desired stability. The anchor can also be used without the buoy as a standalone diving target for swimming practice and underwater games. Floating Buoy The buoy consists of three printed parts. Its geometry provides enough buoyancy to float on the water surface without requiring any additional foam or flotation material . Simply print the three parts, assemble them and attach the rope. The design is lightweight, durable and easy to customize. Printing Notes ⚠️ Please do not modify the recommended print settings. The anchor body has been intentionally designed without top and bottom solid layers . This allows water to quickly enter the exposed infill structure, preventing trapped air and significantly improving the sinking performance. The visible infill on the top and bottom surfaces is part of the design and not a printing defect . Changing these settings may reduce the anchor's performance and prevent it from sinking as intended. Designed for Customization This project was intentionally designed to be modified. Feel free to create your own versions. Future Buoy Ideas The included buoy is only one possible design. Possible alternatives: Classic buoy Star Heart Diamond Fish Shark fin Turtle Octopus Pirate barrel Treasure chest Lifebuoy Flag Balloon Pumpkin Christmas ornament Ghost Skull Crown Rocket UFO Game Ideas One marker already offers plenty of possibilities: Dive around the marker Retrieve the anchor Underwater navigation Swimming practice Diving challenges Time trials Using multiple markers opens up even more ideas: Obstacle courses Treasure hunts Team relay races Underwater slalom Orientation training Marker collection games Custom diving games Printing Recommended Material PLA PETG (recommended for outdoor use) Supports No supports required. Layer Height 0.20 mm Infill 15–20% Assembly Print all parts. Insert the rope through the anchor. Tie the rope inside the anchor. Fill the anchor with ballast. Screw on the bottom cap. Feed the rope through the bottom part of the buoy . Secure the rope with a knot inside the buoy. Assemble the buoy. Adjust the rope length by tying a new knot inside the anchor if necessary. Included Files Editable STEP file Safety This model is a diving game accessory . It is not a lifesaving or flotation device. Always supervise children around water. Use only in safe swimming environments. Remix This project was designed with customization in mind. Feel free to modify, improve and remix the design. description: If you have an above ground pool that is too big for dumping it daily and too small for justifying an expensive vacuum machine setup, then this is the ideal tool for you. My vacuum nozzle is designed with a chamber to add weighted material such as sand, gravel, clay, steel shot or any heavier-than-water media so the nozzle and hose does not float to the top of the water and risk air ingestion into your filter pump. Doing so can result in pump cavitation, damage or underperformance. To complete the setup, you will need to buy the adapter (link below: 1.25” Pool Vacuum Hose Adapter for Intex Above Ground Swimming Pool Surface Skimmer Connector, 32 mm Pool Hose Adapter) here which can be connected to one of your filter inlets when in use. Since it comes in a set of 2, use one of the O-rings from the spare adapter and install it to the vacuum nozzle. You will also need a 1.25" diameter hose for the length you need to reach everywhere in your pool. You can pick up from the local pool store or online; my local pool store sells them by the yard for a good price, better than most online shopping, so check with yours. Fill the chamber with whatever you like, screw the plug in and use some sort of sealant like plumbers pipe dope or super glue. How to use: Remove filter inlet cover on pool liner, attach intex adapter to pool liner inlet, completely fill pool vacuum hose with water to remove all air (keep submerged), attach this printed and weighted nozzle to the hose, attach hose to inlet, start vacuuming! description: Tired of treble hooks snagging your guides, line, clothes, car/truck seat, or fingers? The Hook Guardian Pro keeps your hooks exactly where they belong! This easy-to-mount fishing rod accessory provides a secure parking spot for treble hooks, single hooks, and many lure styles while you're moving between spots, transporting rods, or storing your gear. Designed to help reduce tangles and protect your rod, this compact holder gives anglers a clean, organized way to secure their tackle in seconds. description: Wireless Docking Home Assistant Wall Controller (Guition 3.5") Overview This project is a fully portable ESPHome-powered Home Assistant wall controller built around the Guition 3.5" ESP32-S3 capacitive touchscreen . Unlike traditional wall-mounted control panels, this one can simply be lifted from its magnetic wall dock and continues operating from its internal rechargeable battery. When placed back onto the dock, it automatically recharges through wireless Qi charging , eliminating exposed charging contacts and providing a clean, seamless appearance. The goal of this project was to create a smart home controller that looks like a permanently installed wall panel while remaining completely portable whenever needed. The project includes the complete enclosure, magnetic wall dock and all required mounting parts. The user interface shown in the photos is built with ESPHome + LVGL and can be fully customized to suit your own Home Assistant installation. Features 3.5" capacitive touchscreen ESP32-S3 running ESPHome Home Assistant integration Portable operation with built-in rechargeable battery Magnetic wall docking station Support both portrait and landscape installation Automatic wireless Qi charging Single screw enclosure assembly Fully customizable LVGL interface Integrated Sensors The controller includes several sensors to make it behave intelligently without requiring user interaction. LD2410 Human Presence Sensor The LD2410 detects when someone is standing in front of the controller and automatically wakes the display. VEML7700 Ambient Light Sensor The display brightness automatically adjusts according to the surrounding light conditions. MPU6050 Accelerometer & Gyroscope If the controller is picked up from the wall or simply moved, the display automatically wakes even when no presence is detected. The MPU6050 is also used to detect the controller's orientation. This makes it possible to automatically rotate the user interface or display different pages depending on whether the controller is held in portrait or landscape orientation. The internal temperature sensor of the MPU6050 is also used to monitor the controller's internal temperature. Additional Monitoring The controller also measures: Battery voltage Battery level WiFi signal strength Internal device temperature Audio A miniature speaker is connected directly to the ESP32. It provides audible feedback for every button press and is also exposed to Home Assistant as a Media Player . This allows the controller to play: TTS announcements Notification sounds Doorbell sounds Any other audio supported by ESPHome Smart Power Management To maximize battery life and reduce display wear, several automatic power-saving functions are implemented. The controller automatically adjusts the display brightness according to the ambient light measured by the VEML7700. The display wakes automatically when: someone approaches the controller (LD2410) the controller is picked up or moved (MPU6050) When the controller becomes idle, the backlight turns off while an anti burn-in routine periodically moves the screen contents to protect the display. Wireless Docking System The wall dock contains: Qi wireless charging transmitter 4pcs 6×4 mm neodymium magnets The controller contains: Qi wireless charging receiver 4pcs 6×4 mm neodymium magnets Internal rechargeable Li-Ion battery The magnets automatically align the Qi charging coils, ensuring reliable charging every time the controller is placed on the dock. There are no exposed charging contacts to wear out or become dirty. Mechanical Design The enclosure was designed to be simple to assemble while keeping the exterior clean and minimizing the number of fasteners. Features include: - only one M3 screw holds the entire enclosure together - captive M3 hex nut - slide-in Qi receiver (no glue required) - press-fit Qi transmitter in the wall dock (no glue required) - integrated battery compartment - hidden wiring - removable front assembly The Li-Ion battery is permanently embedded inside the rear cover during printing using a Pause at Height command. After inserting the battery, printing resumes and the remaining layers create three retaining tabs that securely hold it in place without requiring a separate battery holder. Both the wall dock and the controller use four 6×4 mm neodymium magnets . The magnets should be glued into their dedicated pockets using CA glue or epoxy. Besides securely holding the controller in place, they also ensure accurate alignment of the Qi charging coils for reliable wireless charging every time the controller is docked. The Qi transmitter module PCB is designed as a press-fit component. It fits tightly into the wall dock and does not require any glue or additional fasteners. The enclosure wall in front of the VEML7700 ambient light sensor is intentionally made thinner than the rest of the enclosure. This allows more ambient light to reach the sensor, improving the accuracy and responsiveness of the automatic brightness control while keeping the sensor completely hidden from view. The wall dock is designed to support both portrait and landscape installation. The mounting slots allow for fine adjustment during installation, making it easy to perfectly level the dock before tightening the mounting screws. Electrical Design The Guition display uses 1.25 mm JST connectors , so a few additional cables are required to connect the external modules. Two 2-pin connectors are needed for the speaker and the Li-Ion battery. The speaker does not include a connector, while the battery comes with a different connector type, so its original connector must be replaced. The VEML7700 ambient light sensor and the MPU6050 IMU are connected via the I²C bus using a 4-pin connector . The LD2410 presence sensor communicates over UART and connects using an 8-pin connector . The LD2410 requires a 5V power supply , while the Guition board provides a regulated 3.3V output for external modules. To power the LD2410 both when the controller is docked and when it is running from its internal battery, a compact 5V boost converter is used to step the regulated 3.3V supply up to 5V. Printing Notes Due to the heat generated by the Qi receiver during charging, PLA is not recommended . Recommended materials: PETG ASA ABS The battery embedding process requires a Pause at Height command during printing. Software The controller runs entirely on ESPHome and integrates seamlessly with Home Assistant . The interface shown in the photos is only an example. Since everything is based on ESPHome and LVGL , you can freely modify the layout, pages, icons, widgets and functionality to fit your own smart home. description: Smart No-Mess Gravity Bird Feeder (with Hull Separation & Removable Tray) Tired of bird seed scattered all over your floor and a cage constantly full of empty hulls? This Smart No-Mess Gravity Bird Feeder is engineered to keep your bird happy, your cage tidy, and your cleaning routine effortless! Featuring an internal gravity-fed ramp, a built-in perch, a slotted hull-separator grid, and an external slide-out tray, it completely changes how you feed your birds. Key Features & How It Works Automatic Gravity Refill: The sleek internal curved ramp smoothly channels fresh seed down to the feeding trough as your bird eats, preventing clogging and ensuring a steady food supply. No-Mess Hull Separation: The feeding area features a precise integrated grate. When your bird cracks seeds, the empty hulls and debris fall through the slots instead of piling up on top of fresh food or being blown out into your room. Removable Waste Tray: A dedicated drawer slides out completely from the back/outside of the cage. Clean out empty husks in seconds without ever opening the cage door or disturbing your birds. Secure Cage Mounting: Designed with a robust screw-and-washer mount that fits tightly between standard cage bars, keeping the feeder perfectly stable. Removable Slide-In Top Lid: Keeps the main hopper sealed, dust-free, and safe from curious birds trying to sneak in from the top. Components Included Main Hopper Body: The translucent/main vertical tower featuring the curved gravity ramp and cage mounting points. Feeder Base & Perch: The sturdy lower section housing the feeding troughs and integrated bird perch. Slide-Out Waste Tray: The collection drawer that captures discarded hulls. Top Cover / Lid: Features convenient pull tabs for quick refills. Recommended Print Settings To ensure smooth sliding parts, clean grates, and structural durability, use these settings: Material: PETG or PLA Tough (PETG is highly recommended if you intend to wash the feeder in warm water frequently). Use a translucent or clear filament for the main body if you want to see the seed level at a glance! Assembly & Maintenance Note Mounting: Position the feeder against the cage bars, slide the printed or hardware bolt through, and tighten the washer disk from the outside until secure. Hygiene: Because this comes into contact with animal feed, ensure your retraction settings are tuned to avoid stringing where seeds might get caught. description: Why? I'm a huge fan of calisthenics. Over 5 years ago I decided I needed a regimen that could travel with me anywhere, with minimal equipment. Then I would never have an excuse to miss. Pull-ups while traveling can be a challenge. Sometimes there's a playground nearby, sometimes the hotel actually has a pull-up bar. And sometimes there's nothing (work takes me to remote areas). This design uses gravity and your door frame to hold you securely while you do pull-ups. It's meant to replace this travel system: https://a.co/d/0bsIKWrO . I've had issues getting the metal set through TSA (was fine but kept getting flagged), they're heavy, and the price ranges from $35 - $150. My set was around $70. Bambu estimates costs for my printed system to be $16.31 (small boy 70 mm frame) to $22.44 (big boy 90 mm frame). SIZES Frame: Designed for door frames where the wall + casing = 150 mm or around 6 inches thick. For casing of different heights I have two sizes: 70 mm and 90 mm (mine is 70 mm). The 70 mm version can fit everything on a single 256x256 plate, 90 mm will have to be done in pieces. If you're using this for hotel door frames, you never know what size they may have … choose wisely (or print both). Arm: “Small boy” arm is 32 mm deep and 40 mm wide. "Big boy” arm is 32 mm deep and 60 mm wide. Handle: 28 mm diameter (easier to grip but can be more painful). 32 mm diameter (harder to grip but can be less painful). Both are common options with gymnastics rings. SAFETY You are responsible for ensuring your printer, materials, slicer settings, door frame, paracord and use of the provided files and instructions are sufficient to ensure your safety. Testing I weigh 215 lbs. and am wearing a 40 lbs. weighted vest in the torture test you see. Note that I used an earlier and weaker prototype of the “small boy” version . The weakest link is the handle, be sure to properly thread your paracord. I'm confident that if you use the correct filament and settings, and don't put 300+ lbs. on one side, you should be okay. For those who are skeptical or are bigger, use the “big boy” version. Materials and Settings The profile has these by default: Filament: PETG or stronger filament Walls: 7, and 7 shell layers, top and bottom Home Gym I use other 3D printed stuff for some of my home gym equipment and haven't had a problem with safety: https://makerworld.com/collections/29592071 The last photo shows my setup for doing dips at the hotel, using 3D printed rings. ASSEMBLY & USE Arrange the arms so that the “hands” face each other, like a claw. Slide the pin through the large center hole. Thread 1100 lb paracord through one small arm hole, one handle hole, travel under the base of the handle, through the other handle hole, and the other arm hole, then tie with a knot (I used and recommend a square knot). You can thread it so that the handle is perpendicular to the door frame or at a 45 degree angle (see examples in the photos). Open the arms and carefully place over the door frame (if you're concerned about the wall or casing finish, put some electrical tape on the edges that make contact). Grab the handles and slowly lower yourself, shifting your weight to the system (note: the paracord and knot will work out some slack, and you'll shift downward a little).

description: 🦟 Sticky Card Mosquito Trap 📋 Overview This mosquito trap is designed to attract and capture female mosquitoes searching for a location to lay their eggs. The trap uses a sticky card and an organic water mixture to lure mosquitoes before they can reproduce. Unlike traditional mosquito traps, this design specifically targets females looking for breeding sites, helping reduce future mosquito populations around your home or garden. 📦 Required Materials 🪤 Sticky insect card (approximately 80 × 140 mm) 💧 Water 🍂 Dead leaves, grass clippings, dirt, or other organic matter 🔧 Design Features ✅ Easy to assemble and install 💧 Designed to hold an attractant water mixture 🖨️ No supports required 🌧️ Overflow holes prevent water from reaching levels that could become accessible for mosquito breeding 🪤 Replaceable sticky card system 🌡️ Suitable for outdoor use when printed in weather-resistant materials 🖨️ Printing Recommendations PETG is recommended for outdoor durability and weather resistance. For best results: • Print the top cover and grid in translucent PETG . • The included print profiles are optimized to provide some translucency without significantly increasing print time. • If you want greater transparency, reduce print speeds to around 20 mm/s as described here: https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/knowledge-sharing/transparent-petg The remaining parts should be printed in black or another dark color, as darker surfaces help attract mosquitoes into the trap. 💡 How to Use Assemble the trap. Place it in a shaded location away from direct sunlight. Fill the lower container with water. Add dirt, dead leaves, grass clippings, or other organic material. Slide a sticky card in the holder. As the organic material decomposes, it creates an environment that attracts female mosquitoes looking for a place to lay their eggs. Once inside, the mosquitoes become trapped on the adhesive card. ⚠️ Notes • Check and replace sticky cards as needed (I replace mine every 2weeks). • Check the water level • While this trap primarily attracts mosquitoes, it is not species-selective and may occasionally capture other insects. • From my experience, it attracts significantly more mosquitoes than other insects.
