description: This is my 2nd cycloidal drive, which has a few more non-printed parts but in exchange is much more robust and reliable long term. It is optimized for having minimal parts for ease of assembly and maximum reliability. This drive also has, in my opinion, a much better assembly guide. All parts are designed with partially bridged counterbore holes to be printed without supports, the prearranged parts file has all of the parts in the correct orientation. Basically any filament should be fine for printing the parts, as the weak point of the output pins has been replaced with steel on this design. CF filaments may provide higher rigidity and thereby higher efficiency because of less housing flex, but I printed it out of PETG and it works fine. The clearances are a bit loose by default to try and make it work efficiently without modification on as many printers as possible, but if you want to try and tune the clearances for your printer to get lower backlash, the individual CAD files are available for easy modification. Hardware Needed: 3x M4x8mm heat set inserts (shorter is fine) 4x M3x5mm screws 4x M4x18mm screws (a bit longer or shorter is fine) 6x M4x16mm steel dowels (a bit longer or shorter is fine, but it must be =>12mm and < =18mm) Assembly Instructions: Step 1: First, grab the output plate piece and insert the flanged ends of the heat-set inserts to the holes on the plate as shown in the image below. Next, use a soldering iron with a heat-set insert tip to insert the heat-set inserts. After you finish, the plate should look like this: Step 2: First, place the housing onto the NEMA 17 motor and secure it on using the 4 M3x5mm screws as shown below. Then, insert the eccentric1 piece onto the motor shaft, and place one of the cycloidal disks onto the eccentric piece as shown. Now you can also optionally apply lubricant to the lobes of the disk and the eccentric piece. Now, place the eccentric2 piece onto the shaft. It should look like it is offset 180 degrees from the eccentric1 piece. Next, place the 2nd cycloidal disk onto the eccentric2 piece. It is critical that you align the 2nd cycloidal disk correctly with the 1st disk, otherwise the output pins will not fit into the 2 disks correctly. The first and second disk holes should overlap enough for the output pins to fit through all of them. Ensure your disks look like the 1st picture and not the 2nd. You can also add lubricant to the lobes of the 2nd disk and the 2nd eccentric piece now if you wish. Now, add the 6 M4x16mm steel pins to the output piece as shown: Insert the output piece with the pins into the 2 disks. The output plate should lie on top of the 2nd disk as shown, if the pins struggle to fit in check the alignment of the 2nd disk with the 1st. Place the output holder onto the drive and screw it in with 4 M4x18mm screws. That's it, you're good to go now!

description: If you like my design, feel free to click the “ Buy Now ” button (if available) on this page to support me. I may earn a small commission, which helps me keep creating more models. Thanks and have fun! Introduction A bird circulating shower device using the ZC003 rechargeable power kit, designed for budgerigars or similarly sized birds. Similar projects typically use wired-powered finished water pumps, which must be placed near a power source, and routing cables is inconvenient when used in a birdcage. Most also do not provide mounting solutions. The main goal of this project is a more flexible and convenient user experience, free from cable restrictions, allowing it to be placed inside or outside the cage, or mounted Highlights Flexible to use . It can be placed anywhere, or hung inside or outside the birdcage. Quick-release power module . The power module and centrifugal pump are magnetically coupled, solving sealing issues while also allowing the power module to be removed at any time, making charging or cleaning the water basin more convenient. Transparent viewing cover . Used for external mounting, it can be easily disassembled and assembled. Water filtration platform . Provides a standing point for parrots, while filtering large particles of impurities, reducing the likelihood of clogging the water pump and shower. Quick-release shower head . Initially available in two variants: straight and circular. Sufficient battery life . Tested to last 3-4 hours, enough for daily use. Tips Birds may not always be willing to bathe, so don't be impatient if they don't immediately interact after the shower is placed. Budgerigars are more willing to clean themselves in warm, sunny environments. The opposite is true in cold, gloomy weather. When the shower is not in use, it can be left in place. Give the birds some time to get familiar with this small device, and they will lower their guard and be more likely to bathe later. Precautions Noise : Printing gear rings with flexible materials can significantly reduce noise, but it still exists. My budgerigars did not get scared after getting used to it in actual use. Lubrication : If the printer accuracy and filament condition are good, there is no need to lubricate the gears. If lubrication is needed, it is recommended to use low-viscosity lubricating oil instead of grease, as the latter will significantly reduce the output speed and affect the pump's performance. Filament : The main body can be made of PLA/PETG. If the water basin leaks, it is mainly due to insufficient extrusion and excessive gaps between printed lines. Try increasing the flow rate. The gear ring part uses flexible material. Tested with TPU 95A or TPU 90A, the performance difference between the two is small, but both are significantly better than PLA/PETG. It must be thoroughly dried before printing or printed while drying. Magnets : Arrange the magnets as shown in the figure, with adjacent magnets having opposite polarities. Use pause printing for embedding; a pause G-code has been added to plate 1, so resume printing after placing the magnets. Using magnets with different strengths will affect the magnetic coupling effect. Too strong a magnetic force will create greater impeller rotation resistance, leading to weakened water flow; too weak a magnetic force will cause decoupling slippage. This can be adjusted by increasing or decreasing the spacing. The default coupling distance has been optimized. Storage : Place the power module where it is not easily accidentally touched. The power module can be adsorbed onto some iron products, strong adsorption force can impede the motor shaft's rotation. If you accidentally press the switch, the current might continuously generate heat and damage the motor. Charging : Use 5V-1A input Unattended charging is not recommended. Escaping risk : The transparent cover is intended to help reduce the chance of escape but cannot guarantee complete safety. I just realize that budgies may still squeeze through gaps or find other ways to escape. Always supervise your bird and use this product at your own risk. AIGC For a cleaner visual effect, the cover image was AI-modified; all other photos are original real shots. model_name: The Midnight Serenade - Dynamic Woman Sculpture
description: Bring a touch of elegance and dramatic flair to your desk with “The Midnight Serenade” This sculpture was inspired as an explosion of paint coming from the fire red dress. It was not easy to paint over black PLA, so I wonder how it would come if printed in red and paint the black areas instead! This could also be a cool multicolor/bicolor print, with obvious increase in print time and materials. Let me know if you are interested in a multicolor profile! This sculptural piece features a graceful woman standing beside an ornate lamp post, with a flowing dress that mimics the movement of paint, that flows gently over the base and edges of the platform. The design captures a unique, hand-painted aesthetic that creates a bold visual contrast between the deep black structure and the vibrant, flowing red elements. Perfect as a centerpiece or an artistic addition to any collection, this model stands out with its intricate details and dynamic silhouette. ATTENTION: I have tried a lot of supports configuration, and I had a few instances in which the supports under the dress have detached from the base. IF that happens to you, converting the tree supports to strong should solve the problem. I currently left them in organic because I had a few successful print with them so I know they can work well, and this decreases materials used and print time. Size model (can be scaled up or down): 151 x 127 x 197 mm. I will share with you bit of the story behind the failures and swearing while prototyping this model I had a major problem with the “smoothness” of the base, due to an error setting in Top Surface Layer Width to a very low value, which once corrected achieved a smooth as expected flat surface of the base / platform. After solving this, I had supports failing under the dress, after I had adjusted the length of the cloth there and sculpted so that it would require less support. I even considered making it touch the ground at the tip of the folds, but then I would lose some dynamics that goes with the shape of the dress floating so, instead I have adjusted supports. Worked well and the dress was going good, but by changing the supports, I had not noticed that now a support generated to hold her head, was arising from her hip! Which failed mid print, crashing miserably on the build plate. You can well spot the line where I stopped the print (in the painted one) as for sure it would have failed the head. So.. to not waste it, I printed the rest of the model from the layer after cutting it in BambuStudio. Aaaaaanddd I didn't think of the lamp post now being on a ridiculous base, to which the brim I added was insufficient! So… this is what I ended up with! Now is finally all fixed and ready to go!!! I hope you guys enjoy this model :)

If it matches a standard size, choose a size preset first. Presets include common round ducts, flat plastic duct internal sizes, and masonry shaft openings. The size preset only controls the opening shape and dimensions, so it stays focused on fit. Then choose a functional preset. This is the practical "what should it do?" choice: Rain louver grille for a simple removable vent front Louver with printed mesh for insect protection Solid slicer-infill mesh insert when you want the slicer to generate the mesh pattern Solid inspection cover for a small access or revision panel Backdraft shutter for an experimental one-way airflow front Experimental airflow-compensated louver when louvers or mesh reduce too much open area Glue-mount louver when you do not want screw holes Experimental real mesh holder if you want to test clamping a piece of mosquito mesh You can keep the preset or disable selected preset groups and fine-tune manually. For example, you can use a standard D125 opening size with the printed mesh functional preset, then disable only the mesh preset group and choose a different mesh pattern. For manual sizing, choose rectangular or round opening mode first. For rectangular openings, set the wall opening width and height, then choose whether the vent should keep exact custom dimensions or automatically become horizontal or vertical. For round pipe-style openings, set the round opening diameter. Adjust the front frame width, wall insert depth, mesh mode, and louver or shutter settings if needed. By default, the base flange follows the front outside size, so reducing or increasing the front frame keeps the base and front aligned. If the louvers or mesh reduce the effective airflow too much, you can test the experimental airflow compensation mode. The wall insert still stays sized to the real measured opening, while the front grille opening is enlarged from the selected free-area percentage. The base also gets an open plenum pocket behind that larger front opening, so the extra louver area feeds into the real wall opening instead of sitting over a blocked flat surface. Treat this as a sizing aid, not a guaranteed airflow calculation. Real airflow still depends on the duct, wall opening, mesh pattern, print quality, and installation. Do not combine experimental airflow compensation with backdraft shutter front mode. Backdraft shutter mode uses separate moving blades and hinge/stop features, while airflow compensation reshapes the front/base airflow pocket for fixed grille-style fronts. If this unsupported combination is selected, the generator displays a 3D warning text in the output. The printed mesh hole size defaults to 2.0 mm for better airflow and faster default prints. For smaller insects, reduce the printed mesh hole size, but remember that small printed mesh holes reduce airflow and increase print time. The printed mesh strand width defaults to 1.2 mm and can be reduced to 0.4 mm for finer decorative meshes. The mesh cassette clearance is applied per side. The default 0.4 mm clearance reduces the printed mesh cassette by 0.8 mm in both full width and full height. The internal support ramp or ledge remains connected to the wall insert and sits below the mesh cassette. It supports the cassette but does not define the cassette's outer fit size. The printed mesh patterns are generated with an internal rim and full-cell spacing, so square, diamond, slit, and crosshatch meshes avoid tiny leftover edge fragments. Diamond grid uses dense diamond-shaped holes, crosshatch uses wider crossing diagonal ribs, and slit mesh includes multiple cross braces for better stiffness. Orientation slits follow the selected horizontal or vertical layout, while vertical and horizontal slit modes stay manual. The solid mesh pattern creates a full thin insert that can be turned into a slicer-generated mesh by using sparse infill and disabling top and bottom shells. For most first prints, use no mesh or the printed mesh insert. The real mesh holder is experimental: it may be useful for clamping a piece of standard mosquito mesh between the holder and clamp frame, but it should be test printed before relying on it for a final installation. Rear lip depth is automatic by default. It follows the base flange thickness. Printed mesh clearance is handled by the base-side mesh seat/support, so the front lip does not grow when mesh is enabled. Manual rear lip depth is still available for special fit tests. Backdraft shutter mode prints the front frame and the moving shutter blades as separate parts. The blades are narrower than the frame opening and use a blade-width hinge bar with short side hinge pins that press into open side sockets in the front frame, so they have room to rotate instead of binding against the frame. For round wall openings, the wall insert stays round, but the base includes a transition pocket from the round insert to the rectangular shutter interface. In that mode, the optional printed mesh also becomes a rectangular front-pocket insert instead of dropping into the round wall opening. The shutter front, rear lip, blades, hinge pins, and stops then use the same rectangular working layout as the default backdraft mode. The front can also add side stop bridges above the hinge sockets to limit over-opening and a lower stop rail to keep the bottom blade from swinging backward. The default socket shape is hexagonal for more support-friendly printing than a round horizontal hole. Treat this mode as experimental and test fit before printing a large final part, because small moving FDM pivots depend strongly on printer calibration, material, and selected clearances. The external frame shape can be changed independently from the wall opening. Use the default rectangle with rounded corner style for a clean utility vent, or switch to oval, circle, hexagon, octagon, or petal-style flower for a different front style. Rectangular frames can use sharp, rounded, or chamfered corners with one shared corner size. Circle frame mode expands the outside diameter enough to keep rectangular openings inside the circular flange. Print Notes The default output is a print layout with separate parts placed flat on the bed. Individual part output modes also use print-ready orientation, while assembly preview keeps the mounted orientation for fit inspection. Enable exploded assembly preview to separate the stacked parts along the mounting axis. The generator flips the base, front grille, printed mesh, and experimental real mesh holder parts in print modes so they are bed-ready. Assembly preview intentionally keeps the mounted orientation. The default internal mesh support uses a support-free 45-degree ramp for that direction. If you prefer a regular shelf and do not mind support material, switch the mesh support mode to flat ledge. Depending on your printer, material, and cooling, you may want to test a smaller sample first. If fit is too tight, increase the fit clearances before printing a full-size vent. model_name: [V2] Dual Hose Adapter Mod 150mm for portable AC
description: 🚨 UPDATE 2026-06-27 (V2): Complete Redesign! 🚨- focus on printing the slim version. It is all you need, 50% less time and 50% less filament with the same functionality. Only 1 Build plate - no splitting anymore. Big version only left for legacy/looks/A1Mini. More info at the bottom. Pair this with my 150mm Hose through-pass Connector (link) ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Compatibility I designed this adapter for a budget-friendly portable AC bought at "Action" here in Germany. The unit is sold under the house brand KINZO (9000 BTU), but a friend tested it on a Comfee device (7000BTU) and it fits perfectly as well. After doing some research, it turns out this is a very common OEM device base shared by many different brands on the market. While I found some mods for models with corner air intakes, there was nothing clean available for this flat style, so I designed my own. As long as your unit shares the same outer dimensions for the air vent cover (which most of these OEM models do), this adapter will be compatible. It supports portable ACs from various manufacturers, including but not limited to: comfee TRONIC KINZO HOME DELUXE EUHOMY argo MEDION HANTECH (I will expand this list as I receive more feedback from the community. So far, it has been physically verified on Comfee, Argo, Tronic, Hantech and Kinzo devices). 👉 The most important step: Measure your existing intake air vent cover to ensure a match. It should be approximately 219 x 290 mm: 🌬️ Why use a 2-Hose Mod? Standard single-hose ACs push hot air out, creating a vacuum that constantly sucks warm air back into your room through cracks, doors, and walls—meaning you waste energy exhausting air you just cooled. This dual-hose mod fixes that. In my case, it cut both cooling time and energy consumption in half to reach the same room temperature. It's a massive boost to overall efficiency and performance! If you want more detail about this process I can recommend the Video form Technology Connection, explainigng all of it in detail: 🛠️ Materials Needed (BOM, just to connect the adapter to a 150mm hose) 1x 150mm Hose Clamp (Amazon) (you will need multiple) 1x 150mm flexible Hose (Amazon) 1x Outside air intake solution (e.g., my 3D-printed trough-pass connector for 150mm hose) My Setup & Material Tips I used this adapter with a 20mm XPS panel (you can get it easy at a local hardware store, online prices are crazy). which I lined with reflective radiator insulation foil (Amazon). and Aliminium Tape (Amazon). The whole setup cost me less than 10€ at my local hardware store . Also I used my 3D-printed trough-pass connector for the 150mm hose (for 0-60mm panels) You can easily cut XPS with a standard utility knife and simply glue 2 panels together if you have a bigger window. It is lightweight, stable, thermal isolating, completely opaque (light-tight), and seals beautifully, if you take some time to cut it to match your window. If you don't want to use XPS, this design easily adapts to plywood, acrylic, or any other window insert material you prefer. I highly recommend you isolate at least the exhaust site, to not have it act like a heater for the room. Here is a link for isolation (Amazon) , but just a old blanket will also do the trick, if you are on a budget. You find the step by step installation guide in the print profile off the pass-trough if you need more insight. 🖨️ Print & Material Options I highly recommend PETG for durability and easy of use. PLA works (since it should not get too hot) but isn't ideal. ABS/ASA is overkill, but totally okay. If possible, print it in one piece on a large build plate. For smaller printers (like the A1 mini), I have included split profiles. If you print the split version, just use superglue, tape, or plastic welding to fuse the parts together so the adapter stays completely airtight. you only need very small supports for the handle. The rest of the adapter prints without supports and I did not even need a brim. If you have problems with bed adhesion consider a bigger brim. For installation: Clean the brim off if you printed it with one. Then insert the 2 clips into the designated slots (mirrored to the printed guides). They should fit tighly and not come out easy, use some superglue if they are too loose. Swap your AC's stock vent cover with this adapter, connect your 150mm hose, and you are done! Mesh / Filer: If you don't plan to vacuum your radiator regularly I highly encourage the use of a filter. With the big version you can just continue using the original filter, but with some handy fingers you are able to shove the original filter also behind the slim version. For convenience and looks I also added a printable filter that fits perfectly inside the slim version. If you decide to print it, it is very important that your build plate is very clean and you do not use a cold plate, so it releases easy once cooled down. It relies on very fine lines on the first Layer, use the print profiles, the modifiers in the slicer are very important! Changelog: 2026-07-01: I added a printable mesh / filter for the slim version 2026-06-27: V2 - complete redesign 🚀- I realized there was some unused space under the old cover that wasn’t actually occupied air intake. It bugged me from the beginning that the first design was just a tad too big to fit on a single build plate for the X/P/A series printers. After running some prototypes, I managed to squeeze the footprint down just enough to fit mid-size build plates perfectly. This tighter design also allowed me to shrink the overall model, resulting in 50% faster print times and 50% less material - without sacrificing any functionality. A true success! Note: I will leave the old, larger V1 version online for anyone who prefers full coverage (for looks), or in case some AC models have a slightly different air intake design (though I believe most are identical). Also the A1 mini version is too flimsy if I split the Slim version the same way so A1 mini will keep the big version.

description: 🍷 FrosNest – Keep your wine cool, enjoy the moment. 🍷☀️ FrosNest is a wine-serving accessory designed to keep your bottles at their ideal serving temperature for as long as possible during meals, aperitifs, barbecues, and summer gatherings. Compatible with the vast majority of 750 ml wine bottles , FrosNest accommodates a standard ice pack, ice cubes, or a combination of both. Its insulated cooling compartment helps reduce heat exchange while its design promotes the circulation of cool air around the bottle. The sections surrounding the bottle that do not contain a cooling source feature a double-wall construction , creating an insulating air gap that slows heat transfer and improves temperature retention. Designed as a complete wine-serving station, FrosNest also includes a dedicated corkscrew holder and an ergonomic carrying handle, making it easy to transport everything with one hand. 🔄 Update – FrosNest V4 Both V2 and V3 remain fully functional and continue to do exactly what they were designed for: helping keep your bottle at its ideal serving temperature for longer. V4 is not a fix , but rather a natural evolution of the concept, making it even more practical and versatile. What's New in V4 🗑️ The mini trash bin is now fully integrated into the FrosNest. There's no longer a separate accessory to print or store. It's always within reach for the cork, foil capsule, Champagne wire cage, or any small waste, helping keep your table clean and organized. 🧊 The cooling compartment has been enlarged to 104 × 40 mm , making it compatible with a wider variety of commercially available ice packs. 🍾 The corkscrew holder has been redesigned to better accommodate a larger range of waiter's corkscrews while making insertion and removal easier. 🥂 A new optional removable wine glass holder is now available for both V3 and V4. It is compatible with many stemmed wine glasses featuring a stem diameter of less than approximately 9 mm . Up to two holders can be mounted on each side , allowing you to carry up to four wine glasses together with the FrosNest. I hope this new evolution makes FrosNest even more enjoyable to use while preserving everything that made the previous versions so successful. 🍷❄️ 🔄 Update – FrosNest V3 Thanks to your amazing feedback, FrosNest has already evolved! 😊 First of all, the original version remains fully functional and already does exactly what it was designed to do: help keep your bottle at its ideal serving temperature for longer. However, after reading your suggestions and feedback, I wanted to push the concept even further. FrosNest V3 builds upon the original design by improving the circulation of cooled air around the bottle while keeping the same simple, practical, and efficient philosophy. V3 introduces several improvements: ❄️ The cooling compartment has been moved above the bottle. Since cooled air is denser than warm air, this new position promotes a more natural circulation of cool air around the bottle, helping to maintain its serving temperature even more effectively. 🍾 The bottle opening has been increased to 90 mm , making FrosNest compatible with most standard Champagne bottles in addition to regular 750 ml wine bottles. 🎨 The FrosNest logo has been reduced in size , minimizing filament color changes on multi-material printers and reducing filament waste during color swaps. 🗑️ A new optional accessory has been added: a removable mini trash bin , perfect for holding the cork, foil capsule, wire hood, or any small waste that would otherwise end up on the table. A version is available for both FrosNest V2 and FrosNest V3 . A huge thank you to everyone who took the time to share ideas and suggestions. Your feedback has helped make FrosNest V3 an even more refined and versatile design while preserving the spirit of the original concept. 🍷❄️ Features ❄️ Compatible with 160 × 95 × 30 mm ice packs 🧊 Can be used with ice cubes, cold water, or a combination of both 🍷 Compatible with most 750 ml wine bottles 🔒 Insulated lid to reduce cold loss 🌡️ Double-wall insulation around the non-cooled sections 🍾 Integrated corkscrew holder ✋ Ergonomic carrying handle 🖨️ Designed for 3D printing 🌞 Perfect for patios, barbecues, picnics, and outdoor dining Printing Recommendations For the best printing results, do not enable the "Supports on Build Plate Only" option . Print the FrosNest standing upright on its base , exactly as provided in the model files. This orientation has been carefully designed to: ✅ Minimize filament consumption ✅ Generate supports only where they are truly needed ✅ Optimize the watertightness of the cooling compartment ✅ Ensure a reliable print Usage Tips To maximize temperature retention: Use an ice pack, ice cubes, or a combination of both. Adding a small amount of cold water to the cooling compartment increases the contact surface with the ice pack, improving cooling efficiency. On particularly hot days, simply place a lightly damp towel or cloth over both the bottle and the FrosNest to further reduce heat exchange with the surrounding air. Optional Accessory An optional condensation drip tray can also be printed. Placed underneath the FrosNest, it collects condensation and meltwater from the cooling compartment, helping to keep your table clean and dry during outdoor meals and gatherings. Why "FrosNest"? Because every great bottle deserves a comfortable place to rest. FrosNest combines Frost and Nest —a protective home that helps your wine stay at its ideal serving temperature for longer, so every glass can be enjoyed exactly as intended. And thanks to its playful mascot—a cheerful wine bottle enjoying the cool—FrosNest reminds us that even fine wine deserves to relax a little. 😉🍷❄️

The Tomato System – Storm Edition The original Tomato System exceeded all expectations and quickly became one of my most popular gardening designs. It proved that a modular, stackable support system could be easy to print, easy to expand, and adaptable to a wide range of plants. As more growers began using it, one piece of feedback appeared consistently: “Can it be made even stronger?” The Tomato System – Storm Edition is the result. Rather than simply reinforcing the original design, I went back to the drawing board and rethought how the entire structure is assembled. The goal was simple: create a version that is noticeably more rigid, more stable, and better suited for demanding outdoor conditions while maintaining the flexibility that made the original system so popular. A Stronger Approach The biggest change is found in the way the system is assembled. Unlike the original Tomato System, which used push-fit vertical posts and external locking clips, the Storm Edition uses threaded vertical posts that screw directly into each support level. This creates a much stronger mechanical connection between sections and significantly increases the overall rigidity of the structure. The threaded design also introduces a unique advantage. New levels can be added without loosening or affecting the sections below. As your plant grows throughout the season, the support structure can grow with it—one level at a time. Cleaner Assembly, Fewer Parts Because each level is securely connected using threaded posts, the side locking clips used by the original design are no longer necessary. The result is a cleaner appearance, fewer loose components, and a more streamlined assembly process. Simply connect the sections using the supplied posts and continue building upward as needed. Designed Around Plant Growth Every plant grows differently, which is why the Storm Edition includes two lengths of vertical posts. Long posts allow for larger spacing between support levels, while short posts can be used when additional support is needed around fruit-heavy branches or dense growth. By mixing the two lengths, you can fine-tune the structure to suit the shape and growth pattern of your individual plant. Built for the Outdoors For gardeners growing directly in soil, the Storm Edition includes optional Soil Anchors. These pointed attachments screw onto the bottom of the vertical posts and help the structure penetrate the ground more easily. They also provide a more secure footing in loose soil, improving stability and helping the system remain firmly planted even in challenging weather conditions. The “Storm Edition” name wasn’t chosen by accident. Not Just for Garden Beds One of the most requested additions was support for existing potted plants. To solve this, the Storm Edition includes an optional Flat Base accessory that allows the system to be used on patios, balconies, greenhouses, windowsills, and other flat surfaces. Simply place the pot inside the base and build the support structure around it. This makes the system just as useful for container gardening as it is for traditional garden beds. The Next Evolution The original Tomato System remains available and continues to be a fantastic option for many growers. https://makerworld.com/en/models/938466-the-tomato-system#profileId-903723 However, if you’re looking for the strongest, most versatile, and most refined version of the concept, the Storm Edition represents the next step in its evolution: Stronger connections. Greater stability. More flexibility. Better support for growing plants. And just like the original, it’s designed to be easy to print, easy to expand, and built to grow alongside your harvest. 🍅 Happy growing!

Description This model let's you make your own custom bookfinity books inside Bambu Studio. Just select a book size, change the text, and upload an image to make your custom book to store your stuff. This version is with the Latch to lock the book. If you want it without the latch and use just magnets, use this version here . What is Bookfinity? Bookfinity is a storage system that let's you store gridfinity stuff inside custom book shelf toolboxes. These look fantastic on a bookshelf and let's you grab your tools and components with ease. It's the most organised storage solution for any hobby. It consists of two parts: a bottom part which holds the part, and a top cover that includes the hinge. These two parts are aligned with the tabs and need superglue to attach together (Assembly Instructions below). How to use this Easy Edit Model? Step 1 - Select your book thickness Find the book size you want to edit. The 3MF files are organized by the bin height, eg 3U Books take 3U bins. Each profile has the following sizes: 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 3x5, 4x4, 4x5. Step 2 - Select your book Select your book size, and rotate the screen so you're looking underneath like this: Step 3 - Change to Objects On the left hand side, change the Process from Global to Objects. Step 4 - Click on your book Click on the book on the build bed, you'll see the text options on the left hand side. Step 5 - Select Edit Text Right click the main text and press “Edit Text”. A popup will appear Step 6 - Change the text Change the input text and you can change the size and move it around. (You can change the font too, but certain fonts don't print too well). Step 7a - Create an SVG (optional) There are many free SVGs online, and I've uploaded all of the SVGs I've used on Bookfinity on this model. If you need a custom one, you can use ChatGPT with the following prompt: “Create an image of an svg-style stencil with thick black lines of: ” and insert the name of the tool. Step 7b - Convert the PNG to SVG (optional) If you create a PNG, you'll need to convert it to an SVG. You can do it with a free site like FreeConvert. Step 8 - Insert the SVG Right click your book, press “Add Modifier” > “SVG”. TIP: if you insert your SVG, and it's just a rectangle this is because the SVG has an outline / border. This is wrong and won't work. If you generated the SVG using FreeConvert or similar, try change one of the options. on FreeConvert, I found if you go to Advanced Settings and change the "Color Mode" to “Black & White” and redownload it, it fixes this issue. Step 9 - Move, Scale and Rotate your SVG Using the Move, Scale and Rotate buttons, get your SVG where you need it. Step 10 - Set the depth of the SVG Firstly find your SVG on the menu on the left (remember to press “Objects” if you've gone off it). Right click it and press “Edit SVG”. A popup will appear. On the popup, set the Depth to 0.60mm and ensure the “From Surface” distance is 0.00mm. You can use “Use Surface” but it makes it invisible on the prepare tab so harder to use. Step 11 - Set the colour of your SVG On the left hand side, right click the SVG, press “Change Filament” and select the colour you wish to use, eg Black. Step 12: Enable Prime Tower Change Process back to "Global", then under the “Others” tab, find “Prime Tower” and select “Enable”. Move the prime tower so it doesn't clash with your model. This will make the books print much cleaner. Step 13 - Boost the model How to assemble a book Add superglue to the glue area shown below 2. Install the Bolts Install the latch using an M3 x 30mm Bolt, and an M3 Nyloc to the top cover. The nut should be at the top of the book. Install an M3 x 30mm bolt with an M3 Nyloc nut to the bottom cover. 3. Print a Gridfinity holder for your tool / stuff. If you're just looking for storage bins, these Simple Bins are guaranteed to fit. 4. Add Magnets (optional) Insert 4x D4 x 2mm magnets into the cover and base to make the books stay closed. These are available on the Bambu Shop, linked below. Notice a mistake? Got advice / requests? Please leave comments, or DM me (: Remember to also post photos of your books! Posting Remixes Yes! Upload your custom books as remixes for other people to help them out, get inspo and earn yourself some points! Use of AI Some of the SVGs used on the book covers were made using AI. The 3D model was made by human. The cover photo was made on PowerPoint, but an AI background remover tool was used. All other photos are real. Update (25/06/2026) The 7U and 8U versions are currently working progress. Please be patient these take a while to create in Bambu Studio and I'm on Holiday until Mid July.

model_name: Cantilever case for 48 Pencils with Eject Buttons
description: Organize your workspace with this compact, cascading 4-tier pencil and crayon box! Designed with both aesthetics and ergonomics in mind, this cantilever-style box holds up to 48 pencils (12 per tray) and expands smoothly to give you a perfect overview of your color palette. ✨ Key Features: Smart "Eject" Buttons: No more struggling to pick up a pencil. Each slot features a clever built-in button – simply press it, and the pencil pops up for effortless grabbing. Ergonomic Tilt: The bottom tray is equipped with retractable legs. When deployed, the entire organizer tilts toward you. This not only makes reaching for colors easier but also naturally aligns the pencils with the eject buttons using gravity. 100% 3D Printable / No Hardware Required: The entire folding mechanism can be assembled using a custom 3D-printed strap/pin insert that holds everything together perfectly. (Note: Standard M3 screws can be used as an optional alternative). Customizable Magnetic Closure: The trays feature hidden slots for 4x2mm round magnets. Each corner has room for up to 3 magnets. You can use just 1 magnet per corner (as I did in my build) or add more to adjust and fine-tune the exact magnetic pull and snapping force you want when closing the box. ⚙ Printing & Materials: Orientation: All parts are already oriented correctly in the files – just slice and print! Filament: I printed the entire box in PETG, which I highly recommend. You can use PLA for the main trays and body, but the custom strap/pin inserts must be printed in PETG (or ABS/ASA). PLA is too brittle for the mechanical stress of the hinges and may snap. Magnets: 4x2mm round (up to 12 per tray depending on desired strength). 🧩 Printed Parts List & STL Filenames To build the complete 48-pencil organizer (4 tiers), you will need to print the following parts: Part Name Qty STL Filename Notes & Material Inner Tray 4 Inner_Tray_x4.stl Main insert, holds 12 pencils. Outer Tray 4 Outer_Tray_x4.stl Outer shell for each tier. Eject Buttons 48 Eject_Button_x48.stl The lifting mechanism. Frame 4 Frame_x4.stl Aesthetic top trim. Short Link 4 Short_Link_x4.stl Cantilever expansion arms. Long Link 4 Long_Link_x4.stl Cantilever expansion arms. Rear Tilt Legs 1 Rear_Tilt_Legs_x1.stl Deploys for ergonomic tilt. Hinge Strap 8 Hinge_Strap_PETG_x8.stl Print in PETG! 3D printed alternative to M3 screws. you can replace each strap with three M3 screws. 🛠 Additional Hardware Required (Non-Printed) Button Pivot Axis: 4 pieces of standard 1.75mm filament . Cut these to the length of the tray. They serve as a simple, cheap, and effective hinge axis for the eject buttons. Magnets (Optional): 4x2mm round neodymium magnets. The trays feature top and bottom magnet slots in each corner. You can use 1 to 3 magnets per corner depending on how strong you want the snapping force to be. Middle Trays (x2): 8 to 24 magnets per tray (requires both top and bottom slots). Bottom Tray: 4 to 12 magnets (requires top slots only). Top Tray: 4 to 12 magnets (requires bottom slots only). 💡 Pro Tip: I recommend installing top magnets in the top tray as well! A dedicated top cover/lid for easy transport is on my TODO list and will be released in a future update. Linkage Assembly (Choose Option A or B): Option A (100% 3D Printed): Use the 8x printed hinge straps (Hinge_Strap_PETG_x8.stl). Option B (Hardware): Use 24x short M3 screws (6 per tier). 🛠 Assembly Instructions Step 1: Assembling the Inner Trays 1. Gather parts: You need 1 Inner Tray, 12 Eject Buttons, and ~20cm of 1.75mm filament. 2. Position buttons: Place the tray flat and put the 12 buttons into their slots. 3. Thread filament: Push the filament through the side hole, passing through all button hinges. Tip: Cut the filament tip at an angle for easier routing. Twist it if it gets stuck. 4. Trim excess: Cut the filament flush with the outside of the tray. Repeat this entire process 4 times. Step 2: Assembling the Bottom Outer Tray (Tier 1) 1. Attach Links: Counting the side pins from the front: Leave the 1st pinempty, attach a Short Link to the 2nd pin, and a Long Link to the 3rd pin. 2. Attach Legs: Snap the 2 Rear Tilt Legs into the connection points at the back of the tray. 3. Insert Magnets: Place magnets into the top pockets. (Optional: Use a tiny drop of glue to secure them). 4. Attach Frame & Hardware: Snap the Frame onto the top. Secure the links and legs with 6x M3 screws or 2x printed Hinge Straps. Step 3: Stacking and Connecting (Tiers 2, 3, & 4) 1. Add Magnets: Insert magnets into both top and bottom pockets of the new tray. ⚠ CRITICAL: Double-check magnet polarity so the trays attract each other! 2. Shift Linkage: Attach the tray to the tier below. The links shift forward by one slot: The link from the 2nd slot below goes to the 1st slot here. The link from the 3rd slot below goes to the 2nd slot here. 3. Add New Links: • Tier 2: Add a Long Link in the 3rd slot. • Tier 3: Add a Short Link in the 3rd slot. • Tier 4 (Top): Leave the 3rd slot empty. Note: Do not install rear legs on these tiers. 4. Secure: Lock each tier with a Frame and your chosen hardware (screws or printed straps). Step 4: Final Assembly 1. Insert Inner Trays: Press your completed Inner Trays down into the assembled Outer Trays. They are designed for a snug friction fit. 2. Check Direction: Make sure the Eject Buttons are facing the front of the box! 3. Done! Load up your 48 pencils or crayons, extend the rear legs, and enjoy your new cascading organizer. 🚀 To-Do / Future Ideas (V2.0) While I am incredibly happy with how this design turned out and believe it is fully ready to organize your desk right now, a maker's work is never truly done! Here are a few ideas I am exploring for future updates: Dedicated Top Lid: Designing a snap-on cover (utilizing those top magnets) to protect the pencils from dust and make the entire box completely portable. Design Simplification: Exploring ways to merge the inner and outer trays into a single printable piece to reduce both print time and assembly steps. Enhanced Stability: Fine-tuning the cantilever linkage geometry to slightly reduce the backward offset of the expanded tiers, making the fully opened box even more balanced and stable. If you have any feedback or ideas after printing, let me know in the comments!

Versión Multicolor por capas: Este modelo está diseñado y optimizado para imprimir a color realizando pocos cambios por altura de capa (eje Z). Alta eficiencia: ¡El diseño requiere únicamente 10 cambios de color en total! Esto reduce drásticamente el tiempo de impresión, minimiza los cambios de herramienta y genera muchísimo menos desperdicio en sistemas como el AMS de Bambu Lab. También lo hace perfectamente viable para impresoras de un solo extrusor programando simples pausas por capa. Montaje invisible: Su parte trasera es completamente plana. Está pensado para colgarse utilizando cinta de doble cara de montaje o tiras adhesivas (tipo Command), logrando que quede pegado a la pared sin que se vea ningún tipo de clavo o soporte. Para lograr el mejor resultado visual y que los detalles resalten con el contraste adecuado, te sugiero seguir estas indicaciones: Utiliza colores OPACOS o MATE: Es fundamental que el filamento bloquee bien la luz. Los acabados mate (PLA Matte) le otorgan a la pieza un aspecto mejor aspecto y disimulan de maravilla las líneas de capa. Evita filamentos translúcidos: No utilices colores con cierta transparencia. Al imprimirse por capas superpuestas, los filamentos translúcidos permitirán que los colores de las capas inferiores se asomen, "ensuciando" los tonos superiores y arruinando la nitidez del diseño El agujero para colgarlo por detrás está en formato negativo. This project is a parametric decorative Bubble Tray. Fully programmed in OpenSCAD, it features an elegant border made entirely of perfect spheres. The design utilizes a flawless vertical transition between the base and the spheres, eliminating any empty gaps or flat triangles at the absolute bottom (Z=0), ensuring an impeccable fusion finish. --- UNLIMITED CUSTOMIZATION --- The mathematical model automatically scales and calculates the entire distribution of spheres along the perimeter, ensuring accurate tangency and spacing regardless of the chosen length, width, or sphere radius. With support for 1 to 6 layers of stacked spheres, the combinations are virtually endless. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Main Dimensions - Tray Length and Width: Defines the overall size of the round shape. - Base Thickness: Controls the height of the solid internal bottom plate. 2. Sphere Geometry (Advanced Settings) - Sphere Radius: Defines the diameter of the spheres and, consequently, the thickness of the outer wall. Change this to achieve anything from delicate small spheres to massive giant spheres. The model recalculates the required quantity automatically. - Height Ratio: Adjusts the height of the containment border relative to the sphere radius. - Overlap Factor (Penetration): Controls how much the spheres intersect each other laterally. The default (0.20) provides the optimal visual balance and structural strength. 3. Sphere Layers (Towering) - Number of Layers: Create anything from a simple flat tray (1 layer) to a deep basket-style tower with up to 10 perfectly stacked layers. - Vertical Overlap Factor: Controls the mathematical fusion between upper and lower layers (recommended: 0.40). 4. Customization and Details - Bottom Logo: A dedicated space to deboss your brand/logo on the smooth bottom face. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Clean Print Bed: Unlike other beaded models, this project's base is mathematically flat with no angular cuts on the spheres touching the build plate. - Support-Free Design: The sphere geometries are calculated to guarantee a progressive overhang angle easily handled by modern printers. No internal or external supports are required! - Premium Finish Tip: For a truly professional, textured clay or ceramic look, enable the "Fuzzy Skin" feature on the Outside walls only in your slicer! --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal for the vertical curves of the spheres) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Recommended for filling small fusions) - Infill: 10% Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Supports: No supports needed! - Fuzzy Skin (Optional for premium finish): Contour, Thickness: 0.3mm, Point distance: 0.8mm 💡 Pro Tip: Enable Variable/Adaptive Layer Height in your slicer.

description: ✨ Parametric Desk Sign – Create Your Own Personalized Version Transform any name, word, or phrase into a modern 3D printed desk sign. This fully parametric design allows you to create personalized signs while keeping the same clean style and proportions. Adjust your text, size, and thickness to create a perfect display piece for your desk, gaming setup, office, bedroom, events, or as a custom gift. ⭐ Key Features ⚙️ Fully Parametric Design The model automatically adapts to your custom text while maintaining balanced proportions and a strong structure. ✏️ Personalized Text Create your own: Names Gamer tags Room signs Event displays Custom messages Gifts 📏 Adjustable Size & Thickness Scale the sign to fit your space while keeping the design stable and visually balanced. 🖨️ 3MF Ready – Optimized for 3D Printing Prepared for easy printing with clean geometry and maker-friendly setup. 🎨 Color Customization Choose your own filament colors: Two-color swaps Contrasting text and base Premium silk PLA finishes 🚫 Support-Free Printing Designed for clean FDM printing without supports. 🧠 Design Details This is not just a simple text model. The parametric system rebuilds the sign based on your input: Text spacing is adjusted automatically Base length adapts to the text Structure stays balanced Geometry remains clean for printing Each personalized sign becomes a unique version of the design. 📏Here is a quick breakdown of all the parameters in the script, organized by their categories: 1. Global Settings Scale_factor : Multiplies the overall size of the entire model (e.g., 2 makes it twice as big). Center_Z_axis : If true, floats the model in mid-air (useful for viewing). Keep false for 3D printing so it sits flat on the bed. 2. Font Selection Selected_Font : Chooses the font style for your text. 3. Bold Settings Bold_Text : Turns on/off a thickening effect for the text. Bold_thickness : Controls how much extra thickness is added when Bold is turned on. 4. Main Text Settings Your_name : The actual word, name, or phrase you want to display. Font_size : The 2D visual size of the main text. Text_height : The 3D physical thickness (height) of the main text letters. 5. Backplate Settings Back_height : The 3D thickness of the solid base that holds the sign together. Border_size : Adds an extra solid outline/padding around the main text on the backplate. 6. Underline Options Show_underline : Toggles a decorative line underneath the main text. Underline_thickness : How thick the underline bar is. Underline_Gap : The empty vertical space between the bottom of the letters and the underline. Underline_extension : How far the underline sticks out past the left and right edges of the text. 7. Background Text Options Show_background_text : Toggles a large background letter or word (like a watermark behind the main text). Bg_text : The specific letter or word for the background (e.g., the first letter of a name). Bg_size : The visual size of the background text (usually much larger than the main text). Big_letter_height : The 3D thickness of the background text. Set to 0 to make it flat against the backplate. Bg_xy_space : Adds a thick outline/padding around the background text to make it chunkier. Bg_x_offset / Bg_y_offset : Moves the background text left/right and up/down to position it perfectly behind the main text. 8. Color Options Back_color : Sets the color for the base/backplate, the border, and the large background letter. Text_color : Sets the color for the main text and the underline. 🖨️ Print Settings Recommended: Layer height: 0.20 mm / 0.16 mm quality Walls: 2–3 Infill: 10–20% Supports: Not required Great results with color swaps to highlight the raised lettering. ❤️ Share Your Makes I love seeing what people create! Make your own: names tags signs messages Upload your prints and share your personalized desk sign with the community!

description: Hallo guten Tag. Hiermit präsentiere ich euch die Pool Wasserfall/Düse Kombi, Komplett als 3D Druck. Wir wollten gerne einen Wasserfall im Pool haben, hatten aber keine Lust immer umzustecken, bzw. Wasserfall vom Rücklauf abmontieren, und die Düse wieder drauf zu montieren. Somit machte ich mich ans Werk, Vollständig 3D Druckbar und leicht umschaltbar von Düse auf Wasserfall ganz ohne lästiges Umstecken oder Abmontieren. Der Zusammenbau ist leicht verständlich, das Rohr wird in den Grundkorpus von oben eingesteckt bis es klickt. Somit ist das Rohr 360° drehbar. Der Wasserfall Aufsatz wird mit Gewinde ins Rohr eingeschraubt. Die Stellwelle wird so eingeschoben, dass das ovale Loch nach unten zeigt. Nun noch ein kleiner Tropfen Sekundenkleber auf den kleinen Bolzen, diesen dann ins kleine Loch gegenüber der Einschubseite der Stellwelle stecken, kurz trocknen lassen und es kann losgehen. Die Düsenseite ist leicht konisch, sie startet bei 25mm Durchmesser, und geht zum Schaft hin auf 26mm. Ich habe das Düsenloch ein wenig angepasst, um einen stärkeren Strahl zu generieren. Ich nutze eine Sandfilterpumpe von Steinbach, die Drückt ordentlich und liefert durch die Wasserfall/Düse Kombi ein starkes Ergebnis. Wenn die Düsenfunktion aktiviert ist, läuft aus dem Wasserfall minimal Wasser raus, da alles ohne O-Ringe funktioniert. das Stört aber nicht, und ist wirklich minimal. So, genug geschrieben. ich hoffe ihr habt genau so viel Spaß an dem Teil wie wir. Beste Grüße

Das Verkleben der Männlichen mit der Weiblichen Seite würde ich jeweils nur in den Ecken machen um ein austauschen des Netzes bei Defekt gewährleisten zu können ohne den Rahmen neu drucken zu müssen. Mit diesem modularen Fliegengitter-System kannst du dir deinen Fliegengitterrahmen für absolut jedes Fenster maßgeschneidert drucken und zusammenstecken. Durch das clevere Bausteinprinzip kombinierst du einfach die verschiedenen Längenelemente und Eckstücke, bis du genau die Maße deines Fensterrahmens erreichst. Das Konzept: Unendliche Möglichkeiten Das System basiert auf Eckstücken (L-Form) und geraden Verlängerungselementen in verschiedenen Standardlängen, die über ein stabiles Nut-Feder-System (Männlich/Weiblich) zusammengesteckt werden. Die Druckdatei beeinhaltet : Eckstücke: L-Form (Männlich / Weiblich) Verlängerungen: 200 mm, 100 mm, 60 mm, 40 mm (jeweils als Variante Männlich & Weiblich) Tipp: Durch das Kombinieren der verschiedenen Teile (z. B. 200mm + 60mm + 40mm = 300mm) lässt sich nahezu jede benötigte Rahmenlänge exakt abbilden. Zudem Empfehle Ich wie bei Bausteinen für noch mehr Stabilität die Stecksysteme bei der Männlichen- und Weiblichenseite möglichst versetzt zu setzten, wie Hier auf dem Bild : Befestigung an Fensterrahmen: An einem Fenster konnte ich es bei mir in einem 8mm Spalt Zwischen Fensterrahmen und Rollandenschiene setzen, sodass er ohne Irgendwas halten Konnte. Bei einem anderen Fenster, hatte ich leider Keinen Spalt. dort Hab ich es einfach mit 4 Klettbänder (5cm) seitlich jeweils ein Links und Rechts im oberen und unteren Teil am Fensterrahmen befestigt sodass man ohne weiteres den Rolladen benutzen kann. Im Unteren Teil hatte ich ein aussenliegendes Fensterbrett auf dem der Rahmen einfach Stehen kann und so nicht runterrutscht.

This Dog Dental Care Mouth Prop is designed to safely and gently keep your dog's jaw propped open, allowing you to easily access and clean the hard-to-reach rear molars. Inspired by professional veterinary tools, it features a stable bite shelf and an ergonomic outer ring for a secure grip. 📏 Sizing & Customization Guide This model is fully customizable in all dimensions to fit any dog breed, from small terriers to extra-large retrievers. However, to get the perfect fit, you must measure your dog before printing: Muzzle Width: Measure the horizontal width of your dog's snout/jaw. Your print's inner opening needs to be slightly wider than this to clear their lips comfortably without pinching. Bite Height (Opening Gap): Check how wide your dog can comfortably open their mouth without overextending or straining their jaw joint. ⚠️ CRITICAL PRINT SETTINGS (For Safety & Strength) Dogs have immense jaw pressure. To ensure this tool does not crack, splinter, or break during use, do not use standard PLA and follow these specific slicer settings strictly: Material: PETG (Highly recommended for its flexibility and impact resistance. Unlike PLA, PETG deforms under high stress instead of shattering into sharp plastic shards). Wall Loops: 5 - 6 (Thick walls prevent teeth punctures from reaching the internal infill). Post-Processing Recommendation: For long-term use, it is highly recommended to sand the printed part and coat it with a certified food-safe, high-strength epoxy resin . This creates a perfectly smooth, glassy, and washable surface. Alternative: If left raw, treat this as a short-term or limited-use item and clean it thoroughly with pet-safe disinfectant after every single use. Never leave your dog unattended with this device.

description: Inventum AC701 Secondary Intake Hose Adapter / Dual Hose Conversion This is an air duct adapter for the Inventum AC701 portable air conditioner. It allows you to add a secondary intake hose to the rear intake side of the unit. Single-hose portable air conditioners exhaust hot air outside. Because that exhausted air has to be replaced somehow, the room can become slightly negatively pressurized and pull warm outside air back in through gaps, doors, vents, and window seals. This adapter is intended to reduce that effect by allowing the AC unit to draw condenser/intake air through a second hose instead of constantly pulling already-cooled room air. This is not an official Inventum part. Included versions There are three hose-size versions: - 125 mm version — for hoses with approximately 125 mm inner diameter - 145 mm version — for hoses with approximately 145 mm inner diameter - 150 mm version — for hoses with approximately 150 mm inner diameter The listed diameter is the outside diameter of the printed hose connection spigot, intended to match the inside diameter of the hose. Compatibility Designed for: - Inventum AC701 It may fit similar Inventum units, but I have only tested/designed it for the AC701. Recommended material Print this in ABS. The part sits close to a portable AC unit and may be exposed to warm air, sunlight near a window, and higher temperatures than normal indoor prints. For that reason I do **not** recommend PLA. ASA should also work if you prefer it, but ABS is the recommended material. Installation notes - Mount the adapter over the rear intake grille as shown in the photos. - Use a hose size matching the printed version. - Keep the hose as short and straight as practical. - Avoid sharp bends or restrictions. - Make sure the original exhaust hose is still properly routed outside. - Keep intake and exhaust hose openings separated outside so the AC does not pull its own hot exhaust air back in. - After first use, check that the AC still has good airflow and that the printed part does not become too hot. Safety / disclaimer Use at your own risk. This is a modification to the airflow path of the AC unit. Do not block the exhaust, do not restrict airflow, and monitor the unit during the first test run. Stop using the adapter if the AC behaves abnormally, overheats, gives errors, or airflow seems restricted.

Smart Pet Feeder ESP32 Designed, tested and used daily for over 2 months before release. A fully 3D printed smart pet feeder powered by an ESP32. Easily configure feeding schedules through a built-in WiFi web interface without the need for a dedicated app. The feeder uses a servo-driven dispensing mechanism and automatically stores all settings, even after power loss. Perfect for cats and small pets. Real-World Tested 🐾 This feeder is not just a prototype. The design and software have been tested in daily use for more than 2 months before release. During this period, the feeder reliably dispensed food according to schedule and allowed continuous improvements to both the hardware and software. Features ✅ Fully 3D printed design ✅ WiFi setup with captive portal ✅ Mobile-friendly web interface ✅ Multiple feeding schedules ✅ Adjustable feeding duration ✅ Adjustable motor speed ✅ Manual feeding button ✅ RGB status LED ✅ Automatic daylight saving time support ✅ Settings saved in memory ✅ USB powered ✅ Factory reset function Hardware Arduino Nano ESP32 Continuous Rotation Servo RGB LED Push Button USB-C Power Supply Software Arduino IDE WiFiManager ESP32Servo ESP32 WebServer How It Works After powering on, the feeder creates a WiFi setup portal if no network is configured. Once connected to your WiFi network, you can access the built-in web interface from any phone, tablet, or computer on the same network. Feeding schedules, motor speed and feeding duration can all be configured directly from the web page. All settings are automatically saved and restored after power loss. First Setup Power on the feeder. Connect to the WiFi setup network: CatFeeder The WiFi setup page will automatically open on most devices. If it does not open automatically, browse to: 192.168.4.1 Enter your WiFi credentials. The feeder will restart and connect to your WiFi network. Find the assigned IP address in your router. Open that IP address in your browser to access the web interface. Accessing the Web Interface After connecting the feeder to your WiFi network, open the IP address assigned by your router in a web browser. Example: http://192.168.1.150 The IP address can usually be found in your router's connected devices list under: CatFeeder Once connected, you can access the web interface from any phone, tablet, or computer connected to the same WiFi network. Web Interface Guide The Smart Pet Feeder ESP32 includes a built-in web interface that can be accessed from any phone, tablet, or computer connected to the same WiFi network. Note: The screenshots shown on this page may be slightly different from the current version. The final version included with the project uses English labels and buttons . Current Time At the top of the page, the current time is displayed. The ESP32 automatically synchronizes the clock using an internet time server and automatically adjusts for daylight saving time. Speed The Speed slider controls the rotation speed of the servo motor. Lower value = slower feeding Higher value = faster feeding The current percentage is displayed above the slider. Duration The Duration slider controls how long the feeder dispenses food. Displayed in seconds Higher value = larger food portion Feeding Times Under Feeding Times , you can configure up to five automatic feeding schedules. For each feeding time: Left field = Hour (0–23) Right field = Minute (0–59) Add Feeding Time Press the + button to add a new feeding schedule. Maximum: 5 feeding times Remove Feeding Time Press the X button next to a feeding time to remove it. Feed Now Press FEED NOW to immediately dispense food. This does not affect the programmed feeding schedule. Automatic Saving All settings are saved automatically. No save button is required. Settings remain stored after restart or power loss. Status LED The RGB LED indicates the current system status. Color Status Green Connected and ready Orange Feeding in progress Red Reset mode Wiring / Connections ESP32 Connections ESP32 Pin Function GPIO18 Servo Signal GPIO5 Reset Button GPIO10 RGB LED Red GPIO11 RGB LED Blue GPIO12 RGB LED Green VIN / 5V USB-C Power Input GND Common Ground Servo Servo Wire Connection Red 5V Brown GND Orange GPIO18 RGB LED RGB LED Pin Connection Common Anode 5V Red 220Ω → GPIO10 Green 220Ω → GPIO12 Blue 220Ω → GPIO11 Reset Button Button Pin Connection Pin 1 GPIO5 Pin 2 GND Hold the reset button for 3 seconds to perform a factory reset. Factory Reset To completely reset the feeder: Press and hold the reset button for 3 seconds . The RGB LED will indicate that the reset process has started. The ESP32 will erase: Saved WiFi credentials Feeding schedules Speed setting Feeding duration The device will restart automatically. After the restart, the feeder will behave like a brand-new device and will start the WiFi setup process again. Default Settings After Reset Setting Value Speed 30% Duration 2 seconds Feeding Time 1 08:00 Feeding Time 2 08:00 WiFi Not configured Power Supply USB Version USB-C 5V / 2A Power Supply ESP32 powered through VIN Servo powered directly from 5V Common ground shared between all components Recommended Add a 1000µF capacitor between 5V and GND near the servo connector to prevent voltage drops and unexpected ESP32 resets. Chaque aile, sculptée avec une précision envoûtante, capture l’essence d’un papillon en plein vol, ses motifs délicats et ses nervures fines comme des fils de soie. Grâce à l’impression 3D sur support translucide ou mat, les écailles irisées, les motifs géométriques et les détails en relief des ailes s’animent, évoquant la légèreté, la transformation et l’amour éternel. 💬 Un mot sur cette création… Les papillons, messagers des dieux dans de nombreuses cultures, symbolisent l’âme, la renaissance et la beauté éphémère. Cette enveloppe est une célébration de ces créatures fragiles et puissantes à la fois, un hommage à ceux qui osent s’élever et aimer sans limites. Chaque détail est pensé pour transmettre une émotion pure, comme un battement d’aile qui frôle l’âme. 🌟 Pourquoi choisir ce modèle ? ✨ Polyvalent et plein de sens il est Idéal pour : Les lettres d’amour manuscrites (pour une touche d’originalité et d’intimité) Les faire-part de mariage (invitations, cartes de réponse, menus) Les enveloppes de remerciement pour un cadeau spécial ou une attention touchante Les messages secrets ou vœux intimes (à glisser dans un livre ou une boîte à souvenirs) La décoration (suspensions murales pour une chambre d’amoureux, éléments de scrapbooking romantique, détails pour votre papeterie) Les emballages cadeaux (pour des bijoux, des parfums, des lettres ou des surprises sentimentales) 🖨️ Facile à imprimer : Compatible avec la plupart des imprimantes 3D (PLA pour la rigidité, TPU pour la flexibilité). 💡 Conseils d’impression pour un rendu sublime Par défaut sur tous mes modèles, les dimensions de l'enveloppe fermée seront de 11x19 cm pour les modèles rectangulaires et 15c15cm pour les modèles carrés. 📌 N iveau de difficulté sur 5 : ⭐ = facile - ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ = difficile Impression : ⭐☆☆☆☆ - L'impression s'est passé sans encombres Retrait du plateau : ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ - Retrait du plateau relativement facile. ATTENTION aux points, c'est la partie difficile. Utilisez une spatule en plastique pour soulever délicatement le texte, attention à ne pas déchirer le tulle durant l'opération. 📌 Filament recommandé : PLA : Pour une structure rigide et des détails nets (idéal pour les invitations ou les enveloppes "cadre"). Couleurs suggérées : Rouge cerise, rose poudré, blanc nacré, or rose, mais ne bridez pas votre créativité! TPU : Pour une enveloppe souple et pliable (parfaite pour les lettres d’amour à manipuler avec tendresse). Couleurs suggérées : Rose pâle, mauve, vert menthe. 📌 Support d’impression : Utilisez du tulle souple ou rigide car ce modèle est facile a retirer et se maintient bien. Pour un effet métallisé , utilisez un filament spécial ou ajoutez une touche de peinture dorée/argentée après impression. PS : Pour une touche encore plus personnelle, glissez : Une feuille séchée de votre jardin à l’intérieur (comme un papillon qui se pose). Une goutte de parfum sur le coin de l’enveloppe (pour évoquer le vol d’un papillon dans un champ de fleurs). Un mot écrit à la main avec une encre dorée ou argentée !

description: # 🌿 Alocasia Loco Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. description: Parametric Tilt-Window AC Vent Adapter This is a customizable adapter for venting a portable air conditioner through a tilted / tilt-turn window. It changes from a trapezoid window insert into a smooth curved duct and a round hose spigot, so you can fit different window gaps and almost any AC exhaust hose diameter. What you can change Part Main parameters Use Window slit slit_length, slit_gap_top, slit_gap_bottom Match the tilted-window gap / trapezoid opening. AC hose hose_radius Set to half your hose inner diameter: 50 = 100 mm, 62.5 = 125 mm, 75 = 150 mm. Bend bend_radius, bend_angle, bend_duct_thickness Route the hose without a hard kink. Transitions round_transition_length, inlet_transition_length Blend shapes smoothly to reduce flow loss. Window lip inlet_flange_width, inlet_flange_angle_from_face Creates a flared stop/lip at the window side. How to make it airflow-friendly Rule Simple target Preserve cross-section Keep the smallest adapter area close to or above the hose area: A = π × (D/2)². Check the window gap Trapezoid area is roughly slit_length × (top + bottom) / 2. Bigger than hose area is better. Use a large bend radius If space allows, use centerline R ≥ 1.5 × hose diameter. If not, use the largest radius that fits. Avoid abrupt steps Increase round_transition_length and avoid sudden contractions/expansions. Minimize turbulence Smoother transitions + larger radius = fewer eddies and less back pressure. Quick workflow Measure the clear tilted-window gap at the lower and upper end. Enter those values in the OpenSCAD / MakerWorld customizer. Set hose_radius for your AC hose. Increase bend radius / transition length if you have room and want better airflow. Export, slice, and test-fit before long unattended use. Printing note: PLA can soften in sun or warm exhaust air. PETG/ASA is safer for hot windows. Use enough walls/perimeters around the hose spigot.

Bring the mystery of the cosmos into your room with this sleek, modern Black Hole LED Lamp. Designed to look like a stylized black hole or a camera aperture, this ambient light creates a stunning, high-contrast ring of light. When turned off, it doubles as a minimalist piece of wall art. It features an integrated screw mounting system built directly into the back for clean and easy wall installation. Required Hardware This model is specifically designed around the official Bambu Lab LED Lamp Kit - MH001. It snaps perfectly into place for a seamless, solder-free assembly. Model Components The model consists of 4 easy-to-print parts, optimized to prevent light bleeding and maximize diffusion: The Base: The backbone of the lamp where the Bambu Lab LED module securely sits. It features a clean channel for the power cable and an integrated screw mount slot for easy wall hanging. The Reflector Plate: Sits directly onto the base to perfectly bounce and distribute the LED light outward. The Cover: The iconic front face featuring the elegant spiral aperture design. The Reflector Wall: Fits snugly onto the inside of the cover to crisply shape the glowing light ring. Assembly Instructions Putting the lamp together is straightforward and requires no glue if your printer tolerances are well-tuned: Press your Bambu Lab LED Lamp Kit (MH001) into the center of the Base, routing the wire through the designated slot. Mount the Base to the wall using the integrated screw mount system on the back. Place the Reflector Plate onto the mounted Base. Insert the Reflector Wall into the inside groove of the Cover. Align the Cover assembly with the mounted Base, snap them together, plug it in, and enjoy your new lamp! Recommended Print Settings Filament Choice: Use a solid, opaque filament (like Matte Black PLA) for the Base and Cover to prevent light leaking through the plastic. Use a bright White PLA for the Reflector Plate and Reflector Wall to get the best light bounce and brightness. Supports: None needed. The pieces are designed to print flat on the bed. Infill: 15% Gyroid is recommended. Wall Loops: 2 or 3 for a clean surface finish. description: Looking for a reliable self-watering semi-hydro system for Alocasias, Anthuriums, and small Philodendrons? This fully waterproof modular planter system is built around a universal 0.5L disposable plastic cup. Designed for fast, lightweight printing, it combines a wick-based inner pot with a decorative outer pot. A complete setup weighs only about 70 grams and prints in just 2–2.5 hours. The outer pot is available in 14 unique designs. All photos show real prints—no renders here Many similar models rely on a fully 3D-printed water reservoir. While they can work well, achieving a waterproof print requires specialized print settings and a fully calibrated printer, a lot of filament (many walls), and significantly longer print times. Even then, a completely leak-free result cannot always be guaranteed. So why bother when universal 0.5L disposable plastic cups are widely available with almost no cost? Instead of relying on a printed reservoir, this design uses a standard 0.5L disposable plastic cup as the water reservoir. The result is a lightweight, low-cost, reliable, and fully leak-proof planter system that minimizes both print time and filament usage. The inner planter pot is compatible with all common semi-hydro growing media, including Pon, LECA, Fluval Stratum, perlite , and similar substrates. The setup consists of: Printed inner pot 0.5L disposable plastic cup as the water reservoir Printed decorative outer pot A. Inner Pot Volume: approximately 420 ml Reservoir capacity: approximately 120 ml of nutrient solution Two wick holes A tested single-wall design, https://makerworld.com/en/models/2153264-self-watering-alocasia-propagation-cup-with-wick Weight: 13 g, print time: 30 minutes (with printer calibration) Has two large ventilation openings for improved airflow and healthier root development. The ventilation openings can also be used to refill the reservoir without removing the inner pot (I use a large syringe for this purpose), and can be used for the convenient inner pot removal B. Reservoir For the reservoir, a standard European 0.5L disposable plastic cup is used. The size for the reference is: height 145 mm, bottom diameter 60 mm, top diameter 95 mm. C. Decorative Outer Pot The decorative outer pot conceals the plastic cup while maintaining a lightweight and efficient design. Unlike many decorative pots/planters, this design is optimized for low filament usage and fast printing without sacrificing strength or appearance. It features: Double-wall construction for fast printing and low filament usage Weight: 55–65 g, depending on the design Print time: 2–2.5 hours, depending on the design No supports required Cutouts for convenient reservoir removal Currently, there are 14 decorative pot designs available. All versions were designed to print without supports, have been fully tested, and are currently used with Alocasia plants. ( I have more designs ready to share, but first I’d love to see whether this project interests the community. ) Printing Notes Inner Pot PETG is strongly recommended for the inner pot due to its flexibility and superior layer adhesion compared to PLA. I also recommend printing the inner pot in transparent filament to monitor root development and health. Alternatively, transparent and opaque filaments can be combined to match the outer pot color while still allowing root observation (see photos). Outer Pot The outer pot can be printed at a 0.24 mm layer height for faster printing. If your printer struggles with the bottom overhangs, consider printing the first 5 mm at a 0.20 mm layer height. The outer pot can be printed with any filament. I used PLA. A non-transparent filament is recommended to block light and prevent algae growth in the reservoir. For planters placed in direct sunlight, avoid very dark colors to minimize water and substrate heating and potential PLA softening. Filament Usage A complete setup consisting of the plain decorative pot and inner pot requires only approximately 70-80 g of filament and prints in 2–2.5 hours. description: Midea PortaSplit Luftstrom-Aufsatz – Front Airflow Booster Dieser einfache Aufsatz für die Midea PortaSplit richtet den Luftstrom gerader nach vorne aus. Dadurch wird die Luft nicht so stark nach oben oder breit verteilt, sondern gezielter in den Raum geblasen. Das kann helfen, die Reichweite des Luftstroms zu erhöhen und kalte oder warme Luft besser in angrenzende Bereiche oder andere Räume zu leiten. Der Aufsatz ist bewusst simpel konstruiert: schneller Druck, nur ca. 19 g Filament, kein Support nötig — ein kleines, funktionales Upgrade für den Alltag. Der normale Luftschwenker bzw. die Swing-/Lamellenstellung sollte möglichst waagerecht oder leicht nach unten in den Raum ausgerichtet werden. Im Heizmodus und Ventilations-/Lüftermodus kann die PortaSplit diesen niedrigeren Schwenkbereich leichter in Richtung Raum oder Boden nutzen. Im Kühlmodus funktioniert der Aufsatz ebenfalls, die zusätzliche Luftauslass-/Lamellenöffnung muss dort jedoch manuell geöffnet und passend eingestellt werden. Der Aufsatz ersetzt nicht die originale Swing-/Lamellenfunktion, sondern ergänzt sie. Wenn die zusätzliche Öffnung geöffnet und die Lamellen passend ausgerichtet sind, wird der austretende Luftstrom gerader nach vorne geführt und kann dadurch weiter in den Raum reichen. Instead of blowing the air upward or spreading it too widely, the airflow is guided more directly into the room. Wichtiges vorab: Ich habe den Korb in Größe 1 auf Wunsch erstellt. An Größe 1 wollte ich mich eigentlich nicht herantrauen, weil Größe I schon wirklich SEHR klein ist. Da die Bälle einen gewissen Platz brauchen, musste ich auch hier den inneren Teil vom Durchmesser her verkleinern. Im Ergebnis ist das alles schon grenzwertig klein… Das Problem ist, dass ich nicht von 4mm Wandstärke abweichen möchte - immerhin braucht das Teil eine gewisse Stabilität. Nach dem ersten Test-Druck muss ich sagen: Der innere Durchmesser ist wirklich extrem klein… Ich habe keine Ahnung, ob das Teil funktionieren wird. Ich hoffe, die Person, die ihn sich gewünscht hat, testet es und wird hier eine Rückmeldung geben. Da ich selber keine Pumpe für diese Größe habe, konnte ich das Teil nicht in der Praxis testen; die Maße entsprechen aber einer originalen Kartusche, daher muss es eigentlich passen. Ich würde mich freuen, wenn Ihr mir (hoffentlich positive) Rückmeldungen nach dem Druck gebt. So! Und nun zu meinem eigentlichen Text! Ich bin diese nervigen Kartuschenfilter einfach leid gewesen. Auf Sandfilter wollte ich nicht unbedingt umsteigen, da die “normalen” Filterpumpen an sich ja gut funktionieren; vor allem bei kleineren Pools sind diese auch vollkommen ausreichend. Ich dachte mir daher, dass ich das Problem einfach mittels CAD und 3D Drucker selber löse. Herausgekommen sind Filterkörbe in den Größen II bis IV und nun auch in Größe I. Das Teil hat bei den ganzen Löchern natürlich unglaublich viele Außenwände, so dass bei 0,2mm Schichthöhe recht lange Druckzeiten entstehen. Ich stelle Euch das Modell mit meinen Einstellungen zur Verfügung - fühlt Euch frei, z.B. die Schichthöhe und/oder die Druckgeschwindigkeit zu erhöhen (natürlich auf eigene Gefahr 😉). Über Bilder und Bewertungen freue ich mich natürlich sehr! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
