description: A fully 3D-printable Push-to-Open mechanism with 4 tactile click stages and a completely new rotating locking wheel concept. Snap-fit assembly No supports required No additional hardware No tools required 4 parts 1 printing plate Approx. 3 hours print time Approx. 110 g filament Tested with PLA, standard print settings and the printer X1E and X1C I designed a completely new Push-to-Open (Push-to-Lock / Push-Push) mechanism. This model is intended as a functional demonstration of the working principle and can be assembled quickly using snap-fit connections. I plan to use this Push-to-Open principle in future projects. Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. To make the mechanism easier to understand, I added viewing windows to the model so every movement step can be observed clearly. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

Das Getriebe besteht nur aus 3D gedruckten Teilen. Das vorliegende Modell ist ein Stirnradgetriebe mit zwei Zahnrädern: Ritzel (Antriebsrad): 15 Zähne (z1 = 15) Treibrad (Abtriebsrad): 30 Zähne (z2 = 30) Stirnradgetriebe dienen der Übertragung von Drehmomenten und Drehbewegungen zwischen parallelen Wellen. Die Kraftübertragung erfolgt formschlüssig über die Verzahnung der Räder. Funktionsweise und Vorteile Übersetzungsverhältnis: Das Verhältnis der Zähnezahlen (z2/z1 = 30/15 = 2:1) bestimmt die Drehzahl- und Drehmomentwandlung. Das Treibrad dreht sich halb so schnell wie das Ritzel. Das Drehmoment verdoppelt sich am Treibrad (bei idealer Reibungsfreiheit). Drehrichtung: Stirnradgetriebe kehren die Drehrichtung um (Gegensinnige Drehung von An- und Abtrieb). Anwendungsbereiche: Einsatz in Maschinenbau, Fahrzeugtechnik, Robotik und vielen industriellen Anwendungen, wo präzise Bewegungsübertragung erforderlich ist. Zusammenbau: Zuerst wird die Welle und das Ritzel zusammengebaut. Zuerst muss auf die Welle die Passfeder in die Nut und dann das Zahnrad aufgeschoben werden. Anschließend bekommen Welle und Ritzel die passenden Lager. Jetzt bekommen die Gehäuseteile die Stifte welche es zusammenhalten. Es sollte reichen immer nur die diagonalen auszustatten. (Beide Deckel und ein Gehäuseteil) Jetzt kommt der finale Schritt. Beide Wellen ins Gehäuse legen, Gehäuseteil-2 drauf, und jetzt nur noch seitlich die Lagerdeckel montieren. Lernmodell Das 3D-gedruckte Modell eignet sich hervorragend als anschauliches Lernobjekt für: Verständnis von Getriebeprinzipien (Übersetzung, Drehrichtung, Kraftfluss) Demonstration von mechanischen Grundlagen (Zahnflankenkontakt, Eingriffsverhältnisse) Praktische Anwendung in Unterricht, Projekten oder Selbststudium Durch die physische Darstellung werden abstrakte Konzepte greifbar und fördern ein tiefes technisches Verständnis.

A minimalist hand-driven planetarium that turns the six classical planets — Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn — at astronomically accurate relative speeds. 10 cm wide, 5 cm tall. This is a very detailed functioning microscope, other than the zoom. The features: 3 turnable lens tubes (different sizes) Tilting arm Working stage clips Body tube can be adjusted up or down There are 29 parts, with three materials. The white is PETG, the silver is PLA Basic, and I used PLA Tough for the black. You will need superglue, and maybe a bit of hot glue just to be safe. Assembly is relatively easy-to-medium, with it taking around 30-minutes, including the wait time for drying. \ How to assemble: After printing everything with your preferred colors or materials, you need to assemble all 29 parts. Here's how. 1.Glue each of the three small feet to the indents on the bottom of the base. Make sure they are pushed through all the way. 2. Glue the three components of each stage clips together. The stage clips should be sandwiched between the two pins. The pin with the square should be glued onto the bottom of the stage, and the circular pin should fit snugly into the hole in the square. Glue the pins together. 3.Place the gear into the small crevice at the top of the arm. Align the plus shape with the hole. Stick the knob dowel through, and glue the other knob to the protruding dowel. Then, place the stage support onto the arm and hammer the two pins tightly. 4.Push the gear rack into the two indents on the body tube. Push the black eyepiece to the body tube. Glue the lens base to the bottom of the body tube. Make sure the small bump on the top is facing opposite of the rack orientation. Then, glue the swivel to the lens base and the lens turret. IMPORTANT! ONLY GLUE THE MOVING PARTS TO THE ASSIGNED PIECE. 5.Slide the body tube rack down to up into the gear on the arm. You may need a little force, but only a little. 6.Hammer/push the two thicker stage pins through the assembled stage and into the stage support. Glue the stage onto the tip of the stage support for extra stability. 7.Align the large holes of the base and arm and slide the large dowel through. You may need to put a line of hot glue on the dowel to create more resistance when assembled. Glue the other cap on. This is what the finished product is supposed to look like. description: Lazar’s S4 Sport Model Internals and Reactor Catchy Title: Lazar’s S4 Sport Model: Inside the Alien Tech! Detailed Description Ever wanted to step inside the most famous UFO in history? The Man, The Myth: Bob Lazar & S4 The story of Bob Lazar is the cornerstone of modern UFO lore. In 1989, Lazar went public with claims that he was hired to reverse-engineer extraterrestrial technology at S4 , a hidden facility carved into the mountainside near Papoose Lake, just south of Area 51. According to Lazar, he worked on one of nine different discs—specifically the sleek, stainless-steel-looking "Sport Model." He described the craft as having no visible welds, bolts, or wires, powered by an anti-matter reactor that synthesized gravity waves. Current Status & United Nuclear: Today, Bob continues to operate United Nuclear Scientific Equipment and Supplies , a company that provides everything from high-voltage supplies to radioactive isotopes for enthusiasts and researchers. Despite decades of scrutiny, Bob has remained consistent in his story. The New Amazon Special: "S4: The Bob Lazar Story" (2026): If you haven't seen it yet, the new documentary "S4: The Bob Lazar Story" on Amazon Prime is a game-changer. Directed by Luigi Vendittelli, this special features the most realistic CGI recreations of S4 ever produced, showing the interior levels exactly as Bob described them. This 3D model is designed to be the perfect physical companion to that special—allowing you to hold the very tech shown on screen. description: 这是一款机械日地月运行轨道仪，它通过精密的齿轮传动系统，生动模拟了太阳、地球与月球三者之间的运行轨迹和相对位置关系。 这款仪器不仅是一件精美的机械模型，更是一个直观的天文教学工具。它通过手摇曲柄驱动内部齿轮组，带动地球模型绕太阳公转，同时月球模型绕地球公转，完美再现了天体运行的基本规律。其核心设计在于通过不同齿数的齿轮组合，精确还原了地球公转与月球公转的周期比例，使演示过程既科学又富有观赏性。 仪器的中心是一个金色的太阳模型，周围环绕着标有“一月”至“十二月”的刻度盘，用于指示地球在公转轨道上的位置，从而帮助理解四季更替。月球模型则通过一个独立的臂架连接在地球模型上，随着地球一起绕太阳运动，同时自身也在绕地球旋转。 这类仪器的历史可以追溯到18世纪的“七政仪”（orrery），最初用于演示太阳系行星运动。现代版本的三球仪则更专注于日、地、月三者关系，广泛应用于中小学教学、科技馆展览以及天文爱好者收藏。它不仅能演示地球的自转与公转、月球的公转，还能形象地展示日食、月食、月相变化等天文现象，是理解基础天文学概念的绝佳辅助工具。

description: This remix uses the original launch mechanism and adapts it for mounting on a PVC base. If you've never built a PVC bottle rocket launcher before, The King of Random has a helpful YouTube tutorial showing how to construct the base. The launcher uses two stacked O-rings to create a seal. To help the locking mechanism engage securely, use a heat gun to create a very slight bulge in the PVC pipe at the point where the bottle locks onto the launcher. The inside diameter of this model is designed to match standard 1/2-inch PVC pipe . The fit is intentionally tight, so expect some effort when sliding the printed part onto the pipe. It should work with off-the-shelf 1/2-inch PVC from Home Depot and similar hardware stores. If you have zipper wax or another suitable lubricant, applying a small amount to both the PVC pipe and the printed part can make assembly and operation smoother. I have not tested the design without the heat-gun-created bulge. However, if your fit is tight enough, it may work with only the O-rings. Alternatively, a small dab of super glue on the PVC just below the first O-ring (or before installing the gripper arms) may help keep everything securely in place.

Kinetic Galton Board A kinetic Galton board that demonstrates the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution instead of the usual Gaussian you get from a classic bead-and-peg Galton board. It went semi-viral on Instagram (4M+ views), so I'm publishing the files here for anyone who wants to build one. Watch it run: https://www.instagram.com/p/DZauWk2SiXA/ How it works There are two chambers, left and right. The left chamber holds about 400 balls resting on a slider above a fast-spinning cylinder fitted with two fins. The fins agitate the balls and inject energy into the system. The balls collide with each other and with the chamber walls, behaving like gas particles in a box. At the top-right corner of the left chamber there is a small hole, roughly one ball wide. A ball only escapes (effuses) through this hole when it arrives with the right velocity. On the right side there are about 14 bins. The bin dividers are slightly shorter than the height of the escape hole, so a ball that effuses has to fall a small distance before reaching the tops of the bins. The physics is the interesting part: Because the hole is about the size of a single ball, a ball leaving it has essentially no vertical velocity at the moment of escape. So the time it takes to fall the small gap to the bins is the same for every ball . With d = v·t and t constant, the horizontal distance a ball travels (and therefore the bin it lands in) is proportional to its speed at the moment of effusion . Read the bin, and you've effectively measured how fast that ball was moving when it escaped. Do this for all ~400 balls, which have been colliding and exchanging energy like gas molecules, and the bins fill in to trace out the signature Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution . Printing There are two versions depending on what motor you have. Version for CIM (FRC) I built mine around an FRC CIM motor , just because I had some lying around. They're big and frankly overkill for this, but a lot of FRC people have them on hand. If that's you, open the Version for CIM folder and print the STL files there. Version for 775 For everyone else, the most common suitable motor is a 775 . They're cheap and easy to get almost anywhere. Open the Version for 775 folder and print the parts there. Both folders also include the raw STEP files if you want to modify anything. Cover The cover on mine is laser-cut acrylic . If you don't have a laser cutter, there's an STL so you can print it instead out of a transparent material, it just won't be as clear as acrylic. If you want to chase clarity, look up guides on printing crystal-clear PETG, though I didn't have much luck with it myself. Balls You need about 400–600 balls . They are 4 mm diameter , so do not substitute airsoft BBs, those don't work. To save you from duplicating a ball 400 times in your slicer, there's a 20×20 grid of them included. A few notes: Add a brim when printing the grid, otherwise the balls pop off the build plate. The sliced result should look like this: After printing you'll have a sheet with all the balls attached to it. Don't try to pull them off by hand , you'll tear the sheet and it becomes a miserable job getting the sheet off the balls. Instead, use pliers and twist each ball off the sheet. It's tedious, but it works. 400 balls took me about 20 minutes. Assembly and operation You will need 1x 775 motor, 2x M4x8 bolts, 4x M3x8 bolts Assembly is straightforward Place the balls into the device. Insert the slider. Shake the balls into the left chamber. Important: Use the slider to drop the balls onto the agitator while it is already spinning . If the balls surround a stationary agitator and you try to spin it up, it will stall the motor and the whole thing jams. That's it, spin it up and watch the distribution build.

model_name: Wind Turbine Project | Functional Simple Turbine
description: This is a heavily modified and fully functional remix of the excellent "Basic Wind Turbine" by kjt270000 . This remix transforms the original core concept into a practical, power-generating system designed specifically for apartment balconies and off-grid experimentation. This project includes completely redesigned mounting hardware, weatherproofing additions, structural reinforcements, and a complete perfboard electronics enclosure to harness the wind and charge an 18650 lithium-ion battery. 🛠️ What's New in this Remix? Two Optimized Sizes Medium Version: Retains the 24mm motor from the original model. Ideal for standard winds and smaller spaces. Large Version: Upgraded to house a 32mm motor, significantly increasing power generation potential for easier battery charging. Balcony-Ready Mounting System The mounting system has been completely engineered from scratch to easily clamp onto a typical balcony barrier. The Mast: Designed to use a standard 32mm (external diameter) PVC pipe with a 2.5mm wall thickness as the main tower. Free Rotation Yaw: To ensure the turbine can freely track wind direction (yaw) without friction, the design incorporates a standard bearing (27mm External Diameter / 15.5mm Internal Diameter) at the pivot point. Structural & Weatherproofing Upgrades Motor Cover: Added a top cover for the motor housing to improve weather resistance. (Note: While it provides splash and light rain protection, leaving the turbine out in heavy, continuous rain is still not encouraged). Tail Support: A new stabilizing brace was added to the tail section. This prevents the tail from sagging or bending under its own weight over time due to the natural layer orientation of FDM printing. Smart Cable Management On both versions, the main pivot body features a specific internal routing path. The cables run straight from the motor, inside the PVC pipe, and out the bottom. This prevents the wires from wrapping around the mast as the turbine rotates. ⚡ Electronics Overview (No Custom PCB Required!) Hardware Components List Core Modules & Power 1x 18650 Lithium-Ion Battery (3.7V, unprotected cell is fine since the circuit has protection) 1x 18650 Single Cell Battery Holder 1x TP4056 Lithium Battery Charging Module (Ensure you get the version with the built-in protection circuit—it has OUT+ and OUT- pads in addition to B+ and B-). 2x MT3608 DC-DC Step-Up Boost Converter Modules (Often marked as HW-045). Basic Electronic Components 4x Rectifier Diodes (1N4007 are standard, but 1N5819 Schottky diodes are highly recommended here for better efficiency and lower voltage drop). 1x Electrolytic Capacitor (Values around 470µF to 1000µF, rated for at least 16V or 25V). 1x Perfboard / Prototype PCB (Standard dot-matrix board, cut to fit your 3D printed enclosure). Miscellaneous Hookup wire (22-24 AWG stranded wire is ideal for flexibility) Solder How It Works (The Circuit Logic) Input & Rectification: The wind turbine motor generates erratic, fluctuating voltage (and possibly AC depending on the motor). The four diodes act as a Bridge Rectifier , ensuring the electricity flows in the right direction regardless of which way the wind spins the turbine. The Capacitor smooths out this rippling voltage. Boosting to Charge: The turbine might not always generate the 5V needed to charge the battery. The first MT3608 boost converter takes the smoothed voltage and steps it up to a steady 5V. Battery Management: The 5V feeds into the TP4056 module , which safely charges the 18650 battery and protects it from over-charging and over-discharging. Output Power: The 18650 battery outputs around 3.7V. The second MT3608 boost converter takes this battery voltage and steps it up to a stable 5V (or 12V, depending on what you are trying to power with the turbine). Step-by-Step Assembly Guide Important Pre-step: Before soldering the MT3608 modules into the final circuit, connect a temporary power source to their inputs, hook a multimeter to their outputs, and turn the little brass screw on the blue potentiometer until they output exactly your desired voltages (e.g., 5V for the first one). Step 1: The Rectifier Circuit (Power Input) Solder the 4 diodes onto the perfboard in a bridge rectifier configuration. Connect the two wires coming from your wind turbine motor to the AC input sides of the diode bridge. Solder the electrolytic capacitor across the positive and negative outputs of the diode bridge. Note: Capacitors have polarity; ensure the negative stripe side connects to the negative trace. Step 2: Voltage Stabilization (First Boost Converter) Connect the Positive output of the capacitor to the VIN+ on the first MT3608 module. Connect the Negative output of the capacitor to the VIN- on the first MT3608 module. Tune this module to output exactly 5V. Step 3: The Charging Circuit Connect the VOUT+ of the first MT3608 to the IN+ (or standard positive input pad) of the TP4056 module. Connect the VOUT- of the first MT3608 to the IN- of the TP4056 module. Solder the positive (red) wire from the 18650 battery holder to the B+ pad on the TP4056. Solder the negative (black) wire from the battery holder to the B- pad on the TP4056. Step 4: Output Power (Second Boost Converter) Connect the OUT+ pad from the TP4056 to the VIN+ pad of the second MT3608 module. Connect the OUT- pad from the TP4056 to the VIN- pad of the second MT3608 module. Adjust the potentiometer on this second MT3608 to your final desired output voltage (e.g., 5V for charging a phone, 12V for LED strips). Solder your final output wires to the VOUT+ and VOUT- pads of the second MT3608. Enjoy building, and may the wind be in your favor!

description: reimagines the classic marble run through the lens of mathematical topology. Inspired by the Möbius strip a surface with only one side and one boundary this track is designed as a seamless, self-reversing loop. The marble never reaches a dead end; it simply transitions smoothly across the twist, creating a hypnotic, seemingly infinite journey. ⚙ How It Works Gravity-Driven Kinetics: The track is carefully sloped to maintain momentum without external power. Möbius Transition: A calculated 180° twist in the mid-section flips the marble's orientation, allowing it to re-enter the upper segment seamlessly. Optimized Clearances: Internal tunnel diameter is tuned for standard 16mm (5/8") glass marbles with ~1.2mm tolerance for reliable rolling across prints. Physics Reality Check: While it appears perpetual, real-world friction and air resistance will eventually slow the marble. A gentle push or slight track re-leveling restores the loop. model_name: Aqua Jet - the underwater plane to play&experiment
description: In short , the Aqua Jet is a model that invites you to experiment, play and discover . Get ready for the Aqua Jet – your super cool underwater adventure! 🌊 Here you can play, try around and discover real underwater secrets along the way. Do you want to glide comfortably through the water or whiz off like a turbo fish? You decide! 🐟💨 The best thing about it: You can really tinker! Rebuild engines, change the balance and find out why your Aqua Jet sometimes floats, sometimes dives and sometimes takes off. Every dive is a new adventure! Try crazy combinations: put motors and floats in different places and see what happens. Sometimes your Aqua Jet drives smoothly and straight, sometimes it becomes fast and agile like a small water runabout. With the ballast tank, you determine whether your Aqua Jet wants to go up or dive deep. And if he needs more buoyancy - just float on and off you go! Even small changes make a big difference. So: try it out, have fun and jet through the water like a real underwater professional! 🚀🌊 📦 Package Contents In your AquaJetBox you will find: 1 × AquaJet fuselage (3D printed) 2 × canopy for the Aqua Jet (3D printed) 2 × wings – one left and one right (3D printed) 8 × motor mounts for attaching the submersible motors under the wings (3D printed) 1 × motor mount for an underwater motor under the hull (3D printed) 1 × ballast tank with three small caps (3D printed) 2 × air tanks for extra buoyancy (3D printed) 🧩 Recommended Accessories In order for you to try out exciting things like the motorized dive mode or the surface mode , you only need a few extra parts. You can easily order them online - and your Aqua Jet will become a small water‑plane ready for even more fun and experiments! 🌊🚀 2 × Playmobil Unterwassermotor (Blister 5159) 2 × 1.5V AA‑batteries 🧰 Required utensils and work preparation A tube of glue – preferably one like Cementit, which won't damage your Aqua Jet. After all, we want to assemble it, not dissolve 😉 it A work surface that you can cover well and where you feel comfortable. The freshly glued parts should be able to remain there until the glue is really firm. A small pad that you can use when you need some strength – for example, when attaching the engine mounts or attaching the wings. This way, your table won't get dents. 🧭 What goes where? On the drawing you can see exactly where each part on your Aqua Jet is attached . This way you can see step by step which part belongs where and how everything fits together. And best of all, a lot of things are almost self-explanatory! When designing it, we made sure that you can assemble everything easily , logically and with a lot of fun. This makes your Aqua Jet not only cool – but also really easy to understand and discover. 💪 And now: roll up your sleeves – it's time to build! 😊🔧 Free your Aqua Jet from its packaging – it's been waiting long enough to finally get into the water! 🚀 With a little glue and give the two wings their big appearance on the fuselage. The guide tabs show you the right way – all you have to do is glue. Important: The recesses for the suspensions should look downwards... after all, the engines don't want to work 😉 on the head Grab the 8 suspensions and attach them under the wings. Simply apply some glue and click - they sit perfectly in place. Now it's the turn of the fuselage: Glue the suspension at the bottom, click it in – and voilà, your Aqua Jet gets its next upgrade! Time for the ballast tank: Glue the top and bottom halves together (yes, this will be difficult 😉 without glue). Place the 3 lids on the ballast tank – this way you are guaranteed to know where the top is. Off into the fuselage with it! The exact position is not decisive at first – you will experiment later anyway. Important: The openings must point upwards. Now put on the canopy – your Aqua Jet is almost ready to go! To top it off, if you already have the submersible motors, you can attach them now. However, make sure that the adhesive is completely cured. After that, your Aqua Jet is ready for its first use! 🌊✈️ ⚙️ Different setups for the ballast tank 🪂 Glide mode (without motor) In this mode, your Aqua Jet does not need a motor . You fill some water into the ballast tank and push it to the right place. This gives your Aqua Jet the right center of gravity and allows it to glide smoothly and elegantly to the ground. ⚙️ Motorized Configurations This setting shows you how to balance your Aqua Jet well when using two engines . This keeps it stable and drives nicely straight through the water. If you want to install more than two motors , you should also attach the air tanks . They help your Aqua Jet to carry the extra weight - and ensure that it still stays 😊 well balanced 🤿 Motorized dive mode This is where the motor helps. You put enough water in the ballast tank and push it so that your Aqua Jet is well balanced. Then it dives slowly and evenly downwards – in a very controlled manner. 🌊 Motorized Surface Mode In this mode, your Aqua Jet "flies" just below the surface of the water. You decide how much water is in the ballast tank and where it should sit so that your Aqua Jet "flies" the way you want it to. Flying or diving – but not quite the way you want it yet? 🛠️ If your Aqua Jet descends too fast If your Aqua Jet hurtles down like a rock, it has too much water in the ballast tank. Just open a small lid on the tank and let a little water run out . And as you know, when something goes out, something else comes in — in this case, air . The air makes your Aqua Jet lighter, and it sinks more slowly . 🛠️ When your Aqua Jet doesn't want to sink at all If your Aqua Jet hardly dives, it has too little water in the ballast tank — i.e . too much air . Open the small lids again and let some water run in until it is heavy enough. 🛠️ When the nose or tail of your Aqua Jet is pointing upwards Sometimes your Aqua Jet doesn't dive quite straight. Then you can try it out like this: 👉 When the nose is pointing upwards Push the ballast tank back a bit . This makes the front heavier and the Aqua Jet dives straighter. 👉 When the tail is pointing upwards Push the ballast tank forward a bit . Then the rear end becomes heavier and stays down 🌟 Dare to experiment! These are just a few small tips that can help you. But the most important thing is: Try it out for yourself! As you have probably already discovered, the ballast tank has three chambers . Each chamber is a little different far from the center of gravity. Well, do you have any idea what happens if you fill the front, middle or rear chamber? 😊 🧪 Your imagination knows no bounds You can try out a lot of your own ideas. Test, change, move – and see how your Aqua Jet performs underwater. And remember, don't give up until your Aqua Jet dives exactly the way you want it to. With every small step, you get closer to your perfect result. 🚀 You can do it – and it's really fun As you experiment, you'll learn a lot about water, buoyancy, and balance. And best of all, it doesn't feel like learning at all, but like an adventure. Have fun tinkering and discovering! 😄 You could also make it easy for yourself with less reading for you and less writing for us... Maybe you're thinking now: "He could have just written: If you want your Aqua Jet to sink, put more water in the ballast tank. And if it is to rise, put less water in it. And just try to move it in the longitudinal direction" You know what is absolutely right! But sometimes you learn a bit by reading – and if it's explained in an exciting way, it's even really fun 😊 💡 How the idea for the Aqua Jet came about The idea for the Aqua Jet came while playing in the pool. A boomerang was slightly nudged and then glided like a small airplane under water to the ground. We were immediately enthusiastic about this exciting behavior. After that, we tried, tested and improved a lot. Step by step, a spontaneous idea turned into the Aqua Jet – a water toy with which you can experiment, move and learn something along the way. Today, the Aqua Jet provides exciting adventures underwater: it is fast, surprising and simply really fun. 🎨 Customizations to your liking and do you have any ideas? The Aqua Jet is made with a 3D printer. This means: We can customize it according to your wishes! Want a different color ? Or your own inscription ? No problem – we can do all this for you. ⚠️ Very IMPORTANT It's super important to us that you have fun and that you really like your Aqua Jet . If you have any ideas , suggestions or wishes – no matter how small or crazy they sound – just let us know. We are always happy to hear from you and try out your ideas. If you have any questions or need help , you can always contact us. We are happy to be there for you. 💛 Have fun playing with your Aqua Jet! And of course greetings from Leo and Amos

My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model It provides educational models of a lantern bevel gear system and a lantern crown gear system, where the pinion gears in a bevel gear system and a crown gear system are replaced by pin wheels. Brief Description Both a bevel gear and a crown gear, also known as a face gear, transmit rotational motion between two intersecting rotational axes. Usually, a bevel gear is designed to have spherical involute tooth surfaces, while the pinion of a crown gear system is a standard involute spur gear. This model shows that both systems can also be realized with pinion gears having conical or cylindrical teeth. When the pins can spin about their own axes, these gears suffer from very little energy loss due to sliding friction while maintaining very little backlash. The pinion of this lantern bevel gear has conical teeth. Correspondingly, the larger gear has a tooth shape described by a spherical cycloid offset by the pin radius. When the pins can spin about their own axes, the contact becomes purely rolling. The pinion of this lantern crown gear has cylindrical teeth, and the larger gear is designed to be conjugate to it. Like the involute crown gear, it has a diamond-shaped tooth tip, and from its side vertices, a sharp ridge runs down the tooth face and disappears midway. The tooth face outside this ridge contacts the inside face of the cylindrical pin, while the inside part contacts its outside face. This contrasts with the involute face gear, where a finite radial clearance must exist at the tooth root, meaning the tooth face inside the ridge transmits no power. In the lantern system, the tooth face inside the ridge can also transmit power, making the system more rigid and reducing backlash. Even when the pins can spin about their own axes, the contact cannot be purely rolling because the rolling speed varies with radius. Nevertheless, sliding friction is considerably reduced. While planar lantern gears have long been used in clocks and mills — valued for their low friction losses and ability to operate without lubrication — lantern bevel and crown gear configurations have seen little practical use. One likely reason is that their complex tooth geometry makes them difficult and costly to manufacture. Nevertheless, they may find a place in high-value applications where their advantages justify the cost. Reference https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VXcuryyRGbo He tests a lantern bevel system, a tilted cylindrical pinion system and a lantern crown system with rotational pins. Related Models Standard spherical involute bevel gear and involute crown gear are included in “Educational Gear Examples 1” . Planer lantern gears are included in “Educational Gear Examples 3 - Lantern”. Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Though they consume much space in the case, if you arrange them in the way shown in the picture below, you can save space than other configurations. (This configuration is possible with the updated version, Lantern Crown v8. The initial version Lantern Crown v6 did not allow it.) Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing. Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly Place the larger gear first. Insert the shaft of the pinion into the bearing. Snap fit the knob to secure it. Updates 2026-06-07 Saves some space in the case (lantern crown v8) Only the base plate for the lantern crown was modified slightly. In detail, the gears are shifted on the base plate so that they do not interfere with the small knob of the lantern bevel when they are put in the case close to each other. See the “Case” section above to see how they can be stored in the case with minimal space consumption. description: Overview This is a fully 3D printed wheel and chassis system for a trap powered car — a classic physics and engineering project. The design was built for a 4th grade science fair project to investigate how wheel size and tire material affect how far a trap-powered car travels. Three experiments were run per configuration (18 total runs), covering three wheel sizes and two tire materials. The winning combination — large 200mm wheels with TPU rubber tires — averaged 49.1 meters (161 feet) on a single spring release! The car is powered by a standard snap-style rat trap, which stores energy in its spring and releases it through a string wound around the rear drive axle. This design intentionally uses a rat trap rather than a mouse trap — the larger spring arm and stronger spring store significantly more energy, which is why the car travels so far. Build Levels — Start Simple, Go Further This design has three levels of complexity. Print only what you need. Level Plates What You Get 1 — Build the Car Plate 1 only A complete, working trap powered car with small wheels. Great standalone toy or first project. 2 — Wheel Size Experiment Plates 1 + 2 and/or 3 Swap in medium or large rear wheels and measure how far the car travels with each. One variable, easy to test, clear results. 3 — Tire Material Experiment All 4 plates Add TPU rubber tires and compare plastic wheels versus rubber tires. Requires a direct drive printer for TPU. The full science fair setup. Most people only need Plate 1. Print more plates if you want to experiment. How It Works The car converts stored spring energy into motion. When the trap arm releases, it pulls a string wound around the rear drive axle, spinning the wheels and launching the car forward. As the car moves, elastic potential energy from the spring converts to kinetic energy (motion). Wheel size and tire material both matter: Larger wheels cover more distance per rotation and roll over small surface irregularities more easily Rubber (TPU) tires grip the surface better, transferring more energy into forward motion instead of losing it to wheel slip Printed Parts Structural Parts — print in PLA or PETG Part Qty 3MF File Notes Body 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 1 One mounts to each end of the spring trap Arm 1 Complete-Kit — Plate 1 Extends the trap arm for more string travel Arm Cap 1 Complete-Kit — Plate 1 Secures the arm extension to the trap arm Axle 4 Complete-Kit — Plate 1 2 hubs per axle × front + rear axle (fits 1/4" bamboo dowel) Wheel Small (100mm) 4 Complete-Kit — Plate 1 2 front (fixed) + 2 rear (small config) Wheel Medium (150mm) 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 2 Print Plate 2 twice for a pair Wheel Large (200mm) 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 3 Print Plate 3 twice for a pair Everything is in one 3MF file with 4 plates. Plate 1 includes 4 small wheels: 2 for the front axle (always small) and 2 for the rear axle (small-wheel configuration). For medium or large rear wheels, print Plate 2 or Plate 3 twice — front small wheels are already on Plate 1. Tire Treads — print in TPU 95A Part Qty 3MF File Notes Tire Small 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 4 See tire plate note below Tire Medium 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 4 See tire plate note below Tire Large 2 Complete-Kit — Plate 4 See tire plate note below Tires are optional — the car works with plastic wheels only (we tested both!). TPU tires make a big difference though — see the results table below. Tire plate note: Plate 4 uses TPU 95A with supports enabled — filament and supports are already configured in the 3MF. All three tire sizes are arranged concentrically on the plate — the rings nest inside each other because the smaller tires fit through the center hole of the larger ones. To get a matching pair, print Plate 4 twice. To print only one size, delete the other two objects in Bambu Studio before slicing. Non-Printed Materials 1× Rat trap — Victor M205-9 Wide Plastic Pedal (recommended) or equivalent large rat trap. Use a rat trap, not a mouse trap — the stronger spring is essential for distance. 2× Bamboo dowel, 1/4" diameter, ~17.5" long (front axle + rear drive axle). 12" may also work. Dowels vary in straightness and diameter — pick the straightest ones, especially for the axles. If a dowel fits loosely, a small drop of glue holds it. If too tight, try another from the pack. Fishing line (monofilament) — light and strong 1 small metal staple Print Settings Structural Parts (PLA or PETG) Layer height: 0.2mm Walls: 3 Infill: 15% (gyroid or grid) Supports: None required Bed: Textured PEI plate PLA is recommended for most users — it's easier to print and more than strong enough for this application. PETG was used in the original build and also works great. TPU 95A Tires Layer height: 0.2mm Walls: 3 Infill: 15% Print speed: 30–40 mm/s (slow down for TPU reliability) Supports: Enabled (pre-configured in the 3MF for Plate 4) Direct drive extruder required — disable AMS/multi-material system for TPU Assembly Instructions Mount the trap to the body — slide the snap trap into the body's mounting slots Install axles — push bamboo dowels through the front and rear axle holders on the body Attach wheels — press wheels onto the ends of the rear axle Press-fit tires — stretch TPU tires over each wheel rim gradually, working around the rim evenly. Take your time — forcing one side too quickly can crack the wheel. Install arm extension — attach the printed arm to the trap's spring arm using the arm cap Attach string — tie one end of fishing line to the tip of the arm extension. Press a staple into the center of the rear axle and bend one prong out as a small hook. Tie a loop at the other end of the string and hook it onto the staple. When the trap arm releases, it pulls the string until the loop slips off the staple — this clean release is what launches the car. How to Launch Set the trap arm back (use caution — keep fingers clear of the snap mechanism) Wind the string around the center of the rear axle (consistent winding keeps the car straight) Place the car on a smooth, flat surface behind your start line Release the trap arm — the car launches! Tip: Wind the string at the axle center every time. Off-center winding causes the car to veer left or right, reducing distance. String length matters: when fully wound, the loop should slip off the staple just as the trap arm reaches its resting position. Too short and it releases before full energy is transferred; too long and the string tangles in the axle after release. Running It as an Experiment This design was built for a science fair, and it works great as a controlled experiment. Here's how to set one up: 1. State your hypothesis Make a prediction before you test. For example: "I think larger wheels will make the car go farther because each rotation covers more distance." 2. Identify your variables Independent variable (what you change): wheel size, or tire material Dependent variable (what you measure): distance traveled, or time rolling Constants (what stays the same): launch surface, string winding, number of winds, who releases the arm 3. Run multiple trials Do at least 3 runs per configuration and record each individually. Use the average — single runs vary too much to be reliable. 4. Record your data Wheel Size Tire Material Run 1 Run 2 Run 3 Average Small 100mm Plastic Small 100mm Rubber (TPU) Medium 150mm Plastic Medium 150mm Rubber (TPU) Large 200mm Plastic Large 200mm Rubber (TPU) 5. Analyze and conclude Compare your averages. Did the results match your hypothesis? What surprised you? Consider what other variables might have affected your results (surface texture, string length, dowel straightness). Notes & Tips The car can travel a surprisingly long distance — 49 meters is half a football field! Make sure you have plenty of room Surface quality matters — bumps, cracks, and slope all affect results Rubber bands can be used instead of TPU tires as a quick alternative for traction Front wheels are small fixed wheels and don't need to change between experiments Bamboo dowels vary from pack to pack — test a few and use the straightest ones. Axle fit affects both alignment and roll distance.

O SintaxCards é um recurso pedagógico desenvolvido para tornar o ensino de análise sintática mais visual, concreto e interativo. Após imprimir as peças, o professor entrega uma frase impressa e os estudantes identificam a função sintática de cada termo, posicionando as fichas correspondentes. O recurso pode ser utilizado tanto em atividades individuais quanto em duplas, grupos ou desafios entre equipes, tornando as aulas mais dinâmicas e participativas. É ideal para professores de Língua Portuguesa do Ensino Fundamental II, Ensino Médio, cursos preparatórios e reforço escolar. Termos da oração contemplados O conjunto trabalha os principais termos da oração: Sujeito Predicado Objeto direto Objeto indireto Complemento nominal Agente da passiva Adjunto adnominal Adjunto adverbial Aposto Vocativo Predicativo do sujeito Predicativo do objeto Como utilizar Imprima todas as fichas. Entregue uma frase aos alunos. Os estudantes identificam a função sintática de cada termo. Posicionam cada ficha abaixo da palavra ou expressão correspondente. Corrija coletivamente, discutindo as respostas. Também pode ser utilizado em: competições entre equipes; revisão para provas; aulas de reforço; preparação para vestibulares e concursos; atividades de recuperação da aprendizagem. Caso possua impressora com troca automática de filamento, cada termo pode ser impresso em uma cor diferente para facilitar a identificação visual. Caso contrário, o recurso funciona perfeitamente em uma única cor. description: This Rubber Band Powered Helicopter is a simple, fully 3D-printed flying model with no tail boom, no gears, no electronics, and no extra hardware. Just two contra-rotating rotors and a rubber band between them—that is the whole idea. Wind the rotors, store energy in the band, and let go. The top and bottom rotors spin in opposite directions, canceling torque so the body stays stable without a tail rotor. Lift comes from the combined action of both rotors working together. The design is intentionally minimal. Print the parts, add one rubber band, and you are ready to fly. No screws, bearings, motors, or purchased kit parts are required. ------------ A rubber band runs directly between the upper and lower rotors. There are no gears—the band connects the two rotors and does all the work. When you wind the model, the band twists and stores elastic energy. On release, the band unwinds and drives both rotors at the same time—but in opposite directions. Because the rotors turn against each other, their reaction torques cancel out. That is why this helicopter does not need a tail boom or tail rotor. The contra-rotating setup does the job in a clean, compact way. Everything you need is printed in plastic except the rubber band. The fuselage holds the two rotors in alignment and gives you something to grip while winding. ------------- - A 3D printer and filament - One rubber band - One drop of glue That is it. No other parts to buy or hunt for. --------------------- I printed mine on a Bambu Lab A1 mini using PLA. Keep prints light where you can; less weight means better lift from the same rubber band. Use a drop of glue to secure the hook to the upper rotor from the top.

model_name: SMARS rover remake for use with ESP32-WROVER-CAM
description: I've printed the SMARS tracked rover to see if I can adapt to use an ESP32-WROVER-CAM Dev.B microcontroller which has a built-in 2Mpx camera so I can turn it into a tracked mobile, WiFi controlled webcam. Although the ESP32-WROVER-CAM has enough GPIOs to use with the L298N dual motor driver, when the webcam is turned on in the sketch along with the WiFi, there are only 4 usable GPIOs remaining. Luckily, I found that it should be possible to use just the 4 GPIOs to control the two motors, but it also requires that the L298N EN-A and EN-B pins be raised to +5V. If you discarded the two jumpers that usually come with the L298N, then use two DuPont wires to connect the two enable pins on the driver to +5V. The print profile available for the BambuLab A1 Mini worked perfectly although I cannot use the IR sensor mount since the chassis is fully occupied by the L298N and the 2S1P 18650 pack with switch and voltmeter, but more importantly, there are no more GPIOs left to use the IR sensor. As you can see from the photo I took of the result is not very good looking but it does move quite nicely. I have two 100rpm DC motors which give it a decent scurry speed. The code I can share upon request if anyone wants to give it a go. Ping me and I can share the sketch and describe the wiring since it took a bit of experimenting to get the ESP32 to eventually be able to control the two motors as desired.

model_name: Spin & Solve – A Modular Educational Math Toy
description: Spin & Solve transforms everyday math practice into a playful experience where children learn by touching, spinning, writing, and solving. By combining simple mechanical interaction with educational value, the toy encourages curiosity, independent thinking, and joyful learning. Spin & Solve is a modular educational toy designed to make mathematics playful, engaging, and interactive for young children. The toy consists of three rotating blocks: two number blocks and one operator block. Children spin each block to generate random mathematical equations and then solve them independently. The first number block generates a random number, the center block selects a mathematical operator, and the second number block generates another number. The child then writes the equation in a notebook and solves it, transforming traditional math practice into an enjoyable game. The design encourages children to learn through hands-on interaction. The rotating arrows provide satisfying motion, while the colorful elements capture attention and maintain engagement. Since every combination is random, children can create hundreds of unique equations, making learning both challenging and fun. The toy is designed as a multipart 3D print, allowing it to be manufactured on any standard single-color 3D printer without requiring expensive multicolor printing systems. Individual components can be printed separately and assembled easily, making the design accessible, customizable, and sustainable. model_name: Rattleback - Self Reversing Magic Physics Toy
description: A Rattleback is a strange little physics toy that seems to break the rules: spin it one way and it spins normally, spin it the other way and it starts to wobble, stops, then reverses direction by itself. This model was designed around what matters most for a good 3D printed Rattleback: a strong self-reversing effect and easy printing with simple post-processing (no sanding required) Works Straight Off the Printer The print profile orients the model so the curved rattleback contact surface comes out smooth and functional without sanding. It does require supports, but removing them is much easier than sanding and tuning the underside until the effect works. Strong Self-Reversing Effect I tested and refined the rattleback shape by printing and comparing many different versions. After A LOT of testing, I found the perfect shape which can achieve up to around 3 full 360° spins in the “wrong” reverse direction ! It's probably not possible to make it perform much better, but, if you want to try, you can adjust the shape by using the “Customize” button to modify the parametric model, let me know if you find a better shape so I can update the default model! Best Surface for Maximum Effect The surface you spin the rattleback on matters a lot! To get the best reverse-spin effect, use a hard, smooth surface like glass, hard plastic or wood. Too much or too little friction can reduce the effect, or even stop it from working. It’s a small print, but it makes a great physics demo, desk toy or “magic trick” to show friends.

真实月球自转周期与绕地公转周期完全同步（27.3天），因此永远以同一面朝向地球。本设备不设月球自转轴，公转时月面固定指向地心，精准复刻真实天体状态。 2. 专业轨道、天体倾角与模型物理参数 2.1 核心夹角参数 黄赤交角（地轴倾角） ：23.5°，固定不变。是四季、极昼极夜、昼夜长短变化的根本原因。 黄白交角 ：黄道面（地球公转轨道面）与白道面（月球公转轨道面）的夹角为 5°09′ 。本设备通过倾斜的月球公转副臂（或轨道支撑结构）机械实现该夹角，与月球是否具备自转轴无关。 月球自转轴倾角（约1.5°）因设备无月球自转，不涉及演示。 2.2 两大轨道平面 黄道面 ：地球公转轨道平面。 白道面 ：月球公转轨道平面，与黄道面成5°09′。 2.3 模型实物尺寸与间距（桌面适配差异化缩放） 部件 直径 / 间距 太阳模型 36 mm 地球模型 80 mm 月球模型 21 mm 地日中心距 200 mm 地月中心距 120 mm 缩放说明 ： 真实日地直径比约109:1，距离比约11700:1。若在桌面模型上同时保真直径与距离比例，模型将庞大到无法用于教学。因此本设备采用科学差异化缩放： 太阳模型取较小直径（36mm）以避免遮挡光源并保证光照均匀性； 地球模型适当放大（80mm）以便清晰展示表面标注（赤道、回归线、极圈等）； 地轴倾角、黄白交角、光照几何、公转与自转相对运动关系均严格保真 ，所有天文现象的演示原理（四季、极昼极夜、月相、日月食）完全不受影响。 ✅ 该缩放方式属于专业天文教学模型的常规设计，并非科学错误。 3. 整机部件详细说明 部件名称 功能说明 太阳光源模型 模拟平行太阳光，恒定发光。光源规格及供电方式可自行适配。 地球模型（带固定地轴） 内置23.5°固定倾角地轴，表面标注赤道、回归线、极圈。支持自转及公转。 月球模型（潮汐锁定） 无自转，公转时固定面指向地心，沿白道面绕地运行。 地轴岁差旋进调节旋钮 用于初始校准地轴指向或演示岁差。 常规演示中应保持锁定 ，不得用于模拟四季更替。 地球公转主臂 带动地球沿黄道面绕日公转，配合刻度底座显示节气位置。 月球公转副臂 带动月球沿白道面绕地公转， 内置5°09′黄白交角结构 。 刻度底座 标注黄道轨道、二分二至点、四季位置，辅助定位。 电源开关 控制太阳光源启停，可按需适配。 4. 首次操作与天文基准手动归位 本设备为纯手动模型，无自动运行功能。所有位置调节均需人工操作。 基准归位目的 ：设定统一的初始状态，确保后续演示符合天文原理。 手动归位步骤 （纯人工对位）： 将地球公转主臂转至底座 春分刻度 位置。 调节地轴岁差旋进轴，使地轴指向与底座上的“北极指向标记”对齐（若无标记，可设定地轴倾斜方向垂直于日地连线，且北极指向远离太阳的一侧——此为春分标准指向）。 锁定地轴岁差旋进轴 ，后续演示中不再转动。 将月球公转臂转至 朔点（日地之间） 基准位置。 目视检查黄道面、白道面倾角无偏移，完成归位。 核心原则 ：除岁差演示或初始校准外，地轴指向一旦设定，在整个公转演示中必须保持固定。四季、极昼极夜等现象完全由地球公转自动产生，无需手动改变地轴朝向。 5. 基础天体运动演示操作 5.1 昼夜交替与晨昏线 开启光源，匀速转动 地球自转轴 （自西向东）。 面向光源为 昼半球 ，背向为 夜半球 ，明暗交界线为 晨昏圈 。 顺着自转方向，由夜入昼为 晨线 ，由昼入夜为 昏线 。 可观察：晨昏线始终与太阳光线垂直，赤道全年昼夜等长。固定地球转角可展示同一时刻全球昼夜分布。 5.2 太阳直射点周年移动 保持地轴指向固定 （已锁定岁差旋进轴），缓慢转动 地球公转主臂 。 公转过程中，由于地轴倾角固定，太阳直射点会在南北回归线之间移动： 夏至（公转至夏至刻度）直射北回归线 冬至直射南回归线 春分/秋分直射赤道 5.3 四季更替演示（正确方法） 前提 ：地轴指向已锁定，不再调节。 按顺序公转至四个节气刻度，观察光照情况： 节气 公转位置 太阳直射点 北半球季节 南半球季节 春分 春分点 赤道 春季 秋季 夏至 夏至点 北回归线 夏季 冬季 秋分 秋分点 赤道 秋季 春季 冬至 冬至点 南回归线 冬季 夏季 注意 ：演示时 不要 转动地轴岁差旋进旋钮，否则会错误地认为四季需要手动调节地轴指向。 5.4 全球昼夜长短差异 在公转不同位置，观察不同纬度的昼夜长度： 夏至 ：北半球昼长夜短，北极圈极昼；南半球相反。 冬至 ：北半球昼短夜长，北极圈极夜；南半球相反。 春分/秋分 ：全球昼夜平分。 5.5 地球五带划分 通过光照范围与直射点移动，演示热带（南北回归线间）、温带（回归线至极圈）、寒带（极圈以内）的划分。 6. 进阶专业天文现象演示（极昼/极夜） 正确演示前提 ：地轴指向固定（已锁定岁差旋进轴），仅通过公转改变地球在轨道上的位置。 6.1 夏至日北极极昼、南极极夜 开启光源，公转主臂转至 夏至刻度 。 保持地轴指向不变（春分时设定的指向），此时地轴北极自然倾向太阳。 观察晨昏线与北极圈相切，北极圈内全为白昼（极昼），南极圈内全为黑夜（极夜）。 转动地球自转轴，极昼/极夜区域不改变。 6.2 冬至日南极极昼、北极极夜 公转主臂转至 冬至刻度 。 地轴指向仍为初始设定，此时地轴南极倾向太阳。 晨昏线与南极圈相切，南极圈内极昼，北极圈内极夜。 6.3 春分、秋分无极昼极夜 公转至春分或秋分刻度，太阳直射赤道，晨昏线过两极，全球昼夜等长，无极昼极夜。 6.4 极昼极夜范围渐变演示 缓慢连续转动公转主臂，观察极昼/极夜范围从极点逐步扩大至极圈，再逐步缩小的动态过程，完整还原全年变化。 7. 月相、日食、月食完整演示（结合黄白交角） 7.1 月相周期演示 开启光源，手动转动 月球公转轴 ，月球沿白道面公转。观察月球被照亮部分的形状变化： 新月（朔）→娥眉月→上弦月→盈凸月→满月（望）→亏凸月→下弦月→残月→新月。 （因潮汐锁定，月球同一面始终朝向地球，但被照亮区域随公转位置变化。） 7.2 日食演示（朔日限定） 将月球转至 日—地之间（朔点） ，并微调月球公转角度以抵消黄白交角偏差，使日、月、地三者近似共线。此时月球影子落在地球上，可演示日全食/日偏食效果。 解释 ：因黄白交角存在，多数朔日不共线，故日食罕见。 7.3 月食演示（望日限定） 将月球转至 日—地延长线（望点） ，微调角度使日、地、月共线，地球阴影覆盖月球，演示月食。同理，并非每望日都发生。 8. 标准操作注意事项 四轴结构精密，转动需轻柔匀速，禁止暴力操作。 常规演示中地轴岁差旋进轴应保持锁定 ，仅当演示岁差或初始校准时方可调节。 演示晨昏线、极昼极夜、日月食时，建议在暗光环境下进行。 可根据需要自主适配光源亮度与供电方式。 设备为精密模型，禁止摔落、撞击、浸泡；儿童操作需成人陪同。 禁止私自拆卸轴体，以免四轴联动精度失效。 9. 常见故障与原理答疑 Q1：为什么月球不会自转？是否为缺陷？ A：不是缺陷。真实月球为潮汐锁定，自转与公转周期相同，永远同一面朝地。本设备科学还原该特性。 Q2：为什么演示四季时不需要转动地轴岁差旋进旋钮？ A：真实地球公转中，地轴在空间中的指向保持恒定（指向北极星附近）。四季更替完全由公转位置改变太阳直射点而产生。若在公转中手动旋转地轴，将得到错误原理。本设备的地轴岁差旋进轴仅用于初始校准或演示岁差。 Q3：为什么太阳模型比地球小？ A：这是为了桌面教学的可行性而进行的工程缩放。真实比例无法在桌面模型中实现，本设备牺牲尺寸比例但保留了所有角度、光照几何和相对运动关系，不影响任何天文现象的教学。 Q4：黄白交角5°09′是如何实现的？月球没有自转轴会影响吗？ A：黄白交角是月球公转轨道面（白道面）与地球公转轨道面（黄道面）的夹角，通过倾斜的月球公转副臂机械实现，与月球是否自转无关。本设备正确保留该夹角，用于演示日月食发生条件。 Q5：为什么无法每次朔望日都演示日月食？ A：设备精准还原了5°09′黄白交角，多数朔望日三者不共线，与现实一致，非故障。 Q6：极昼极夜、晨昏线演示效果不明显怎么办？ A：检查公转位置是否准确对应节气刻度，并确认地轴指向已锁定且倾角无误（未误触岁差旋钮）。重新按第4章归位即可。 Q7：晨昏线为什么不会和经线完全重合？ A：仅春分、秋分两天太阳直射赤道，晨昏线与经线重合；其余时间因地轴倾角，晨昏线与经线存在夹角，本设备可完整呈现该变化。

description: 5-Speed Manual Gearbox with Reverse This is a fully functional, highly detailed 5-speed manual transmission model (plus Reverse) designed for educational demonstration, engineering enthusiasts, or anyone who loves mechanical design. Every major internal component of a real manual transmission is represented here, including the input shaft, counter shaft, main output shaft, synchronizer hubs, synchronizer rings, sliding sleeves, and a reverse idler gear. The multi-colored gear assembly makes it incredibly easy to visualize how shifting gears changes the drive ratios from the input shaft to the output shaft. Parts & Components List All components are designed to print at 100% scale (1:1) for a perfect mechanical fit. The model is organized into the following components: Shafts: INPUTSHAFT (Input Shaft) Counter (Counter Shaft) Shaft (Main Shaft) Output Gears: 26 34 38 44 44 reverse Synchronizer Assembly: HUB GEAR 17 14 (Synchronizer Hub) HUB GEAR 20 17 (Synchronizer Hub) SLEAVE GEAR (Synchronizer Sleeve) SYNC RING (Synchronizer Rings) Reverse Mechanism: IDLEAR GEAR V2 (Reverse Idler Gear) Display Stand & Hardware: Stand Part 1 & Stand Part 2 Stand Holder Part 1 & Stand Holder Part 2 14mm bolt & Pin SNAP RING & SNAP TO IDLER SHAFT Assembly & Printing Tips Color Coding: For the best visual effect, consider printing the matching gear sets on the main shaft and counter shaft in distinct colors (as shown in the project photos) to easily identify each speed. Tolerances: This is a mechanical model with interlocking parts. Ensure your printer's flow rate and X/Y tolerances are well-calibrated so the gears spin smoothly and the synchronizer sleeves slide without binding. Post-Processing: A small amount of plastic-safe lubricant (like silicone grease) on the shafts and gear teeth can drastically improve the smoothness of the manual shifting action.

Dancing Servos Project This project creates the illusion of synchronized “dancing” using 16 servo motors controlled through a PCA9685 16-channel servo driver. An RGB LED module (WS2812B, 8 LEDs) is integrated to match the motion with dynamic lighting effects. The core concept is straightforward: all servos are connected to the PCA9685 driver, which is controlled via I2C from an Arduino. The system uses the Adafruit PWM Servo Driver library (Adafruit_PWMServoDriver.h) alongside the Wire library for communication. The RGB LEDs are controlled separately using the FastLED library, allowing precise timing and color synchronization with the servo movements. Power management is critical. The PCA9685 requires 5V from the Arduino for logic, but the servos must be powered by an external 5V supply to avoid overloading the board. The LED module also requires its own external power source, as each RGB LED can draw up to 60mA at full brightness. A simple educational electromagnetic motor powered by a battery, copper coil, and magnet. Perfect for learning the basics of electricity, magnetism, and motor mechanics. Designed as an easy beginner electronics project with a clean 3D printed base. How to Build: This simple electromagnetic motor works by using a battery, a copper wire coil, and a permanent magnet to create rotational movement. First, bend two paper clips so they can hold the coil while still allowing it to spin freely. Attach the paper clips to the battery or the 3D-printed holder using electrical tape, making sure they are stable and properly aligned. Next, create a coil by winding insulated copper wire into a circular shape with around 6–10 turns, leaving two wire ends sticking out on each side. Carefully remove the insulation from the wire ends: only strip the insolation from one site this is impotent if done on both it wont function. This allows the electric current to switch on and off during rotation, which keeps the motor spinning. Place the coil into the paper clip supports so it can rotate with minimal friction. Then position a permanent magnet directly underneath the coil. Once the battery is connected, give the coil a small push with your finger. The magnetic field generated by the current inside the coil interacts with the permanent magnet, causing the coil to continuously rotate and creating a simple electric motor. Sacapuntas señuelo para exámenes: “No apoyamos las malas practicas que deriven de este modelo, es simplemente la aportación de un modelo 3d, recuerden estudiar para sus exámenes.” -Autor- Este proyecto es prácticamente un bloc de notas encubierto para situaciones educativas complicadas o simplemente para pasarse notas en clase o como notas secretas entre amigos. Se imprime en una placa y es muy fácil de ensamblar: -Primero pega una tira larga de papel con una fina capa de pegamento en los rodillos. -Espera unos momentos a que seque el pegamento. -Enrolla la tira de papel en uno de los dos rodillos alineando la orientación de las notas al orificio rectangular por donde se verán. -Inserta los rodillos primero en la parte trasera del soporte para los mismos y después al orificio donde insertaras el lápiz. -Coloca la base de los rodillos en la carcasa principal: Gira un poco el modelo para que entre en el canal para mejor agarre. -Inserta la tapa inferior para el orificio de vista. Como operar: -Desliza la tapa del orificio del visor -Inserta un lapiz en el orificio del rodillo en donde esta enrollada la hoja y girala en sentido al segundo rodillo de manera que desenrolle un poco tira de papel. -Posteriormente inserta el lapiz en el segundo rodillo y gira para ver el contenido de la tira de papel. Notas: -La primera vez inserta los rodillos en el mecanismo sin tira de papel y gíralos para que el mecanismo se sienta mas fluido al usar. -Si lo requiere lima las pestañas si no las requieres tan ajustadas.

description: Descubriendo a Pitágoras – Demostración práctica interactiva ¿Cómo demostrar visualmente que la suma de los cuadrados de los catetos es igual al cuadrado de la hipotenusa? Las piezas almacenadas en los dos cuadrados de los catetos pueden extraerse y reorganizarse para rellenar completamente el cuadrado de la hipotenusa, demostrando físicamente la relación: h² = c² + c² El conjunto se guarda en una práctica caja circular con tapa de rosca, ideal para el aula, actividades educativas, aprendizaje en casa o simplemente para los amantes de las matemáticas y los objetos didácticos impresos en 3D. 1. Description du modèle Conçu par le maker français Mojoptix en 2015, ce cadran solaire est une véritable prouesse de géométrie mathématique. Le concept : Sans aucune pile, moteur ou électronique, il affiche l'heure sous forme de chiffres numériques lumineux directement projetés au centre de son ombre. L'intérieur de la pièce maîtresse (le gnomon) ressemble à un "gruyère" complexe calculé pour ne laisser passer les rayons du soleil qu'à des angles et des moments très précis. Plage horaire : Il affiche l'heure de 10:00 à 16:00 , avec une mise à jour toutes les 20 minutes . Ajustement : Il est possible de faire pivoter le gnomon pour ajuster l'heure avec précision et gérer facilement le passage à l'heure d'été ou d'hiver. 2. Ce qu'il faut imprimer et acheter 🛒 Matériel non imprimé à prévoir : 1 pot de confiture vide (il sert de base stable et de réceptacle). 3 vis M6 (tête plate, longueur = 20 mm). 1 vis M6 (tête plate, longueur = 50 mm). 4 écrous M6. 4 rondelles M6 (diamètre extérieur inférieur à 14 mm). 🖨️ Conseils d'impression importants : Le matériau : Utilisez impérativement de l' ABS ou de l' ASA . Le PLA va se déformer rapidement sous la chaleur du soleil et est sensible aux UV à long terme. La pièce magique (Gnomon) : N'imprimez que le fichier correspondant à votre hémisphère : Gnomon_Northen (Hémisphère Nord) ou Gnomon_Southern (Hémisphère Sud). Résolution : Imprimez le Gnomon avec une hauteur de couche fine de 0.1 mm ou moins . Si les couches sont trop épaisses, la lumière passera mal et les chiffres ne s'afficheront pas correctement. Les autres pièces de structure peuvent être imprimées plus grossièrement. 3. Tutoriel de montage et d'assemblage Étape 1 : Nettoyage des pièces Après l'impression, prenez la pièce appelée "bottom part" (le couvercle qui se visse sur le pot de confiture). À l'intérieur, cassez les deux très minces demi-cylindres imprimés : il s'agit d'un support sacrificiel conçu pour être retiré. Étape 2 : Assemblage de la base de fixation Prenez le couvercle imprimé (bottom part). Utilisez les 3 vis M6 de 20 mm , les rondelles et les écrous pour venir fixer les bras de support sur le couvercle. Vissez fermement le couvercle sur votre pot de confiture (vous pouvez remplir le pot de sable ou de cailloux pour le lester afin qu'il ne s'envole pas au moindre coup de vent). Étape 3 : Fixation du Gnomon (Le bloc horaire) Prenez la grande vis M6 de 50 mm . Glissez-la à travers l'axe du gnomon et connectez-la au support supérieur fixé sur le pot. Ajoutez une rondelle et l'écrou M6 restant. Ne serrez pas l'écrou au maximum immédiatement, car vous aurez besoin de faire pivoter la pièce pour les réglages. 4. Comment le régler pour qu'il affiche la bonne heure ? 🧭 Pour que la magie opère, le cadran solaire doit être correctement incliné et orienté. 1. L'orientation (Le Nord) Placez votre cadran solaire à un endroit très ensoleillé. Le gnomon (le tube principal) doit être parfaitement aligné sur l'axe Nord-Sud . La partie haute du tube doit pointer vers le Nord géographique (si vous êtes dans l'hémisphère nord). 2. L'inclinaison (La Latitude) L'angle entre le sol et le gnomon dépend de votre position géographique (votre latitude). Le concepteur recommande d'ajuster l'angle selon la saison pour obtenir les chiffres les plus lumineux possibles : Au printemps et en été : Inclinez l'objet à un angle égal à : Votre Latitude - 10°. En automne et en hiver : Inclinez l'objet à un angle égal à : Votre Latitude + 10°. (Exemple : Si vous êtes à Paris, la latitude est d'environ 49°. En été, vous réglerez l'inclinaison à 39°). 3. La synchronisation Regardez votre montre (assurez-vous qu'il soit entre 10h et 16h). Faites doucement pivoter le gnomon sur lui-même autour de son axe jusqu'à ce que le chiffre lumineux projeté dans l'ombre corresponde exactement à l'heure actuelle. Une fois l'heure calée, serrez l'écrou pour bloquer la position.

description: This Boxer Air Engine is a modular flat-four style pneumatic engine inspired by the classic boxer layout, where opposing pistons move in opposite directions for smooth, balanced motion. The full assembly is built from 4 separate single-cylinder air engines, and each one can run on its own. This lets you print, build, and test each cylinder module individually before installing them in the shared frame and combining them into the complete boxer engine. Each single-cylinder module is based on my previous single-cylinder engine concept, but with an updated crankshaft design: - Square front shaft - Square rear socket (hole) These features allow the crankshafts to connect end-to-end so all four cylinders can be phased correctly in the final boxer setup. --------------------- I printed mine on a Bambu Lab A1 mini using PLA. I used a little baby oil for lubrication. Some sanding or light filing is to be expected, but usually not very much. All moving parts must move very easily for the engines to work correctly. This engine can run from a balloon, an air duster, or an air compressor. ------------------------------- - Mark each crankshaft and flywheel with a marker before final assembly. - Align timing so Cylinders 1 and 2 are on their power strokes at the same time. - Align Cylinders 3 and 4 the same way with each other, but opposite phase to Cylinders 1 and 2. This staged approach makes troubleshooting easier and helps ensure a smooth-running final engine. ----------------- - Modular design: 4 independent single-cylinder engines combine into one boxer engine. - Each cylinder can be tested individually before full assembly. - Interlocking square crankshaft ends simplify mechanical coupling. - Correct phase alignment is critical for balanced boxer operation. - Marking parts helps maintain timing during final build.

description: LLAVERO DE APOYO PARA APRENDER INGLÉS Tarde o temprano llega el momento en que los más pequeños empiezan a estudiar inglés y necesitan memorizar vocabulario, estructuras básicas y expresiones frecuentes. Coco lives in the ancient canals of Zoora, where he spends hours almost motionless, eyes wide open and snout just touching the water. He likes to stay so still that he can feel even the tiniest vibration, because he says that water, too, remembers. One afternoon, he saw several bubbles rise in a strange order: three in a row, a pause… and a final, slower one. Coco followed that same rhythm, and the water trembled for a moment. Then, beneath the surface, a very thin blue line appeared, crossing the canal. Coco understood something important: the rhythm that stirred the stones also made the water respond. Thus, part of the mystery was solved. The ancient path doesn't change shape as it passes beneath Zoora: it maintains the same pulse, whether it crosses the earth, the roots, or the canals. Since then, Coco knows that not all answers are found by moving around more… sometimes they appear when one learns to be still and listen. Moral: Sometimes, when you learn to listen calmly, you discover that many answers were already there.

Mahi mahi are one of the most abundant gamefish in the ocean. Their numbers and great tasting meat makes them a top target for anglers. They are distinguished by their large foreheads (in males only), vibrant blue, green, and yellow colors, and their body-length dorsal fins. Females can spawn 2-3 times a year laying 80,000-1,000,000 eggs during each spawn! This incredibly fast reproduction rate has allowed them to spread globally, inhabiting temperate and tropical latitudes around the globe. They swim fast too, up to 57 mph (92 km/h). Anglers typically look for floating clumps of sargasso weed or frigate birds near reefs to find the fish and then use a variety of baits and lures to catch them. I've never caught one of these fish but its very high on my wishlist. As for the model, it uses interlocking scale units to achieve a swimming motion. The model is printed in halves that are aligned with the registration pin and glued together. The standard model uses 5 colors and requires 2 AMS units, but I've provided a modified print profile where the pupil is navy instead of black, lowering the number of colors to 4 so the model can be printed with just 1 AMS. This is my first saltwater fish model and I hope you enjoy it! Happy printing (and fishing)!

Section Lore Name The Bellworn Undertaker Role in the Ruined City Boss miniature, gravekeeper, executioner, and unwilling guardian of the dead Origin When the Breach opened, the dead of the city did not remain buried. Corpses whispered beneath the stones, graves split open, and the fallen began to return as twisted echoes of themselves. The Bargain In desperation, the last remaining wardens chained a cathedral bell to a condemned executioner and sealed his face beneath a funeral mask. He was sent into the ruins to collect what the living could no longer face. What He Does With every toll of the bell on his back, restless spirits are drawn toward him. With every step, he drags the dead closer to the Breach, where their echoes can be silenced. What People Say Some claim he was once a humble gravekeeper. Others believe he was the first man to look into the Breach and survive. Current Legend Now he wanders the ruined city as The Bellworn Undertaker , collecting skulls, names, and unfinished sins. He does not speak. He does not sleep. He only follows the whispers beneath the stones. Warning Where his bell rings, scavengers flee. Where his axe falls, the Breach grows quiet — but only for a moment. Printing & Support Removal Notes This model is intended as a dark fantasy boss miniature and contains many small atmospheric details, including chains, skulls, a large weapon, and the bell structure on the back. For the 8 cm boss-scale version , support removal is manageable, but requires care. The chains on the back may break if supports are removed too aggressively, and the hanging heads/skulls should be handled gently. The supports underneath the bell are very difficult to remove cleanly at this size; they can be left in place if needed, as they are mostly hidden and do not strongly affect the overall look. For larger prints around 12 cm , support removal becomes much easier. The chains, skulls, bell frame, and weapon details have more room to separate from the supports, making cleanup smoother and safer. I recommend printing this model in PLA Matte , as supports tend to come off more easily compared with standard PLA, and the matte surface works very well for grim dark-fantasy miniatures. Before printing, make sure to clean your build plate and tune your filament settings for your own filament to get the best possible result. Proper bed adhesion, calibrated temperature, and support settings will make a big difference for this model.

Flitzy vive en los Prados de Bruma, donde le gusta posarse sobre las flores más pequeñas y mover las alas muy despacio. Dice que no todo lo importante hace ruido; algunas cosas solo cambian el aire. Una tarde encontró una flor cerrada que no se abría con el sol ni con la lluvia. Flitzy no intentó forzarla. Solo batió las alas con suavidad a su alrededor. Entonces el polen salió flotando y dibujó por un instante una línea azul sobre la hierba. No era un camino nuevo: era una parte del camino antiguo que ya estaba allí, pero que solo aparecía cuando algo se movía con delicadeza. Así Flitzy entendió una pequeña parte del misterio: Zoora no siempre responde a la fuerza, al ritmo o a la velocidad. A veces responde a los gestos más suaves. Desde entonces, Flitzy vuela con cuidado, sabiendo que incluso unas alas pequeñas pueden despertar algo grande. Moraleja: A veces, un gesto suave puede conseguir más que empujar con fuerza.

Nutty vive en el Bosque Hueco, donde guarda semillas y bellotas en escondites tan bien pensados que nunca suele olvidar ninguno. Le gusta tenerlo todo en orden, porque dice que cuando algo cambia de sitio… es porque quiere decir algo. Durante varios días, una de sus bellotas aparecía siempre fuera del escondite. Nutty pensó que alguien se la movía, pero una mañana decidió esperar en silencio para verlo con sus propios ojos. Entonces descubrió algo sorprendente: una raíz azul muy fina asomó bajo la tierra y empujó la bellota suavemente hasta dejarla junto a otras tres, formando una pequeña fila. Así entendió una parte del misterio: las raíces azules no solo marcaban por dónde pasaba el camino antiguo… también movían pequeñas cosas para señalar que ese camino estaba despertando. Desde entonces, Nutty ya no se enfada cuando algo aparece fuera de lugar. Ahora sabe que, a veces, incluso el desorden puede ser una pista. Moraleja: A veces, lo que parece un error puede ser justo la señal que necesitabas.

Al caer la tarde seguía allí, y justo entonces vio algo que otros no habían notado: a distintas horas del día, la luz iba marcando pequeñas líneas en la corteza, una tras otra, hasta formar la misma curva del camino antiguo. Así entendió una pequeña parte del misterio. Algunas pistas de Zoora no están escondidas por el lugar, sino por el momento: solo aparecen completas cuando se les da el tiempo que necesitan. Desde entonces, Dozy ya no siente que vaya tarde. Ahora sabe que avanzar despacio también puede ayudarte a ver lo que otros pasan por alto. Moraleja: No todo llega tarde por ir lento; a veces ir despacio es justo lo que te permite entenderlo.

When something unnatural occurs, there are always those who try to harness the power. This arcane portal tries to convert and tame the power of the breach by channeling its power in the crystal. Barily holding it together with a magical barrier, inscribed with a language few understand and magical chains anchored tightly to three ancient pillars. Marked with Trinity Knots for binding power. This arcane portal is designed with geometric shapes as inspiration. Starting with three pillars, marked with trinity knots, the symbol of unity and binding, it holds a central floating crystal above a portal/light. With variable toppers, where you can switch out the top of the pillars or even the pillars entirely, this arcane portal can be used in multiple sessions. For example: Crystal floating chained to 3 pillars 3 pillars with normal top 3 pillars with crystal tops 3 crystal clusters normal bases, as a stepping stone. With the rotating arrow center, you can incorporate a puzzle aspect where your party needs to rotate it a certain way, unlocking the magical powers of the pillars, to help the party channel the arcane energy from the portal. With the LED light in the middle, you can simply press your remote to change the color of the center portal to fit your story. Don't have the LED light (yet)? no worries, I also included a print profile where you can 3D print your portal center. The design is available in 1 giant disc (25 cm diameter) or cut up into 4 pieces using plugs to connect them. I've also added the design without plugs, incase you don't want to use the pillars at all. The entire design barely has supports and is assembled very very easily. Assembly Connect the 4 sides of the circle by using the plugs. It is made in a way that you cannot put the wrong ones together. Either side has either 2 or 3 connectors that are round or a hexagon.
