🎸 NaNaNa Na… hier kommt der Hard Rock Brummbär! 🤘 Der Hard Rock Brummbär ist meine kleine Hommage an eine der größten Rockbands aller Zeiten – und natürlich an alle, die den Rock'n'Roll im Herzen tragen. Denn eines ist sicher: Dieser Bär ist definitiv nicht auf dem Highway to Hell , sondern auf dem Highway to Druckspaß unterwegs! Es handelt sich um ein Update meines bereits bekannten AMS-Modells – mit einigen Verbesserungen und jetzt auch als NoAMS-Version . Also kein Highway to Müll , sondern Rock or Print! Das Modell ist 140 mm hoch und sollte sich problemlos skalieren lassen – natürlich wie immer ohne Garantie. Gedruckt wurde mit einer Schichthöhe von 0,16 mm und einer 0,4-mm-Düse . Zum Einsatz kam BambuLab-Filament. Für den Zusammenbau braucht ihr lediglich etwas Kleber und ein klein wenig Druck – nicht den von der Bandprobe, sondern den auf die Bauteile. 😄 Je nach Drucker und Filament kann die Passgenauigkeit leicht variieren. Also keine Panik, wenn hier und da ein bisschen nachgearbeitet werden muss – das gehört manchmal einfach zum Rock'n'Roll. Bei den Farben könnt ihr euch komplett austoben: Ob klassisch in Schwarz, düster im Gothic-Look oder als knalliger Regenbogenbär – erlaubt ist, was gefällt! In der 3MF-Datei ist selbstverständlich auch wieder Fuzzy Skin enthalten. Wie gewohnt gibt es: ein Profil nach Objekt (2 Druckplatten), ein Profil nach Ebene (mehrere Druckplatten) sowie ein zusätzliches Profil für die Kappe mit AC/DC-Schriftzug .( ansonsten ist die Kappe schwarz ) Dafür wird allerdings ein AMS benötigt. Der Support lässt sich problemlos entfernen. Lediglich unter der Kappe solltet ihr darauf achten, alle Reste sauber zu entfernen. Für alle Multitool-Drucker oder H2C-Besitzer: Ihr könnt auch PETG als Supportmaterial verwenden. Eine genaue Anleitung gibt es von mir dafür nicht – ein bisschen Eigeninitiative hat schließlich noch niemandem geschadet. 😉 Zum Schluss noch eine kleine Info in eigener Sache: Mit diesem Modell verabschiede ich mich erst einmal in die Sommerpause . Zeit, die Akkus wieder aufzuladen, neue Ideen zu sammeln und den kreativen Verstärker etwas abkühlen zu lassen. Ab Mitte bis Ende August geht es dann wieder mit neuen Modellen weiter. Ich wünsche euch schon jetzt einen fantastischen Sommer, einen erholsamen Urlaub und natürlich viele erfolgreiche Drucke. Wenn euch meine Arbeit gefällt, freue ich mich wie immer riesig über ein Like , einen Boost oder ein nettes Feedback . Ihr seid einfach spitze! Keep on rockin' – und lasst die Drucker glühen! 🤘 Ganz liebe Grüße Euer Lemmy3Dprint

The existing abundance of crystals and emeralds remains, but new ones form at a normal rate. Customizing Dragons FTD p33 You can customize any dragon's stat block to reflect the dragon's unique character. Minor changes such as those below are easy to make and have no impact on a dragon's challenge rating. Languages. Most dragons prefer to speak Draconic but learn Common for dealing with allies and minions. But given their high Intelligence and long life span, dragons can easily learn additional languages. You can add languages to a dragon's stat block. Skills. Most dragons are proficient in the Perception and Stealth skills, and many dragons have additional skill proficiencies. As with languages, you can customize a dragon's skill list (even doubling their proficiency bonus with certain skills) to reflect particular interests and activities. You can also give a dragon tool proficiencies, particularly if the dragon spends time in Humanoid form. Other Traits and Actions. Its statistics and capabilities are otherwise replaced by those of the new form, except any class features or legendary actions of that form. Flyby. The dragon is an agile flier, quick to fly out of enemies' reach.The dragon doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach. Mimicry. Impersonating characters or their allies could be a fun trick for a crafty dragon.The dragon can mimic any sounds it has heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 17 Wisdom (Insight) check. Rejuvenation. You might decide that dragons in your campaign, being an essential part of the Material Plane, are nearly impossible to destroy. A dragon's life essence might be preserved in the egg from which it first emerged, in its hoard, or in a cavernous hall at the center of the world, just as a lich's essence is hidden in a phylactery.If it has an essence-preserving object, a destroyed dragon gains a new body in 1d10 days, regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. The new body appears within 5 feet of the object. Special Senses. Most dragons have blindsight and darkvision. You might upgrade blindsight to truesight, or you could give a dragon with a burrowing speed tremorsense. Tunneler. description: Inspired by the works of Emerson Tung's Tankhead, a alternate world history where the instead of tracked tanks, the battlefield is now traversed by heavy walking tank mechs. Remix was done by using multiple chassis and arranging them to allow three turrets, modifying the original fuel tanks to represent to massive amount of energy needed for such a machine. Tracks were removed and I added walker legs and ball joints to be able to move the legs.

A miniature customizable Victorian stairway (45 degrees). This can fit any length, left or right. It includes four different brackets for the side decoration. You choose which of these you like. This model includes all the pieces for both a stairway and a railing - and a horizontal railing. The pieces are organized on plates. First plate : Victorian stairway parts including large rounded bottom step, a newel post, side brackets, baluster, railing, decorative panel, and top post. Second plate : Victorian railing parts including two different posts, a baluster, railing, and decorative panel. Third Plate : stringer, tread, and large, rounded bottom step. If you have no stairway at all, start with the stringer and clone the number treads you need. The stringer is in two pieces. The larger one is approximately 8 inches including the large rounded bottom step. If you need 10 inches, also print the small stringer part. For other heights, just cut stringer parts as needed. If you want a stairway railing, print parts from plate 1. The railing is cut at 45 degrees on each end. You will need to re-cut one end to your desired length. Right now, it is oriented top down on the plate, as the top is the widest part. You will want either a baluster or a panel for each step. Also choose which of the decorative side brackets you want (see photos). If you want a horizontal railing, use parts from plate 2 with the railing cut at 90 degrees on each end. You will need to re-cut one end to your desired length. Also, you might be interested to know the balusters and the railing posts are based on some of Michelangelo's drawings. DIORAMA DE LA PELÍCULA OFICIAL DE BACKROOMS - Kane Parsons (Kane pixels) Diorama basado en la nueva gran película de este 2026, Backrooms , del director Kane Parsons. Hecha completamente de PLA y encastrable con todas sus partes. ATENCIÓN , puede llegar a requerir zonas con pegamento para lograr mejor sostenibilidad o aspecto. El diorama cuenta con modificaciones de aspecto post-impresión para lograr mejores acabados realistas, entre los materiales se cuenta con tiras led genéricas , interruptores , hojas autoadhesivas y cristales . Los Backrooms son una famosa leyenda urbana de internet y un fenómeno de creepypasta que describe un entramado infinito de dimensiones alternas compuestas por pasillos de oficinas vacíos, caracterizados por paredes con papel tapiz amarillento, alfombras húmedas y el constante zumbido de luces fluorescentes. Este concepto se originó específicamente el 12 de mayo de 2019 en el foro de internet 4chan , cuando un usuario anónimo publicó una fotografía de una habitación amarilla de aspecto inquietante en un hilo sobre "imágenes malditas". La inquietud visual que genera este espacio se asocia directamente con el concepto de espacios liminales , lugares de transición que al estar completamente desiertos provocan una profunda sensación de desolación, extrañeza y nostalgia. A partir de esa publicación inicial, la comunidad expandió el universo creando diferentes "niveles", entidades hostiles que habitan las sombras y complejas reglas de supervivencia para quienes "salen de la realidad" por accidente. Su popularidad se disparó a nivel global gracias a los videojuegos independientes y, sobre todo, a la viralización de cortometrajes de terror analógico en YouTube, consolidándolo como uno de los mitos de terror digital más influyentes de los últimos tiempos. Puedes apoyarme generando visión de este modelo anteriormente publicado en Reddit (maximusss999, u/Gloomy-Adeptness5647) , y en mi cuenta de Instagram donde estaré publicando mis modelos más recientes de MakerWorld. Una mención en Instagram a Mike ( @ mike_horror_arts ) por colaborar en el armado y procesado de esta figura para hacerla realidad, allí puedes ver el video completo del proceso y distribución con una gran cadena de cines del país.

model_name: Rocky - 1/6 Scale with Better Joints for Play
tags: project hail mary|Rocky|toys|articulated|poseable|rocky the eridian|one sixth scale
description: This is a remix of the officially released model of Rocky from Project Hail Mary. I wasn’t happy with the stability or range of motion of the articulated figure’s joints — my kids think Rocky is really cute, and they wanted something they could actually play with. This is my attempt to make that work. This version of Rocky can balance on any three legs and can hold a variety of poses. As I was working on this, I also noticed that the official model’s shoulder joints were lower than that of the actual puppet used in the film, and one arm was attached at the wrong angle. I’ve attempted to fix those issues too. The joints are all snap-in ball-and-socket joints. I reversed the direction of the shoulder joints so that the sockets are in the torso rather than in the arms. The elbow joints are all ball-and-socket variations too, because even though they only need to rotate in one direction, that seemed more secure. I am sure this isn’t perfect (I have not worked with articulated figures before) but it’s a definite improvement over the original. This version is scaled up to 1/6 scale (matches many dolls and action figures). I haven’t tested the joints at any other scale. TO ASSEMBLE: The pieces aren’t labeled (I didn’t like having visible numbers on the figure) so I’ve included the original assembly diagram for reference. Snapping the joints together can be tricky. Use an even, firm pressure, and if it seems necessary, apply heat to the socket side of the joint (I used a little bit of boiling water). I found this to be necessary with some brands of filament but not with others. Notes: You should trim or file down any uneven places on the ball joints, such as where the supports were connected, so they’re as close to a perfect sphere as possible. This will help keep the joints from wearing out. While you can (carefully) take apart the joints after putting them together, they’ll get loose if you do this repeatedly, so I recommend against it. It would be easier to paint Rocky before putting them together, but if you do, you’ll want to be extra careful with the assembly so that your hard work doesn’t go to waste (I did snap a couple of joints when assembling test prints). There are two options (open hand and fist) for the first leg, but once assembled they’re not really interchangeable, so just pick which one you want at the start. I’ve had much better luck avoiding print failures if I print the pieces one at a time. The first print profile has them all one plate, but I’ve also provided a second profile with the pieces separated out to print individually. I’ve only tested this with PLA. I don’t know if other types of material will have the same give necessary to snap the joints together.

The Pacific Halibut ( Hippoglossus stenolepis) is one weird looking fish. It's completely flat, it's 2 eyes are on the same side of it's head, and it's underside is completely white despite it's top side being a dark olive or brown color. Believe it or not each of these strange adaptations help this fish become an apex predator. Their flat shapes and eye placement allow them to hug the ocean floor and look for prey. Their color scheme (known as countershading) makes it easy for them to hide from predators and prey. If viewed from below their white bellies blend in with the light from above and if viewed from above they blend in with the sand and sediment of the ocean floor. While countershading is common in nature, halibut take it to the extreme with completely blank white undersides. They live in the cold (3-8C) waters of the North Pacific at depths of 180-450 ft. During the spawning season the fish dive to depths of 600 ft and females lay 500,000-4,000,000 eggs per year. The eggs hatch after 15 days and the fry circulate with current for hundreds of miles. Halibut are a prized species for sport fisherman in Alaska due to their high quality meat and massive size. While most anglers catch fish weighing 20 lbs or less, 150 lb fish are not uncommon. The state record specimen weighed a staggering 459 lbs and a replica hangs in the Anchorage airport. For thousands of years, native Alaskans used special hand-carved V-shaped hooks when fishing for halibut, designed to catch medium sized fish, but spare larger ones. This was because they wanted to spare the spawning females to protect the species, but also because hooking a monster without modern watercraft or gear could be a life-threatening experience. Today, to catch these fish, rods are secured to the side of the boat and outfitted with a 5lb lead weight, a hook, and bait. The weight pulls the bait all the way down and then bounces along the bottom with the motion of the waves. When a fish bites, the fisherman then has to retrieve the weight and the fish up through hundreds of feet of water, a few inches at a time. I've been fortunate enough to fish for halibut twice and its a ton of fun, even catching the small ones. This model uses interlocking scale units that allow the model to “swim” just like my other articulated fish models. This model prints in one piece and doesn't need any glue or a registration pin. It also uses only 4 colors and fits on an A1-mini. I printed one in brown and dark green, but if you have a dark olive colored filament, that would be the best match. Happy printing (and fishing)!

description: Welcome to Hoth, where the weather is terrible, the Empire has arrived, and everyone is suddenly very interested in evacuating. This Mini Hoth moving diorama is my snowy follow-up to my Mini Tatooine tile, designed for BamBam Design’s Mini Train system. Instead of sand, twin suns, and suspicious Jawa activity, this one brings Echo Base, snowspeeders, walkers, turrets, and a small but very dramatic Imperial problem to your layout. The scene features Echo Base with the ion cannon, an AT-ST standing guard near the base doors, a fallen AT-AT in the centre of the battlefield, and GR-75 Rebel transports being escorted away by two X-wings. Around the battlefield, T-47 Snowspeeders race across the frozen surface of Hoth, with Imperial INT-4s in pursuit, inspired by their appearance in The Mandalorian and Grogu . The wheel has 13 magnet slots, so you can keep it simple with just a couple of craft or fill the whole thing with a tiny high-speed chase through the snow. Add as many or as few Snowspeeders and INT-4s as you like, depending on whether you want a small patrol or full frozen chaos. I’ve included a few different versions of the small craft to make printing a bit easier. The T-47 Snowspeeders come in both 3-colour and 4-colour versions, and the Imperial INT-4 comes in both 2-colour and 3-colour versions. I’ve also included an alternate AT-ST with solid legs, just in case the standard tiny chicken legs decide they don’t want to cooperate with your printer. This design uses the same 4mm x 2mm magnets as the rest of the Mini Train dioramas for compatibility with the existing system. This design is an authorized remix based on the Mini Train Collection by BamBam Design: https://linktr.ee/bambamdesign It is fully compatible with other tiles in the Mini Train series. Assembly Assembly is quite straightforward—just follow the photos for the correct placement of each part. Start by gluing the base and terrain sections together. They align using two small locating pins, while the fallen AT-AT and ion cannon also help position everything correctly. Once the base is assembled, glue the remaining scenery pieces into place. The two X-wings are glued directly to the GR-75 Medium Transport, which is then mounted using a short offcut of 1.75mm filament. Glue the 4mm × 2mm magnets into the Snowspeeders, INT-4s, and the magnet pins. Take your time and make sure all the magnet polarities are correct before gluing. To install the rotating wheel, place the Snowspeeders and INT-4s into the track first. Position the magnet pins underneath them, spacing them to match the slots in the wheel. Once everything is aligned, simply push the wheel onto the axle in the base. The first few times you turn the wheel, the magnets may feel a little sticky as they settle in. After a few rotations, everything will move much more freely and smoothly.

He has a friend playing this Left handed model of the Fender Jazz Bass. I also made a Right handed equivalent of this bass guitar. There should be two profiles posted. I only printed the left handed model. The right handed model is an exact copy of the lefts profile, so it should come out with the same results. This model also has a first for any of my models. For any guitar model normally I use 0.25mm fishing line, because to scale the strings are very small. However, for the bass guitar since the strings are so much bigger. I decided to use the 3D printer to make strings. I think the result turned out quite nicely. In order to make them fit in the pegs slot. I used a hobby knife to carefully enlarge the slot by slicing away material within the slotted area. I do take requests for guitar models. It does often take me a while to get around to finish them. This one I think he will be pleased with the end result. Now he can print his buddy a miniature replica.

These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible. Across all my collections, I focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, and fine details. Where possible, I also try to capture their natural movement or pose, so each model feels as close to real life as possible. Some models include articulated parts (hinge / flexi) that replicate natural motion and flexibility. Other models are non-articulated and focus more on lifelike appearance and detail. In some cases, parts such as legs can be carefully adjusted using heat to achieve a more natural pose. If you do this, always apply heat gently and gradually, as excessive heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized to achieve the best balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling them down can cause issues – moving parts may fuse, small hinges may not work correctly, or fine details might not print properly. Safety notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing models too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a risk of choking. If you adjust parts using heat, always proceed carefully. I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print – it really motivates me to keep creating. Commercial licenses are also available through MakerWorld Membership. You can also find my YouTube channel there, where I share ASMR videos of support removal and other 3D printing content. When the fracture split the sky, the city didn't just break—it began to think in a twisted, horrific language. The alleyway containing the private archive of Brother Kaelen’s monastery was crowded with fleeing scholars, acolytes, and panicked citizens when the first wave of thick, purple fog rolled through. Instead of suffocating them, the volatile magical energy fused their physical bodies, their desperate panic, and their final, wide-eyed moments of terror directly into the stone walls they were trying to escape. Over weeks of continuous exposure to the Breach, this mass of flesh didn't die; it reorganized. The masonry and the meat became one. The stone pillars sprouted rooting tendrils, and the collective panic of a hundred dying souls manifested as a cluster of weeping, blinking eyes that scan the fog. It can no longer move, but it has become an apex predator of the ruins, luring in unsuspecting scavengers and adding their mass to its ever-growing form.

description: Astraea, The Last Witness Category Elite Boss • Eternal Guardian • The Breach Collection Description Astraea, The Last Witness, is one of the oldest surviving beings ever touched by The Breach. Neither fully mortal nor entirely stone, she exists as an eternal observer of realities long since consumed, her vigil spanning forgotten ages and broken worlds. This highly detailed miniature depicts Astraea in a moment of solemn watchfulness, crouched upon ancient ruins as though suspended between motion and stillness. Her weathered wings fold protectively around her form while countless fractures spread across her stone-like skin, revealing the lingering scars left by centuries spent in the presence of impossible forces. Her elegant ram-like horns, crouched gargoyle posture, and hauntingly human expression create a striking silhouette that immediately commands attention on the tabletop. When the first fractures appeared, civilizations believed they were witnessing isolated disasters. They were wrong. The fractures were only the beginning of a catastrophe that would become known as The Breach . As worlds collapsed and timelines intertwined, a single entity emerged from the growing wound between realities. The Worldbinder. Some believe she created The Breach. Others believe she is the only force preventing its complete collapse. No one truly knows. What is known is that Astraea witnessed the moment everything changed. She watched entire worlds disappear. She watched memories unravel. She watched history itself rewritten. And while countless guardians abandoned their posts, Astraea remained. The unimaginable energies released during that moment transformed her forever. Her flesh hardened into living stone. Her wings became monuments to an age already forgotten. Time itself ceased to hold power over her. Unable to age. Unable to die. Unable to forget. Now Astraea silently watches the forgotten places where realities overlap and the veil between worlds grows dangerously thin. Some believe she protects ancient secrets powerful enough to erase civilizations. Others whisper that she serves the Worldbinder herself. The truth has been lost to history. Only one certainty remains. Where Astraea keeps watch, reality has already begun to fracture. I've gotten some lovely feedback and compliments on the armchair model, which really helped me stay motivated through the creation and testing process for this one. I hope you enjoy this project if you decide to give it a try, and I look forward to seeing your creations! Let me know if you have any struggles and I will try to help (I check in here a couple times a week most of the time). What to gather up once you've printed the files: Tools: Sharp scissors, craft knife, tweezers (Optional: pinking shears, applique or nail scissors with a curved blade) Glues: glue stick, preferred structural/assembly glue, preferred fabric/craft glue Textile materials: something for batting (i prefer cotton), something for upholstery material (still prefer cotton) Other handy stuff if you have it already: A piece of photo paper to put under templates while gluesticking them, rubber brayer to smooth fabric on templates, Fray Check. More detailed remarks on materials: Quilting cotton or muslin in a small print. I recommend this for beginners particularly as it's much easier to glue than synthetics, both for sticking purposes, and for not making the fabric look stupid and jacked up. You don't need a lot of fabric. I didn't even have an eighth yard left of that pink flowered fabric I used. Batting/padding. I use Warm & Natural cotton batting usually, and it's my favorite since it's easy to shape and kind of smoosh into position even if it's not perfect at first. I've also upholstered with synthetic felt or fleece, or even untextured paper towels for very small scale work. If you don't mind doing more layers, you'll be fine using a thinner batting. You could also make the cushions less dramatically stuffed. Probably the most important thing is choosing a batting material you like working with, that won't look lumpy or show through the fabric in a way you don't like. Glue. For this project I used an Elmers Craft Bond extra strength glue stick, Gorilla brand wood glue, because it sets up pretty quick and sticks to PLA better than you'd expect, and Bearly Art craft glue. Bearly Art is a bit pricey in my opinion, so I don't necessarily love to recommend it to others. Suggested alternate adhesives: Most of the Aleene's product line. Beacon FabriTac. The main things you want to accomplish adhesive-wise are listed below by use case: For the thin plastic panels use a glue stick to attach the fabric, because it's an easy way to get good enough coverage to keep the fabric from wrinkling. Suggestions: most glue sticks are probably fine. For structural gluing of PLA panels to PLA, or for gluing raw fabric edges to PLA where it'll be covered later , use something that grabs well and cures firm. Suggestions: most of the Aleene's product line but especially turbo tacky. Beacon FabriTac. Gorilla wood glue. For gluing fabric to fabric , use something that won't dry stiff in a place you want the fabric to look plush or flat. Wood glue will dry hard and you want a more flexible hold. It's smart to test the glue on your particular fabric to make sure it cooperates and doesn't bleed through and look awful. Suggestions: Bearly Art if you got the bucks, Beacon FabriTac, Aleene's.

description: Fake eggs (also called nest eggs, ceramic eggs, wooden eggs, or training eggs) are commonly used for a few reasons: If you dont have chickens, this is also a fun thing for your children to paint. The egg is modeled after a real egg from my chickens. You can scale it up or down if needed. Don't blame me if you try to boil these. ;) So back to why fake eggs are a good thing. They; 🥚 Encourage hens to lay in the nesting boxes Young hens that are just starting to lay often look for a suitable place by following other hens. Seeing an egg in a nest box signals that it’s a safe place to lay. 🥚 Reduce eggs being laid in random places If your chickens are hiding eggs around the garden, placing fake eggs in the nest boxes can help redirect them. 🥚 Discourage egg eating Some fake eggs are made from plastic, hard ceramic or wood. If a hen pecks at one expecting to find something yummy inside, she gets no reward and may lose interest in pecking eggs. Plastic eggs can be preferable because they can break with no reward inside. Hard eggs can cause the hen to peck another egg if it doesn't break. This doesn’t always work, but it can help. 🥚 Help with broodiness management A few fake eggs can be left under a broody hen if you want her to stay settled while waiting for fertile eggs to arrive. For a backyard flock, placing 1–2 fake eggs in each nesting box is usually enough. Chickens don’t seem to care whether the egg is real, ceramic, plastic, or wooden—as long as it looks roughly like an egg. Since the egg doesn't have any flat surfaces you might have to sand the bottom a little if you want a perfectly smooth egg shape. BUT the chickens wont care.

description: Other practical models from the Mecha Series (click the image to jump) Model Introduction: Mecha Style Storage Series 6th Release: Model 0-6 Drawer Storage Box — Infinitely Stackable, Push-to-Open, with Self-Locking Rebound Mechanism Per community requests, I created a stackable storage box for this series — but basic stackable designs are boring, and regular 3D-printed drawers have stiff, clunky operation.I took inspiration from my home's push-to-open drawers and magnetic rebound cabinet doors (my most-used, most convenient furniture) and merged both mechanisms into Model 0-6. Real furniture hardware has perfect rebound and self-locking, so I tested many methods to replicate that feel, finally landing on this 0-6 design: 1、After over 20 iterations (T﹏T) before release, Model 0-6's stability, reliability, and smooth operation are nearly on par with my home's push-to-open drawers and magnetic cabinet doors.The self-locking switch remains highly stable even when mounted vertically, supports ultra-frequent use, and has a detachable design — you can maintain and replace the consumable rubber band in just 2 minutes (standard rubber bands last 6 to 12 months).(Why rubber bands? 3D-printed springs have terrible durability, and most people don't have properly sized hardware springs on hand. Rubber bands are universally accessible, work with any size, are easy to trim to fit the model, and have decent durability. As an open-source creator, I want everyone who loves this design to be able to print and assemble it hassle-free.) 2、Stackable — a feature requested by many community members: Model 0-6 supports infinite stacking, and each layer can be opened and closed smoothly and independently while stacked. 3、 Spacious storage : Each layer has an internal dimension of 170×152×54mm, with an overall external size of 205×183×71mm.You can optionally install dividers for each layer as needed, and the inner box is removable — making it much easier to locate small items. Printing & Assembly Notes : (Please read the assembly instructions in the attachment carefully — it includes solutions for all common issues you may encounter!) Assembly supplies needed : Glue, lubricant (not mandatory but highly recommended — it will greatly improve the model's opening and closing smoothness)、 Parts required (per layer) : 4pcs 5×2mm strong magnets, 2pcs rubber bands— 3cm diameter rubber bands are recommended, or you can cut and tie any size rubber band you have on hand to fit.The rubber band MUST be tight enough to deliver sufficient tension! Stretch loose rubber bands properly! A slack rubber band will fail to push the drawer out and overcome the magnet's holding force! Printing tips : Prevent warping and layer smearing by ensuring your build plate has strong adhesion. Clean your build plate before printing (for textured build plates: scrub with a sponge + dish soap for several minutes to restore adhesion) or apply a glue stick. Box-style models have large flat bases — using a low-temperature build plate can effectively prevent base warping!⚠️ A build plate with poor adhesion may cause severe warping, which will interfere with model assembly and even render the part completely unusable! Do NOT use low-strength filaments for moving parts and bolts: this includes specialty filaments like matte, silk, transparent, and Lite variants (these are only suitable for printing casings and decorative parts). Recommended filaments : PLA Basic and PETG Basic. Default filament setup : Bambu Lab PLA Basic in Silver, Dark Gray, Light Gray, and Warm Yellow (4 colors total). Feel free to use your own custom color combinations! If you enjoy this series, please consider following me! I'll keep creating more designs, and I promise every storage model in this line will be original, practical, and packed with creative details.

description: Turn filament waste into something practical. This compression mold allows you to recycle purge lines, failed prints, supports, and filament offcuts into solid reusable coasters. Instead of throwing filament waste away, it can be reheated and compressed into a durable coaster with a completely unique appearance. Every coaster is different, creating colourful patterns from the random mix of filament scraps used during the process. Available Sizes Choose the size that best suits your needs: • 80mm Diameter – Compact size, ideal for smaller cups and saving filament. • 100mm Diameter – Larger size, perfect for mugs, glasses, and larger drinks. Both versions produce a coaster approximately 5mm thick . How It Works The mold consists of a base and compression plunger. Filament scraps are placed inside the mold and heated using a heat gun or hair dryer until the material softens. The plunger is then pressed down to compress the softened filament. Vent holes in the plunger allow trapped air to escape, helping create a denser finished coaster. When compressing the material, the lip of the plunger eventually contacts the base of the mold. This acts as a built-in stop and automatically forms a coaster of the correct thickness. The mold cavity includes a slight taper, helping the finished coaster release easily once cooled. The coaster can then be pushed out using the hole in the base. 🔧 How To Use Before use, please read the safety notes below. Safety Notes • Use in a well-ventilated area when heating or processing filament scrap • Avoid inhaling fumes from melted or heated plastics • Do not overheat filament — excessive heat may release harmful fumes • Keep away from children during heating or processing • Use appropriate tools and heat sources responsibly Collect filament purge lines, supports, failed prints, or scrap filament. Cut larger pieces into smaller sections so they pack into the mold more easily. For best results, break H2D purge waste into smaller pieces before use, as it is denser than standard purge. Fill the mold cavity with a layer of filament waste. Heat the material using a heat gun or hair dryer until it softens. Insert the plunger and compress the softened plastic. Add another layer of filament waste and repeat the heating and compression process. Continue building the coaster one layer at a time until the required thickness is reached and the plunger lip contacts the base. Allow the mold to cool completely. Push the finished coaster out through the hole in the base. You now have a unique recycled filament coaster ready to use. Print Recommendations • Material: PETG minimum recommended • Layer Height: 0.2 mm • Walls: 4 • Infill: 25% (found to be stable during testing) • Supports: Not required PLA is not recommended due to the heating involved when softening filament scraps. A small amount of oil or release agent can assist with removal, although it is generally not required thanks to the tapered mold design. description: Adjustable Phone Stand: Print-in-Place A stable, adjustable viewing angle is essential for any desk setup. Unfortunately, many 3D printed phone stands either lack these basic features or overcompensate with complex designs. I wanted to create a solution that delivers that functionality while keeping the design clean, stripped back, and highly printable. Key Features: Print-in-Place Locking Hinge: The hinge features a built-in locking function that engages when clamping pressure is applied, holding firm at your desired viewing angle. Weighted Base (Optional): The base includes internal cavities designed for metal counterweights (fits 8 x M5x20mm dowel pins). While they are not strictly necessary, the extra weight does improve stability and gives the stand a premium feel. Case-Friendly Cradle: Tested with a Pixel 8 Pro (both with and without a case). It is specifically designed with cases in mind, rounded-edge cases will sit more securely, allowing the stand to support more acute viewing angles. Assembly Guide Freeing the Hinge: The print-in-place tolerances are tight. Breaking the hinge free requires a little force so please take care and try to distribute the pressure evenly so you don't stress a small area. If it is stubborn, gently use a pry tool between the joints. Adding the Weights (Optional): Turn the base over and insert your metal dowel pins into the cylindrical cavities. Press-fit the printed caps over the holes to lock the pins safely inside. Assembling the Clamp: Bring the two halves of the threaded pin together and screw them tightly into the knob. Push this assembly through the hole in the phone cradle until it stops. Once you have set your desired angle, simply turn the knob clockwise to increase the clamping pressure and lock the hinge. Technical Printability Because this model features functioning print-in-place hinges and threads, tuning your filament tolerances will yield the smoothest results. Some of the internal walls get as close as 0.1mm, so a precision printer is required. Note: I printed mine on a Bambu Lab P1S and slowed most of the speed settings down to ensure accuracy. Layer Height: Use 0.20mm for the main body and 0.10mm for the threaded pin to ensure the threads operate smoothly. Walls & Infill: Use 3 wall loops for added structural strength and 15% infill . Material Recommendations: I highly recommend Bambu PLA-CF or PLA Matte for a clean, premium finish. Ensure you are using a well-tuned profile and dry filament to prevent the hinges from fusing. I went through a lot of prototyping fine-tuning the clearances to ensure the hinges break free cleanly while remaining strong. If you run into any issues with tolerances or fitment, please let me know in the comments!

description: Please read full description; must be comfortable with Bambu Studio re-scaling/re-sizing, and adding a negative part. The magnet hole is designed with “crush ribs” (wavy outside edge of magnet hole) to grab onto the magnet for a snug fit. In my experience the magnet hole width needs to be about .2mm larger than the magnet for PLA and about .3 larger than the magnet for PETG. Example: for 10x2mm magnets, the best size magnet hole for my printer settings was 10.20x2.05mm. Important: Print a test print. Different printers, filament, print settings (# of walls) will affect the snugness of the press-fit. Use a caliper to measure your magnets. Choose a test print depending on the orientation you plan to print your magnet holes for your model. Flat Orientation Standing/Vertical orientation - no supports needed (notice the point of the hole edge is oriented upward to allow a smooth overhang.) There is a large, medium and small version for each orientation. small is best for testing up to 10mm magnets medium is best for testing 10mm-18mm magnets large is best for testing 18-20mm magnets. Rescale the 9 magnet hole sizes in the test print so you can dial in the best snug fit. Uncheck the uniform scale check box when resizing. It may take a few tests prints. Continue adjusting the hole sizes with each test print until you have a snug fit. Use the same filament and print settings you plan to use for the model you are planning to insert the magnets into. Once you have dialed in the best size, open the MagnetOctagonNegativePart file and resize it. Then you can add this part to your model. Open your model file, In Object Settings > Add Negative Part > Load.. > Choose MagnetOctagonNegativePart file. You may need to move, rotate the part to get it where you need to in your model. description: After a lot of work, testing, and community feedback, I'm happy to share what I consider one of my most refined designs so far: the Nintendo Switch 2 Travel Case - Ultimate Edition . This new version has been redesigned deeply to be more durable, easier to assemble, and accessible to as many makers as possible. What's New in Ultimate Edition? Fully Screwless Assembly One of the biggest improvements is the complete removal of screws. The entire case now uses integrated locking tabs and slot systems, eliminating the need for additional hardware. Benefits: No screws to buy or source Faster and easier assembly No risk of overtightening screws and damaging printed parts Cleaner and more reliable construction Improved Game Cartridge Retention System The cartridge holders has been completely redesigned. The original design relied on the tension of flexible plastic tabs to keep cartridges in place. Over time, PLA can slowly deform, reducing the holding force. The new system uses two small locking tabs that mechanically retain each cartridge, ensuring secure storage even after long-term use. No more loose cartridges! Increased Structural Strength I reviewed and reinforced several attachment points throughout the design to improve overall durability and robustness. New Print-in-Place Handle Lid Following many requests from users of the XXL version, I created a new print-in-place lid with an integrated handle . This lid offers: Comfortable carrying handle No assembly required Full compatibility with the existing attachment system The only trade-off is storage capacity: Handle lid: 12 game cartridges Standard lids: 24 game cartridges Normal and XXL Versions Unified The previous Normal and XXL versions have now been merged into a single project. Print profiles are organized according to the different lid designs. Standard Profiles Include Each standard profile contains: One lid design The base A plate containing all attachment components: Switch 2 retaining bar 2 lid locking clips 2 wrist-strap holders Assembly Instructions Assembly is simple and requires no tools. 1. Install the Wrist-Strap Holders Insert one holder on each side of the case. These parts are optional and can be omitted if you don't use wrist straps. 2. Install the Switch Retaining Bar Insert the retaining bar into the dedicated slot inside the base. 3. Install the Lid Locking Clips Insert one side of the clip into its slot first, then gently slide the other side into place. Repeat for the second clip. 4. Attach the Lid to the Base The lid uses the same installation principle as the clips. Start by engaging one side, then progressively work the opposite side into the base slots. A gentle opening and closing motion during installation can help the lid slide into place more easily. XXL Profile Includes XXL base Nintendo Switch 2 support insert Print-in-place handle lid Pro Controller insert Divider insert The handle lid can be replaced by any standard lid since they all use the exact same attachment system. XXL Accessories Pro Controller Insert Designed to securely hold a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller. For even better retention, you can optionally add an elastic band. You can install up to two controller inserts inside the XXL base simultaneously. Divider Insert Allows better organization of accessories. Up to three dividers can be installed inside the XXL base. XXL box accessories video: How to use it? Here's a short video showing how to fit the Switch 2, wrist straps, joy-cons and game cartridges in the case Future Updates I will continue adding new lid designs over time. If you have ideas, suggestions, or specific themes you'd like to see, feel free to leave a comment. Community feedback is what helped shape this V2, and I'd love to hear your ideas for future additions. Thank you for your support, your feedback, and all the makes you've shared. Enjoy the build!

Wer dreht, kennt das Problem: Tabak, Filter, Blättchen — alles liegt irgendwo verteilt herum. Diese Box löst das. WAS REINPASST: ✔ Drehtabak bis 30g (passt zu Pueblo, Manitou, American Spirit & Co.) ✔ Bis zu 100 Drehfilter bis 8 mm im separaten Schiebefach ✔ Blättchen Einzel- und Doppelpack ✔ Integrierte Befüll Hilfe — sauber und schnell drehen ohne Fummelei PERFEKT ALS GESCHENK: ✔ Ideal für Dreher & Raucher die Ordnung schätzen ✔ Tolle Geschenkidee zu Geburtstag, Weihnachten und Werbegeschenk ✔ Individuelle Farben, Optikmuster und Personalisierung auf Anfrage möglich Info: Ich habe es mit eine Effekt Smooth Platte gedruckt aber das ich sie überlassen welche sie bevorzugen, aktivieren sie die Automatische Konturloch-Kompensation damit alle kreis Bohrungen passen. Ich habe außerdem die außen Linie auf 0,6 mm breite geändert und wand Richtung von innen nach außen gedruckt das spart Stützen zeit und Geld, nur der obere teil der box brauche Stützen da die Trennung von Filterfach zu Blättchen Fach eine Fliegende wand haben um mehr platz für Filter zu schaffen, ( hier müssen sie Stützen nur auf Druck platte deaktivieren). Aber in mein druck Profil ist alles Bereits Fertig. Aufbau: Sie brauche Sekundenkleber und Neo-Dyn Magnete: 8x N52 3x3 mm und 4x N35 10x3 mm Zu beachten die 3x3 mm Mag. Sollte N52 sein um optimal schließ-kraft zu erzeugen (kein Mag in diesem fall vom Aliexpress kaufen da ich immer schlechte Erfahrung damit hatte immer zu klein oder zu schwach und bei 3 mm Mag ist es entscheidend das die Qualität stimmt). Bei die 10x3 mm Mag. können sie auch die schwachen N35 kaufen da die kraft ausreichend ist, auch hier zu beachten das die Maß Genauigkeit bei Aliexpress Produkten nicht 100% passt deswegen ich im Platte 3 eine distanzscheibe mit gelegt habe, mit 0,2 mm Höhe damit sie es unter der Mag. ausgleichen können falls die Magnete weniger als 3 mm aufweisen, drucken sie hier für die Anzahl die sie brauchen und oder passen sie der höhe der distanzscheibe an. Tabakdeckel und Filterdeckel: Hier für lassen sie sich zeit da die Toleranzen sehr klein sind und alles genau passend konstruiert ist. Durch langsames biegen lassen sich die teile in der richtige Stellung bringen, (Der untere teil vom Filterdeckel muss mit Sekunden Kleber befestigt werden). Blättchen Halter auch hier achten sie auf der richtiger Einbau Richtung (Siehe Fotos). Viel Spaß beim Drucken… und lassen sie mir wissen wie es ihnen Gefällt.

description: This is a big sturdy corner clamp for woodworking. It allows you to gently clamp 2 pieces of wood at 90 degrees to each other for gluing. Can handle wood up to 60mm wide in the jaw. Has a double clamp system each side so you can hold the wood with less pressure and less chance of marking the work. A long bed helps make each length of wood parallel to each other. Corner is open at the bottom so any squeeze out of glue doesn't stick the work to the tool. Sides are open to allow a brad nailer to get in. Comes with optional aux clamp for long lengths of wood to ensure the work doesn't sag. This is a big clamp, the chassis requires a bed size of at least 245x245mm (sorry A1 mini users) so any Bambu machine A1 and upwards will work. Other machines will also work as long as the bed is at least 245x245mm. The clamp is designed to hold you work while glue sets or while bad nails are fixed in. It is not designed to put a lot of pressure on. As such, any material should work fine from PLA upwards (although I have found wood glue easier to remove from PETG/ABS). Assembly is simple. The example below is for the Aux clamp, howerver for the main corner clamp its the same procedure repeated 4 times. First place the jaw into the chassis, with the bolt hole inthe jaw aligning with the bolt hole in the chassis. Screw the bolt into the thread until the jaw just starts to move. Then turn it over, and insert the fixing pin into the slot underneath. Push this until it goes through the chassis fully into the jaw. The 2 pins are designed to flex slightly inwards with the top of the prong each side gripping the inside of the jaw. The bolt is now fixed into the chassis and turning the handle will screw the jaw back and forth. Note the 2 holes in the top of the jaw. These are there if you want to push the pin back out from the top.

An over-engineered self-clamping vertical laptop stand with a print-in-place hinge and a printed leaf spring to open the stand when the laptop is removed. Two lengths of stand are provided as options - 99mm and 159mm. Features: The clamp automatically adjusts to the size and shape of most laptops. The weight of the laptop creates leverage on the arms to clamp the laptop securely in place. The print-in-place hinge is very strong and prints easily and reliably (no post-processing or force required). Enables maximum cooling of a laptop (place the front of the laptop into the base of the stand, so that the fan/heat outlets are at the top). Includes an optional (but recommended) TPU pad for the laptop to sit on. Includes optional TPU pads for the top of the arms (the parts that rest against the laptop). Uses a printed leaf spring, which opens the clamp when the laptop is removed. Assembly: The leaf spring has to be bent as shown below, then pushed together. Note the position of the notch when bending the spring. Push the leaf spring together to make the spring unit and then push that into the slot in the end of the clamp. Note that the notch must be placed as shown. to the bottom-right of the slot Push the spring all the way into the slot. It should sit flush against the outside of the slot. If you've printed the TPU Tray Pad, it pushes into place and is held there using the hexagonal knobs on the pad that push into the hexagonal slots on the tray. If you've printed the TPU Arm Pads, push them onto the top of each arm. Usage: The front of the laptop should be placed into the clamp, so that the back of the laptop is sitting up high. This allows the best heat dissapation from the laptop. If the laptop is “loose” or unstable in the clamp, turn the clamp (or the laptop) around (180 degrees horizontally). The clamp will normally work much better in one combination of the orientation of the laptop and clamp (this is due to the profile of the front edges of laptops, which are not symmetric. The clamp has been designed to take advantage of this to provide maximum clamping and stability in one orientation). Filament recommendations: The leaf spring should be printed in PETG, ABS or PC. Do not use PLA or PA as it will distort and be less effective over time. The TPU Tray Pad can be printed using TPU, TPE or PEBA 95A, 90A or 85A (and probably softer than that too). Generally speaking, the softer the better, but 95A works pretty well. PEBA filament is ideal due to it's better rebound than TPU or TPE. The clamp should ideally be printed in PETG, ABS, ASA or PC. Filaments that creep (PLA and PA) will also work but may not be suitable for long term use or if the laptop gets very hot (exceeding the heat distortion temperature of the filament).

Modular Shoe Rack I have created this modular shoe rack to organize our footwear better. The whole model was designed to be modular and customizable in width. The framework is 3d printed from PLA and takes in five wooden round rails of 19 mm diameter per compartment. Depending on your location you can use these examples (DE: OBI , Bauhaus ) or anything similar. Make sure the rails don't fit too tightly. If you cant push them in relatively easy sand them down using some sandpaper. If you try to squeeze them in too hard the layers of the frame might seperate! The model measures 300 mm in depth. There are two sizes for the frame height: 150 mm and 200 mm. You can stack them modularly however you please and need. For the top compartment there is also an endpiece to give the whole rack a rounder appearance. TPU feet for a softer stand are also included. Printing and Assembly To print the model you should get an exaple wood piece that you plan to use. Test: I included a test part on plate 5 to verify the measurements. Start by printing one compartment by printing the same plate (plate 1 for 150 mm, or plate 2 for 200 mm) twice. Cut the wooden rails to the length you want your Rack to be. You will need five rails per compartment. Please note that 28 mm of the rail go into each side of the frame. The total width of the rack will be the length of your rails + 4 mm. For cutting I suggest using a stopper so you can always adjust your rails to exactly the same length. Make sure you sand down three centimenters at each end of each rail untill the glide in with some resistance. Then mount all five rails to one side of the frame. Make sure they all went in the same depth. Place the other side of the frame on the other ends of the rails. I mounted with the rails pointing up and used a piece of wood which I hit gently with a hammer. Repeat steps 1. to 4. for each compartment you need. Make sure the compartments couplers on the frame bottom fit into the slots on the top of the other compartments. Don't clip them in before making sure the setup is correct. The clips are tight and very hard to remove. Print the end pieces by printing plate 3 twice. Print the TPU feet. I suggest printing them by object for optimal quality, however I included a profile for people whose printer can only print by layer. Assemble the whole thing by placing the rack compartments on top of each other and gently hitting it from above (I used just my fist) until they clip in. Place all the footwear you have in it. If you run out of space: EXPAND! Voilà: Order in the shoe section!

Hyoja-son — Korea’s Traditional Back Scratcher I have an old back scratcher that has been with me for over 15 years. It’s not expensive or particularly special, but somehow it became a natural part of my daily life. Whenever my back itches, I reach for it. It has always been there, sitting in its usual spot. This is a very typical Korean-style back scratcher. Made of wood, with finger-like prongs at the end, it scratches surprisingly well. Recently, I realized I needed one more. I could have simply bought a new one, but then a thought crossed my mind: “What if I make one myself?” And if I was going to make one, I wanted to recreate the one that had been with me for so many years. That’s how this model was born. The Meaning Behind the Engraved Words: "효자손" (Hyo-ja-son): Literally meaning “the hand of a devoted child.” It symbolizes the care and devotion a child shows to their parents. "孝道" (Hyo-do): Meaning "the way of filial piety." It represents the warm heart and thoughtfulness we hold for our family. Through MakerWorld, I hope more people can discover interesting everyday objects from Korea. And for Korean users, I hope this model brings back a small sense of nostalgia— perhaps reminding them of the familiar back scratcher that once hung somewhere in their childhood home.

description: 🏹 Arrow F.O.C. Gauge - Misuratore di Precisione con Asola di Marcatura Cerchi la massima precisione per le tue frecce? Questo strumento compatto ed ergonomico è progettato per gli arcieri e i costruttori di frecce che desiderano calcolare e ottimizzare il baricentro ( F.O.C. - Front of Center ) in modo scientifico e ripetibile. Grazie alla livella a bolla superiore , puoi verificare istantaneamente la planarità del sistema. La vera innovazione di questo design è la finestra interna con asola di marcatura : una volta trovato il punto di equilibrio perfetto, potrai infilare un pennarello a punta fine per segnare l'asta in modo preciso, stabile e senza rischiare che la freccia scivoli via durante l'operazione. ✨ Caratteristiche Principali Asola di Marcatura Dedicata: Evita errori segnando la freccia direttamente sul punto di pivot tramite la fessura frontale. Alloggiamento Livella a Bolla: Sede superiore pronta per ospitare una bolla cilindrica standard (facilmente reperibile online o nei brico). Hardware a Costo Zero: Non servono viti o perni metallici. Il sistema sfrutta un meccanismo a cerniera azionato da un pezzo di filamento di scarto. Stampa Pulita bicolore: Ottimizzato per essere stampato in parti separate, permettendo l'effetto bicolore (es. Nero/Oro) anche su stampanti a singolo filamento (senza AMS) e senza sprechi. 💡 Istruzioni di Assemblaggio (Perno Fai-da-Te) Il montaggio è incredibilmente semplice e richiede meno di 2 minuti: Allinea l'elemento oscillante interno (giallo nelle foto) con il corpo principale esterno (nero). Inserisci uno spezzone di normale filamento per stampa 3D da 1.75 mm attraverso il foro passante del perno centrale. Taglia il filamento lasciando circa 1-2 mm di eccedenza su ciascun lato. Usa un accendino per bruciare leggermente le due estremità del filamento. Appena la plastica si scalda e crea una micro-sfera, premila subito contro il corpo dello strumento (ad esempio aiutandoti con il piatto metallico dell'accendino) per ribadirla e sigillare il perno in posizione. Incolla la livella a bolla cilindrica (consigliata 10x30mm) nella sede superiore con una goccia di colla cianoacrilica (Super Attack). 📊 Dati Tecnici e Parametri di Slicing Il modello è leggero, economico e veloce da produrre. Ecco i dati reali ricavati dallo slicing: Materiale Richiesto: Solo ~6,18 metri di filamento (circa 18,43 grammi ). Costo Stimato Materiale: Appena 0,37 € . Tempo di Stampa del Modello: 1 ora e 3 minuti. Tempo Totale (con calibrazioni e timelapse): 1 ora e 12 minuti. Altezza dello strato consigliata: 0.20 mm (o 0.16 mm per una precisione maggiore sui fori). Supporti: Non necessari. 🎯 Come usarlo per calcolare il F.O.C. Appoggia lo strumento su un tavolo e verifica che la bolla sia perfettamente al centro. Posiziona la freccia (completa di punta, cocca e alette) sull'incavo della culletta oscillante. Muovi la freccia finché la bolla dello strumento non torna perfettamente in bolla al centro. Prendi un pennarello sottile, infilalo nell'asola frontale e traccia una linea sulla freccia. Quello è il tuo esatto punto di equilibrio (Center of Gravity)!

model_name: SKADIS for P1S / X1C side panel - custom sized
description: 3D printed SKADIS for BambuLab P1S and X1C I thought to utilise the rather empty space of my P1S to mount a SKADIS board, but none of the available original SKADIS sizes fit the P1S / X1C side panel. Therefore, I created this model which fits on the side of a BambuLab P1S or X1C. 💡Features: almost everything is 3D printable, needs only 3 M4x10 screws (even those are optional) keyed dovetail connection between the boards for strong fit significant clearance between the board and printers side panel + TPU spacers to prevent scratching mounted using printed hooks on a stock printer setup rigid and universal The SKADIS itself was generated from the parametric model by user @Line Arc Line from printables ( Parametric SKADIS Board Generator ). Kudos to the designer! Dimensions of the final SKADIS: 32 x 42 x 5.3 mm Most parts can be printed out of PLA but the mounting hooks need to be printed out of PETG, ASA or another less brittle material than PLA . The reason is, that those parts need to be flexed quite a lot to snap into place during mounting. 📜Part list and filaments: You will need the following printed parts. All are present in the submitted print profile and split into plates ( see below ). 4x SKADIS plates labelled 1-4 - PLA or any other material 6x spacers with three pins - PLA or any other material 3x spacers with a M4 hole - PLA or any other material 3x thin washers with a M4 hole (can be replaced by metal washers as well) - PLA or any other material 9x spacer caps - TPU (optional) 2x top mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) 2x bottom mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) Non-printed parts 3x M4x10 screws 🖨️ Print instructions: Before you print all the pieces consider printing the TEST model first (see print profile). It's a quick 20 min to check if the settings fit your printer tolerances and setup. The provided print profiles have all settings dialed in and are ready to print (Bambu Handy App friendly). Just print each plate once and you should have everything you need: Plates 1-4 (PLA, ~350g total, 2h30min each): SKADIS parts labeled 1-4. Plate 5 (PLA, ~7g, 22 min): 6x stand-offs with pins, 3x normal standoffs and 3x spacers Plate 6 (TPU, ~4g, 22 min): 9x TPU caps for the stand-offs Plate 7 (PETG/ASA, ~12g, 30 min): 3x top and 3x bottom mounting hooks ( only two needed each, the other ones are spare ) 🔩 Assembly: A picture-assisted assembly and mounting guide is provided in the description. I strongly recommend to use that. You will find the text-based instruction below. Depending on the tolerances of your printer, the SKADIS pieces may go together either quite tight or be a little bit loose. I dialed the tolerances in for my P1S and the pieces grab onto each other quite well. Glue is not required for the assembly but is strongly recommended to prevent the whole thing from disassembling if you plan to hang something heavy from it. DO NOT use cyanoacrylate-based superglue especially if you printed the parts out of black (or dark) plastic. In my experience the glue emits some kind of vapour while drying which stains the plastic white. Instead, use a little bit of dedicated PLA glue or two-component resin glue. If the pieces go in quite tight you may use a rubber hammer to jam the pieces together which would probably hold quite well even without glue. Place piece 1 on a flat surface with the number 1 facing upward Hold piece 2 with the marking facing the top and slide into piece 1 from the top Repeat steps 1 and 2 for pieces 3 and 4 respectively Connect all pieces together by sliding the 1-2 piece into the 3-4 piece Insert the spacers with 3 legs into respective holes on the back of the board. The use of glue is advised if you are certain that you assembled the pieces right. Place the small spacers at the indicated spots at the front of the board. Insert the M4x?? screw from the front through the spacer and through the SKADIS hole. Screw in the remaining long spacers onto the M4 screws Cover all spacers with the TPU caps by inserting them into the respective holes 🪜Mounting: Remove the top glass of your P1S or X1C printer Hold the top mounting bracket with the SKADIS hook facing to the left. Flex the bracket and slide the right hand latch onto the frame where the glass sits on top. Straighten the left side of the bracket so it snaps into place. Repeat the same process for the other top mounting bracket Hang the assembled SKADIS onto the top brackets as indicated. Insert the bottom brackets into the indicated holes. Flex the right side of the bracket so it passes the bottom edge of the printer chassis and snaps into place. Repeat for the second bracket Now you are done and ready to go! Have fun! If you encounter any issues, feel free to comment or write me a DM, maybe I'll be able to help you. Post your makes, I'm curious how yours will look like ;) Cheers and all the best!😉 Fun fact: I finished the project in 2024 and it has been mounted on my P1S since without any issues. I just now finally found the time to document and release it properly. I hope you find it useful ;)

description: Square Kumihimo disc for flat bracelets This is a square Kumihimo disc to make flat bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has ten (10) horizontal and vertical notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The top and bottom horizontal rows are labelled 1-10 and the left and right side vertical columns are labelled A-J to make it easier to stay oriented while making your Kumihimo weaving bracelet. The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. description: Short description A 3D printed 250 mm face disc sander with an adjustable work table, dust extraction port, weighted base option, and a customizable electronics compartment for different motors, power supplies, and PWM controllers. Description This project is a 250 mm face disc sander , designed as a compact bench-top sanding machine for small workshop tasks, edge sanding, finishing 3D prints, plastics, wood, and similar materials. The construction is divided into multiple 3D printed parts that are assembled together using screws. Threaded inserts are used in places where a strong and reusable thread is required. The sander includes an adjustable work table and a rear outlet for connecting a vacuum cleaner for dust extraction. The lower base part is designed so it can be filled with sand or another suitable material to increase the weight and stability of the entire machine. After assembly, the sanding disc should be trued and leveled using sandpaper. I then applied a PROXXON 28968 silicone adhesive film to the disc, which makes it easy to replace individual sanding sheets. Sanding sheets compatible with the PROXXON 28060 TSG 250/E can be used, or any other suitable 250 mm sanding discs. Electronics and motor In my build I used the following motor: JGB37-550, 160 rpm, 12 V The PWM controller I used is this one: https://www.laskakit.cz/pwm-regulator-otacek-motoru-10a--80w/ The power supply, wiring, and PWM controller must be correctly sized according to the motor you choose. If you use a different motor, make sure to adapt the motor mount, power supply, controller, and wiring accordingly. To make the project easier to modify, I include two parts as STEP files: Bruska - DrzakElektroniky – the lower electronics holder / base where the power supply and PWM controller are mounted, Bruska - HorniVicko – the cover with the input connector. This allows you to easily modify the design for your own power supply, connector, motor, or speed controller. Important safety warning This specific version is designed with an internal power supply connected to 230 V AC mains voltage . 230 V AC is dangerous and potentially lethal . If you do not have the required electrical qualification, certification, or sufficient experience working with mains voltage equipment, do not use 230 V AC inside this sander . In that case, I strongly recommend modifying the project for a safer external 12 V or 24 V DC power supply , depending on the motor used. For example, you can use an external power adapter and bring only low-voltage DC power into the sander. Building, modifying, and using this machine is entirely at your own risk. The author accepts no responsibility for damage, injury, fire, electric shock, or any other consequences resulting from building, modifying, or using this sander. hreaded inserts used The project uses the following threaded inserts: M3 standard: https://www.prusa3d.com/cs/produkt/zavitove-vlozky-m3-standard-100-kusu/ M4 standard: https://www.prusa3d.com/cs/produkt/zavitove-vlozky-m4-standard-50-kusu/ M4 short: https://www.prusa3d.com/cs/produkt/zavitove-vlozky-m4-kratke-50-kusu/ Sanding disc and sanding sheets The sanding disc diameter is 250 mm . For the Bruska - VickoPredniKapsy part, another 2 magnets of the same size — 8 mm diameter and 3 mm height — are glued in after printing. I recommend using a sufficient number of walls/perimeters and appropriate infill to give the parts enough strength. After printing, check the flatness of the mating surfaces, hole accuracy, and proper installation of the threaded inserts. description: Overview A customizable Skadis holder for round stuff, where you set the diameter and it does the rest. It hangs a row of round cups on an IKEA Skadis pegboard and holds just about anything cylindrical: glue sticks, markers, highlighters, screwdriver handles, small bottles, hobby paints, spray cans and WD-40. You really only set two things, the object diameter and how many cups you want. From there the customizer sizes the cups, packs them in next to each other and puts a Skadis hook behind each one at the nearest real slot. Heavy or wide cups get a second peg on their own so they can't tip out, and everything else is optional. Measure the object itself and type that number in, the model adds the fit gap for you so you're not left guessing tolerances (the optional floor hole works the same way). One thing worth doing before a big run: print a single cup first. Printer tolerances vary, so even if you know yours it pays to slice one cup at your diameter and check the object actually drops in before you print a whole row. A two-minute test is a lot cheaper than redoing a full board that came out a hair too tight. If the fit is off, nudge the Clearance a little (0.2 is snug, 0.3 is the default, 0.4 is looser) and reprint that one cup. Set the diameter — the customizer sizes every cup to fit. Highlights Diameter 10 to 80 mm, 1 to 12 cups in a row. Mixed sizes in the same row, so a wide can sits happily next to slim glue sticks. Heavy cups get a double peg automatically, and there's a thin-profile mode for short rows. Optional hole through the floor to pass a tool or screwdriver through. Native Skadis hook that fits both real Skadis (5 mm) and printed boards. Dimensions. The default 3 cup, 21 mm row comes out around 100 x 35 x 30 mm. Yours will depend on the diameter and count you choose. Compatibility. IKEA Skadis and Skadis-compatible printed pegboards (5x15 mm slots on a 40 mm grid). Cylinders up to 80 mm outside diameter. Printing. Print it standing up, with the panel flat on the bed and the cups opening upward. Any material is fine (PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA, PC). PETG is a solid all-rounder and PLA works perfectly well. Use a 0.4 or 0.6 mm nozzle and skip 0.8, which softens the detail and the fit. A bit of support on the rear pegs, none under the cups. Full customizer guide Every setting, if you want to fine-tune. What the settings control — diameter, clearance, wall, cup height, floor. Setting Default What it does Object diameter 21 mm The object's exact body diameter, 10–80 mm (any decimal). Measure it — the model adds the fit gap for you (set by Clearance). Count 3 Number of cups in the row, 1–12. Cup height 30 mm How far the cup wraps the object, 5–100 mm. Taller = steadier for tall/heavy items. Warns if a cup is too short for its diameter. Per-cup size off (0) Optional: give one cup its own diameter and/or height (0 = use the main size). Sits right under the main size. Pegs per cup auto (0) 0 = auto: 1 peg for light items, 2 for heavy/large. Or force 1–3. Heavy threshold 40 mm A cup at/above this diameter auto-gets a second peg. Single peg row off Thin-profile mode — forces all pegs into one row for the lowest backboard (best for short, light items). Clearance 0.3 mm The fit gap added to the diameter — applied to both the cup bore and the floor hole (a 30 mm object → a 30.3 mm bore). Measure exact and let the model add it. 0.3 (default) suits most prints — snug but slides in; 0.2 is very snug (only if you trust your printer); 0.4 plays it safe (looser). Wall 2.4 mm Cup wall thickness. Gap between cups 4 mm Spacing between neighbouring cups. Floor thickness 2 mm Every cup has a closed floor; this sets it. Floor hole 0 (off) The exact diameter of a tool/device to pass through every cup's floor (or to drain) — the model adds the same clearance as the cup. Any decimal. Per-cup override available. Plate thickness / margin / radius 3 / 5 / 7 mm Back panel: thickness, border around the cups, corner rounding. Board thickness 5 mm The Skadis board the pocket fits, 4–7 mm (standard Skadis is 5). Setup tips Measure exact, leave the tolerance to the model. Enter the object's true diameter, and if you use the floor hole, the true diameter of whatever goes through it. The model adds the Clearance to both, so you don't need to pad your own measurement. 0.3 (the default) suits most prints, snug but it still slides in. 0.2 is very snug, only worth it if you trust your printer. 0.4 plays it safe. One cup, two pegs. A single cup on one peg sits snug on the board, but with only one peg it can rotate a touch and a knock can twist it. For a steady single holder, set Pegs per cup to 2 so the two stacked pegs lock the rotation. (Auto already does this for heavy cups, and a row of three or more braces itself anyway.) Heavy or tall items. Keep it on auto (or force 2 pegs) and use a taller cup. Don't put a full can in single peg row mode, because it really wants the double peg. Thin profile. Turn on Single peg row for short items, like a tray of stubby markers, to get the lowest backboard possible. The pegs snap to the 40 mm Skadis grid, so a peg can sit slightly off a cup's centre and very close cups will share a peg. That's fine for light rows. Board grip. The default 5 mm board thickness fits standard Skadis. Drop it a little for a firmer grip on a thinner or printed board. How the pegs work Each cup gets a native Skadis hook that fills a 5x15 slot and catches behind the board. Heavy or wide cups (at or above the heavy threshold) automatically get a second peg stacked one slot below the first , a vertical pair that stops a full can from tipping out. Slim cups keep a single hook. Either way, every peg drops into a real slot at the same time. Turning on Single peg row overrides all of that and forces one thin row. The native hook catches behind the board. Hooks straight onto an IKEA Skadis board. Mixed sizes in one row Every cup uses the main diameter unless you give it one of its own. Set just the cup you want bigger and a wide can will still pack in tight next to a slim glue stick, with every hook landing in a real slot. The panel sizes itself to whatever row you build. Any size in one row — a fat can beside slim cups. anno_mixed.png Floor holes (optional) Cups are closed by default. You can open a hole through the floor, on every cup or just one, for a few reasons: to pass a screwdriver or tool through (handle in the cup, shaft poking out the bottom), to let a long object stick out the bottom, or to push something up from below to pop it out. Measure the exact diameter of whatever goes through and the model adds the same fit gap as the cup (the hole comes out as your diameter plus clearance), so it's a clean, snug pass-through. Print settings Setting Value Material Any. PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA or PC. PETG is a great everyday pick (fine indoors too) and PLA is perfectly fine. There's no real material limit here. The pricier engineering filaments just add heat and strength you probably don't need. Nozzle 0.4 or 0.6 mm (both print cleanly). Avoid 0.8 because it loses fine detail and the fit tolerances don't come out right. description: “I wish I didn't have so much light on my welding project!” - Nobody, ever Welding is a dark art. I don't mean that it is evil or rooted in the occult…I mean I can't see anything! Setting up shop lights is a pain, and there is never enough light on my welding bench. Such was the challenge I faced. Not being overly industrious and somewhat on the cheap side, I decided that the solution was to use a good cheap LED flashlight (torch for those of you who still live in medieval times and use the metric system). My first thought was (as always when facing a task that requires creativity), DUCT TAPE!" This is the result. It is a super-simple, super-cheap, quick solution that although you may not admit it, you already love. It is a one-piece bracket that prints in a few minutes and attaches to your welding helmet's pivot bolt. The tension nut holds it in place, and a zip tie (my #2 go-to after duct tape) holds the flashlight on. Cheap. Quick. Easy. Pick any 3. Although it is a basic design, this little gem does have some nice features: Raised ribs around the mounting hole to help keep it from slipping under the tension nut Wide slots to accommodate whatever zip ties you may have lying around A concave section that the flashlight rests in to keep it from going all wonky on you Thin but flexible to accommodate being banged around, because you know you toss your welding helmet around a lot So go ahead. Download it and print it. Once you use it, you will wonder why you didn't think of it. description: 32-slot Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets This is a beginner friendly round Kumihimo disc to make round bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has 32 marked notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded circle slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The notches are labelled 1-32 and the notes are marked every 8th slot with a large dot to indicate starting points for common 8-string weaves (at 8, 16, 24 and 32), as well as every 4th slot in between for 16-string weaves with a smaller circle (at 4, 12, 20 and 28). The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels and markings. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos.
