A fully 3D-printed folding wall shelf that tucks flat against the wall when not in use and deploys a load-bearing support arm when you need it — practical, space-saving, and finished with a honeycomb underside for style. -- Why I made this - Most wall shelves are permanent fixtures. I wanted something that earns its space — a shelf that disappears when you don't need it and holds its own when you do. This design is 100% 3D printed (minus the wall screws and anchors you'll source locally) and built around a real folding mechanism rather than a novelty hinge. -- What it is - The shelf folds on a set of printed hinge knuckles: fold it up and it sits flush against the wall, fold it down and a pivoting support arm locks it into a horizontal position capable of handling real everyday loads. The underside of the shelf panel features a honeycomb pattern — so the face you see when it's folded up looks intentional, not bare plastic. All the structural work is done by the shelf panel, the support arm, and the hinge knuckles. The only hardware you need are wall screws and anchors appropriate for your wall type. -- Design details **Folding hinge knuckles** — printed-in geometry, no metal hardware at the pivot **Pivoting support arm** — braces the shelf against downward load when deployed **Honeycomb underside** — decorative and visible when the shelf is stowed -- How to print - Print in PLA+ for a lightweight indoor shelf or PETG if you want better humidity and temperature resistance. Either material works well here. ORIENTATION MATTERS, ALWAYS ORIENT IN A WAY WHERE LOADS WONT SHEAR THE Z LAYERING OF THE PRINT. - **Shelf panel** — lay flat on the bed, largest face down. - **Support arm** — lay flat on face so layer lines run along the arm's length; this puts the strongest layer orientation against bending loads, which is exactly where you need it. - **Hinge knuckles** — This is the trickier one, check overhanging geometry in your slicer before printing; orientation matters. - **20-30% infill** on all structural parts and many walls 4-5 (support arm, hinge knuckles, and cradle). ### Tips - Run a test fit of the hinge knuckles before final assembly — tolerances can vary slightly between printers; a quick pass with a small file cleans things up in seconds. - When mounting to drywall, use wall anchors rated for at least the load you plan to put on the shelf — the print will hold, so make sure the wall fastening matches. - PETG is the better choice for garages, laundry rooms, or anywhere with temperature swings or moisture. ### Assembly / Instructions 1. Print all parts: shelf panel, support arm, hinge knuckles/wall brackets and cradle. Check orientation notes before slicing. 2. Dry-fit the wall bracket onto the shelf panel. Verify smooth pivot motion; lightly sand or file any tight spots. 3. Attach the wall brackets shelf panel and place against the wall, level it out and mark the holes for each wall bracket. 4. Drill out marked holes and install anchors. 5. Place shelf with attached wall brackets against wall and screw into newly installed anchors (verify swinging action of shelf before installing) MY SHELF HAS BEEN INSTALLED FOR OVER 2 MONTHS WITH A SMALL PLANTER ON TOP, EVERYTHING IS HOLDING UP WITH NO SIGNS OF DEFORMATION OR STRESS. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Symmetric Pattern Generator Perfect for panels & drawer faces. I recently designed 3D printed drawers with Kumiko and Hexagon faces, and all of the generator I could find online never generator what I needed: Controllable frame dimensions / thickness Controllable pattern size or quantity to fill the frame in a perfectly symmetric way Controllable border padding Editable notch (optional) This script is perfect for anyone looking for an easy and quick way to generate patterns or panels. Very useful for laser cutting or CAD as well. HOW TO USE Panel Size - Thickness Width & Height: control the size of the panel in mm Thickness: control the thickness of your frame Notch Add notch: toggle the notch function on/off Notch width / height: control the size of you notch Notch radius: Control the roundness of your notch ends Notch border: control the border thickness around your notch Border padding Border top / right / bottom / left: control the thickness of the padding around your frame Pattern style Pattern style: Select between 16 pattern styles (more to come) Size mode: this is the critical modifier: by size: the frame will be filled with repetitive patterns of the selected size. Very useful when making different panels where you want the pattern to stay consistent on different frame sizes. by count: the frame will be filled with exactly the selected “n patterns” number of the pattern. IF you select 7 “n patterns”, the frame will be filled with 7 patterns, the script will calculate the pattern size to make it fit exactly the width (working on making it height / width selectable). Use this if you want a perfectly symmetric pattern where left and right ends are identical (imagine a mirror in the middle of the frame). Pattern size: select the size of each pattern in mm (only when size mode is by size ) n patterns: select the exact amount of patterns to fill the frame width (only when size mode is by count ) Branch thickness: control the thickness of your patterns. For 3d printing, avoid going under 1.5mm Inner Thickness: control the thickness of inner branches (only currently used for the Boxes patterns) Export to SVG / DXF or more formats I designed this script to firstly export to DXF to work with Fusion360 and my laser cutting software. Unfortunately, MakerWorld limits the export to only STL (3MF is a zip archive of STL + print settings). If you are interested in exporting to more formats for your workflow, please send me a private message. Patterns To Do Still plenty of work to make this script the absolute ultimate: New patterns to come (especially Kumiko patterns) Link the inner thickness control to all the applicable patterns (Kumiko & lattice especially) Different styles of notches (rectangular for example) Side tabs: useful for frames that lock into a slot

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

You tell it what you carry and it builds the box around you: a **bento-style grid** interior, a **personalised two-colour lid**, a **click-stop hinge** that holds itself open, and an **ergonomic thumb latch** — all auto-sized, all support-free. > 👉 **Press the “Customize” button** to open it in MakerWorld’s parametric editor and dial in your own box right in the browser — no software to install. Then download your `.3mf`/`.stl` and print. --- ## ✨ Highlights - 🧩 **Bento-grid interior** — drop vials, syringes, or wipe slots into a Row × Column grid; the box **auto-sizes** around your loadout. - 💉 **Holds your whole kit** — 3 / 5 / 10 ml vials (standing *or* laid on their side), open syringe bins, and vertical wipe slots. - 🏷️ **Personalised lid** — flush **two-colour text + graphics** (great with Bambu AMS), 40+ fonts including bold, aggressive display faces. - 🔗 **Click-stop hinge** — the lid **holds open** at set angles instead of flopping, and is engineered to survive **thousands of open/close cycles** in PLA. - 👍 **Ergonomic latch** — a smooth thumb-pry lip pops the lid with one finger; still snaps shut securely. - 🖨️ **Prints clean** — watertight and **support-free**; tuned for Bambu Lab and every FDM printer. --- ## 🧩 The Bento Grid (how the interior works) The inside is a grid of **`grid_rows × grid_cols`** quadrants. You drop a **component** into each cell, and the box grows to fit: | Component | What it is | Footprint | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **vial1 / vial2** | pockets of your two chosen vial sizes | `cols × rows` | **auto-fills** the compartment; each can stand up **or lay flat** | | **syringe** | an **open deep bin** for U100 syringes | `count×20 × 130 mm` | floor→ceiling, no wasted solid; syringes lie in & stack | | **wipe** | a **vertical slot** for 50×50 mm wipe packets on edge | `(count×5) × 50 mm` | ~5 mm ≈ 10 wipes; +5 mm per count | | **empty** | a solid spacer | — | for gaps / future use | **How the sizing works (so it always fits):** - **Column widths** grow to the widest cell in that column; **row lengths** grow to the longest cell in that row — a clean table layout. So a 130 mm syringe makes its whole row 130 mm long, and the vial cell next to it **auto-fills** that length with more vials. - **Box height = your tallest item** (a standing 10 ml is 54 mm; a standing wipe is 50 mm — whichever is tallest sets the height so the lid still closes). - **Partition walls** turn each cell into a real compartment. `partition_level` sets their height: **0 = none, 1 = 25 %, 2 = 50 %, 3 = 75 %, 4 = full**. ``` grid_cols ───────────────► Example default 2×2: ┌──────────────┬───────────────┐ │ vial1 (3 ml) │ syringe bin │ r1c1 = vial1 (3 ml) r1c2 = syringe ×2 │ auto-filled │ ▭▭ open/deep │ r2c1 = vial2 (10 ml) r2c2 = wipe ×3 ├──────────────┼───────────────┤ │ vial2 (10 ml)│ wipe slot ▮▮ │ └──────────────┴───────────────┘ ``` ### 💊 Vial catalog | Vial | Size | Pocket | |---|---|---| | **3 ml** | Ø16 × 40 mm | Ø17 | | **5 ml** | Ø22 × 40 mm | Ø23 | | **10 ml** | Ø22 × 54 mm | Ø23 | Pick which two sizes you want with `vial1_type` / `vial2_type` (sizes are editable in **`[Content Catalog]`**). --- ## 🎛️ How to use the parametric controls Open **Customize** and you’ll see the settings grouped into sections. Here’s what each group does: ### `[Grid]` — the layout skeleton - **`grid_rows` / `grid_cols`** — how many quadrants (e.g. 2 × 2). - **`partition_level`** — divider-wall height, `0`–`4` (none → full). ### `[Row 1] / [Row 2] / [Row 3]` — fill each cell - **`r1c1` … `r3c3`** — the component in each cell: `vial1`, `vial2`, `syringe`, `wipe`, or `empty`. - **`r1c1_n` …** — the **count** (vials wide, syringe width, or wipe thickness). - **`r1c1_rows` …** — vial **rows deep** for *that* quadrant (`0` = use the default), so every cell can have its own R × C. ### `[Vial Types]` — vials behaviour - **`vial1_type` / `vial2_type`** — `3ml` / `5ml` / `10ml`. - **`vial1_orient` / `vial2_orient`** — `standing` or **`flat`** (lays the vials in round side cradles). - **`vial_pack`** — `fill` (maximise how many fit) or `exact` (place exactly your R × C). - **`vial_align`** — `spread` (outer vials hug the walls, evenly indexed) or `center` (centred block). - **`vial_wall_clear`** — gap kept to the walls so pockets never break out. ### `[Box Height]` - **`height_override`** — `0` = **AUTO** (sized to the tallest item). Set a value to force a total height. - **`extra_height`** — add head-room above the auto height. ### `[Output]` — what to render - **`show_bottom`** — the tray. **`show_top`** — the lid. **`show_combined`** — lid sitting on the box (preview). - **`show_contents`** — draws translucent mock vials/syringes/wipes so you can eyeball the loadout. **Turn it OFF before exporting** — it’s preview-only. - The **console report** tells you the grid, box W × L × H, what each cell holds, and warns if anything is too big for your plate. > 💡 **Tip:** export **once with `show_bottom`** and **once with `show_top`** — that’s your tray + lid. --- ## 🏷️ Personalise the Lid — flush two-colour Text & Graphics The lid top can carry a **flush, co-planar** label — *not* embossed or engraved, but a second-colour region in the same surface (perfect for **Bambu AMS / MakerWorld multi-colour**). **Text** and **Design** are independent — use either or **both**, each with its own colour and placement. **Orientation frame:** picture the closed box with the **latch toward you** (front) and the **hinge at the back**. Everything is placed in that frame — `halign` = your left/right, `valign` `top` = hinge / `bottom` = latch. ### `[Lid Text]` - **`lid_text_on`**, **`lid_text`** (+ optional **`lid_text_line2`**), **`lid_text_color`**. - **`lid_font`** — a dropdown of clean classics **plus aggressive / manly display faces**: Oswald, **Anton**, **Bebas Neue**, **Archivo Black**, **Black Ops One**, Bungee, Bangers, Teko, Russo One, Orbitron, Audiowide, Staatliches, Monoton, Permanent Marker, **Alfa Slab One**, **Ultra**, **Bevan**, **Passion One**, **Titan One**, **Squada One**, **Rajdhani**, **Chakra Petch**, **Wallpoet**, **Goldman**, **Michroma**, **Stardos Stencil**, **Special Elite**, **Rye**, **Metal Mania**, **Pirata One**, **UnifrakturCook**, **New Rocker**, **Germania One**, and more. - **`lid_font_custom`** — type **any** font name to use it instead (this is a searchable **font picker** in MakerWorld’s editor). - **`lid_text_weight`** — Regular / Bold / Black / … ⚠️ **Set this to `Regular` for single-weight display fonts** (Anton, Bebas Neue, Bangers, Black Ops One, Alfa Slab One, etc.) or they fall back to the default. - **`lid_text_size`** — a real font size in mm (`0` = no text); it **auto-shrinks to fit** so long words never run off the edge. - **Alignment + padding** — `lid_text_halign` / `lid_text_valign` **anchor the text to that edge and grow it inward** (right-align fills right→left, left-align fills left→right — never cut off). **`lid_text_pad_l/r/t/b`** inset each side in mm to nudge it perfectly. - **`lid_text_orient`** — `horizontal` or `vertical`. ### `[Lid Design]` - **`lid_design_on`**, **`lid_design`** — `molecule`, `helix`, `honeycomb`, `logo`, or full-lid tilings `helix-full` / `honeycomb-full`. - **`lid_design_orient`** — horizontal / vertical / corner-TL/TR/BL/BR, plus **`halign` / `valign` / `pad`** (same edge-anchored behaviour as the text) and **`lid_pattern_scale`** for size. - **`lid_design_color`** — the design colour. **Layering:** where text and a design overlap, the **text reads on top** (the design is relieved out from under the letters), each in its own colour. > 🎨 **To print in two colours:** render the lid (`show_top`) and **export as 3MF** — each colour region becomes its own material for the AMS. (A single-material STL is also fully watertight.) --- ## 🔗 Hinge & Latch — engineered, not guessed **Ergonomic latch pry-lip** — a smooth, rounded ridge you hook a thumb under to pop the lid. Hulled (no sharp edges), self-supporting underside, and clear of the snap bump so the **secure close is unchanged**. Set with `latch_relief` / `latch_relief_size`. **Click-stop detent hinge** — the open lid **clicks and holds** at set angles instead of flopping. A rounded nub on the lid drops into rounded dimples on the barrel ends — and because the detent lives on the **hinge end faces**, it needs **no supports at any angle**. - **`detent_angles_deg`** = `[90, 120, 140, 160, 180, 210]` (210 = full-open back-stop) — edit to taste. - **`detent_phase`** nudges the click angles; **`detent_nub_proud`** firms the click; **`detent_bore_extra`** adds local relief *only* if a test print snaps on too stiffly. - This design survived a **multi-pass adversarial stress-test** — it’s tuned to flex the long lid spring by only a few tenths of a millimetre per click (low strain) with filleted features for fatigue life. **Third (center) hinge** — on wide boxes the long barrel can sag, so a center support cradle is **added automatically** when the box `width ≥ third_hinge_width_threshold` (160 mm) or when you set `enable_third_hinge`. The lid still snaps on in one motion and prints support-free. > 🧪 **Pro tip:** print a quick **one-knuckle test coupon** first to feel the snap + click, then fine-tune `detent_phase` / `detent_nub_proud` before committing to a big box. --- ## 🖨️ Print settings & tips - **Material:** PLA is great; **PETG** is tougher for the hinge. - **Layer height:** 0.20 mm. **Supports:** ❌ none needed — everything opens upward. - **Orientation:** print the **tray on its floor**, the **lid on its rim / top-face-down** (the slicer plates them correctly from the exported files). - **Two-colour lid:** assign the text/design region a second filament in the AMS (use the **3MF**). - **Vial fit:** `vial_clearance` controls the radial gap; `vial_z_clearance` is the air gap above a vial so the lid clears a crimp/flip cap. - **Hinge stringing/snapping at layer lines?** Slow the top layers, raise min-layer-time to ~10 s, or bump temp +5 °C. --- ## 📦 What’s included - The **parametric model** (`.scad`) — the whole project, fully customizable on MakerWorld. - A set of **ready-to-print example STLs** (various grids). - The built-in **lid designs** (molecule / helix / honeycomb) and the optional logo. --- ## ❤️ About / License Designed from scratch by **Keaton Hoskins** — MakerWorld **@thehoskins**. 🌬️ Tronic TLK 7000 C2 Zwei-Schlauch-Adapter | Massiver Effizienz-Boost! 🚀Hole das absolute Maximum aus deinem Tronic TLK 7000 C2 (Lidl Hausmarke) oder baugleichen mobilen Klimageräten! Dieses smarte, zweiteilige Upgrade verwandelt deine ineffiziente Einschlauch-Klimaanlage in ein hocheffizientes Zwei-Schlauch-System . Das Ergebnis: Der Raum wird deutlich schneller kalt, das Gerät verbraucht weniger Strom und du kannst spürbar größere Flächen kühlen. 💡 Warum ist dieses Design ein Gamechanger? (Die Physik dahinter) Das Problem im Originalzustand (Einschlauch): Mobile Klimageräte nutzen die mühsam gekühlte Raumluft, um den heißen Kompressor im Inneren zu kühlen, und blasen diese Luft durch den originalen Abluftschlauch nach draußen. Dadurch entsteht in der Wohnung ein massiver Unterdruck . Die Folge: Knallheiße Sommerluft (30°C+) wird permanent durch jede Türritze, jedes Schlüsselloch und jede Fensterdichtung von draußen wieder in die Wohnung gesaugt. Ein endloser, extrem ineffizienter Kampf! Die Lösung mit diesem Adapter (Zwei-Schlauch): Dieser zweiteilige Aufsatz kapselt das untere Ansauggitter (den Heißluft-Kreislauf des Kompressors) komplett ab. Über den neuen, zweiten Schlauch (Zuluft) saugt das Gerät die Luft zur Kühlung der Technik direkt von draußen an. Über den originalen Schlauch wird sie wieder nach draußen geblasen. Der Clou: In deiner Wohnung entsteht kein Unterdruck mehr! Die Raumluft wird im Inneren nur noch im Kreis gesaugt, eiskalt gefiltert und wieder abgegeben. Die Kälte bleibt im Raum, die Hitze bleibt draußen. Die Effizienz steigt um bis zu 50%! 🔩 Benötigtes Zusatzmaterial (BOM) Für den Zusammenbau und die Montage benötigst du folgendes Zubehör: 8x M3 Einschmelzgewinde (Gewindeeinsätze / Heat-Set Inserts, z.B. Ruthex) 8x M3 Zylinderkopfschrauben (M3x10mm oder M3x12mm sind ideal) Mindestens 6x Kabelbinder (um den Basisrahmen am Gitter der Klimaanlage zu fixieren) 1x Zusätzlicher flexibler Schlauch (Abluft-/Zuluftschlauch, Durchmesser passend zum gedruckten Stutzen wählen) (Zudem vielleicht ein Abdichtband für Fenster - bekommt man in jedem Baumarkt) Disclaimer: Notfalls lassen sich die zwei Teile ebenfalls mit dünnen Kabelbindern zusammenfügen OHNE die Einschmelzgewinde (ist so nur eleganter) 🛠️ Montageanleitung Das clevere, zweiteilige Design macht die Installation und spätere Wartung kinderleicht: Gewinde vorbereiten: Schmelze die 8x M3 Gewindeeinsätze mit einem Lötkolben vorsichtig in die dafür vorgesehenen Löcher des flachen Montagerahmens . Rahmen fixieren: Setze den Montagerahmen auf das untere Gitter der Klimaanlage. Nutze mindestens 6 Kabelbinder , um den Rahmen bombenfest am Kunststoffgitter zu verzurren (siehe Projektbild). Knipse die Enden der Kabelbinder sauber ab. Trichter aufschrauben: Setze den großen Trichteraufsatz auf den Rahmen und verschraube ihn mit den 8x M3 Schrauben. Vorteil: Für Filterreinigungen oder den Wintertransport kannst du den Trichter jederzeit abschrauben, ohne die Kabelbinder zu beschädigen! Schlauch anschließen: Stecke deinen neuen Zuluftschlauch auf den Stutzen und führe ihn (zusammen mit dem originalen Abluftschlauch) nach draußen – am besten durch eine feste Rollladen- oder Fensterblende. 🖨️ Empfohlene Druckeinstellungen (Print Settings) Material: PETG (ABS oder ASA) absolut empfohlen! Da die Schläuche und die Rückseite des Klimageräts im Hochsommer sehr warm werden können, ist normales PLA nicht hitzebeständig genug und könnte sich mit der Zeit verformen. Wände / Peripherie (Walls): Mindestens 3 bis 4 Wandlinien . Das Bauteil muss absolut luftdicht sein, damit keine Falschluft gezogen wird. Infill: 20% - 25% (Gyroid oder Grid) Support: Empfohlen! Viel Spaß beim Drucken und beim Genießen einer endlich richtig kalten Wohnung! Wenn dir das Design gefällt, freue ich mich über ein Like und ein Bild deines Makes! ❄️

model_name: Muleta para niños con palo de escoba
description: Esta muleta para niños fue diseñada por Montmaker.3D, el diseño contempló la evaluación mecánica para el material PETG, dando como resultado que es recomendable imprimir en PETG o superior. Es importante resaltar que no deben modificar el archivo, si lo hacen no nos hacemos responsables por cualquier perjuicio ocasionado. Consideraciones de impresión: Material : PETG o Superior (No usar PLA). Usar TPU para la base. Descarga el .3mf y usa las configuraciones tal como se presentan ahi, si no tienes bambu studio, por favor, instalalo y adapta el modelo antes de imprimir, este modelo tiene modificadores que aseguran la rigidez. Personaliza con stickers, coloca mensajes de aliento, esto va para niños. Imprime SOLO si es necesario, siempre recomiendo usar una de aluminio, si no esta disponible usar esta temporalmente. Paso a paso: 1. Debes imprimir el aro para que asegures que el diametro del palo de escoba coincida con el modelo, en caso que no, reduce maximo un 2% del modelo, para incrementar el tamaño no hay problema. El diámetro correcto es el que ofrece fricción suficiente para moverlo, no debe quedar suelto. No imprimas el modelo sin hacer este paso, el modelo debe coincidir con el diámetro del palo que estes usando. No imprimas el modelo genericamente, ya que, el diametro no coincidirá. 2. Coloca la pieza de TPU abajo como si fuera una escoba normal, no es necesario apretar mas de lo suficiente. 3. Introduce la primera tuerca con la parte ancha hacia abajo y la parte fina hacia arriba, colocala a la altura del paciente (Proximamente mas recomendaciones de esto sobre las alturas). 4. Introduce el mango inferior. 5. Aprieta la tuerca gentilmente hasta que ya no gire gentilmente, luego girar 1/4" de vuelta con la mano, no usar herramientas, asegurate que no deslice. NO SOBRE APRIETES, SI SE DEZLIZA ES QUE NO SEGUISTE BIEN LAS RECOMENDACIÓN DEL PASO 1 6. Introduce la 2da tuerca tal como el paso #3. 7. Introcuce el mango superior. 8. Repite el paso 5. 9. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

The desired area MUST be painted using the Fuzzy Skin Painting tool in Bambu Studio. Without Fuzzy Skin Painting, the carbon fiber weave effect will NOT appear. Failure to follow these steps will result in the modifier having no visible effect. Create a realistic carbon fiber weave effect on your 3D prints using a reusable modifier. Unlike embossed textures, this method produces the appearance of woven carbon fiber directly during printing, creating a clean, premium finish without changing the original model geometry. Simply import the modifier into your slicer, position it over the desired surface, paint the desired area with Fuzzy Skin Painting , then slice and print. ✨ Features Realistic carbon fiber weave appearance Original model geometry remains unchanged Easy to position, rotate, and resize Reusable on multiple models Ideal for electronics cases, automotive accessories, tool organizers, display stands, and decorative parts 📖 How to Use Import your model into Bambu Studio . Add the supplied modifier. Position and scale the modifier over the desired surface. Paint the target area using Fuzzy Skin Painting . Slice and print. 📌 Notes The weave direction can be rotated to match your design. Multiple modifiers can be combined to cover larger surfaces. Only the selected area is affected; the rest of the model remains unchanged. The modifier can be reused on virtually any compatible model. ⚙️ Quick Setup Guide Follow these steps to apply the Carbon Fiber Weave effect. ① Import the Modifier Import your model into Bambu Studio . Add Carbon Fiber Modifier.stl as a Modifier . Position and scale the modifier to cover the desired area. Configure the modifier using the following settings: Fuzzy Skin : None (allow painting) ② Enable Fuzzy Skin Select the model (not the modifier), then go to: Objects → [Your Model] → Others → Fuzzy Skin Configure the following setting: Generator Mode : Displacement Noise Type : Classic Point Distance : 0.1 mm Thickness : 0.1 mm Important: Apply this setting to the model , not to Carbon Fiber Modifier.stl . ③ Paint the Desired Area Select the Fuzzy Skin Painting tool and paint only the surface where you want the carbon fiber weave effect to appear. ④ Slice and Print Slice and print the model as usual. The carbon fiber weave pattern will appear only on the painted area . ❤️ Share Your Prints If you create something using this modifier, I'd love to see your results. model_name: BikeBuddy – Compact Locking Bike Phone Mount (f3d)
description: Deutsche Version weiter unten. BikeBuddy – Compact Locking Bike Phone Mount Meet BikeBuddy: a deliberately tiny, spring-loaded phone mount that clamps onto your bike and politely refuses to let go. It was designed to sit flush and sleek on a VanMoof frame, but thanks to two interchangeable bases it adapts to just about any tube you point it at. At its core sits a printed spring mechanism that locks your phone in place with a satisfying click — and keeps it there over cobblestones, potholes, and the curbs you swore you'd avoid. KEY FEATURES • Compact, low-profile design — looks like it belongs on the bike, not bolted on as an afterthought • Printed spring + twist-lock mechanism: clicks in, stays in • Mount your phone in multiple orientations — portrait or landscape, your call • Two bases included: round and flat/square — for round tubes and flat frame sections • No exotic hardware: two cable ties, one M3 nut, one M3 countersunk screw COMPATIBILITY — PLEASE READ BikeBuddy is the mount only — the phone case is not included. It is built for one specific, very popular twist-lock bike phone case system. If you own that case (or a universal adapter for it), it clicks straight on. Not sure yours fits? Check the photos — if your case locks on the same way, you're good to go. This is an independent, community-made design. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by any phone-case or bicycle manufacturer. All trademarks are the property of their respective owners. WHAT YOU NEED (NOT PRINTED) • 2x cable ties (zip ties) • 1x M3 nut • 1x M3 countersunk (flat-head) screw — M3x16 for the round base, M3x22 for the flat base RECOMMENDED MATERIALS • Body: PLA-CF — stiff, dimensionally stable, clean matte finish. Heads-up: like all PLA it can soften in a hot car or direct summer sun. If your bike lives outdoors in the heat, print the body in PETG-CF, ASA or PA-CF instead. • Spring: PETG — softer and far more fatigue-resistant than PLA, so it flexes again and again without snapping. TPU would be even softer, but too soft for a crisp lock — PETG is the sweet spot. PRINT SETTINGS 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer height. Two ready-made print profiles are included in the download — just use them as provided. Everything is already correctly oriented for maximum quality, so no support juggling required. WANT TO ADAPT IT TO YOUR FRAME? Need the base as an editable Fusion 360 (.f3d) file to tweak it for your own bike? Just message me and I'll be happy to share it. ASSEMBLY Assembly is genuinely simple — you can follow it straight from the photos. 1. Assemble all the parts as shown. 2. Hold everything together with the M3 countersunk screw and M3 nut. 3. description: 64-Slot Large Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets This is a large round Kumihimo disc featuring 64 slots for strings to make complex high string-count round bracelets with up to 40 strings, using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. A 64-slot Kumihimo disc is typically used for weaves with more than 16 strings at a time as the complexity of keeping track of the strings increases if they are too densely packed together. The below picture shows the disc with a 24-string pattern using 12 different colors at the same time to create the large pattern. The disc has 64 marked notches to hold the strings in place and allowing to easily make high string-count weaves through the rounded circle slot in the center for the Kumihimo weaving pattern to form. The notches are labelled 1-64 and additionally the notches are marked every 16th slot with a large dot to indicate starting points for 8-string weaves (at16, 32, 48 and 64), as well as every 8th slot in between for 16-string weaves with a smaller circle (at 8,24, 40 and 56), as well as every 4th slot in between the 16- and 8-slot markers for 32-string weaves with a small diamond dot (at 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, 52 and 60). The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels and markings. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. I recommend a string diameter of up to 2mm in thickness (pictured above are a mix of 1mm an 2mm strings). Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. Save your charging cables from entanglements. This project explores the idea of using a simple shape to produce an accessory that is useful both in function and in form. My design philosophy is simple and human centered design. This project is a continuation in exploring this philosophy. The C-Cable Sleeve is designed with the traveler and commuter in mind. When transitioning between different environments, we depend on various electronic devices to guide us along the way. The C-Cable Sleeve protects and secures the life line that keeps these electronic devices operational. This ensures we never go blind while transitioning between different environments. I commute a lot and had problems with my charging cables tangling in my bag and pockets. Some have prematurely stop working because they were severely kinked breaking down the cables internal conductive wires. This left me with a non functional cable leading to my phone battery exhausted during my travels. That awful experience inspired the C-Cable Sleeve project. The C-Cable is a storage solution that keeps cables neat and secure. The circular shape is easy to hold and the slide cover mechanism allows for easy access and stow when finish. The C-Cable Sleeve is a result of my main design philosophy of simple and human centered design. With my design philosophy in mind, I started with a simple C shape to be the foundation to build upon. The letter C has a gap that is ideal to slide cables through. By layering two C shapes together, the gaps in both C can be opened and closed by a simple rotation. The human centered design features affordances and signifiers that provides ease of use. The various ridges along the device supports the rotating of the cover. The long exposed gap at one end of the device is a pinch point to easily spin the cover if there is too much resistance in movement. More Information There are currently three options of the C-Cable Sleeve available. There is an option for a standard 3-6ft charging cable, ethernet cable, and PC/Laptop power cord. The design is also scalable in bambu studio for a custom sizing. Therefore the C-Cable Sleeve is adaptable to secure any size cable. Each version are in separate print profiles to help reduce confusion. Each print profile is labeled for the available option. I made to different sizes as an option. description: A replacement end piece for the exhaust hose of portable air conditioners that use a 150 mm spiral hose . Unlike most stock end pieces — which only have a couple of short ribs and tend to slip off the hose — this one has a continuous helical thread . You simply screw it on and it stays put. The flat, wide outlet is made to slide through window seal covers (the zip-up "AirLock" type) and into the gap between the open window and the frame. Because it's fully parametric , you can dial it in to your exact hose and window in the Customize panel — no CAD needed. Why you might want this It holds. A real screw thread grips the hose all the way around, so it won't pull out under the weight or movement of the hose. Fits tight windows. Set the slot depth to match your window gap; the wide flat outlet keeps the airflow cross-section up so the AC doesn't choke. Optional retainer ring that wedges the tip behind the seal's zipper so it can't slide back out. Adapts to other hoses. Expose the thread pitch, diameter and direction — works for many 150 mm-class spiral hoses, not just one brand. How to use the Customizer Measure your hose: outer diameter over the spiral ribs, and the pitch (rib-to-rib spacing — easiest is to measure across 5 ribs and divide by 5). Set Hose Outer Diameter , Thread Pitch and Tightening Direction (many AC hoses tighten left / counter-clockwise — check yours). Set Slot Width and Slot Depth to your window. Turn the Retainer Ring on if you want it to lock into the seal zipper. Print a test ring first: set Thread Turns to 1–1.5, print just the collar (a few minutes) and check it screws onto your hose cleanly and in the right direction. Then bump Thread Turns back to 3 and print the full part. Recommended print settings Material: PETG (the exhaust air is warm and the part may sit in sunlight — PLA can soften and sag). 0.2 mm layers (or 0.28 mm for a faster draft — the thread works fine at 0.28). 4–5 walls, ~20–30 % infill, no supports needed (overhangs are shallow). Brim recommended for bed adhesion. The model is already oriented print-ready (flat outlet face on the bed). Compatibility Designed and field-tested for the 150 mm spiral exhaust hose of the Proklima GPC12AN (Bauhaus). The measured hose is Ø ≈ 150.8 mm over the ribs, 16 mm pitch, left-hand. Many other portable-AC hoses in the 150 mm class are similar — measure yours and adjust the thread parameters to match.

This is a no-drill, no-damage organizer that slides over the edge of a shelf, cabinet door, drawer front, or partition and grips it by friction. Everything is adjustable in the MakerWorld customizer: - **Panel Fit** — set the exact thickness of the edge you are clamping, plus a grip clearance for an easy slide-on fit. The back lip drops down behind the panel to stop the holder from tipping forward under load. - **Hook** — choose how far the hook reaches out and how tall the upturned lip is so items do not slide off. - **Body** — set the overall width and wall thickness for the strength you need. - **Discrete Hooks** — optionally split the front into several separate hook fingers across the width (great for keys, cables, or utensils) instead of one continuous ledge. Measure your edge and add ~0.4–0.6 mm clearance for a snug slide-on fit; reduce clearance or add a strip of tape for a tighter grip. - `back_drop` longer = more anti-tip leverage for heavier items. - `hook_up = 0` gives a flat shelf instead of a hook. - Enable `split_hooks` and set `hook_count` for multiple separate fingers. - For a non-marring, higher-grip version, print in TPU or line the inside of the clamp with a thin strip of foam tape.

description: Use a small amount of lubricant oil for a smoother experience and longer a longer spin time. Lubricant oil tubes are included with all Bambu Labs printers. I’ve done it -- I’ve finally made the perfect 3D-Printed Bearing. It uses 8 carefully crafted and prototyped rollers to evenly distribute the force when rotating , making this bearing much smoother than a standard joint. Most bearings you see out and about are ball bearings , but there is one big problem when it comes to 3d printing ball bearings . You can never get a perfect ball because layers are steps and the steps are short in the middle, but at the ends they are big . That is why I opted for roller bearings but these rollers just clump together at one side so I had to design a cage for them. The shape of the roller fits perfectly in into the inner and outer shell , keeping them in place . The cage is those pieces that you see in between the rollers but it is not that simple . They are all connected together with engineered bridging and other fancy tricks . The main reason why this was so challenging is because this fidget is entirely print in place . That means that it requires no external hardware or assembly , allowing you to just pop it off the build plate and start spinning . After over 50 versions of this model, it is finally done and It truly deserves the title of ‘Ultimate’ . It has a clean aesthetic, with an interesting pattern spread across the sides and top, making it perfect for fidgeting with and keeping on display when not in use. Taking under 57 minutes and 15.02 grams of filament to print, this fidget bearing is ideal for anyone who enjoys a smooth yet compact spinner. Membership Want to sell my 3D printed fidget toys? Membership Want to join an exclusive community and get early access to prints like this one and get commercial sales licenses? Join my membership The Ultimate Players Kit just got a huge upgrade. I've taken quite a bit of community feedback and transformed the Ultimate Players Kit into something truly special: an ancient tome guarding the knowledge of your character. Included is: A leather sculpted exterior No more arachne wheels Stats with included modifiers and saving throws Gold tracker Wider and deeper dice slots Plus it just looks cool as heck Class insignias for decoration Assembly Instructions Assemble the outer cover Using filament for the hinge pins, link the top cover to the spine, then the spine to the bottom cover. Add Connectors to the cover insides Using the included tool, attach the connectors to the insides of the covers. It is important that you add the connectors to the covers first, and not to the tray and tracker inserts. Add the inserts Snap in the tray to the bottom cover, then the tracker frame to the top cover, taking care that the untextured side of them both face into the spine. Add the corner decorations Using a drop or two of CA glue (super glue) or hot glue, affix the corner decorations. The decorations with only one lip goes on the spine side, and the decorations with corner lips go on the outside. Add your insignia I highly recommend using hot glue/hot melt for this. It will make for easier changing when you want to play a new character. Add the lock mechanisms The lock prints with in place supports that need to be removed (see pictures). Once removed, the receiver (the part of the lock without the prongs) gets added to the tray (bottom). Similar to the cover, add the connectors to the lock, then clip the lock to the frame. Be sure to attach the receiver so that the opening faces upwards (towards the clasp) Add the clasp to the tracker frame in a similar fashion to the receiver (connectors into the part, then clip the part to the tracker frame.) Be sure that when adding the clasp, the prongs are facing downwards towards the receiver. Finally, add the decoration to the locks. Build the trackers There are 8 slots for trackers, but only 7 rods. This is intentional, because I have left an open slot for customization in the future. The top half holds the stats, which gets 4 rods, and the bottom half holds skills which get 3 rods. Please see the model photos for which wheels go in which place. I highly recommend using a pick to micro adjust the wheels to get a nice fitment. It is important to note: the panels that cover the wheels are over sized. This is intentional. Because of the print orientation, they have quite a bit of flex allowed and they act as pins to hold the rods in place once assembled. Once all of the tracker wheels are on the rods, it is time to add the panels on top of them. This is the most fiddly, frustrating bit, but take heart: They do fit and it is very satisfying when they do. Print Settings I highly recommend using my print profiles rather than the STLs. I have done a lot of supports painting and speed changed for the metal parts. The wheel geometry has been re-worked so that arachne wall generation is no longer necessary. The covers and spine were designed to be printed standing upwards for optimal resolution of the texture. The rods should be printed with ~30% infill. This is to stop them flexing too much when spanning large gaps. The snap connector holes on the trays do not need supports. The lock mechanism has included supports in the model. A1 Mini Users This is likely going to be a challenging print for A1M. I recommend slowing your printer down and having a super clean plate: washed with hot water and dawn dish soap. Please also monitor your first layer and slow your print speed for the very tall prints. Upgrading from v2/v3 Most of the parts in this one are not compatible with v2/v3. However I took special caution when designing the windows for the wheels to keep them the same size as the previous version because the wheels are the most time intensive parts to print. As such, the wheels from v2/v3 will fit in this version The rods are slightly wider in diameter, so expect a tight fit, but width wise they do work (I have tested it myself.) I do highly recommend printing a new set of wheels however, the inner geometry has been reinforced for a more clicky wheel with less plastic deformation. Make sure the print bed is clean, so that the components do not have adhesion problems. Use the recommended materials. I'll be more than happy to see what crazy color combinations you can come up with XD, I therefore kindly ask you to post pictures of the printed toy in the comments:) During printing: Make sure the first three layers are printed correctly (serious errors often occur in the first layer). If you use a bed slinger , slow down the print speed to prevent tall components from falling. Check on your printer every now and then to make sure everything is running smoothly. Once the printer is finished, don't remove the components immediately, but wait 5-10 minutes for them to cool . Removing them too quickly will cause slight deformation of the PLA, which could cause problems with the toy's operation. After printing: Gently remove the supports and make sure the brim is completely removed. Some supports require a little more force and patience to remove, even if optimized. For part 26_PLA it is essential, to ensure accurate operation, that the top surface (the green one) that rests on the supports is smooth after their removal. Therefore any remaining support must be removed. Use the following tutorial to assemble the toy. For assembly it is recommended/necessary to use the following tools: Tweezers are required/recommended to insert the filament pieces and remove any supports Superglue is required to glue the parts together as shown in the tutorial Scissors are needed to cut the pieces of filament to the appropriate length Using the toy: Although it is purely a toy, it is necessary to know how to use and handle it correctly. While I've spent a lot of time designing this toy, it's not perfect , and as a result, malfunctions may occasionally occur . Here's a list of potential malfunctions and possible fixes: In this case, component 6_PLA (it's like a flap), which should lock the second cartridge, fails, causing the second cartridge to also be loaded and thus block the toy from functioning. This error can be caused by several factors, including a defect in component 6_PLA that causes it to be incorrectly bent (due to improper gluing or damage caused during handling), or a problem with the magazine spring, which, if overly tense, pushes the cartridge too hard, eventually bending the part. The solution is to temporarily remove the trigger assembly to bend component 6_PLA slightly inward (therefore towards the opposite), but not too much, so that it can still assume the retracted position during the toy operation. Particular care must be taken not to bend it too much, and especially not to bend it without pressing on the glued section, which, if not done, can cause the glue to fail. This error can be very annoying if the cartridges are loaded, as it often causes the projectile to break inside the barrel. I haven't yet fully clarified the circumstances under which this can happen. The few times it happened to me was when holding the toy tilted too far to the right. If you find this malfunction occurring too often, I'll release a new version of the 26_PLA component (the carrier) that should fix the problem. General maintenance of parts/components Being a plastic toy, this model can break if used too aggressively. Therefore, I recommend handling it with care. Since the model is made of plastic, 3D-printed parts like springs or flaps tend to deform if left under tension for a long time. Therefore, to preserve the correct functioning of the toy as much as possible, it is recommended to remove the trigger group when not playing with the toy, and position the handle as shown in the figure (in partially loaded position). model_name: Lever Action Blaster | Working Slingshot Toy
description: This model is a low-power, custom-built toy blaster of my own original design . Ensured to have no internal functionality related to actual complicated gas powered, dangerous mechanisms, methods of modifying them, or inclusion of similar parts or aesthetics. This is strictly a slingshot mechanism , that is tensioned by a lever and connected by snap joints. Functionally and aesthetically, it is the equivalent of a foam dart blaster. All future projects strictly follow these standards, and I will now communicate this directly, not indirectly. — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — [ " Reaper-26" | Lever Action Blaster ] [ Assembly tutorial, More showcases, and rubber band sizes below ] After 4 months of designing and the headache of 100+ reprinted parts from failed tests, I am glad to finally share my hard work here, free of charge, of course. I am finally glad to get this off my back. I will try to upload another model in… 2-3 weeks?…. As long as everything works. This lever action blaster, which I have named the Reaper-26 , is a fully functional toy slingshot powered by rubber bands. I designed this to give a satisfying process of individual round loading and a lever action mechanism that makes handling it a satisfying process, even outside of launching toy bullets. The video below will demonstrate the satisfying clicking sounds the blaster makes when loading. Showcase and Assembly Video: Please watch the last 30 seconds of the video, it contains essential information about how to load it. Improper loading can cause jams and not allow more prop bullets to be inserted. For those who do not have access to YouTube, I am in the process of making an instruction PDF in 2-3 days, these take a lot of effort, almost as much as the video itself. List of features I want to highlight: Individual round loading An internal magazine, that stores fake bullets in the lower barrel. Fake bullet storage on the stock, allowing quick reloads after you empty the internal toy magazine Adjustable and variable rubber band hooks, which I implemented so that many different rubber band diameters can work (I hope this helps with accessibility). The slingshot, magazine, and trigger rubber bands can all be accessed externally without taking the whole thing apart , which is an improvement from my previous model. Unlike traditional bullet launching devices, this toy blaster is 65% more effective because it utilizes the entire projectile, rather than leaving the cartridge to waste. Distance: Averaging from various tests from eye level: 5.0-5.7 Meters 16-18 Feet The launching distance is the same as the my former Deagle. If yours does not reach this distance, then you need stronger bands or they are getting caught and causing friction. Thick rubber bands give more power, please don't use very thin ones. I saw a lot of people do that on my last model… Rubber bands used: Just because I used these exact ones doesn't mean you have to. In fact, these were just lying around my house, so maybe yours could perform even better. The rubber bands attached as part of the Makers Supply are as close to the dimensions as possible. Slingshot, trigger, and magazine feeder rubber bands (Blue) Height - 3-4mm Diameter - 50mm 5-7 rubber bands, with 3-5 being on the slingshot Internal feeder rubber band (Purple) Height - 1.5mm Diameter - 40mm One rubber band used I primarily designed this model to be as accessible as possible . It only requires rubber bands and one spool; every part snaps or slots together without the requirement of glue or screws . The snap joints allow you to disassemble the blaster whenever you want by using a lot of force. There are no permanent joints, but they are strong enough to where you cannot break them unintentionally. The project is for those seeking a more sophisticated and functional model with many parts. The assembly is a hands-on and enjoyable process in itself. If you enjoy working with intricate projects, snapping and slotting parts together, or building, then you will find the assembly enjoyable like I did. Membership Earn a stream of revenue and stand out from the crowd by selling my unique and interactive model for a premium, start now by signing up for my commercial license. Custom Toy Attachments: I loved how there were people on my former model who would tweak the parts aesthetically or functionality, and I want to support that. There is currently a snap joint on the top rail that can suit an attachment. I uploaded one design of my own as a print profile. But if you want to make one yourself and upload it, there is a file of the rail attachment piece, that you can easily add a model of whatever you want to. Once you are done, you can attach it as a print profile for others to try out! Reward the points to yourself, not me. Miscellaneous: The project unfortunately is too large to be printed with the A1 mini , I promise any dedicated A1 mini users that my next model will be supported by it, I plan to upload it soon in the near future (2-3 weeks if my idea works easily). I would like to thank @luca_dilo for the targets , I used his target print profile for his “Spring Gun V3” and they turned great. Go check him and his models out! These targets were actually my first ever multicolor print. By downloading, printing, or utilizing this design, you agree to the following terms and conditions: I assume no liability or responsibility for any injury, damage, or loss resulting from inappropriate use of the toy. Users accept all risks and responsibility associated with the design, and release the creator and platform from any claims or liabilities arising. Do not shoot or aim at people, pets, or cowboys without their permission (good luck getting it from your dog) Even though it is a toy, like most toys, it still poses danger to your eyes, so exercise caution. Do not look into the barrel, even if you think nothing is inside of it. Keep out of reach for children under 6 years old. The small parts could present a choking hazard. Treat this blaster legally as an airsoft or foam gun, and follow any regulations or local laws regarding them. This includes private property requirements or printing the barrel in orange. — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — Things that can go wrong on your end and the solutions: Last time 20k people downloaded my former model, and at that scale there might be issues or missed steps for some. So, I want to improve the process by adding this section here. These are all the potential issues I can think of or have occurred to me in the past 4 months of designing. This is a complicated model so these might not be intuitive. Jams or cannot be loaded The projectile slips out when pushing back or unresponsive trigger Weak/no launching -You inserted the toy bullets in a way where they are angled slightly, and they are getting caught on something. When loading, make sure they get straightly positioned and resting on the elevator wall - The magazine tension is too strong (can also cause angled projectiles) - The loading door is not properly going back (The band is weak or broken) and is getting caught - You are not fully moving the lever into place ← too much tension can cause this - You are attempting to load while there is already a projectile in tension - Loading too quickly or aggressively -The trigger tension is too low and cannot hold the projectile in place while it is tensioned, or it does not have enough strength to go back into place -The trigger insert came out a little bit and the transfer bar is uneven. This can also cause an unresponsive trigger -There is already a projectile hidden improperly inside the barrel. Hold the trigger and shake to drop it out (this happens to me) - Way too much slingshot tension -The strength and number of your bands are the biggest factor, thin bands might not be strong enough to fire. - The bands are rubbing against the sides - You just need to add more, ideally you want 4-5 bands that extend to the furthest hook for maximum acceleration - You are not pulling the lever back into place - There is something hidden in the barrel (this happens to me) Also if you ever encounter any jams, removing the rubber bands on the slingshot easily loosens everything up. Rubber bands breaking: Use thicker rubber bands, I have been using this model consistently and tested it to ensure no breakage. Parts not joining well: Different printers and colors can cause size variation, which is frustrating as a designer, but I have added elements to prevent this. For the best chances to get your parts like mine, print yours in the same color. A P1S is also how I printed mine incase you have one. I hope this helps facilitate the process, if you are encountering a different error, please double check your assembly or print quality . But if you have a genuine issue, you can DM me and will be glad to help if you double checked everything. Thank you to everyone that prints this project!!! Photos of your prints are appreciated, I see every one of them and I am curious what you think! ( I only see a lifeless download statistic if you don't) Also please thank my girlfriend in the comments for helping me write/edit the description, and for helping out with other parts of the project. She would love to see them! I love creating models to share for free If you like my work here, and want to support me, you can tip on my By Me A Coffee page
