description: H2 Series Multi-Mount System | FTS, TPU Feed Assist & Modular Spool System A modular mounting system for H2 Series printers that combines the Filament Track Switch, TPU Feed Assist, and interchangeable spool system into a single mounting platform. Includes an editable Shapr3D source file and multiple spool hub sizes. Designed to minimize supports, reduce print time, and adapt to different printer layouts. Why I Made This As more accessories become available for the H2 Series printers, users are often forced to choose between mounting a Filament Track Switch, TPU Feed Assist, external spool holder, or other accessories because they all compete for the same mounting location. I wanted a cleaner solution that would allow multiple accessories to share a single mounting point while remaining completely modular and adaptable to different setups. The result is the H2 Series Multi-Mount System. Compatible With - H2C - H2D - H2S Features: - Supports Filament Track Switch mounting - Supports TPU Feed Assist mounting - Modular spool system - Multiple Filament Track Switch mounting orientations - Vertical, horizontal, and angled FTS mounting options - Adjustable mounting positions for improved PTFE routing - Interchangeable spool hubs - Optimized for minimal supports - Includes editable Shapr3D source file - Designed for future expansion and customization What's Included - STL files - 3MF print profile - STEP file - Editable Shapr3D source file Modular Design This system was designed so you only print the components you need. The Filament Track Switch can be mounted vertically, horizontally, or at an angle depending on your AMS placement and filament routing requirements. The spool system uses a locking hub design that allows spool hubs to be quickly installed, removed, or exchanged. Included spool hub sizes: - 50 mm - 70 mm - 110 mm The modular architecture also allows future accessories and custom modifications to be added without redesigning the entire system. Editable Shapr3D File Included This project includes the original editable Shapr3D source file. Modify mounting locations, create custom accessories, adjust spool sizes, or expand the system to fit your own workflow. New to CAD? Try Shapr3D here: https://link.shapr3d.com/make A free version is available, making it easy to learn, customize, and create your own modifications. Recommended Print Settings Material: - PETG Recommended Support Material: - PLA Support Interfaces Recommended This design was intentionally broken into separate modular components and optimized to be printed with minimal supports. Only a few small interface areas require support material, making cleanup quick and easy while significantly reducing print time. PETG is recommended due to its increased heat resistance and durability around the printer environment. Installation Notes The Filament Track Switch uses the hardware included in the printer accessory bag labeled “For Extruder.” A complete assembly and installation video is included and demonstrates: - TPU Feed Assist installation - Modular spool holder assembly - Filament Track Switch mounting options - Installation onto the printer If you build one, I'd love to see how you've customized it for your setup. description: 🧩 COMPONENTS OF THE BENCHMARK – ACCURATE EXPLANATION 📍 THE SPIKES Vertical needles that test whether the printer can print VERY small details . ✔ If they remain straight and sharp = stable printer ❌ If they bend or become rounded = vibration or precision problem 📐 THE ANGLED OVERHANGS First overhang: 5°, 15°, 25°, 35°, 45°, 55°, 65°, 75° Second overhang: 10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°, 80° They test how well the filament can hold its shape without supports at different angles. ➡ When an overhang starts to collapse or ripple = that is the limit of your printer ✨ If it stays perfect = the printer can go even further ⚙️ THE FOUR CALIBRATABLE FEET These are the parts you can rotate labeled 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 . They test the printer’s tolerance . ✔ If a foot does NOT move = the printer is precise at that level ❌ If it moves easily = it cannot reach that level of precision 📏 THE SMALL CYLINDERS AND THE LABELS The labels ( 20.5, 15.5, 10.5, 5.5 ) indicate the intended size of the cylinders. ✔ If the cylinder matches the exact size = dimensional accuracy is correct ❌ If it is larger or smaller = calibration issue

(Veja o guia abaixo de como personalizar no fatiador). ✍️ Como Personalizar a sua Tira de Texto no Bambu Studio Criar uma placa com o seu nome ou frase personalizada é extremamente simples e não requer nenhum software externo de modelagem 3D: 1. Abra o projeto no Bambu Studio e vá até a Placa Personalize sua Escrita. 2. Clique com o botão direito sobre a tira em branco, selecione Add Part (Adicionar Parte) e depois Text (Texto). 3. No menu de texto, digite o nome ou a frase desejada (ex: "PRESIDENTE FIEL", "RESERVA DO TIMÃO" ou o seu próprio nome). 4. Ajuste a fonte, altere o tipo para Emboss (Relevo) e defina a espessura para que as letras fiquem saltadas (cerca de 1mm a 1.5mm é o ideal para o encaixe perfeito). 5. Posicione o texto centralizado sobre a placa, selecione a cor desejada usando o seu filamento (como o branco para contrastar com a base preta) e pronto! Aqueça a mesa da sua impressora (build plate) a 80°C. 2. Deixe o símbolo ou a sua tira de frase personalizada sobre a mesa aquecida por 1 a 2 minutos. 3. Assim que o plástico amolecer levemente, retire-o com cuidado e molde-o diretamente contra o corpo curvo da caneca ou da base. 4. Segure na posição por alguns segundos até esfriar para que o filamento memorize o formato curvo. description: Hello, I'm Lee, and I'd like to share my design for a side-mounted enclosed Dry Box for the Centauri Carbon 2. I have really enjoyed my new CC2, but I have always felt that it was lacking an enclosed MFS. I felt like all my filament was getting dusty and absorbing moisture. So, I visited all the maker websites looking for a solution, but I found that most designs were somewhat lacking or cumbersome to use. After coming up short in my search, I decided to make one myself. This design is mostly airtight and can maintain humidity levels at least 15% to 20% lower than the surrounding environment. It utilizes the existing retracting spools and mounting points, and I also tried to preserve the printer's unique design and aesthetic. It took a lot of effort and time, but I am quite proud of the outcome. I designed every piece to print without supports and tried to make assembly as easy as possible. Almost everything screws together, and glue is used only as a sealant, not for structural strength. I have included a customizable plate to hold a hygrometer, and I designed the enclosure to mount to the side of the printer so it does not need to be disassembled for routine maintenance or when the printer needs to be moved. With all that being said, I've decided to share this design for free, and I hope you all love it as much as I do. Update: I added a version for the Centauri Carbon 1. I don't own one of these printers so please verify mounting locations before printing. I found a very accurate model of it online so it should be good. I added new instructions but the only difference between the 2 is the mounting locations of the main body. Features All parts of this model are designed to print without supports and were printed in PLA. All pieces screw together, and glue is used only for sealing purposes, not structural support. The box mounts to the side of the CC2 using the existing spool retraction mounting holes. It is designed with two large desiccant boxes to help keep filament clean and dry. Many of the parts require a multi-filament system to print the graphical designs, but they can also be printed without one. Assembly instructions are attached. model_name: X2D Dual AMS 2 Pro Glass Riser
description: No supports, no glue, no screws, only about 1.1kg of filament, and 2 days of print time! I wanted something simple that raised the glass and got my 2 AMS 2 Pro units off of my desk. This is what I came up with… This is by far the largest model I have created to date. I recently purchased the X2D and wanted a place to mount my 2 AMS 2 Pro units. I also was very annoyed by the sound the PTFE tubes made hitting the glass all the time. This riser raises the glass by 18mm which, for me, has provided more than enough clearance to solve the anoying clicking sound and prevent wear on my tubes. My final product ended up with a bit more sag in the middle than I was hoping for, but I am very happy with its strength. I am not using any glue or fasteners. The way this thing is designed, it will not dissassemble itself unless something was to fail. I could probably get some sag out if I glued the parts together, but I want to be able to take it apart and make improvements in the future without having to repint the whole thing! Besides, I don't think these AMS units are going anywhere. There is a depression for the feet to prevent them from walking off the edge. I have run about 50 hours of prints since I put this thing up and it is holding up well so far. During design, I printed some parts of an earlier version on my A1 and the parts fit together VERY tightly. Without changing the tolerances of the model, my final version was printed 100% on the X2D. These final parts fit together with a bit more wiggle room. While this can probably be partially (or majorially) attributed to the difference between a bed slinger and a core xy machine, I think this is also a good example of the differences you might experience from printer to printer. I am happy knowing that even with two different machines, I am able to put the thing together successfully. The sides are SKADIS boards because I was lacking creativity and thought this was a decent solution for accessories storage. The boards are at 45 degrees so you will have to pick and choose what you use accordingly, but this is the 3D printing community after all - if what you want doesn't exist just create it! There is a little pin that gets inserted in the front corner brackets to hold the SKADIS boards in place when taking things on and off of it. The parts are numbered to assist with assembly and I would be happy to provide instructions for assembly if needed, but it is honestly very self explanitory. The parts only go together one way. However, I will say the last things to go on are the supports that go front to back (blue in my printed version). I assembled the glass riser first, put in the TPU gaskets, built the front rail, then the back rail, connected them with the SKADIS boards, connected them with the front to back supports, then slid the whole thing down onto the sides of the glass riser. If you plan to use glue, I would certainly recommend making sure you understand how everything goes together first!

Präzisions-Gießaufsatz für Glasflaschen Verwandle nahezu jede Glasflasche in eine praktische Gießhilfe für Zimmerpflanzen, Kräuter oder Jungpflanzen. Der Aufsatz wurde für viele in Deutschland erhältliche Glasflaschen mit Schraubverschluss entwickelt. Je nach Flaschentyp passt er auch auf verschiedene Kunststoffflaschen mit vergleichbarer Gewindegröße. Besonderheit Im Gegensatz zu einer klassischen Gießkanne gibt dieser Aufsatz das Wasser nicht dauerhaft frei. Die Wasserabgabe erfolgt durch Kippen und leichtes Schütteln der Flasche. Dadurch entsteht ein feiner Sprüh- bzw. Gießeffekt, der besonders für empfindliche Pflanzen, Jungpflanzen, Kräuter und kleine Pflanzgefäße geeignet ist. Nicht nur für Pflanzen Der feine Sprühnebel eignet sich auch hervorragend zur Erfrischung an heißen Sommertagen. Einfach eine Glasflasche mit Wasser füllen, den Aufsatz aufschrauben und durch leichtes Schütteln einen angenehmen Wassernebel erzeugen. Ideal für Garten, Terrasse, Sport, Spaziergänge oder unterwegs. description: A First of its Kind Exclusive Model designed to improve your AMS 2 Pro Storage!!! Featuring a new split design, the back end of this bracket has specialized holes designed for a washer and screw and may be mounted directly into your studs or drywall, and features a channel running up the back for a set of skadis pins. Also introducing a new size ! In addition to the standard size mount, the new Wide bracket not only has the benefit of being able to be closely stacked with another mounted AMS to allow you to still lift the lid of the bottom unit, it has the added benefit of allowing you to mount each side of the mount directly into wood studs behind drywall for a super secure hold on the wall! This is a great choice if you have limited space or are mounting these side by side with another bracket. When mounting the standard size in drywall, I recommend mounting one side into studs, and using strong anchors in the other side. A full AMS weighs roughly 50lbs, please use appropriate anchors. Each of these brackets have ample cable and ptfe tube clearance behind them. WIDE SIZE : Fits under and wide around the AMS and mounts across 21 skadis holes. and DOES have clearance to open another ams mounted underneath provided you are properly spacing the AMS units on your skadis board or wall. This is a great choice to “stack” your AMS units vertically to save space. Additionally, the screw holes on this unit are about 416mm across which if your house was built correctly, should center your screws almost perfectly on two studs ensuring a super secure hold on your wall. Each of these brackets have ample cable and ptfe tube clearance behind them. Each part and build plate in the design is labeled and color coded for ease of use, the skadis pins are compatible with each bracket, but need to be installed on the back ends, they will not provide proper cable clearance if you do not use the back end pieces. If you are wall mounting your bracket, you do not need to print the skadis pins. PARTS : I designed the holes on the bracket to be used with a #8 washer and #10 screws, the screws i recommend should be FLAT HEAD and 3" to 3-½" long. You want to make sure you have proper clearance to drill into your drywall and studs to have a secure fit. Washers MUST BE USED and please do not overtighten the screws, this is just plastic afterall. I have also included a template for your wall to mark out and level your ams. this is a two piece design, with minimal walls and infill, only to be used as a wall template to properly line up holes. please print this plate, and tape the two pieces together, and the inside holes line up with the standard bracket, and outside holes line up with the wide bracket. A word of note when choosing colors for this mount, if you are printing with a multicolor or gradient filament, since the parts do not all build at the same time or on the same plate, the lines or color shift will not line up on the final product and may look silly to you, I recommend using a solid color to print this. CUSTOMIZABLE DIY FILAMENT/BOOK SHELF SEVERAL RISER OPTIONS CUSTOMIZE TO FIT YOUR SPACE NOTE: REQUIRES SOME WORK WITH WOOD As part of my new print room, I designed this DIY shelf system to maximize the space I had available for my filament storage dry boxes and keep them organized. At the same time l wanted something truly unique and nice to look at. I decided to share it here in case others want to try it themselves. Please read all of the information and the attached instructions before starting. Overall, it may not be a huge cost savings compared to an Ikea or other purchasable bookshelf (though the larger it is the more it will save), but being able to make it the exact length and height you want is not possible with those options. Plus, the looks of this are so much better IMO. The riser options include: Diamondplate Pattern Lattice Pattern Square & Compass Vertical Bolts (these are only recommended for middle risers) FYI If you are interested in the filament labels or drybox kits shown in the pictures, you can find them here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1193463-filament-labels-with-logos https://makerworld.com/en/models/2561229-4l-dry-box-kit-for-outer-spool-desiccant-trays ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ PURCHASED PARTS SHELVES The shelves themselves are made of ¾” wood and the risers are designed to fit a shelf depth of 234mm (9-3/8”). Your shelf length will be whatever length you want for your needs (more on that in the instructions below). This means you can source the shelving a number of different ways. Buy standard ¾” shelf boards and trim them to size. The ends are covered and the back not visible so you could get them pre-finished if you can make clean cuts. Buy a ¾” MDF sheet and cut or have the hardware store cut to the correct depth and whatever length you decide, then paint as needed. This is the option I chose. Buy a ¾” plywood sheet and cut or have the hardware store cut to the correct depth and whatever length you decide. Then you would need to add edging to the front edge to cover the layer lines before painting. HARDWARE Threaded wood inserts – ¼” or M6 x ¾” or 20mm (9) Inserts are required PER SHELF I used these: https://a.co/d/0hchaaFy Flattened or Button Head Screws – ¼”x1-1/2” or M6x35 (18) screws per intermediate shelf, (9) screws per top and bottom shelf I used these: https://a.co/d/00rvAgmG IF you are going to use the Square and Compass Risers, you will also need (4) M5 heat press inserts (any length up to 12mm max) and (4) M5x20mm Socket Head Screws PER RISER to connect the pieces together. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PRINTED PARTS You will need the following printed parts from the print profile of your choice: RISERS – Selection and quantity are up to you. Generally, you will need 2 risers per shelf and if you feel it needs a middle riser. Bolt Risers are only recommended as a middle riser and require 3 per riser. Square and Compass Risers include 3 pieces per riser that need assembled – main riser, top, and bottom. RISER CONNECTORS – These slide onto the shelf and connect to the risers. You will need 2 side connectors (and 1 middle connector if you chose a middle riser) per shelf. The top shelf has special Top Riser Connectors. Bolt Risers do not need any Riser Connectors but are only recommended as a middle riser. BOLT SPACERS – These get bolted to the shelves to interconnect the risers and riser connectors. You will need the same quantity as the screws – 18 per intermediate shelf, 9 per top and bottom shelf. FEET - You can attach any feet of your liking to the bottom using the ¼" threaded holes. The ones in the picture which I recommend I had previously released here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2498728-hd-adjustable-leveling-foot Now let’s talk about print orientation. There are 2 print profiles – one with the risers and connectors oriented flat on the bed, and one with risers and connectors oriented vertically. Depending on your filament of choice, printing orientation will change how the color looks. Square & Compass Risers and Bolt Risers must be printed vertically unless you are willing to get creative with supports. Vertical printing creates a higher resolution but is much more challenging to print. The hardest part with vertical printing is the Riser Connectors because the opening for the shelf requires supports. You can use a special support material but this adds layer time which can cause a “benchy hull” line from the big difference in layer time. Not using special support material (like I didn’t) creates a rough interface. Not too big of a deal since it is sitting flat against the shelf, but I had to make little trim pieces to cover the exposed outer edge. Those are included if you need them. If you like the look or the filament color doesn't change, another option would be to print the risers vertically and the connectors flat. This would be kind of the “best of both worlds”. I chose a shiny filament, so orientation made a big difference in the color. Here is a comparison of the two print orientations: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- FILAMENT SELECTION The majority of the loading is in compression (buckling) so material requirements aren’t too bad. I recommend a MINIMUM of a PLA+ that has decent impact strength. A good Tough PLA+ like the one Bambu has, Sunlu’s PLA+ 2.0, or Polymaker Polylite PLA PRO would be decent options. I would avoid basic matte or silk PLA’s as their brittleness and layer adhesion may not make it appropriate. PETG will generally hold up a little better but is more difficult to print. I chose Tinmorry Space Grey Metallic PETG because it gave me a nice “steel” look and I printed vertically. Seams and retraction were a big challenge however and took me a couple tries. I have attached the assembly instruction and basic assembly dimensions. Length is based on the one I built and fit the dry boxes shown in the pictures perfectly, but you can adjust to the length you want for your needs. Thank you and if you decide to do this project, I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

description: TIP: Make several insertions and removals of the half nuts in your hand before you do the actual installation, it will break-in the joint and makes it easier to install UPDATE 1: To ease the rear installation, I designed a slightly different platform for locking the half-nut in place, print profile and instructions are updated. UPDATE: I slightly modified the nut to make it a little tighter (only 0.02mm increase of the tooth width). The print profile has been updated. Due to the tighter profile inserting the half nut parrallel to the platform edge (step 9) might be more difficult. I advise to insert it to the leadscrew at a slight angle and then rotate to verify it does not go too much beyond the front face. Also, the rear nut will be really hard to clip… You may want to cut a bit of the protrusion (one side or the other whether you're left or right-handed (or both)), it could make it easier. If you really cannot clip them together (it took me almost 20 minutes just to do it this time!), you will certainly have to do it from the back removing the rear panel. To avoid this, I will try to come up with a tool (done, see update 1) to make it easier from the front. _____________________________________________________________ One of the issue experienced on Bambu H2 printers is the leadscrew nut failing. The nut (mainly the rear nut) starts to develop wear until it fails completely with stripped thread. It does not happen on all printers and those which failed have several 1,000hrs of print time except on some occasions when it failed sooner. Bambu support is reacting well in those cases, providing a full leadscrew kit to replace the failed nut(s) and leadscrews but the replacement takes several hours and a lot of disassembly/re-assembly and you may not afford this down time especially if the failed printer is part of a print farm. My rear nut currently has about 0.85mm of play with about 1,800hrs of use. It is still printing fine and bamboo provided me with a leadscrew kit but I figured I could design a quick fix that take less than 10min for each nut replacement with no removal. I have made several prototypes for the 2-part nut to make sure it can easily clip but still require some force so that when clipped it operates like a whole nut. The installation posts and installation platforms have also required some thorough testing to make sure that without any removal and references from a new leadscrew installation, the clocking of the nut to the sliding support is still exactly right. This can be done as an interim fix until Bambu ships the leadscrew kit replacement to you or you can decide it to be a permanent fix. Although I only printed a dozen of models since the replacement of the 3 leadscrew nuts, I’m fairly confident although I cannot guarantee the nut longevity, that they may hold a long time and given how easy and quick they can now be replaced, I know I will let them on my printer and see how it goes in the long run. The nuts are printed in ASA and the rest of the kit in PLA. The nut replacement requires absolutely no other removal than the nuts themselves and the rear nut can be installed from inside the printer not even requiring removal of the back panel. Instructions: Do not fear the long instructions, it's really easy to do Note: The following instructions have steps numbered, 1,2,3... The process is mainly the same for the fronts or the rear nut but when it is different, there will be a 1.a or 5.a to define the changes for the rear nut. Bring the 2 half nuts you’ve just printed together and clip them between your thumb and index finger (you may need both hands for that initial assembly). You will then feel the force required to do it but this first installation will break-in a bit the assembly so that it will require a little bit less force during actual installation. Use a flat head screwdriver to separate the 2 halves using one of the slots provided on either side. Install the 3 posts around each of the linear rod. The posts simply clip around the rods. The rear post has a deeper recess that goes on the top to wrap around the top sliding bearing. The front post ends have different geometry, the smaller diameter goes at the bottom. Clip them so that the post slot is facing the leadscrew (required to be able to install the installation platforms later). In the menu access the Z travel and lower the bed until it touches the posts. Start with 10mm and finish with several passes of 1mm until the bed touches the posts. You will hear a slight humming from your Z motor when contact occurs. Keep the printer ON during the whole process, the Z motor will then stay energized so that the leadscrews cannot rotate. Note: Do one nut after the other to guarantee perfect alignment, start with the fronts as they are easier to do Remove the 3 screws holding the nut to its slider. The screws are coated with red Loctite so you will need a fair amount of force initially to break the bond and although they will still be somewhat hard to turn, they will then unscrew more easily. Tip: break the bond and slighly unscrew all 3 screws before removing them. Please use good hex driver or hex bits, the space is limited and please do not damage the hex on the screws or you will be in big trouble, use GOOD TOOLS (I wouldn't use the bambu allen key!) Insert the removal/guide tube around the leadscrew, slide it up against the bottom of the nut and rotate slightly until the 3 fingers insert into the 3 tapped hole. Unscrew the nut until it’s out of the slider and remove the guide Rotate the original nut to the bottom of the leadscrew Insert the front installation platform between the rod and the leadscrew 8.a. ( For the rear nut ). You should really keep the rear post in place if you can but if you really need more room, slide it out gently and remove it then install the installation platform from the back of the leadscrew. It will be a little difficult to install it but I can assure you it fits :). Place it up then rotate it down from the back Place the top half-nut (the one with the 2 holes) behind the leadscrew and engage the thread. The goal is to install it parallel to the front of the platform, it should easily engage the leadscrew and it should not move more when you move it clockwise (or just a tiny bit). 9.a. ( For the rear nut ). The goal is to install it parallel to the reference groove on the platform and it should not move more when you move it clockwise (or just a tiny bit). Keep the half-nut you’ve just installed on the leadscrew thread by pushing it with your fingers so it does not disengage. 10.a ( For the rear nut ). Install the nut lock behind the nut. Bring the lock forward against the rear of the nut without moving it and then push on the lock to lock it on the platform With your fingers still holding on the half-nut use your other hand to present the second half-nut in one of the cavity (the nuts have a chamfered groove on one side and a chamfered protrusion on the other so that they will perfectly align) 11.a ( For the rear nut ). The first insertion should be on the left side which will make full insertion later easier Clip the 2 half-nuts together by pressing between your thumb and index finger (you will certainly also need your other hand for the force required to clip the 2 half-nuts). This force is per design but not that much that it can’t be easily done. If you feel it needs a lot of force, it might means you did not align them correctly. 12.a ( For the rear nut ). Push hard with your thumb against the open side to clip. The nut lock will keep the nut in position. Note: You can verify the nut is placed properly on the leadscrew by unscrewing and screwing it back down to the platform, it should stay parallel to the front of it (a minor angle is OK). Optionally, if your original nut is not stripped completely and you can still screw it on the leadscrew, you can double-check the alignment by removing the platform, bring both original and plastic nut together, and check the hole alignment by inserting a piece of filament in any one of the holes. If it’s not aligned, it means you have jumped one tooth during installation, remove the half-nut (a slot is provided on both sides to insert a flat head screwdriver) and re-do. Remove the platform and rotate the original nut all the way down if it’s not already there. Take a 1minute break to breeze until you proceed Insert the guide tool around the leadscrew and insert it in the 3 holes of the new nut. 15.a. ( For the rear nut ). Re-install by sliding back in the rear post you removed at step 9.a., rotate it to the side so that you have enough room to rotate the guide tool with one or 2 fingers :) While keeping the bed seated against the post by pushing down on the slider, rotate the tool up until the nut contacts the inner bottom of the slider. With the bed pushed down and the nut fully in contact, the holes should almost align. You should need to slightly unscrew just a little bit to make them align nicely. If it requires more than just a bit (about a hole size or just a hair more), you may have done the installation wrong and need to redo it. Insert the 3 new screws (BT3x10), though the slider and into the nuts and screw them on an alternating pattern until they are fully seated (seated only not tightened). Move up the bed in the menu 2 mm and seat the screws again on an alternating pattern (seated only not tightened). Now, unscrew them all one half turn so that the nut can slightly move around its position Move up the bed in the menu 10mm Remove the guide tube, the 3 posts and anything you may have placed below the bed In the menu bring the bed down until it contacts the bottom of the printer (same as before, several 10mm travels initially, then 1mm steps until contact) Now you can screw tight the 3 nut screws (the leadscrew have some degrees of liberty in all directions but not at the bottom where it is guided by the bearing, this is why the final tightening of the nut needs to be done there so that it’s fully concentric to the leadscrew). Do the same for the 2 other nuts. DONE! Note: When you’re done replacing the 3 nuts, run a bed levelling calibration. Note: I added for download a gcode file for breaking-in the freshly new installed nuts. Makerworld does not accept gcode as a file so I renamed it .stp to upload. Download it from the STL/CAD Files download option, rename the .stp to .gcode and put it at the root of your USB key, you can then print the gcode from the printer's menu. What the gcode does is a homing followed by 6 travels up and down of the bed. The file is the same for H2S/H2D/H2C. Note: You may notice that when all nuts are replaced and you bring the bed fully down against the bottom of the printer, all 3 sliders seat nicely with no gap on any of the 3 which is certainly better than when you received your printer (one of my slider had a couple of tenths gap). It means assembly is perfect but a tramming may be required if it was not the condition before replacement… When I replaced my nuts, I checked my tramming but as I only had a 0.1mm max bed out of tram from left to right and front to back, I left it like that and just run a bed levelling calibration. I left the tramming for later :). At least just do a quick tramming check at least. It shouldn't be too offset and that's a good check that the installation was done properly. Note: The removed nuts are now sitting at the bottom of the leadscrew, they will not reduce the vertical travel as they will just bury in the slider with the bed is fully at the bottom but I was afraid they could behave as a jam nut against the bearing and the leadscrew threads and risking locking the leadscrew. It did not happen to me yet certainly due to some slack in the worn nut threads that prevented it but your mileage may vary. You may want to put a safety wire or a cable tie or a piece of tape around the leadscrew below the nut for extra safety so it will not stay fully down against the bearing.
A2L Extruder Cable Chain. It will prevent the cable from drooping into the printing area. Enjoy!

This project intends to reduce the amount of harmful gases produced during the 3D printing process by creating a slight negative pressure in the chamber to reduce or eliminate them leaking out. It does this by automatically controlling a fume extractor fan based on what your Bambu printers are doing. It uses a 3D printed filter box with active charcoal and an ESP32 to poll one or two Bambu printers for status information and ramp a set of fans up and down based on the printer status. It also gives basic printer status information through a dashboard. Although this project was initially designed around two printers it can easily be used for one printer with no modifications other than printing a cap for the non-used intake. In fact I personally recommended using one printer per filter box for simplicity. Using more than two printers is also possible but is an advanced use case requiring some modifications to the code or possibly the 3D printed model and is not required for a standard one or two printer setup. This is a advanced build involving a printed filter box, a ESP32 micro controller, programming, wiring, and a read-only cloud connection between the ESP32 and your Bambu account. I tried to make it as simple as possible without requiring soldering, heat-sets, etc but it is still a involved project. I do not want to discourage anyone from attempting this but it does have multiple pieces that all need to come together for a successful working system. There are two print profiles with active carbon: One with a open bottom which makes it easier to mount the components but requires a longer print time due to supports and one with a solid bottom that prints quicker but might be a little harder to navigate inside. In my pictures I used the open bottom but the closed bottom is sturdier. You can also save some time by using a 0.6 nozzle @ 0.18 layer height or for the solid bottom model switching the “lid” color to match the box color. The lid for each version slides in so you have to be mindful of shrinkage. In my example, and in the print profiles, I'm using Bambu ABS for the box and Bambu ABS-GF for the lids as it has minimal shrinkage. The third print profile is for those of you that already vent to the outside but want to automate this process. It's a simple scaled down box with one input and one output and no filters but otherwise follows the same system and logic. The full read-me, Bill of Material, programming code, assembly instructions, and programming guide is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ADYDesigns/BambuAFE/ This project also relies on getting the fumes from your printer to this project. My recommendation is @Made.In.Meidling exhaust system: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1880330-slim-h2-quicklock-exhaust-system-updated . Instead of reinventing the wheel I used, with permission, the threaded connections from their system on my model so it is 100% compatible with theirs. NOTE : Bambu can, at any time, change the access to printer status through their cloud. If that does happen there is already code in place so you may manually turn on the fans using a single potentiometer. This way the main goal of this project can still be accomplished just in a less automatic way or if you want to use this with a non-Bambu printer. This is detailed on GitHub under the Manual Mode section.

description: I designed this filament storage case to organize a large number of filament spools and make them quick and easy to access. The cases can be stacked vertically and arranged side by side. Because the lid opens from the front, you can remove the filament you need without moving the other cases. The case includes a large clear window, a hygrometer mount, a desiccant compartment, and a TPU gasket. These features make your filament easier to identify, access, and store. I hope this design helps you keep your 3D printing workspace organized and easy to use. I have uploaded a video explaining this model on YouTube: https://youtu.be/SJGec_SRGWo Main Features Access Your Spool Without Moving the Stack The lid opens from the front. Even when several cases are stacked vertically or placed side by side, you can open each case individually without removing the cases above it. This is especially useful when storing a large number of filament spools in a limited space. Large Clear Window The lid has a large clear window. By using a transparent acrylic or PVC sheet, you can check the filament color, remaining amount, and surface texture without opening the case. The lid locking nut can be printed with the same filament stored inside the case. This allows it to be used as a color sample. If you have a label printer, adding labels such as PLA, PETG, ABS, or TPU will make your filament collection even easier to organize. Spool Pull-Out Part In most cases, you can simply open the lid and remove the spool by hand. If the spool is difficult to reach, use the included filament pull-out part. Pulling this part forward makes it easier to bring the spool toward the front of the case. The rear section of the pull-out part also includes a compartment for silica gel or another desiccant. Check the Humidity Without Opening the Case A small hygrometer can be installed in the lid. This allows you to check the internal humidity at any time without opening the case. A TPU gasket is installed between the lid and the case body. Double-sided tape is also used around the clear window to help reduce air leakage and maintain a stable internal humidity. This case does not include an active heating or drying function. It is designed to store filament that has already been dried and to help protect it from moisture when used together with desiccant. Required Parts 3D-Printed Parts Case body Lid TPU gasket Spool pull-out part Lid-locking bolt Lid-locking nut Printing the lid-locking nut with the same filament stored inside the case allows it to be used as a color sample. Additional Parts Small Hygrometer ×1 A small rectangular hygrometer is recommended. Desiccant Silica gel or a similar desiccant can be used. Clear Sheet ×1 Acrylic, PVC, or another transparent sheet can be used. Size: 74 × 185 mm Thickness supported by the standard model: 0.5–0.6 mm The thickness of commonly available clear sheets may vary depending on your region or supplier. If you would like to use a different thickness, such as a 1 mm sheet, please leave a comment with the required thickness. Even if there is only one request, I plan to prepare a lid file that supports that thickness. M3 Socket Head Cap Screws ×2 Length: 25～30 mm These screws are used as hinge pins on the left and right sides of the lid. No nuts are used with these M4 screws. They are simply inserted from both sides. Double-Sided Tape Width: 5 mm This is used to attach the clear sheet and the hygrometer. Assembly Instructions 1. Install the Printed Lid-Locking Bolt Install the 3D-printed lid-locking bolt into the hook on the inside of the case body. Insert the part from inside the case, then slide it sideways along the hook until it is secured. Check the photos for the correct position and orientation. The part used in this step is the 3D-printed lid-locking bolt. It is not one of the metal M4 screws. 2. Install the TPU Gasket Fit the TPU gasket around the front opening of the case body. Make sure the gasket is installed evenly and is not twisted or lifted away from the surface. Any twisting or lifting may affect how well the lid seals against the case. 3. Attach the Clear Sheet to the Lid The rear side of the lid has a recessed area for attaching the clear sheet. Apply 5 mm-wide double-sided tape around this recessed area. The tape should form a continuous loop around the window without any gaps. Gaps may allow air to enter the case and reduce the effectiveness of the seal. Remove the protective backing from the tape and attach the clear sheet, cut to 74 × 185 mm. Align the clear sheet carefully. If the sheet is misaligned, it may interfere with the TPU gasket and reduce the effectiveness of the seal. Before permanently attaching it, confirm that the sheet fits correctly in the intended position. 4. Install the Hygrometer Attach the small hygrometer to the smaller window in the lid. Secure it directly with a small amount of double-sided tape. Use only the minimum amount of tape needed to hold the hygrometer in place. If it is attached too firmly, it may be difficult to remove when replacing the hygrometer or disposing of the case. 5. Attach the Lid to the Case Body Align the hinge sections on both sides of the lid with the holes in the case body. Insert one M4 socket head cap screw from each side. Do not tighten the M3 screws. Simply insert them from the left and right sides. No nuts are used in this step. Insert each screw only far enough that it does not significantly protrude from the side of the case. After installation, check that the lid opens and closes smoothly. 6. Insert the Spool Pull-Out Part If you are using desiccant, place it in the compartment at the rear of the filament pull-out part. Insert the pull-out part into the rear of the case body. Place the filament spool on top of it. 7. Install the Lid-Locking Nut Close the lid and attach the 3D-printed lid-locking nut from the front. Printing this nut with the same filament stored inside the case allows it to be used as a color sample for identifying the contents. You can also add a label showing the material type, such as PLA, PETG, ABS, or TPU. How to Use Remove the lid-locking nut and open the lid toward the front. Remove the filament spool directly by hand. If the spool is difficult to reach, pull the filament pull-out part toward the front of the case. Each case can be opened individually while the cases remain stacked vertically or arranged side by side. Important Notes This case is designed to store already-dried filament and help reduce moisture absorption during storage. It does not actively dry filament that has already absorbed a large amount of moisture. When necessary, dry the filament with a filament dryer before placing it in the case. The position of the clear sheet, gaps in the double-sided tape, and the condition of the TPU gasket will affect the quality of the seal. After assembly, check the following: The clear sheet is correctly aligned and is not lifting away from the lid. There are no gaps in the double-sided tape. The TPU gasket is not twisted or lifted. The lid opens and closes smoothly. The M3 screws do not significantly protrude from the sides of the case. The hygrometer is securely attached. Check the hygrometer regularly and replace or regenerate the desiccant when necessary.

Master Filament Calibration Suite One Model. One Workflow. Every Calibration Test You Need. I have grabbed a bunch of different models made by other users and some of my own to help you calibrate and learn yourself. Tired of searching through dozens of separate calibration models every time you open a new spool? The Master Filament Calibration Suite brings together the essential calibration tests required to tune almost any filament into a single organized workflow. Instead of guessing where to start or jumping between unrelated tests, this suite follows a logical order that allows each calibration to build on the last, helping you create accurate filament profiles with less wasted time and material. Whether you're tuning PLA, PETG, ASA, ABS, TPU, Nylon, or specialty materials, this workflow is designed to help you achieve consistent, repeatable results. Why This Exists Many calibration collections provide the tests but not the process. The order of calibration matters. Running a flow test before finding the correct temperature, or fine-tuning Pressure Advance before establishing proper extrusion settings, can lead to misleading results and unnecessary reprints. This suite is organized to follow a practical calibration sequence that progressively refines your filament profile from broad adjustments to fine tuning. Recommended Calibration Workflow 1. Pressure Advance (Rough) Establish a baseline Pressure Advance value to improve extrusion consistency and reduce corner artifacts before moving on to other calibrations. 2. Temperature Tower Identify the optimal printing temperature by evaluating surface quality, layer adhesion, stringing, bridging, and overhang performance. 3. Maximum Volumetric Speed (MVS) Determine the maximum flow rate your printer and filament combination can sustain while maintaining print quality. 4. Flow Rate (Rough) Quickly narrow down the correct extrusion range using larger adjustment steps. 5. Flow Rate (Fine) Fine-tune extrusion settings for improved dimensional accuracy, cleaner surfaces, and better overall print quality. 6. Pressure Advance (Fine) Perform a final Pressure Advance calibration after flow and temperature have been optimized for the most accurate result. 7. Retraction Reduce stringing, blobs, and unwanted oozing by finding the optimal retraction settings for your filament. 8. Bridging Flow Calibrate extrusion specifically for bridge performance to improve unsupported spans and reduce sagging. 9. Bridging Speed Determine the optimal bridge printing speed to achieve cleaner, stronger bridges with minimal drooping. Included Documentation The PDF attached will explain the process and has the pictures for where to put what and how to use this calibration suite. Each test includes an explanation of: What the test measures How to evaluate the results Which slicer settings to adjust How much to adjust them by What common failures look like For users who want a deeper understanding of the calibration process, detailed documentation may also be provided through an accompanying Google Doc covering each test in greater depth. Designed For New filament profiles Unknown filament brands Specialty materials Printer tuning Consistent print quality Faster setup of new spools Reduced trial and error The Goal The goal isn't simply to pass a collection of calibration tests. The goal is to provide a repeatable workflow that helps makers quickly and confidently tune any filament while minimizing wasted material, failed prints, and frustration. If this suite helps you save time, filament, or failed prints, consider leaving a like, rating, or boost so other makers can discover it too. Happy Printing!

The Perfect Plastic Scraper This simple but effective plastic scraper is designed for removing stubborn prints from your build plate without damaging the surface. At 7 inches long and 2⅜ inches wide at the blade, it provides plenty of leverage while remaining lightweight and easy to use. The blade corners are intentionally rounded to help prevent gouging or scratching your build plate. The model is designed with three perimeter walls for added strength and durability. Printing out of PLA works great, and would probably even be stronger in PETG. The scraper uses approximately 20g of filament, so each scraper costs only about $0.30 to print. Since they’re inexpensive and handy to have around, consider printing a few and keeping them near your printers in any work area, and anywhere you might need a scraper. This tool is especially useful for removing prints that tend to adhere strongly to the build plate, such as TPU and PETG parts. For the Bambu Lab A1 Mini, the scraper appears to print the quickest when placed diagonally on the build plate, although it can also be printed horizontally without issue. Happy printing!

I probably could get one more column in (make it 42mm wider), but the machine moves a lot and I didn't want the stand to be two narrow, and allow movement from side to side. So I designed a set of stands for the left side, the printer is symmetric so left and right sides are the same, and then added a larger drawer from side to side that goes all the way to the back of the printer. Also made the stand 70mm high to allow deep Gridfinity bins or to double stack if wanted. For the stands, I picked up some 0.4mm rubber feet from Amazon ( https://www.amazon.com/Self-Adhesive-Anti-Sliding-Anti-Scratch-Protectors-Appliances/dp/B0D78JL5DV/ref=sr_1_21_sspa?crid=C59LOUHZ4FV6&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.-s7Ym3GGMWo2vKQXRMJyE2S7Xm38RoJplcMfpV8SZvi1OtYVC4HxHSFXeZhWVH07ir_jBVlZlqNhVIqwTcGbP5coeeBmdjVdU-79FjG17JghO9AIKsPJjmHEGidRTeCM6YfcB9vxEeDgSd9ZMtpNs6gMlTdsx26i3w55cw6rQ1R6VJZ4HxfMV1OdbRTXJKYss6YYc3bJMYG9GP6fJ3pRwCcLFrK8REsHqVFFewSbplEDjP_NPLjtb7sxJAF5RHBCM_cR0rErJAycfCXKZJXlB6EN67MG5Ck_9SVJx_HDrwA.VJiUKqblApFn_Lf1wyd3zCxJ0BcUJ7VAi4in3qGA_PQ&dib_tag=se&keywords=non%2Bslip%2Bself%2Bstick&qid=1780918386&sprefix=non%2Bslip%2Bself%2Bstick%2Caps%2C194&sr=8-21-spons&sp_csd=d2lkZ2V0TmFtZT1zcF9tdGY&th=1 ), to prevent it from sliding. The main stand is a bit filament heavy, I used PETG, but I used 10% Gyroid, except where the printer feet are located, those have modifiers to use 15% Grid Infill, for added support. I will be adding a profile with the Gridfinity Grid. Assembly is petty simple, the two parts of the stand have dovetails that just slide into each other, you can use a rubber mallet to make sure its level. The drawer uses dovetails and has guides on the side, after assembly glue the filler pieces into the sides and base. If you wonder why I didn't use Orange for the base, it was because I have a lot of Black PETG. description: A1 Vibration Damping Pods Inspired from the use of damping in the A2L. These mount to the brace that connects the X-axis to the Z-axis screws instead of the gantry. The mount is the point were any vibrations and or resonance would travel to the print head via the X-Axis – this way both X and Z axis have damping. Plus, space on my gantry is at a premium! French Riviera premium. I used Iron Sand (Iron Filings) - available on Amazon, or anywhere you buy your overpriced scientific supplies - as the damping material. This is better for high frequency vibrations than bearings or BB's and way better than marshmallows. Each bottom clip is secured with an M3x6 button head, coarse thread, screw. They are a tight slip fit by design but are removable if needed. They do not interfere with printer maintenance or your relationship with your mother-in-law. Disclaimer ~ Iron Sand is used in a wide variety of applications for this purpose. I don't have the equipment, nor interest to do a bunch of testing to say how effective these may be in this application on this device. I have seen varying guides of how to calculate damping material v’s object mass. This is just the direct application of theory. Feel free to test and comment with your results below. * Assembly- Fill each compartment to approximately ¾ full. I used a hobby syringe. Make sure to fill them equally so they weigh the same on each side! Use a scale to weigh each compartment as you fill them. Mine weighed 57grams each, once filled. Your results may vary. but, if they weigh the same as mine we can be twinzies. Seal each compartment by gluing a plug in the fill port. Or fill each port with a glue plug. Insert into X-axis brace from the top. Will be a snug fit by design. Grunting and cursing may ease the process. Make sure they sit all the way down. My brackets had some significant burrs, so you may need to de-burr or perform some fitment of the Pods. Insert clip from below. Or lower the printer onto the clip. Secure bottom and pod together with the M3x6 button head coarse thread screw. Tighten until something snaps! And of course -recalibrate… or don’t.. you do you. *These may give you buttery smooth prints, or bring about the end of times, or do absolutely nothing at all. Either way, I stand by option three. California Prop 67 warning - this print and its materials may cause dullness, averageness, and or mediocrity. If you develop feelings of apathy that last for more than 3 hours - who cares!

description: Filament Storage Rack with Fix-Clips Description I am a teacher and normally I design educational models. The Fix-Clips help secure the modules together, but overall stability will still depend on the height of the stack, the weight distribution, and where the rack is placed. Schwingungskompensation für A1 und A2L Bambu Lab hat mit dem A2L gezeigt, wie wirkungsvoll eine adaptive Schwingungskompensation das Druckbild verbessern kann. Das zugrunde liegende Prinzip ist ebenso einfach wie bewährt und findet auch in hochwertigen Werkzeugen Anwendung. Ein rückstoßfreier Hammer etwa besitzt eine Kammer, die mit Stahlschrot oder Sand gefüllt ist. Beim Aufprall bewegt sich das Füllmaterial zeitversetzt nach, absorbiert einen Teil der Rückprallenergie und reduziert so unerwünschte Schwingungen. Das Ergebnis ist eine kontrolliertere Bewegung ohne störendes Hüpfen oder Nachfedern. Da der Querträger des A2L dieselben Abmessungen aufweist, liegt es nahe, dieses Dämpferkonzept auch dort einzusetzen. Gerade bei hohen Druckgeschwindigkeiten lässt sich das Schwingungsverhalten dadurch zusätzlich optimieren. Aus diesem Grund habe ich für den A1 und A2L einen Schwingungsdämpfer entwickelt. Er absorbiert Bewegungsenergie sowohl in der X- als auch in der Y-Achse und trägt damit zu einem ruhigeren Lauf des Druckers bei. Besonders dann, wenn das AMS lite oder Filament-Rollen oben auf dem Gerät montiert sind, werden störende Bewegungen deutlich reduziert. Das sorgt insbesondere bei schnellen Druckvorgängen für ein saubereres und gleichmäßigeres Druckbild. Die Schwingungskompensatoren bestehen aus einem Behälter mit integrierten Schwallwänden. Diese begrenzen die freie Bewegung des Füllmaterials, erhöhen die Reibung im Inneren und verbessern dadurch die Energieabsorption. Ihre volle Wirkung entfalten die Dämpfer vor allem bei kleinen, schnellen Bewegungen. Material Für die Montage werden weder Klebstoff noch Schrauben benötigt. Zum Befüllen empfehle ich feinkörnigen Sand, da er eine besonders gute Dämpfungswirkung ermöglicht. Druck Für den Druck eignet sich PETG besonders gut, da die Halteklammern über den oberen Träger gesteckt werden und PLA dafür in der Regel zu spröde ist. Montage Befüllen Sie die Behälter bis zur Oberkante der Schwallwände mit Sand. Nach oben sollte etwas Luft verbleiben, damit sich das Füllmaterial frei bewegen kann. Verschließen Sie die Behälter mit den Deckeln und stecken Sie anschließend die seitlichen Clips mit der Öffnung nach unten auf. Die Form des Deckels gibt die korrekte Position automatisch vor. Stecken Sie die Schwingungsdämpfer links und rechts auf den oberen Querträger des Druckers auf. Die Dämpfer sind zudem kompatibel, wenn das AMS lite oben montiert ist. Funktionsprüfung Nach dem Druck können Sie die Wirkung der Dämpfer direkt prüfen: Füllen Sie eine Kammer wie beschrieben mit Sand, verschließen Sie beide Kammern mit den Deckeln und fixieren Sie sie mit den Clips. Schütteln Sie anschließend zunächst den leeren und danach den gefüllten Absorber mit der Hand. Der Unterschied in der Dämpfungswirkung ist dabei deutlich spürbar. Wichtig Vergessen Sie nicht nach der Montage eine neue Kalibrierung des Druckers durchzuführen!

Ultra-Light Reusable Filament Spool I designed this reusable filament spool to solve two problems I found with many existing designs: they were either unnecessarily heavy or didn't hold the filament securely, causing tangles during printing. This spool weighs only 82 grams in total ( 41 grams per half ) while remaining strong where it matters most. Why this design is different The unique spoke pattern isn't just for looksit was designed to maximize strength while minimizing material use. Only 82g of filament for a complete spool Approximately 1.5 hours to print each half Spokes intersect in the center, creating high structural density where the spool experiences the greatest loads. The outer edge uses less material because it doesn't require the same level of reinforcement. This results in an elegant, lightweight, and efficient structure that uses filament only where it is needed. To my knowledge, I haven't seen another reusable filament spool using this type of spoke structure. description: Description This model works with a X2D or a P2S, adding only 53mm to the depth of the printer, and it vents the printer to connect to a 3.75 inch (100mm) or 75mm diameter hose. For the X2D, the fan, control board, air filter and hardware from the factory installed External Exhaust Fan can be reused for this model, but you will need to get 22 BT2x5 self-tapping screws (or equivalent) and an M3x12 screw for the Latch pivots (listed in the Bill of Materials above). For the P2S, it works with the components provided by the Bambu P2S External Exhaust Fan Kit and supports the External Exhaust Air Filter (listed in the Bill of Materials above). Note: Before you order the External Exhaust Fan Kit from Bambu inspect the back of your printer. If there is no exhaust port on the back panel, then you have an early version of the printer and will need to order the External Exhaust Fan Kit + Rear Panel option from Bambu (which doesn't cost extra). And install the new rear panel before you can install the External Exhaust Fan upgrade. Instructions installing the rear panel are here . NOTE: 5 output stage options are currently offered, distributed across several print profiles: Low Profile Vertical Active Fan Vent P2S X2D Vx.3m, Plate 4 - 3.75 inch hose adapter Low Profile Active P2S Fan Vent Vx.3mf, Plate 3 - Fan Grille Low Profile Fan Vent P2S 75mm Hose Adapter Vx.3MF, Plate 1 - 75mm hose adapter Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF, Plate 1 or 3 - 3.75 inch adapter Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF, Plate 2 or 4 - 75mm adapter This model is divided into 4 parts: the Base Module, Vertical Extension, Fan Module, and Output Stage (Hose Adapter/Fan Grille). This partitioning allows easy modification of any component without needing to reprint the other components. For example, the Hose Adapter can be easily replaced to support different hose sizes. Let me know in the comments the Inner Diameter (ID) of the particular hose that you need. Assembly Base Assembly The first step is to assemble the Fan Vent Base. The two types of clips (as shown in Figure 1 ) are inserted into the Fan Vent Base (Low Profile Fan Vent P2S V4.stl) in the positions indicated in Figure 2 . Figure 1 : Low Profile Fan Vent Clips Be sure to orientate all the clips to point in the same direction, as indicated by the green arrow in Figure 2 . Then insert the BT2x5 self-tapping screws, provided with the Bambu kit, from the opposite side (see the green arrows in Figure 15 ) and secure the Clips with the screws. Figure 2 : Base Clip Attachment Finally apply the pre-cut black Foam Tape provided with the Bambu Kit to the Base. Confirm the correct position before pasting to avoid errors. Ensure the foam is aligned with the edge, and paste the four strips of top foam one by one as shown in Figure 2 . If you have an X2D and can't peel the tape of the factory fan cover, search for "1mm foam tape" on Amazon, they offer many options. If available, insert the External Exhaust Air Filter . Fan Module The next step is to assemble the Fan Module. Latches Each Latch consists of two parts: Body and Latch. First install the Latch Body part ( Figure 3 ) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Note: The screws act as shafts. Do not over-tighten them otherwise the Latch will not work smoothly. Figure 3 : Latch Body Installation Next install the Latch Latch part ( Figure 4 ) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Figure 4 : Latch Latch Installation Now use the same process to attach the Latch components on the opposite of the Fan Module for the Base, and on the top and bottom of the Fan Module for the Hose Adapter, as shown in Figure 5 . Figure 5 : Hose Adapter Latches Fan Installation Before continuing remove any leftover support material from around the inside of the Connector Holes ( Figure 6 ) and the ‘top’ inside surface of the PCB case (as indicated by the blue arrow in Figure 6 ). And ensure that PCB connectors fit through the holes, and the PCB fits snugly against the top surface of the PCB case. Route the fan cable through the Fan Cable Hole as shown in Figure 6 and Figure 8 . Figure 6 : PCB Case Then press the fan into the Fan Module with the orientation shown in Figure 7 , while pulling on the fan cable. Note that the gasket that wraps around the fan is facing out. Also the airflow direction arrow on the side of the fan must be facing out as well. The surface of the fan should be flush with the surface of the fan module. Figure 7 : Fan Orientation PCB Installation Connect the Fan Cable to the PCB then fit the connectors into the connector holes ( Figure 6 ) and rotate the PCB so that it flat against the bottom of the PCB case. Finally use a BT2x5 self-tapping screw to secure the PCB to the Fan Module. Only one screw is necessary, because the left side of the PCB is held in place by its connectors. Figure 8 : PCB Installation Now press the PCB Cover into the PCB Case. Make sure that the Connector Baffles (as shown in Figure 9 ) are over the connectors. Also make sure that there is no left over support material in the slots that the cover will clip into, otherwise it will not seat tightly. Figure 9 : PCB Cover Output Stage There are 5 Output Stage options. The Output Stage printing choices are discussed at the beginning of this Description, for the various options. Only print the Plate associated with the option that you choose! For all options, you will need to press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Hose Adapter Module so that it seats as show in Figure 10 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Hose Adapter. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 10 : Hose Adapter Fan Grill Similar to the Hose Adapter ( Figure 10 ), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Fan Grille so that it seats as show in Figure 11 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Fan Grille. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 11 : Fan Grille Right Angle Hose Adapters Similar to the Hose Adapter ( Figure 10 ), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Right Angle Hose Adapter so that it seats as show in Figure 12 . Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Right Angle Adapters. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 12 : 3.75inch and 75mm Right Angle Hose Adapters The Right Angle Hose Adapters can be attached with the hose facing up, down, forward, or backwards. The Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF file includes two versions of the 3.75 inch and 75mm adapters: One with normal Tree supports and the other using tree supports and PETG as an interface layer. I added the PETG interface versions, which add about 3.5 hours to the print time, to see if they would significantly improve the surface quality. I didn't see a improvement that I was hoping for, especially considering the additional print time, but I left them in the file. Final Installation If attached, tear off the sticker on the printer’s rear panel exhaust port. If there is no exhaust port on the back panel, they you will need to order the “External Exhaust Fan Kit + Rear Panel” option from Bambu. Figure 14 : Sticker Removal Base Module Hold the Base Module and align the clips with the slots on the rear panel. Press the Base Module firmly against the rear panel to compress the foam gasket, then slide it to the left (as indicated by the red dashed arrow in Figure 15 ). You should feel the module snap into place to the preset installation position of the rear panel. The green arrows indicate where the BT2x5 self-tapping screws are inserted to secure the clips. Figure 15 : Base Module Installation Vertical Extension A single M3x10mm screw through the Extension Mounting Screw Hole (Green Arrow in Figure 16 and Figure 17 ). is used to attach the Vertical Extension to the Base Module. Figure 16 : Extension Mounting Screw Hole Remove the Allen screw from the center/top of the back plate. Fit the Vertical Extension to the Base Module (Red Arrow) and use an M3x10mm Screw and the same hole that you just removed the screw from (Green Arrow in Figure 17 ) to attach the Vertical Extension to the back panel. Figure 17 : Base Module Installation Fan Module Fit the Fan Module to the Vertical Extension, then use the top and bottom latches to secure it in place (Green Arrows in Figure 18 ). After installation, connect the 6PIN cable between the fan connector to the corresponding connector of the buffer. Figure 18 : Fan Module Installation Output Adapter Finally fit the selected Output Adapter to the Fan Module, then use the front and back latches to secure it in place. Figure 19 shows the installation of the Fan Grill. X2D Support Test – Multi-Material Support Benchmark Dieses Modell wurde speziell entwickelt, um die Qualität von Supportstrukturen und Multi-Material-Drucke objektiv zu bewerten. Durch die verschiedenen Überhänge, Aussparungen, Brücken und Kontaktflächen eignet sich der Test hervorragend, um die Druckqualität unterschiedlicher Materialkombinationen zu vergleichen und optimale Einstellungen für saubere Support-Oberflächen zu finden. Was wird getestet? Oberflächenqualität über Supportstrukturen Maßhaltigkeit kritischer Geometrien Qualität von Überhängen und Brücken Trennbarkeit der Supports Einfluss verschiedener Interface-Materialien Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch Vorteile von Multi-Material Supports Durch die Verwendung eines separaten Support-Interface-Materials lassen sich deutlich sauberere Unterseiten und Kontaktflächen erzielen als mit Supports aus dem gleichen Material. Besonders bei anspruchsvollen Überhängen können dadurch: glattere Oberflächen bessere Maßhaltigkeit weniger Nacharbeit einfachere Supportentfernung erreicht werden. Empfohlene Druckvarianten Variante 1 – Nur Support-Interface in anderem Material (empfohlen) Hier wird das Modell und die eigentlichen Supportstrukturen mit dem Hauptmaterial gedruckt. Lediglich die Support-Schnittstellen (Support Interface Layers) werden mit einem zweiten Material erzeugt. Beispiel: Modell: PETG Supports: PETG Support Interface: PLA Diese Methode bietet in der Regel das beste Verhältnis aus Druckqualität, Materialverbrauch und Druckzeit. Variante 2 – Komplette Supports in anderem Material Alternativ können sowohl die Supportstrukturen als auch die Support-Schnittstellen vollständig aus einem zweiten Material gedruckt werden. Beispiel: Modell: PETG Supports + Interface: PLA Diese Variante kann die Trennbarkeit weiter verbessern, erhöht jedoch den Materialwechsel erheblich. Wichtig: Durch die vielen Werkzeugwechsel zwischen den Materialien verlängert sich die Druckzeit deutlich und es entsteht zusätzlicher Materialabfall durch Spülvorgänge. Für die meisten Anwendungen ist daher Variante 1 die sinnvollere Wahl. Empfohlene Materialkombinationen PLA ↔ PETG PETG ↔ PLA ASA ↔ Support Material ABS ↔ Support Material Viel Spaß beim Testen! Teile gerne deine Ergebnisse, Einstellungen und Materialkombinationen in den Kommentaren, damit andere Nutzer von deinen Erfahrungen profitieren können. Gedruckt habe ich die Box in zwei Farben (macht ein AMS notwendig) und mit PETG . Ich empfehle PETG, da es flexibel und robust für den Einsatz mit Silika Gel ist. The foam gently compresses the silica bed, preventing the beads from shifting while the spool rotates. This almost completely eliminates rattling and also minimizes abrasion, reducing long term silica dust. I've been using this simple trick for years, and it works remarkably well. Test Supporti PLA vs Interfaccia PETG In questo test ho confrontato due configurazioni di supporto per verificare la qualità della superficie e la facilità di rimozione: Configurazione 1 (sinistra) Modello: PLA Supporti principali: PLA Interfaccia di contatto: PETG Configurazione 2 (destra) Modello: PLA Supporti e interfaccia: PLA Risultati La combinazione PLA + PETG ha mostrato una separazione quasi perfetta tra pezzo e supporto. Grazie alla scarsa adesione tra i due materiali, l'interfaccia in PETG si stacca facilmente lasciando una superficie più pulita e definita. Con i supporti realizzati interamente in PLA, invece, l'adesione è maggiore: la rimozione richiede più forza e la superficie inferiore tende a non presentare molti segni lasciati dai supporti grazie ai test effettuati e profilo calibrato (alla fine ti metterò il link per il profilo calibrato). Vantaggi dell'interfaccia PETG ✅ Supporti più facili da rimuovere ✅ Migliore finitura delle superfici supportate ✅ Minore rischio di danneggiare il pezzo durante la rimozione ✅ Possibilità di ridurre il gap dell'interfaccia per ottenere dettagli migliori Nota Importante La tecnica funziona in entrambe le direzioni: Pezzo in PLA + interfaccia supporti in PETG Pezzo in PETG + interfaccia supporti in PLA Poiché PLA e PETG aderiscono poco tra loro, è possibile utilizzare uno dei due materiali come interfaccia di separazione per ottenere supporti facilmente removibili. Impostazioni consigliate Materiale modello: PLA o PETG Materiale interfaccia supporti: materiale opposto al modello Interfaccia supporti: 2-4 layer Distanza Z superiore: 0 mm (o molto ridotta) Torre di spurgo consigliata per evitare contaminazioni tra i materiali Conclusione Se disponi di una stampante con AMS o doppio estrusore, utilizzare un materiale diverso per l'interfaccia dei supporti è uno dei modi più efficaci per ottenere superfici migliori e supporti che si rimuovono quasi senza sforzo. In questo test la combinazione PLA/PETG ha dimostrato chiaramente il vantaggio rispetto ai supporti tradizionali realizzati con un solo materiale. description: This is a magnetic PTFE tube guide I made for my Bambu Lab H2C external TPU feed setup. I designed this to be a simple no-disassembly solution. Some similar tube guides require removing printer screws or replacing factory hardware with longer screws. This one does not require any of that. Just insert one 15x3 mm magnet during the print, place the guide in the location shown in the photos, and route the PTFE tube through it. The mount is shaped to fit directly into that specific spot on the rear/side of the H2 Series printer. Once installed in that location, the surrounding printer features help keep it from sliding forward, backward, up, or down during normal use. I use this together with an internal H2 Series PTFE Y-splitter for TPU/external feeding. The splitter handles the internal tube routing, and this magnetic guide keeps the outside PTFE tube positioned cleanly before it enters the printer. Splitter I use this with: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2285947-h2-series-ptfe-y-split-for-tpu-or-external?from=search#profileId-2493512 Features No printer disassembly required No screws to remove No longer replacement screws needed No adhesive or permanent modification Uses one embedded 15x3 mm magnet Designed to fit the specific rear/side mounting location shown in the photos Helps keep the external TPU feed tube aligned and controlled Works as a companion part for an internal PTFE Y-splitter setup Easy to remove if you want to go back to the factory setup Strong magnetic hold Compatibility Designed and tested on my Bambu Lab H2C. This should also be useful for other H2 Series machines with the same or similar rear PTFE tube layout, but I have only personally tested it on the H2C. Check the mounting location on your machine before printing. This model does not replace the internal splitter. It is only the external magnetic tube guide shown in the photos. Required Hardware 1x 15x3 mm round magnet The included print profile has a pause so the magnet can be inserted during the print. Printing Notes At the pause: Insert the 15x3 mm magnet into the pocket. Make sure the magnet is fully seated and sitting flat. Confirm it is not sticking up into the nozzle path. Resume the print. I recommend checking your magnet fit before printing multiple parts, since magnet sizes can vary slightly between suppliers. Installation Place the guide in the same rear/side location shown in the photos. The part is shaped to fit that area and stay located there with the embedded magnet. Route the PTFE tube through the guide and into your external TPU feed path. Adjust the tube path so there are no sharp bends or unnecessary drag.

description: Y-AXIS SPRAY-OIL INJECTOR — Bambu Lab H2 Spray controllato, dispersione zero. ✨ Cosa Trovi Uno strumento che risolve il problema della gestione dei fluidi sulla guida Y — senza complicarti il flusso di lavoro. Adattamento Perfetto: Si avvolge attorno alla guida lineare dell'asse Y con 1 mm di tolleranza sul diametro. Controllo Pressione: L'ugello dedicato riduce la pressione dello spray prima che colpisca la guida, evitando schizzi incontrollati. Sistema di Recupero: Due camere di raccolta intercettano il lubrificante in eccesso. Pulizia Garantita: Il design minimizza la dispersione; la tua postazione di lavoro rimane pulita dopo ogni applicazione. Compatibilità Universale: Progettato per accogliere le cannucce a diametro standard 2.2mm (utilizzate dalla stragrande maggioranza dei prodotti spray come per la maggior parte degli oli sintetici). 📋 Specifiche Rapide Dettaglio Valore Materiale PETG (scelta tecnica per resistenza a solventi e oli) Altezza Layer 0,1 mm consigliata Design Ugello Porta spray a pressione ridotta Supporti Non necessari Compatibilità Universale: barre da 12mm; Cannucce standard da 2,2mm (es: WD-40, olio spray del tipo desiderato) 🔧 Come Funziona Il sistema segue il ciclo di manutenzione completo della guida in tre passaggi distinti. Ognuno ha un ruolo fondamentale per garantire che la macchina duri nel tempo. Passaggio 1 — Sgrassaggio Alcol isopropilico e panno antistatico morbido . L'alcol è fondamentale per pulire a fondo. Passaggio 2 — Lubrificazione (Olio spray a vostra scelta) Solo ora la guida è pronta per l'olio, che aderirà in modo uniforme e duraturo. Posiziona lo strumento sulla guida. Inserisci la cannuccia dell'olio spray che hai scelto. Spruzza: le camere laterali contengono l'eccesso, mentre il design distribuisce uniformemente il prodotto lungo tutta la corsa. Il movimento della stampante farà il resto del lavoro durante la stampa. 🎁 Completa il Tuo Setup Z-Axis System — Stessa precisione, applicata all'asse Z. X-Axis Injector — Completa il trio di manutenzione per tutte le tue guide. ⚠️ Note Tecniche Importanti Perché PETG? A differenza del PLA, il PETG offre la resistenza chimica necessaria per non deformarsi a contatto con solventi leggeri o oli minerali (come ad esempio quello al silicone). Pulizia è Sicurezza: Il design a spray controllato evita che i lubrificanti finiscano nei motori o nelle parti elettroniche, proteggendo la tua stampante. Segui l'Ordine: Rispetta la sequenza Sgrassare →→ Lubrificare . Invertire questi passaggi compromette l'efficacia della manutenzione. Scarica e stampa per una manutenzione professionale.
