description: Apple Watch Ultra Bike Mount (Garmin Ecosystem Adapter) A precision-engineered, two-piece adapter designed to mount an Apple Watch Ultra onto any standard Garmin-compatible bike mount. This project allows cyclists to leverage the advanced capabilities of the Apple Watch Ultra—such as its high-accuracy GPS, fitness applications, and ultra-bright display—as a dedicated, handlebar-mounted cycling computer. Technical Design and Locking Mechanism The architecture of this mount completely eliminates the need for screws, adhesives, or mechanical fasteners. Instead, it relies on an interlocking two-piece geometry and the structural physics of the Garmin mount interface: Preparation: Remove the watch straps from the Apple Watch Ultra housing. Alignment: Enclose the watch chassis within the upper and lower halves of the adapter. Engagement: Insert and rotate the assembled unit into the standard Garmin handlebar mount. Structural Clamp Principle: As the adapter is rotated into the Garmin mount, the mounting tabs are compressed uniformly by the receiver's internal ramp geometry. This mechanical pressure forces the two halves of the adapter to lock securely around the watch chassis. The assembly remains entirely rigid, eliminating play and securing the device against high-vibration environments, including gravel and mountain biking. Key Features Cost-Effective Integration: Utilizes existing hardware to replace expensive, dedicated cycling computers. Chassis Protection: The adapter shell conforms tightly to the titanium bezel of the Apple Watch Ultra, shielding it from impacts and road debris. Unobstructed Display: The low-profile bezel design ensures full visibility of the screen and maintains touchscreen accessibility for real-time telemetry and navigation. Zero-Hardware Assembly: A 100% 3D-printed solution requiring no additional components or post-processing hardware. Recommended Print Settings To withstand outdoor exposure and mechanical stress during operation, engineering-grade filaments are highly recommended: Material: PETG, ASA, or ABS (for UV resistance and thermal stability under direct sunlight). PLA is not recommended due to its low heat deflection temperature. Layer Height: 0.16 mm to 0.20 mm (critical for the dimensional accuracy of the Garmin mounting tabs). Wall Loops: Minimum of 4 (essential for the structural integrity of the interlocking tabs). Infill: 30% to 40% (Gyroid pattern recommended for multi-directional strength). Supports: Depending on print orientation, Tree Supports are recommended to ensure clean internal mating surfaces. Thank you for downloading. model_name: Motorized TurnTable with Interchangeable Top Plate
description: TurnTable is a motorized rotating platform designed for displaying, photographing, and filming 3D prints, scale models, collectibles, and other creations. No soldering required – all electronics use Maker's Supply components and simple plug-and-play connections Whether you want to showcase a model on your desk, create smooth 360° product videos, or record eye-catching MakerWorld clips, TurnTable provides a simple and reliable rotating display solution. The platform uses a gear-driven drive system powered by a compact DC motor and supported by ball-bearing rollers for smooth, stable rotation. The integrated speed controller allows the rotation speed to be adjusted to suit different display and filming needs. A key feature of the design is the removable top plate . It drops into position without screws, making it easy to swap display surfaces or create custom platform designs while keeping the same drive system. The included top plate has a diameter of 220 mm , providing ample space for most 3D prints, collectibles, and scale models. Because the top plate is a separate component, larger or custom-designed plates can easily be created while reusing the same base and drive mechanism. The top plate is also included as a STEP file to make customization easy. Design your own display surfaces, photography plates, photogrammetry/scanning plates, model-specific platforms, or even larger top plates to suit your needs, all while reusing the same base and drive mechanism. Features No soldering required Uses only readily available Maker's Supply components Simple plug-and-play assembly Easy electrical connections using Maker's Supply modules Smooth 360° rotation Adjustable rotation speed Integrated on/off switch Stable ball-bearing supported platform Removable and interchangeable top plate Assembly: Insert the bearing in the center gear Insert 3 dowels in 3 bearings Insert the center dowel in the base plate Insert the assembled bearings in the slots in the base plate Secure the Self Locking Switch and the Potentiometer Board in the electronics compartment with four screws. Pull the small connector from the USB cable through the small square cutout on the electronics compartment from the outside to inside. Connect the SH connector from the USB cable to the IN port of the Power Distribution Board (PDB) Connect the Self-Locking Button Switch cable from SW0 on the PDB to the switch. Connect the Potentiometer cable from SW1 on the PDB to the Potentiometer Board. Connect the Motor to CH1 on the Power Distribution Board. Secure the Power Distribution Board with the connected cables in the Baseplate with 2 screws Install the electronics compartment in the base plate using two screws Assemble the reduction gear kit TIP: I put a piece of duct tape under the motor to reduce vibrations further. Install the motor cover Press the main gear assembly onto the center shaft. Avoid applying excessive force. Excessive pressure may push the center shaft too far into the gear, causing increased friction and preventing smooth rotation. Install the pinion gear. The pinion gear is intentionally positioned slightly lower than the main gear. Install the topcover Disc Congratulations, you've completed your TurnTable. If you like, you can make custom top cover discs in other colors or even a top cover for scanning; the step file is included.

description: Spulenadapter für 250 Gramm Spulen mit einfacher Anpassung je nach Spulenbreite oder Innenduchmesser / Kerndurchmesser der Spule!! Adapter sollte für nahezu jede Spule passen, er kann sehr einfach angepasst werden ohne CAD!! Siehe untenstehende Beschreibungen…! Druckprofile Standard: “Spulenadapter ASA” und "Spulenadapter PETG": Da ich keinen passenden Spulenadapter für meine 250 Gramm Spulen gefunden haben (250 Gramm Spulen von 3D Jake (PLA) und Spulen von RECREUS (TPU Spulen: zum Trocknen im AMS HT)), habe ich diesen hier konstruiert. Dieser passen für meine 250 Gramm-Spulen von 3D JAKE und von RECREUS welche einen Innenduchmesser (Spulenkern) von ca. 52 mm bis 53 mm haben, ca. 42 mm bis 43 mm breit sind und einen Aussendurchmesser von 139 mm bis 142 mm. Der Spulenadapter passt für mein AMS 2 PRO und auch für mein AMS HT und da ich den Adapter auch für das AMS HT verwende habe ich eine Variante aus PETG und auch eine Variante aus ASA gedruckt. Die Druckprofile sind mit Modifier ausgeführt wodurch nur der Bereich mit dem Gewinde eine höhere Wandanzahl aufweist wodurch beim Drucken Filament gespart wird aber die Spule trotzdem sehr stabil ist. Das Aussengewinde des Körper 1 ist 40 mm lang und versinkt im Körper 2 ca. 16 mm weit, im zusammengeschraubtem Zustand hat die Spule dann eine Breite von ca. 67 mm mit meinen oben genannten Spulen. Druckprofil: “Körper 2 mit durchgängigem Gewinde” Bei diesem Druckprofil ist das Gewinde des Körper 2 durchgehen wodurch das Aussengewinde des Körper 1 durch den Körper 2 hindurch geschraubt werden kann damit der Spulenadapter auch für Spulen mit einer anderen Spulenbreite oder Innendurchmesser / Kerndurchmesser passt. Bitte hier darauf achten, dass das überstehende Gewinde, bei sehr schmalen Spulen, nicht im AMS ansteht oder schleift!! Druckprofil: "Körper1 Gewindelänge anpassbar" Anpassen des Körper 1 für Spulen mit anderer Spulenbreiten oder anderem Innendurchmessern / Kernduchmessern: Da meine Konstruktion ein relativ langes Gewinde hat, im vergleich zu anderen Konstruktionen, kann man die Länge der Gewindes sehr einfach anpassen damit der Spulenadapter auch für Spulen mit einer anderen Spulenbreite oder einem anderen Innendurchmesser/Kerndurchmesser passt. Hierfür habe ich das Druckprofil “ Spulenadapter Gewindelänge 33 mm" hinzugefügt. Dieses beinhaltet eine “negatives Teil” durch welches die Länge des Gewindes, des Körper 1, auf 33 mm gekürzt wird. Wenn man diese 3mf im Slicer öffnet kann die Z - Position des "negative Teil", mit der Funktion “Bewegen”, sehr einfach geändert werden wodurch das Gewinde länger und kürzer gemacht werden kann und somit auch für andere 250 Gramm spulen angepasst werden kann. Einfach im Slicer das “negative Teil” anklicken , dann oben, in der Auswahlleiste, auf “Bewegen” klicken , und dann das “negative Teil” mit dem Blauen Pfeil nach oben oder nach unten schieben ODER in der Zeile “Position” in der Spalze “Z” den aktuellen Wert von 73 mm um die entsprechenden mm erhöhen oder reduzieren . Wenn man den Wert von 73 mm auf 70 mm reduziert wird die Gewindelänge von 33 mm auf 30 mm reduziert und passt somit für schmalere Spulen oder Spulen mit einem größeren Innendurchmesser. Somit kann man die Spule sehr einfach auf seine eigen Spulen angepasst werden. Ich wünsche viel Spaß beim Drucken und hoffe, dass dieser Druck auch für andere Personen so hilfreich ist wie dieser für mich ist.

Here we are again, 3D printing enthusiasts! It's mid-2026 and, after more than a year, I'm back with a new version of the "Great Calibrator," thanks to the success of previous versions. The model has undergone a redesign, losing some of the components that had been added to the main model over time and acquiring new ones (few, but effective). But the most impressive aspect is its compactness, precision, and ease of reading the tests, all while, of course, providing a good amount of stress to both your printer's steppers and nozzles, as well as the filament you're testing. Use is as simple and intuitive as ever: once printing is complete, let the print bed cool completely , then fold it and remove the main base. If your printer (or filament, or both) are already well calibrated, you'll notice that many parts will remain attached to the bed or will move away from it without remaining connected to the main base. This should (definitely) happen for the hinge and the bolt, as well as (probably) for the pins with the widest tolerance. Pins 3 and below may require a little pressure on the top. Caution: Don't use excessive force or tools to force a pin out. The goal is to read the tolerance allowed by the printer/filament combination under the conditions you printed under. An extreme unsuccessful print A successful print Let's review the model's components. Walls: The walls surrounding the main base should measure 0.8 mm , consisting of two 0.4 mm walls (the width of the standard nozzle). Turrets: As in previous versions, there are two turrets with a suspended sinusoidal upper part for support testing. You can therefore easily distinguish which method you prefer based on the results obtained. NOTE: There are two versions: the standard single-material version and the dual-material version that uses PETG and PLA for support separation. You'll notice some differences… Bridges: The bridge test is always present (the one on the far left with slopes of 45°, 60°, and the dreaded 75°) which, in theory, shouldn't pose any problems for your printers. I remind you that a "bridge" is a joint distance between two support points , and the different slopes are supported by two side walls. Half-bridges: Just like the bridges, to their right, at the center, you'll find the slopes for testing a half-bridge . What is it? Very simple, it's an overhang supported by a support on only one side , and the Great Calibrator gives you the ability to check the results for both sides. Overhang: A classic among classics, located to the right of the half-bridge, it has always been the biggest problem for a 3D printer: the "suspended" filament, meaning it's printed in "air" without any support. It depends on the extrusion capacity, filament cooling, rigidity, and the airflow system to your nozzle. The slopes don't change, but the 75° slope is more or less where the limit of what a filament printer can achieve stable overhanging ends. To verify them, it's not only important to note whether the lower part is aligned and not "spaghetti-like," but also to verify that the upper part can be completed with a good-looking top surface. Blades: The so-called "blades" have always been a distinctive feature of the Great Calibrator , as they allow for verification, and therefore adjustment, of the complexity of an extrusion balanced between thicknesses and spacing. These "blades" have a thickness that, from top to bottom, gradually decreases from 1.2 mm to a minimum of 0.4 mm (standard nozzle), with minimum distances that also decrease ( down to 0.05 ). The last distance may not be read at the slicer level, unless corrections are made or extrusion is somehow forced. This test (slicer stress) can therefore be verified already during the slicing phase without having to force printing in priority (the parameters provided with the model ensure that the last two blades are joined). Stringing stress cones : Here's another classic, placed in the center of the base, with the peculiarity that has always distinguished the Great Calibrator : the cones are not parallel to each other and not all perpendicular to the base. Obtaining a clean, smooth slin, complete cones, and no stringing will depend greatly on the quality of the filament, the extrusion temperatures, the quality of the nozzles, and so on. As you can see from the images, I managed to achieve excellent results with a simple A1 and a basic PLA filament from Bambulab . M-K-Nick : It's not the name of a rapper or a DJ, but the name of the "mechanical" innovation of the calibrator. Its shape and thickness are very unique and were specifically designed to be "easy" to print. The result should be a piece with properties that are elastic enough to be removed from the base without any effort (if your fingers aren't very fine, try using a simple tweezers, but don't force it. It should come out easily, despite the mechanical "block" caused by its particular shape). Bolt with its Nut: Here it is again, the essential bolt for testing the nut printed in the base circle. A well-calibrated printer should not cause any problems, so the nut should be easily screwed and unscrewed onto the bolt. The thread is standard, but the tolerance is approximately 0.2 mm between each wall, resulting in a total tolerance (circumference) of 0.4 mm. Som e problems may arise from the overhang required by creating the nut thread and/or the bolt itself . Parallelepiped dimensions : The block, as you can easily see, should measure 50 mm wide and 10 mm high and deep. Take the measurement, avoiding getting too close to the Base. Hinge: The other mechanical part of the Great Calibrator is this sort of "3-plate hinge" that can be used to test the possibility of performing some "on-plate direct printing" operations on mechanical parts. The plates that make up the hinge must be able to release with minimal effort and, once released, after a few bends to the left and right, they should have a fluid movement. Finally, don't forget the writing on the base, which must be perfectly legible: “ THE GREAT CALIBRATOR V1.0 BETA 04/2026" (yes... exactly, I started redesigning it in April lol)”. Try it, send me the print results and let's compare them. Together, we'll find solutions to the most common 3D printing problems and, above all, let's make "THE GREAT CALIBRATOR" a unique and indispensable model for all enthusiasts. description: Most spool desiccant containers on MakerWorld are designed to hold as much desiccant as possible. Notes This design was created to answer a simple question: Why use 40–60 g of desiccant and a large printed container when a spool only needs a fraction of that? So funny story. I love printing things. Therefore I have a lot of plastic waste from poop to supports etc…. A while ago my husband says “your going to need a dumpster for all that plastic”. Then my neighbor noticed the several bags of plastic “poop” I have and said the exact thing. And only when my nephew comes over and says the same thing once again I thought to myself, I need to make a little dumpster to catch all the poop my printer makes. I pictured the Home Alone 2 movie where the house Kevin rigs up has a chute outside the window going into a dumpster. So that's where the idea for project came from. There are tons of “poop” bins and baskets for the other printers but I wanted to make one for my new Bambu Lab A2L printer. She's a beast. Very detailed and prints well. I love it. It does shake the house though being a large sized bed slinger. I have been printing on silent mode to calm it down in most cases. This took me a week to create. A little longer than usual but I needed to get the tolerances perfecta. My main goal was to make it easy and reliable to print. That was the challenge. I tried several ways to get the chute to print as one piece but it never worked out. So clip or bracket that connects to the printer is separate and has to be glued to the chute. I did make a connection socket so the two fit together perfectly so all is needed is a drop of cyanoacrylate glue (Super Glue) or something similar on each edge of the connection opening and hold it in place for the appropriate time (depending on your glue). I have printed 19 sets of the chute and bracket and glued them together successfully with no problem. Supports were absolutely necessary to accomplish my goal. I tried to keep the settings simple but tweaked the settings like the top and bottom Z distance, speed etc… to get dumpster and chute to come out clean. Just be sure to keep my settings. You can add to them if you please but it wont be necessary as you can tell by my photos. I have had several people that don't have a printer me to print them one just because they wanted the cute little bin. I have even been changing the sizes per their requests. The dumpster itself is scalable and you can make a smaller or larger one depending on your needs. I am sure it will have many uses. If this becomes popular enough or I get a few requests I will consider making the bracket portion for the A1 and A1 Mini printers. Thank you ahead of time and please enjoy. Have a nice day.

description: This is a lower profile Chamber Exhaust Fan than the official Bambu “ P2S Chamber Exhaust Fan Kit ”. It uses the same $20 Bambu P2S chamber exhaust fan kit parts . Though design may appear similar to the Original Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan in some ways, it is an entirely different, scratch built design. This design is not in any way associated with Bambu, so use this design at your own risk. No warranties are given. This project was a collaboration with MadMopar (over on MakerWorld). MadMopar had the original idea for a lower profile exhaust duct for the P2S, ran multiple prototypes, provided suggestions and feedback to refine the design, and also provided all the images of the printed design. So a big thanks goes out to MadMopar ! PLEASE NOTE: This profile does not include the poop chute shown in the pics (and the baseplate included here is not compatible with that poop chute design). This model only includes a basic (flat) plate for the poop chute. If you want to use Mc2.project3D's “ Inspectable Waste Chute – Series P / X / H2 ” which is shown in the pics , you will be able to find a remixed backplate and slide which are compatible with that designat the link below (due to the MakerWorld Exclusive License): https://makerworld.com/en/models/2920654-baseplate-only-for-the-inspectable-waste-chute#profileId-3267976 Between MadMopar and myself, many hours have been spent polishing the design, testing and improving it. I feel it is completed, and the one of these ducts in operation currently (with the 2" duct) has been performing well. But if you make or use this design and see anything that could be improved, please provide feedback (positive or negative). I cannot guarantee that the changes will be made, but I will check the comments. I don't own the P2S myself, so if you have a problem, providing pics and accurate measurements would be very helpful. Functionally, this design differs from the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan design in the following key ways: This design has a lower overall profile, which can help in setups with limited room behind the printer. This design uses magnets to hold the duct on, instead of the latches on the stock Bambu design. It was thought that the magnetic attachment would make the duct easier to install or remove when there is limited space behind the printer. This design shifts the whole Exhaust Fan to the left a few mm, which allows for more poop chute options. This does however move the poop chute mount a bit away from the printer, which could be a problem with some poop chute designs (YMMV). This design has an optional TPU gasket, or can be used with 1/16" (1.58mm) thick foam tape, between the backplate and printer, to reduce air leakage. This design does not have room for a HEPA filter , which the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust design does allow for. This design is strictly for venting the chamber either outside or to a separate air cleaner. This design is a bit more complex and expensive to build, since it uses 16x 10x3mm cylinder magnets to hold the duct on, and requires more filament. Currently there are only ducts for a 2" or 2.5" (inside diameter) hose, with options for ducts that angle out at 45°, 90° and straight out from the printer. The 2.5" ducts are untested , and you can find them at the following link: https://www.printables.com/model/1754424-25-ducts-for-bambu-p2s-and-p1-exhaust-see-descript I may add additional ducts in the future, but I plan to upload the STEP models for this design to help with remixing the design. I may upload this in the future to MakerWorld, so I kindly ask that you please do not upload this design to MakerWorld. Thanks for understanding. To build this, the following hardware is needed (in addition to the Bambu P2S Exhaust Fan Kit): 2x M3x20 FHCS (Flat Head Cap Screws) 2x M3x14 (upto 20mm long) FHCS 4x M5x10 Self-Tapping Case Fan Screws 16x 10x3mm Cylinder Magnets 1/16" foam tape (optional) and not needed if using the TPU Gasket Superglue Printing: There are two main profiles available for the main parts. One of the main profiles is set up for ABS and uses brims and mouse ears to help with bed adhesion. The other main profile is set up with PETG, and does not use brims. Both profiles use a textured build plate, however both also specify an Engineering Plate for the optional TPU gasket. The Engineering Plate for TPU is just a suggestion, but I recommend using a smoother plate with glue as a release agent, since TPU tends to aggressively stick to the textured plates. There are additional profiles for the 2" ducts. Any future duct sizes will also have a separate profile. The image below shows the layout of the profile. The only options, aside from the TPU gasket, are the three L-Clip choices. The L-Clips mount into the baseplate, and help to hold the vent fan to the back of the printer, along with 2 screws around the poop chute. The L-Clips are available in different lengths, depending on how the vent fan is configured. There are different L-Clip sizes for using 1/16" foam tape, the optional TPU gasket, or no tape and no TPU gasket (which will probably allow more leakage of air). These options are described below the image: Referring to the above image, the L-Clip options are: A. L-Clips used with 1/16" foam tape (plate 04) B. L-Clips used without the foam tape or TPU gasket (plate 05) C. L-Clips used with the TPU gasket on plate 06 (plate 04) The 3mf profiles included were set up using Bambu Studio v2.7.1.57 and include the following: 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_PETG_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile without brims, for PETG) 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_ABS_w_BRIMS_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile with brims, for ABS) v6Z_2in_Ducts_only.3mf (45°, 90°, dual, and straight through 2" ducts) V1F_2-5in_Ducts.3mf (UNTESTED 45°, 90°, and straight through 2" ducts) The individual STEP models will be added later, when the license is changed to allow for remixing. Assembly: First decide if you plan to use the optional TPU cover, or 1/16" foam tape before gathering the parts. This will determine which type of L-hook is used, and which plates need to be printed. See the above information under “Printing” to decide which size L-Clips you need to use. Start by installing the L-Clips into the baseplate. These will need a bit of glue to hold them in place. Next, remove the two screws around the poop chute. These will be re-installed in the following steps, through the baseplate. If the TPU cover (shown in orange) is going to be used, install it on the baseplate: Install the baseplate onto the back of the printer. First start the right side L-Clip hooks in the corresponding holes on the printer metal backplate, then start the left side hooks. When both are in place and the baseplate will sit flush to the printer, slide the baseplate leftward until it stops. At this point the holes on the plate should align with the holes for the screws around the poop chute which were removed in step 3. These two screws can now be re-installed through the baseplate to help secure it to the printer. Install 8 of the 10x3 cylinder magnets into the cover as shown. Pay special attention to the polarity of these magnets, and how they are installed, so they will attract the magnets which will be installed in the duct. It can help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. I recommend installing the magnets so the poles are all pointed in the same direction, which will make things easier later. A drop of superglue will help secure them. Install the fan into the cover of the printer, using the M5x10 self-tapping fan screws. Make sure the fan power cable wraps either around the top or bottom side of the fan, and will not become pinched. Connect the fan cable to the board from the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit. Use the 3 screws included with the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit to install the board into the cover. You can use the small wire management slot (circled in green) to manage the extra wire. Double check that the wiring is connected and none of the fan wires are pinched (or will get pinched during the next assembly steps). Install the cover (with the fan and board previously installed) onto the baseplate using the M3 flat head screws: Install 8 of the 10x3mm cylinder magnets into the fan duct. Pay special attention to the polarity of the magnets here, since they should all be set up to attract the magnets already installed in the fan cover. It may help to set the magnets onto the fan cover magnets, prior to installing, so you can verify they will attract and not repel. If your magnets are not all set up as north or south on the fan cover and duct, be sure to orient the duct in the final position before installing magnets in it, otherwise it may attract on some and repell on others. It can also help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. A drop of superglue may help them stay. description: 一板在手，测试无忧！ 这是一个集成了多种经典校准项目的3D打印综合测试模型，无需打印多个测试件，即可快速评估打印机的整体状态与参数设置。 模型尺寸小巧，耗材消耗少，适合： ✓ 新打印机验机 ✓ 更换耗材后校准 ✓ 调整切片参数验证 ✓ 打印机维护保养检查 ✓ 不同材料打印性能对比 测试项目说明 1. 收缩率测试（Shrinkage） 用于检测模型实际尺寸与设计尺寸的偏差。 重点观察： 长度尺寸是否准确 XY方向收缩情况 常见问题： 尺寸偏小 孔位缩小 装配件配合困难 可能原因： 材料收缩率较大 流量设置过高 冷却不足 解决方案： 调整XY补偿 校准Flow Ratio 优化打印温度 2. 悬垂测试（Overhang） 用于评估无需支撑时的打印能力。 测试角度： 10°~80° 重点观察： 边缘下垂 表面粗糙 层线变形 塌腰等 可能原因： 风扇风量不足 打印温度过高 打印速度过快 角度过大，超过打印极限 解决方案： 增大冷却风量 降低喷嘴温度 减小外壁速度 添加支撑 3. 搭桥测试（Bridging） 用于测试跨空打印能力。 重点观察： 中间是否下垂 是否出现拉丝 桥面是否平整 可能原因： 冷却不足 挤出量过小 速度设置不合理 解决方案： 提高桥接风扇速度 加大桥接流量 4. 球形效果测试（Sphere Quality） 用于检测曲面打印质量。 重点观察： 圆滑程度 层纹均匀性 接缝表现 可能原因： Z轴抖动 振纹（Ghosting） 机械间隙 解决方案： 检查皮带张力 校准Z轴 5. 拉丝测试（Stringing） 通过多个尖塔检测耗材拉丝情况。 重点观察： 塔之间是否出现细丝 丝线粗细程度 可能原因： 回抽不足 温度过高 耗材受潮 解决方案： 增大回抽距离 降低打印温度 烘干耗材 6. 尖锥测试（Spike Test） 用于测试尖端细节表现能力。 重点观察： 尖端是否完整 是否融化变钝 可能原因： 温度过高 冷却不足 解决方案： 降低温度 提高最小层时间 增加冷却风量 7. 色卡测试（Color Sample） 方便记录不同厚度耗材颜色效果。 用途： 耗材展示 配色参考 打印样品留档 8. 薄壁测试（Thin Wall） 测试打印机极限壁厚能力。 重点观察： 是否缺层 是否断裂 实际壁厚误差 可能原因： 流量不准 喷嘴磨损 挤出系统异常 解决方案： 校准流量 检查喷嘴状态 9. 表面质量测试（Surface Finish） 观察打印层纹与整体表面表现。 重点观察： 层纹均匀性 振纹 接缝质量 可能原因： 速度过快 机械共振 温度不匹配 解决方案： 调整加速度 优化打印温度 校准流量 10. 填充结构展示（Infill Pattern） 模型内置拓竹切片软件的全部填充结构： 可用于： 学习不同填充结构特点 对比强度与打印速度 如果这个模型对你有所帮助，欢迎点赞、助力、收藏并上传你的打印成果！ 祝大家打印顺利，层层完美！

description: X2D Support Test – Multi-Material Support Benchmark Dieses Modell wurde speziell entwickelt, um die Qualität von Supportstrukturen und Multi-Material-Drucke objektiv zu bewerten. Durch die verschiedenen Überhänge, Aussparungen, Brücken und Kontaktflächen eignet sich der Test hervorragend, um die Druckqualität unterschiedlicher Materialkombinationen zu vergleichen und optimale Einstellungen für saubere Support-Oberflächen zu finden. Was wird getestet? Oberflächenqualität über Supportstrukturen Maßhaltigkeit kritischer Geometrien Qualität von Überhängen und Brücken Trennbarkeit der Supports Einfluss verschiedener Interface-Materialien Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch Vorteile von Multi-Material Supports Durch die Verwendung eines separaten Support-Interface-Materials lassen sich deutlich sauberere Unterseiten und Kontaktflächen erzielen als mit Supports aus dem gleichen Material. Besonders bei anspruchsvollen Überhängen können dadurch: glattere Oberflächen bessere Maßhaltigkeit weniger Nacharbeit einfachere Supportentfernung erreicht werden. Empfohlene Druckvarianten Variante 1 – Nur Support-Interface in anderem Material (empfohlen) Hier wird das Modell und die eigentlichen Supportstrukturen mit dem Hauptmaterial gedruckt. Lediglich die Support-Schnittstellen (Support Interface Layers) werden mit einem zweiten Material erzeugt. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports: PLA Support Interface: PETG Diese Methode bietet in der Regel das beste Verhältnis aus Druckqualität, Materialverbrauch und Druckzeit. Variante 2 – Komplette Supports in anderem Material Alternativ können sowohl die Supportstrukturen als auch die Support-Schnittstellen vollständig aus einem zweiten Material gedruckt werden. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports + Interface: PETG Diese Variante kann die Trennbarkeit weiter verbessern, erhöht jedoch den Materialwechsel erheblich. Wichtig: Durch die vielen Werkzeugwechsel zwischen den Materialien verlängert sich die Druckzeit deutlich und es entsteht zusätzlicher Materialabfall durch Spülvorgänge. Für die meisten Anwendungen ist daher Variante 1 die sinnvollere Wahl. Empfohlene Materialkombinationen PLA ↔ PETG PETG ↔ PLA ASA ↔ Support Material ABS ↔ Support Material Viel Spaß beim Testen! Teile gerne deine Ergebnisse, Einstellungen und Materialkombinationen in den Kommentaren, damit andere Nutzer von deinen Erfahrungen profitieren können. Hinweis Die Vorschaubilder und Darstellungen in diesem Eintrag wurden mithilfe von KI-generierten Grafiken erstellt und dienen ausschließlich der Veranschaulichung des Druckkonzepts. Das tatsächliche Druckergebnis kann je nach Drucker, Material und Einstellungen abweichen.

Hanuman is the main character and a heroic general in the Thai literary work *Ramakien* (based on India’s *Ramayana* epic). He is the son of Phra Phai (the Wind God) and Nang Sawaha, having been conceived when a weapon of Shiva struck and entered Sawaha’s mouth. **Distinctive Characteristics and Supernatural Powers:** **Appearance:** Hanuman is a white monkey (with a white body), wearing earrings (*kundala*), possessing diamond-like fur and crystal-like fangs. When displaying his full power, he appears with four faces and eight arms. **Special Abilities:** He can fly through the air, transform his shape, enlarge his body to a gigantic size, extend his tail to great lengths, and even yawn stars and moons into existence. **Immortality:** As the son of the Wind God, if he is killed by an enemy’s weapon, he can immediately return to life as long as the wind blows upon his body. **Personality and Role:** Hanuman is deeply loyal to Rama and serves as a commander of the army in the war against Ravana’s forces, ultimately helping secure victory. Unlike the original Indian version, where Hanuman is a celibate devotee, the Hanuman of Thai literature is portrayed as flirtatious and romantic. description: Update June 18, 2026 There's been an update to the hinge left and right part, they now fit both the original AMS lid and the Eibos Tetras/Dyas lid. To "upgrade", all you need to reprint are the actual hinges. The print profiles have been updated as well. Thanks to @Skood for the feedback! About This is an AMS to AMS 2 Pro Lid Conversion, it's needed for using the Eibos Tetras or Dyas lid on the AMS 2 Pro. It is also required for the upcoming Hydra x Tetras and Kraken x Tetras mods for the AMS 2 Pro, which is the main reason for this release. The other upside is it acts as a lid riser, allowing for larger spools to be used. Support All my designs and mods on MakerWorld are free to use and remix. They have a non-commercial license. If you enjoy this or any of my other designs you can send me a small donation using the link below. Thanks :) https://www.paypal.me/humebeamengineering Bill of Materials You need some M3 socket heads. If you've used any of my mods in the past you probably have all you need already. The following M3 socket heads are needed: 18 x M3-12 mm Meaning 12 mm long screws (the threaded part). The length is not super crucial, you can use a little shorter if needed but not too long (max length is 14 mm). If you don't have any at home it's best to grab this kit, it will have everything you need for this build and more: 150 pcs M3 Hex Socket Head Kit Print settings All parts print without supports. The main parts print upside down while the hinges and the middle rear print normally. If you're not certain, please use the included 3MF file where everything is rotated correctly. I recommend using 3 walls and 15% gyroid infill or higher. If you intend on using a heater, either stock AMS 2 Pro or Tetras, I recommend printing it in ABS or ASA or higher heat deflection temp. Assembly Instructions Remove AMS 2 Pro lid from the box, it sits with four hex head screws from below, two on each side below the hinge. Use a 2.0 mm hex key to remove them. Keep these screws for later as you reuse them for the assembly of this mod. In this example I'm using an empty AMS 2 Pro box and original AMS lid rather than a Tetras lid but the assembly is the same. For a nice look you can have the main parts in one colour and the accents in another, in my case I went with Prusament ASA Galaxy Black for the main parts and Prusament ASA Pro Green in the accents (hinges, lid lock bars etc. Remove the lid gasket from the AMS 2 Pro. It just sits with double sided tape from below and you don't have to keep the stickyness or even the double sided tape of the bottom of the gasket as it will sit with press fit (U-shaped slot with top edge) once you're done with the mod so it will stay in place. To remove the gasket, you can just pull and tilt it a little with a hex tool then just pull it straight up and out. Now before you continue, please dry mount all socket heads in the printed parts. The reason for this is to ensure they screw in correctly as they self thread into the printed parts. Do this for all 20 screw holes including the hinges, example below just shows on the front joint block. Front Assembly Assemble the three front parts using the two front joints. Here you can use two of the stock screws you got when you removed the stock lid. They go in the countersunk holes in the front left and right parts, into the front joints, the rectangular piece with cut corners in green in the pic below. At the same time, screw down the locking bars using 2 x M3-12 mm socket heads so that they are fully tightened. Ensure you turn the original locking bars for the lid site fully sideways on both sides as the lid conversion installs above it, take a look at the cutouts two pictures above. Press in the "front" assembled piece in the slot. Rear Assembly Next, continue with the middle rear, rear left and rear right pieces. It should now look something like this. If there seem to be minor gaps don't worry, the parts overlap so they fully interlock and do in fact seal fully together with the gasket. Screw Assembly In Place Now it's time to screw the assembly to the AMS box to ensure everything sits in place with no gaps. Use 16 x M3-12 mm socket heads and washers and screw from below, you should see the screw holes if you flip the box upside down or turn it on its side, do whatever you feel is easier. Screw them down fully so it sits gapless but don't overtighten them, remember these just screw into plastic. But be careful and it will be fine. Do the same for both sides. And also the two rear screw locations (those screw into the middle rear piece): Install AMS 2 Pro Gasket You can use either the original AMS gasket or the AMS 2 Pro gasket but since you're likely installing the Tetras (or one of my Tetras mods) you'll likely use the AMS 2 Pro gasket here. As with all gaskets, begin with the corners, press the gasket down and center it using a 2.5 mm hex tool. Do all four corners first, it will not look perfect but it will once you are done. :) Continue doing the same at the middle and quarter positions. Once you have done that you can just tilt and slide the hex tool across the gasket and spread it evenly, ensuring the gasket slot is centered in the middle (it should do that automatically). The gasket should now be perfectly centered in the printed slot. Installing the original AMS lid (or Eibos Tetras/Dyas lid) Most likely you are installing the Eibos Tetras/Dyas lid but it also fits the original AMS lid. To install the lid, just place the left and right printed hinges into the lid, they are marked L for left and R for right. :) Top image is the Tetras, bottom image is of the original AMS lid. Notice! For the Tetras/Dyas lid, the hinge pins are slotted and only fit into the printed hinge in a certain angle, just line up and press it all the way in and you're good to go. Then press it down into the slot at the rear and fasten it with 6 x M3-12 mm socket heads and washers, same as the rest of the printed parts. All done! Test closing the lid and that the locking tabs hold it down firmly. The lid should seal fully in the gasket.

In the Customizer, edit: text_line_1 : main text, for example PETG text_line_2 : optional second line, for example 55C text_line_1_size : size of the first line text_line_2_size : size of the second line line_spacing : distance between the two text lines font_family : choose the font font_style : regular, bold, italic, etc. Leave text_line_2 empty if you want a single-line tag. Batch tags Use batch_tags.scad if you want to generate several tags at once. Similarly to the single tag generator, in Batch text settings you can adjust: single_line_text_size : text size used for one-line tags double_line_1_text_size : text size used for the first line of two-line tags double_line_2_text_size : text size used for the second line of two-line tags line_spacing : distance between the two text lines font_family : choose the font font_style : regular, bold, italic, etc. In the batch_texts field: Use a comma , to separate different tags. Use a vertical bar | to split one tag into two lines. Examples: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA PETG|CF → PETG will be in first row, CF in the second PLA, PETG|55C, ABS|70C, ASA, TPU This will generate multiple tags in one plate. model_name: Printer test model when buying used printers 50g
description: Ever buy a used printer and not be confident that it works as advertised? Don't take that gamble! Send the seller this test model to run prior to you arriving, and request that they leave it on the build plate as proof that the printer works as advertised. There is no denying that the printer printed it, if its still stuck to the build plate when you arrive! This model is not a calibration model , it does not test over hangs, extrusion, nothing like that. This test was designed to make sure the printer can print most of the build plate, as well as show that the Z axis is clean and not bend. You can scale it up or down, but going too small will make that first layer pretty thin. I recommend scaling so the bottom is only 1 layer thick. That will show you how even the bed is and if the printer can print big flat models. The vertical part will show the z axis wear and tear, as well as show layer shifts, VFAs, ghosting and overall print quality. Check around the engraved letters for ghosting and VFAs, check around the corners to see proper extrusion and cornering and ringing, check the circle section to see if there are visible layer shifting. Finally check the pyramid top to ensure it can complete a top without knocking the entire model below over. Again, this is not a test of calibration, just a simple test model for you to be confident that the used printer you are buying can perform basic 3D printer tasks. I am uploading profiles for most current BambuLab Printers, as well as including the STL for other printers.

model_name: A1, A2L Swiveling PTFE Tube Guide - Parametric
description: Bambu A1 and A2L Swiveling PTFE Tube Guide - Parametric, with Print-in-Place Ball Joint If you've ever glanced over mid-print and noticed your drybox or your AMS Lite slowly sliding toward the print bed - pulled there by a taut filament tube - this one's for you. PTFE tube management is one of those details that seems trivial until it isn't. A loose or unsecured tube puts real tension on whatever it's attached to: a desktop spool holder, an AMS Lite, or a drybox on a shelf. Some existing guides rely on a dovetail joint or a friction fit that works fine in theory - until the repeated motion of printing slowly works the joint loose, and by the time you notice something is wrong, your setup has already been dragged somewhere it shouldn't be. I learned this the hard way so I designed my own. My design uses a fully print-in-place ball joint: it articulates freely so the tube always follows the print head without resistance, but the ball is physically captured inside the housing - there's no clip, no friction fit, nothing that can pull apart under load. The lever is printed horizontally so its strength doesn't rely on layer adhesion at all. And the C-clip uses a carefully angled opening that holds the tubes in place during normal use. Fully Parametric Configure four values to match your setup: Guide placement - top of the printer (usually for external spools) or towards the front (usually for a side-mounted AMS Lite) Guide diameter - size the C-clip to your tube count and diameter Lever length - a short lever works for most prints; increase it if you frequently print very tall models and need more slack Ball joint offset - position the guide towards the front, center, or back of the top bar Pre-configured standard variants are published alongside this model, so if your setup is typical you can go straight to printing without touching a single parameter. Printing note After printing, gently move the lever in the joint until it becomes loose and starts swiveling. Longer lever variants require a small horizontal bridge support under the lever. The included print profiles handle this automatically. Happy printing !

model_name: Flashforge Adventurer 5M Full Enclosure Mod MIX
description: Flashforge Adventurer 5M Full Enclosure Mod MIX Este projeto transforma a Flashforge Adventurer 5M numa máquina fechada, mais organizada e com aspeto mais “premium”, mantendo o acesso fácil à impressora e melhorando a proteção contra correntes de ar, pó e variações de temperatura. O design foi pensado para usar peças impressas em 3D juntamente com painéis transparentes, criando uma estrutura fechada mas funcional. Inclui portas frontais, painéis laterais, suportes, dobradiças, puxadores, gaveta inferior, suporte para ferramentas e vários detalhes estéticos em cor secundária. Ideal para quem quer melhorar a Adventurer 5M sem perder acesso ao interior da impressora. Principais características Enclosure completo para a Flashforge Adventurer 5M Estrutura modular impressa em várias peças Portas frontais transparentes com dobradiças impressas Painéis laterais transparentes Tampa superior transparente Melhor proteção contra correntes de ar Ajuda a manter temperatura mais estável dentro da câmara Gaveta inferior para ferramentas ou acessórios Suportes laterais para ferramentas Suporte/encaixe para termómetro/higrómetro Moldura para o ecrã original Design com peças decorativas em cor secundária Compatível com setup com AMS/spool externo ao lado Visual inspirado em enclosure industrial/modular Materiais recomendados Para melhores resultados recomendo imprimir as peças principais em: PETG ASA ABS PLA+ apenas se não forem usadas temperaturas de câmara muito altas As peças decorativas, puxadores, dobradiças e suportes podem ser impressas em PLA/PETG sem problema. No projeto das fotos foram usadas cores: Cinzento para a estrutura principal Preto para a base e algumas partes inferiores Laranja para detalhes, dobradiças, puxadores e peças decorativas Alguns detalhes adicionais em azul/verde Painéis transparentes Este enclosure foi pensado para usar painéis transparentes em acrílico, policarbonato ou material semelhante. Recomendo usar: Acrílico transparente de 2 mm a 3 mm ou Policarbonato transparente de 2 mm a 3 mm O policarbonato é mais resistente, mas o acrílico é mais fácil de encontrar e cortar. Peças incluídas O projeto inclui várias peças separadas para facilitar a impressão: Colunas frontais Colunas traseiras Molduras superiores Molduras inferiores Dobradiças das portas Fechos/puxadores Moldura do ecrã Gaveta inferior frontal Suportes de ferramentas Peças decorativas Suportes laterais Peças para fixação dos painéis Componentes superiores para tampa/painel acrílico As peças foram divididas para caberem na cama da Adventurer 5M. Montagem A montagem é simples, mas recomendo montar por etapas: Imprimir todas as peças principais da estrutura. Montar primeiro as colunas laterais/frontais. Instalar as peças superiores e inferiores. Cortar e testar os painéis transparentes. Montar as portas frontais com dobradiças. Instalar os fechos e puxadores. Colocar a tampa superior transparente. Ajustar folgas e alinhar as portas. Adicionar gaveta, suportes e acessórios. Não apertes todos os parafusos logo no início. É melhor deixar alguma folga, alinhar tudo e só depois apertar definitivamente. Hardware necessário Pode variar conforme a montagem, mas em geral vais precisar de: Parafusos M3 Porcas M3 Algumas porcas inseridas ou porcas normais Ímanes pequenos, se quiseres melhorar o fecho das portas Painéis acrílicos/policarbonato Fita dupla face ou parafusos, dependendo da fixação escolhida Termómetro/higrómetro pequeno, opcional LEDs, opcional Definições de impressão recomendadas Para peças estruturais: Altura de camada: 0.20 mm Paredes: 3 a 4 Infill: 15% a 25% Top/Bottom: 4 ou mais camadas Suportes: conforme orientação da peça Material: PETG/ASA/ABS recomendado Para peças decorativas: Altura de camada: 0.16 mm ou 0.20 mm Paredes: 2 a 3 Infill: 10% a 15% As peças maiores devem ser impressas com boa adesão à mesa para evitar warping. Notas importantes Este mod não é uma peça oficial da Flashforge. Verifica sempre se o movimento da cabeça de impressão, cama e cabos não fica bloqueado após a montagem. Se imprimires materiais que libertam mais calor ou gases, garante ventilação adequada. Para PLA, deixa a porta aberta ou controla a temperatura interna para evitar amolecimento do filamento durante impressões longas. Resultado final O resultado é uma Adventurer 5M totalmente modificada, com aspeto muito mais robusto e organizado. A impressora fica protegida, visualmente mais limpa e com muito mais espaço para acessórios, ferramentas e melhorias futuras. Este projeto é ideal para quem gosta de modificar a impressora, melhorar o setup e dar à AD5M um visual único.

这类箱式高速打印机，加装顶部增高架已是玩家主流刚需改装，具备两大不可替代的核心价值：一是有效抬升机身，彻底解决机型通病的特氟龙管长期摩擦顶盖、磨损破皮的问题，大幅延长耗材管路寿命；二是搭配磁吸开窗结构，可在夏季高温打印场景下开启腔体对流，快速释放机身积热，避免高温掉速、打印瑕疵。 本套 顶部磁吸外排模组 ，正是基于成熟的增高架散热专属开发、针对性升级迭代，需 搭载独家磁吸散热增高架及其专属后板 集管路防护、官方外排套件、磁吸对流散热、废气定向外排、物件收纳、排风管道承重于一体 的完整顶部生态系统。 整套结构对位精准、风道闭环、稳固性拉满，是 适配拓竹 X2D/P2S 机型 、兼顾日常散热与废气外排需求的最优多功能组合方案。本模组无法单独适配原厂裸机，需搭配磁吸增高架基座，不支持裸机独立使用， 磁吸散热增高架对于拓竹X/P系列打印机增益巨大，几乎是必打配件 ，并搭配上独家改装的一体式带抽屉多功能增高架能够充分发挥机器顶部优势，老玩家亲测好用（X2D拆了原装外排换成这款方案）， 具体优势介绍详见上面的链接 。 二、原厂后置排风结构缺陷 & 本方案改良优势 原厂后置排风结构核心问题： 原厂风扇后置居中安装，长期使用存在 两大硬伤 ： ①顶部积热无法散除 ：热空气自然上浮，打印热源全部堆积在腔体顶部， 但原厂低位排风无法带走顶部滞留高温 ，容易造成腔体积热，挤出机堵头、打印不稳定，舱内异味残留久。 ② 丝杆易积灰积油泥 ： 后置风路会直接穿过丝杆传动区域 ，打印粉尘、碎屑被气流持续吹附至丝杆润滑脂表面，长期堆积形成油泥，增大运行阻力、加剧磨损，需要频繁拆机维护清洁，设备养护成本高。 ③ P2S 机型改造成本高 ：传统后置改装大多需要更换全新机身后板，改动成本高、通用性差、不够轻量化。 本套顶部外排方案核心改进： ①风道完全合理化： 风扇移至机身最顶端，正对积热区定点抽风，热气、废气、粉尘上浮即被抽出，腔体降温更快、排风更彻底。 ②全程保护丝杆传动结构： 风路不再经过丝杆区域，从根源杜绝粉尘油污堆积，大幅延长丝杆保养周期，保持传动精度与顺滑度。 ③无需更换机身背板 ：配套专属原厂后开孔密封打印件，直接封闭机身底部、背部原生出风乱流通道，集中风压向上排风，无损机身、零替换硬件。 ④磁吸无损、拆装自由： 背部多点强磁对位，贴合增高架专用台面，打印不震动、不异响、不脱落，可徒手快拆复原，维护极其方便。 ⑤适配加厚风管外排场景： 可搭配独家带抽屉多功能一体式增高架，自带外挂点位，在适配铝箔排风管以外，可稳定挂载加厚布基排风软管，解决重管下坠、拉扯壳体问题，适配长期密闭房间打印除味散热。 三、整体结构与功能说明 双模式顶盖通用： 提供直排、管道外排两款顶盖，通风良好环境用直排模式散热更快；居家密闭环境可接风管将废气异味直接导出室外。 原厂电路完全复用： 沿用原厂风扇主板，走线垂直规整，直连机身缓冲器接口，无绕线、无龙门干涉，运行稳定。 整机风道闭环： 增高架抬升机身 + 背部底部密封 + 侧窗对流泄压 + 顶部定点抽风，散热效率远超原厂结构。 四、安装指南！！ 全程 无损机身 、 无需改机 ，仅打印件+简单零件装配即可完成 打印须知： 打印完所需零件后即可开始安装，底座 区分 X2D、P2S 两款专用底壳不可通用 （X2D底壳有规避远程挤出机），对应机型打印对应底壳； 顶盖两款机型通用，分为 直排款与管道外排款 ，外排款细分为 无挂钩款与带挂钩款 ， 优先推荐打印带挂钩顶盖并配套同款挂钩 ； 若已打印 适配本散热模组的增高架版本 则无需打印后部出风口挡板； 原厂 背板保留散热孔 则 必须打印 封闭风道挡板 ； 配置文件里给 X2D双头机型 配套了三套 PETG 主料 + PLA 支撑双料打印文件（可互换），支撑易拆除，无双料打印需求可选用全套单料版本，全部打印参数已预设完毕，导入 BambuStudio 仅核对耗材配置即可使用。 1. 预埋热熔螺母（前置关键步骤） 所有风扇与壳体固定位需预埋热熔螺母，防止长期拆装滑丝、锁止不紧： 风扇底部固定孔：使用 M3×3×4.2 热熔螺母【红箭头】 description: I am a big fan of star wars and the mandalorian.. A few weeks ago i saw a video of the new mandalorian and grogu water sipper on disneyland.. i think it is so cool that i made one myself.. using a water bottle i got from aliexpress and modified it into a mandalorian jetpack.. Here are the things you'll need for the build: water bottle - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c4KHeTTF nylon ribbon straps 38mm - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c3ToSnqZ water sipper nozzle - my affiliate links on aliexpress.. https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c3CnCPsZ https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c2QrQKgN drill bit - to drill a hole in the water bottle cap compression springs - 7x12mm I printed mine using PLA for the metalic color but for durability you might want to print it using PETG or ABS.. Add a layer coating of transparent UV spray for protection of the jetpack.. once everything is printed.. test fit the bottle and mark where to drill the hole on the bottle.. you need to insert the tube through all the parts before assembling.. all jetpack parts will have pegs as well as butterfly inserts that needs to be glued on.. it will be easier to assemble left and right side rather than top and bottom.. the lock arms need 2 filament insert to hold the lock in place the bottom of the jetpack will have a screw on cap.. the cap is spring loaded to push the bottle out when the locking mechanism is pushed.. For the straps i made 2 version.. 1 with the sipper tube holder.. the belt straps are 1meter long each.. it should fit a child.. you might want to extend it a bit around20-40cm for adults.. The whole backpack weight about 1kg without water in it.. It uses about 1.1kg filament.. I used PLA silk silver for the jetpack.. I have also made a version with grogu hanging on the jetpack just like the disneyland version.. it does make the jetpack slightly heavier.. The grogu is printed in seperate colors so no need for AMS for it.. I will only share the grogu add-on model on makerworld once i have reach 200 BOOST for the jetpack .. or if you can't wait for that.. you can purchase the grogu add-on on my buymeacoffee page for USD4.. description: Want a realistic life-size V40 Mini Grenade with a flying handle? This model is 100% brand new from the ground-up with stronger parts, easy screw-on assembly, and enhanced realism. What is the v40 Mini Grenade? The V40 Mini Grenade is an unusually compact fragmentation hand grenade developed in the Netherlands that is roughly the size of a golf ball. Weighing just 4.8 ounces, it allowed soldiers to carry the weapon in much greater quantities than standard fragmentation grenades. It gained historical fame for its utilization by U.S. special operations units during the Vietnam War. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu Filaments used Metal Iron Gray black Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Bambu Matte Dark Green is the closest Bambu filament Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the peg into the grenade topper as you see below. 2. Then insert a metal spring int the same way. 3. Lastly, screw the topper onto the body of the grenade – it helps to do this upside down or sideways so the spring doesn't fall out. Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the printed plastic spring into the grenade topper as you see below. Make sure the peg at the top of the spring is sticking out the top, rotate it until it pops out if not. 2. Lastly, screw the topper onto the grenade body – its easiest if you do this upside down or sideways.

For ultimate outdoor durability and UV protection (crucial if you troop in sunny weather), use SUNLU ASA Filament . For multi-part prop builds like the helmet visor, utility belt, and large chest plates, conventional superglues are a weak point waiting to snap on the showroom floor. Instead, I highly recommend plastic welding your seams together. By using a hot stapler / plastic welder kit, you can melt metal reinforcing staples directly across the interior seams of your prints, followed by smoothing the plastic over with a hot iron attachment. description: Wearable Iron Man MK3 helmet , fully optimized for printing on all 3D printers, including the A1 Mini. Stop wasting your time and start printing this masterpiece! The model dimensions are designed based on what I consider the international standard: Budwin's Sizing Head No. 3 , whom I deeply thank for making it available and making everyone's life easier. Main Features & Smart Cutting No Harsh Cuts: The cuts follow the helmet's design lines, making the joints invisible from the outside for a clean look. No Circling: Dividing the model into pieces eliminates the "stair-stepping" effect on the dome typical of single-piece prints, ensuring a smooth surface with no sanding needed. Easy Printing: Splitting the project reduces individual print session times and the risk of failures, making it accessible to anyone with any printer. Multi-Color Without AMS: The black and gold parts are separated from the main body, allowing you to print them directly with the correct color filament even without an automatic material system. Improved Ergonomics and Fit: The back section has been modified for a complete design, the ears have been hollowed out to increase width, and the eyes are perforated to ensure visibility. Custom Display Stand: In the last photo, you can see this fantastic stand custom-made for this helmet to display it at its best! Magnetic Mechanics (No Electronics!) By following the video instructions and watching the uploaded GIFs, you can achieve a fully functional mechanical opening without the need for complex circuits. Magnetic Back: The first GIF shows you how to implement a magnetic closure that improves fit when wearing the helmet. On plate number 9, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed to close the back of the mask. Magnetic Faceplate: The second GIF shows you how to implement magnets that allow the mask to open and lock onto the upper section. High-quality magnets are recommended for a stronger hold. On plates number 10 and 11, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed for this purpose. Hidden Magnet Clips: The front and back clips have a different design. The front ones are specifically engineered to completely hide the magnets from view; however, they require a stronger magnet grip, so feel free to use the clips from plate 9 for both purposes. However, you still need Plate 10 because it has the taller clips used to keep the faceplate open! Maximum Freedom: By separating the magnet holders from the main structure of the helmet, the final choice is up to you: you can use this magnetic system, implement your own motorized electronic mechanisms, or simply weld all the pieces together. 🛠️ Assembly Guide The pieces must be joined after printing. Among the uploaded photos, you will also find a visual diagram explaining how to pair them. You can use glue, but for the best results, a permanent bond, and high mechanical resistance, I recommend using a soldering iron or a 3D pen to carefully melt and weld the joints from the inside . I welded the entire helmet myself without any problems, as you can see for yourself from the photos of the finished project! Pro-tip: I recommend starting by joining the top and back-top pieces. Since they are the largest parts, they are the trickiest, join them by gently pressing the two parts together to ensure there is no gap. All of this makes this mask a masterpiece! Happy printing! - GB

description: This is the elven sword Sting , Frodo's sword from The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. The sword is designed in a full-scale 1:1 size and has an overall length of 559 mm . Both the blade and the guard feature the original Elvish inscriptions. Maegnas aen estar nín – dagnir in yngyl im = "Sting is my name; I am the bane of spiders." The core of the sword consists of a 490 mm long M5 threaded rod , which mechanically connects all parts into one solid assembly without the use of glue. A safety M5 nut is embedded in the Blade_up part. A second safety M5 nut is inserted into the Grip part, which is designed for two-color filament printing using an AMS system. A standard M5 nut is embedded in the Pommel_A part. The assembly procedure and part layout can be seen in the exploded_view drawing located in the gallery of this model. For an impressive effect, the blade is printed using fluorescent PLA filament that glows blue in the dark after being exposed to light, just as Sting glowed blue in the movies when orcs were nearby. For the blade, I used Spectrum PLA Glow in the Dark Blue filament. To further enhance the display and allow the sword to be hung on a wall, I also designed a dedicated wall mount. The wall mount features beautiful golden ornaments and the inscription from the One Ring: The base of the wall mount is printed in two separate parts, which are fastened together using three M5×30 socket head screws and nuts . A separately printed ring featuring the inscription from the One Ring, along with the golden ornaments, is glued into the base. The sword itself is supported by two M6 L-hooks with a length of 60 mm . The assembly and all individual parts can be seen in the exploded_view image located in the gallery of this model. The threaded rod, screws, nuts, and L-hooks can be purchased at any Hobby market. The print profile is well-tuned and easy to print, making this project suitable for everyone. I hope this sword brings you joy, and enjoy its blue glow during the evening hours—it is truly an impressive sight, just like in the The Lord of the Rings movies. Happy printing!

Important Note The original model is a little rough in places, so I would not really recommend printing this unless you are planning to fill, sand, and finish it properly. It can absolutely look great once cleaned up, but this is not really a “print it, pull it off the bed, done” type of model. description: Want a replica of an early war WW2 88mm Tiger Tank round with an optional casing? This model easily screws together and includes insertable text so you don't need an AMS. There's an optional casing (the brass/gold part below the round) that you can print that also screws together. What makes this an early war shell? When the WW2 Tiger I tank first entered service around 1942, Germany still had enough copper that they could produce shells with copper driving bands. This round has copper driving bands (signified by the KPS markings) and doesn't include the hardened ballistic cap that was introduced later in the war (which is signified by a white painted tip and a “1” painted near the tip). Later in the war, Germany didn't have enough copper so they switched to a soft sintered iron instead of copper (signified by FES markings). Bambu filaments used Shell/Round Metal Iron Gray Black Matte White Matte Red Sunlu Silk Red Copper ( Amazon link ) Closest Bambu filament is Silk+ Rose Gold Optional Brass Casing GiantArm Silk Gold ( Amazon link ) Closest Bambu filament is Silk+ Gold Assembly takes seconds Simply screw together the pieces as you see below: Then insert the text into the corresponding holes. Make sure you shine a light into the holes and make sure all the support material is removed before inserting the text. Its also a good idea to keep track of the order of the text and insert right after removing the letters from the plate. Ensure that the curved side is facing out. Optional Brass Casing Simply screw the pieces together and then insert the round into the top. Note: if you are printing this casing to fit the older v1 88mm round that was previously released, then print the adapter in addition to the casing so it fits more snugly.

description: Instant Ronin Double Tanto - Magnetic Knives Channel your inner samurai with the Instant Ronin - Double Tanto (Magnetic Edition) ! This isn't just a pair of sleek 3D-printable props—it's a fully mechanical, dual-sword ecosystem. By utilising a precise arrangement of 5-off 6mm x 3mm magnets per sword, these Tantos completely ditch traditional metal springs for solid-state physics. But here is the real kicker: One sword acts as the activator for the other. Mating the companion sword into the other triggers the magnetic mechanisms, releasing the internal locks and allowing for an instant, seamless locking - and the reverse when withdrawing. Absolutely zero glue required. Every magnet pocket has been engineered for a perfect, satisfying, push-fit. Print two, link them up, and prepare to lose hours of your life to the ultimate fidget experience. Features Triple-Action Magnetic Mechanics: Uses opposing and attracting magnetic fields to safely lock the blades closed, assist the deployment, and lock them open. 5-Magnet Precision Layout: Optimised specifically for standard, high-strength 6mm x 3mm cylinder magnets (5-off per sword). 100% Glue-Free Assembly: Meticulously tuned tolerances mean every magnet snaps tightly into place. Save the superglue for fixing the things you break with the Tanto. Zero Mechanical Springs: No metal springs to find, bend, fatigue, or lose tension over time—magnetism doesn't wear out! Dual-Tanto Blade Profile: A sleek, aggressive geometric aesthetic that looks as sharp as the mechanism feels. Maximum Fidget Factor Magnet Assembly Guide ⚠️ Crucial Tip: Because these are a push-fit, double-check your magnet orientation before you press them home. Getting a backward magnet out of a tight 3D-printed pocket is a special kind of pain you don't want to experience. Use a spare magnet as a reference tool! Follow this exact sequence to ensure the polarity works flawlessly, see my sectioned CAD image and assembly pictures to help with the below: The Master Slider Magnet [1]: Push a magnet into the bottom pocket of the Blade Slider . This can face any direction you like. Once it’s in, this magnet is the "Master" that dictates the rest of the build. The Extended Lock [2]: Press a magnet into the lower forward pocket of the Handle . This magnet must REPEL Magnet #1. (This repelling force is the secret sauce that lifts the slider up into the notch to lock the blade open!) The Retracted Lock [3]: Press a magnet into the bottom rear pocket of the Handle . This magnet must ATTRACT Magnet #1, snapping the blade securely closed so they doesn't slide apart when closed. The Kinetic "Spring" Caps [4]: Press one magnet into each of the two Circular Caps at the top hilt. Both of these magnets must REPEL each other, creating that crisp, snappy detent.

description: Ultimate Static Prop Gun: Springfield Armory Hellcat Model Description Bring one of the most iconic modern micro-compact firearms to life with this ultra-detailed, 1:1 scale replica of the Springfield Armory Hellcat . This is a completely solid, non-firing static prop gun designed with absolute safety and realism in mind. This model features zero moving parts —the slide, trigger, magazine, and safety switches are completely fused into the mold. It cannot chamber ammunition, chamber BBs, or fire projectiles of any kind , making it a 100% inert, convention-safe prop. Designed with precision in CAD, this version comes fully decked out with an integrated low-profile Red Dot Reflex Sight and a tactical Barrel Compensator (often mistaken for a compact suppressor) attached to the threaded muzzle for the ultimate tactical look. It is strictly a display piece, cosplay accessory, training aid, or film prop. The History of the Springfield Armory Hellcat Introduced in 2019, the Springfield Armory Hellcat revolutionized the concealed carry market. It was engineered to claim the title of the world’s highest-capacity micro-compact 9mm handgun. Despite its incredibly small footprint, it introduced a class-leading magazine capacity that shook the firearms industry, immediately competing with legendary models like the Sig Sauer P365 and the Glock 43X. Known for its distinct "Adaptive Grip Texture" and its Optics Ready (OSP) configuration, the Hellcat quickly became a favorite for everyday carry. This particular static prop gun replicates the upgraded tactical variants, mimicking the look of the Hellcat RDP (Rapid Defense Package), which includes a front self-indexing compensator to mitigate muzzle rise and an integrated micro red dot for lightning-fast target acquisition. Where to Use, Remix, & Keywords Because this is a completely non-functional static prop gun, it is incredibly versatile and safe for public environments! Cosplay & Costuming: An excellent addition for near-future sci-fi soldiers, secret agents, tactical detectives, or modern military builds. Because it has no moving parts, it easily passes strict convention weapon-check guidelines. Remix Potential: You can easily mesh or split this file to embed weights in the grip for a realistic hand-feel, hollow out the optic hood to place a colored plastic lens inside the red dot scope, or adapt the rail interface to test custom under-barrel laser and flashlight molds. Keywords: Springfield Hellcat, Static Prop Gun, Non-Firing Replica, 3D Printed Pistol, Toy Gun Prop, Con-Safe Weapon, Tactical Handgun, Red Dot Sight, Hellcat RDP, Inert Display Model, Military Cosplay, Fake Pistol. Print Settings & Material Recommendations To capture the intricate grip texturing and the clean overhangs on the compensator without losing surface quality, material choice is key. Recommended Filament: For the black tactical version, I highly recommend printing the slide and frame in SUNLU Matte PLA Black to eliminate shiny plastic layer lines and give it a premium, injection-molded look. For the grey prototype or a paint-ready base, SUNLU Standard PLA Grey or their highly durable SUNLU PLA+ (Plus) offers incredible impact resistance and flawless finish quality. Supports: Tree supports are highly recommended for the trigger guard, optics hood, and compensator overhangs. Ensure your bridging settings are dialed in for a clean finish! Assembly Instructions Depending on how you slice the model for your build plate, you may need to fuse the frame, slide, or muzzle attachments. For a seamless, permanent bond that will survive conventions and accidental drops, I recommend ARKA KRAFTPROTZ UNIVERSAL Superglue . Its high-strength bonding formula fuses the PLA surfaces cleanly without leaving unsightly white residue. description: Ghostbusters 1984 (GB1), 1989 (GB2) and Frozen Empire Proton Pack Replacement Bellows Replace the suppled bellows from the Hasbro Ghostbusters '84 Proton Pack with a more screen accurate alternative. The original pack includes bellows that more closely resemble the Ghostbusters II design, featuring the visible screw head at the end. This replacement reuses the original screw in base from the supplied bellows while providing a cleaner, more authentic Ghostbusters (1984) appearance. Full assembly instructions included below. EDIT - 1/7/26 - GB2 and Frozen Empire options added. ----- Enjoying this model? ----- Before you start Clean your print bed and hot end Clean your plate first, following your usual routine. Dish soap works best, clean and then rinse thoroughly, ensure the plate is dry and free of debris before putting back in the printer. Leftover filament residue on your hot end can cause unwanted colour streaks, which will show very clearly against any light parts of the print. Please inspect your hot end before starting the print, if you spot any clumps or leftover filament, follow Bambu's recommended cleaning guide to remove. Print requirements No AMS is required for this model. To use without an AMS, please add a pause on Layer 9 of the second build plate, allowing you to swap from the bronze/copper filament to silver before printing continues. The model is designed to reuse the original screw-in bottom section from the factory Hasbro bellows. ----- Printing The supplied print profile has been tuned for a balance between print quality and print time. For the best results, print directly from the included 3MF profile rather than importing the STL files into your slicer. The profile is tuned for supports, speed an ironing. Optional improvements Reducing the layer height further will produce a smoother, more machined appearance, although print time will increase. Ironing is enabled on the top surface of the silver section. The included settings produced the best results with my test filament, but I highly recommend printing an ironing calibration test first, as the ideal settings can vary between filament brands and colours. ----- Customisation The supplied print profile uses bronze/copper and silver filament to closely match the appearance of the original prop, but alternative metallic colours can easily be used to suit your own build. ----- Assembly Assembly is straightforward. What you will need (printed parts and original bellows): Remove the original screw-in base from the Hasbro bellows. Remove the supports, these can be a bit tricky, but take your time and they'll come out Glue the printed parts together using a suitable adhesive. Start with the base part (with the cylinder), then attach the first section with the cutout screw holes. There are some guide holes to help you position the part, also visually line up the screw holes with the base. Now glue in place all of the other bronze / copper pieces, I would suggest lining up the seems on the parts to keep things looking as neat as possible. Once done, then put the top part in place, then set aside for the glue to dry. Once dry, you can now screw in the part we removed from the Hasbro bellows, lining up the screw holes with the matching raised circle parts underneath, once done, you can now attach to your pack! ----- Troubleshooting If your silver top surface does not produce the finish you were expecting, adjust the ironing settings after printing a calibration test for your chosen filament. For the intended results, always use the supplied 3MF print profile rather than importing the raw STL or STEP files directly, as important print settings and the filament change pause are already configured. ----- Disclaimer This is an unofficial replacement part designed to improve the appearance of the Hasbro Ghostbusters 84 Proton Pack. description: ⚔️ Full-Scale Halo Energy Sword Cosplay Replica The .3mf features a small version for sizing/scaling, or a fully scaled, 1-to-1 version you print in pieces and assemble with glue (and a plastic welder which I would recommend). 🌌 Lore & History The Type-1 Energy Weapon/Sword (T-1 EW/S) is the ultimate close-quarters plasma weapon wielded by the Sangheili (Elite) species within the Covenant Empire. In lore, it is considered a holy weapon, reserved exclusively for high-ranking Sangheili such as Zealots, Ultras, Honor Guards, and Special Operations officers. Carrying strict cultural rules and serving as a fierce symbol of nobility and martial skill, this iconic weapon projects twin blades of superheated plasma stabilized by a powerful magnetic field—capable of boiling and penetrating almost any armor or material in a single, lethal strike. 🛠️ Detailed Model Description & Functionality This is a high-fidelity, full-scale 1:1 replica of the legendary Halo Energy Sword, meticulously engineered from the ground up for clean 3D printing and seamless assembly. The model separates the curved, ergonomic hilt housing from the sweeping twin plasma blades to maximize print quality, minimize necessary supports, and allow you to print individual components in their correct orientation and colors. To ensure maximum structural integrity when walking convention floors, the design features internal alignment channels built directly into the split blade segments and handle components. This allows you to slide robust alignment pins into place, completely eliminating any shearing points or misalignment during final assembly. Sizing & Scaling for Your Build: Because this is a prominent piece of cosplay weaponry that needs to fit your height and proportions perfectly, exact sizing is key. If you need to scale down the hilt to match your grip or slice it to fit a specific build plate, check out my comprehensive video guide: How to size, scale, cut, pin and orient armor or any model inside Bambu Studios or Orca . For the curved, ceremonial hilt, SUNLU Silk PLA (Silver or Gunmetal Gray) delivers a premium metallic sheen straight off the build plate without requiring a complex paint job. 🧪 Professional Assembly Glue Because this full-sized replica is divided into interlocking sections, a rigid bond is crucial. For joining the blade halves and handle together over the alignment pins, I highly recommend ARKA KRAFTPROTZ UNIVERSAL Superglue . Its industrial-strength bond ensures your sword will remain completely rock-solid during intense photoshoot posing or crowded convention troopings. 🔄 Remix Potential & Creative Context While this model makes an incredible standalone wall display or cosplay prop, it serves as an excellent canvas for creative makers: LED NeoPixel Mod: The split blade construction makes it incredibly easy to hollow out the core in your slicer, creating a channel to run addressable LED strips for a live, pulsing plasma lighting effect. description: Wax seals are fantastic at adding a level of class to letters, in sealing envelopes, or for attatching tags to brithday and christmas presents. Personally I plan on using them for creating immersive TTRPG props for my D&D game, so that I can hand them printed notices ( like these free ones ). Unfortunately, having a wax seal stamp design for every occasion, affiliation, or character can get expensive… so why not design and 3D print them? This is my first attempt at creating a design using one of my illustrations for Fantastical Geographic's debut . This design uses measurements taken from a proper wood and metal wax seal stamp so that the proportions of your seal will be similar, but also so that you can simply swap out the head and handle as you see fit as these are modeled separately. Or if you have a lot of metal stamp heads already you could simply want some fancy handles to accompany them instead of swapping things out. The head design and print profile have been optimized for 0.2mm nozzles as my experiments showed this yielded the best results. The head prints face up and uses ironing to create a smooth stamping surface for easy release, however, it is IMPORTANT to note that your ironing settings may need adjusting as this varies depending on printer, filament type, filament brand, and filament color! I've opted for PLA as it's the most accessible for many printers. If you are interested in reading my experiments I will be uploading a full write-up on my website of how I achieved the cleanest wax seal and release of the stamp (link to come). The TLDR is: 0.2 mm nozzle Head printed face up with ironing on 0.08mm layer height. 50% Infill 100% cooling Release Agent - A thin layer applied with an old brush Pre-cooling - Place the stamp in the freezer for 10-15 minutes (make sure to apply release agent first) Wait - Leave the stamp in the wax for about 1 minute before gently peeling off Additional Notes: I have included a 0.4mm nozzle profile, however, I was not able to get the ironing as smooth as the 0.2mm. It is there primarily for printing the handle, which doesn't require the high detail. These results were achieved with a tuned PLA filament profile for my machine. Your mileage may vary.
