(Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. description: So recently, I designed and printed Rick Sanchez's Portal gun. It's a simple design, especially the electronics, since I only needed it to work for a short period of time, but you can do better than me and put some proper electronics in there. The body is printed in gray PLA The knob, covering the ON / OFF switch is printed in black PLA The screen is printed in red PLA And the Light's and dome on top are printed in clear PLA. Just glue in three LED's into the LED-caps and put them in the corresponding holes. For the LED's in the dome, I soldered 20 LED's together in parallel and stacked them up. The rest of the electronics fit in the body of the Portal gun. The handle has a lid, attached with a filament hinge and is made with a hole, to run wires out if needed. Hope you enjoy my design, that being said, Happy printing. :)

description: 💀 Ancient Ram Skull & Spine Cosplay Staff (6-Foot) Model Description Unleash your inner sorcerer, necromancer, or dark druid with this hyper-detailed, 6-foot epic prop staff ! Designed entirely from scratch, this original design features an anatomically striking ram skull seamlessly fused to a winding, realistic spinal column that tapers perfectly into a sleek, clean staff handle. As seen in THE ATTACHED IMAGES, the curvature of the horns and the deep detailing of the vertebrae create an ominous, high-fidelity silhouette perfect for conventions, display, or stage performance. The mesh structure is optimized to hold crisp lines while remaining highly balanced across its full length. Functional Design & Assembly This massive 6-foot staff is split and keyed for easy printing on standard beds. Because this model is a large-scale prop meant to be swung, carried, and shown off, structural integrity is key. Assembly Note: To bond the staff sections, horns, and vertebrae securely, I highly recommend using ARKA KRAFTPROTZ UNIVERSAL Superglue . It provides an unyielding, high-strength bond that keeps large multi-part assemblies rigid under pressure. You can also use a plastic welding kit, which I would!!! Print Settings & Filament Recommendations Because this is a large functional prop that requires excellent layer adhesion and high impact resistance, material selection matters. I am proudly sponsored by SUNLU , and their engineering filaments are absolutely perfect for a build of this scale. Main Shaft & Spine: I highly recommend using SUNLU PETG Filament or their high-toughness PLA for maximum durability to ensure the handle won't snap if bumped. The Skull & Horns: For a flawless bone texture that minimizes visible layer lines, print the skull using SUNLU Matte PLA or their Silk PLA line for a more magical, metallic sheen on the horns. Cosplay Sizing, Scaling, and Cutting Because this prop needs to fit your height and your printer bed perfectly, scaling and slicing are crucial. If you need to scale the staff up or down to match your body proportions exactly, use my custom-designed tool: Cosplay Calipers - Measuring Tool for Armor and Prop Sizing . Need help figuring out how to chop this massive 6-foot file up, add registration pins, and orient it on your build plate? Watch my step-by-step masterclass here: How to size, scale, cut, pin and orient armor or any model inside Bambu Studios or Orca . Versatility & Remix Ideas While this stands alone as an incredible warlock staff, the files are incredibly modular! You can easily cut the spine away from the handle in your slicer to create a devastating, one-handed mace or a macabre wall trophy. description: Descripción de la Máscara de Astaroth (Diseño 3D) La máscara de Astaroth, creada en Nomad Sculpt, es una pieza impresionante que captura la esencia de este demonio mitológico con un toque moderno y mecánico. Está dividida en varias partes que ofrecen una visión detallada y un diseño funcional para su impresión en 3D. Mandíbula y Colmillos: La mandíbula de la máscara está esculpida con detalles complejos, destacando los colmillos afilados y prominentes que refuerzan la feroz apariencia del demonio. Los colmillos, que se extienden hacia afuera, tienen un diseño puntiagudo que evoca agresividad y poder. Los músculos de la mandíbula también están detallados, mostrando un diseño anatómico realista, lo que le da a la pieza una sensación de vitalidad y energía demoníaca. Cuernos: Los cuernos, que son uno de los rasgos más característicos de Astaroth, se curvan hacia arriba y hacia atrás. Están diseñados con una estética híbrida, combinando elementos naturales y mecánicos. La base de los cuernos está adornada con detalles cibernéticos, como paneles de metal, y un acabado brillante que le da un aire futurista. Los cuernos parecen estar forjados de un material resistente, lo que aumenta la sensación de fuerza y dominación que emana de la pieza. Parte Frontal y Detalles de la cara: La parte frontal de la máscara está adornada con líneas musculares que recuerdan la piel roja del demonio, destacando su fuerza y agresividad. La estructura parece de algún tipo de metal o aleación, con detalles como placas y juntas mecánicas que refuerzan su aspecto futurista. Se pueden observar pequeños detalles como circuitos y luces sutiles incrustadas, que dan una sensación de una criatura mitad orgánica, mitad tecnológica. Parte de la Nuca: La parte posterior de la máscara (nuca) tiene un diseño que es tanto orgánico como mecánico. El contorno tiene un acabado más suave, pero con elementos metálicos que terminan en un conjunto de líneas geométricas que evocan una sensación de integración con el cuerpo y un concepto de “cyberdemonio”. Esto hace que la máscara no solo se vea temible desde el frente, sino también desde atrás. Diseño para Impresión 3D: La máscara está diseñada para ser dividida en varias partes que se pueden imprimir individualmente y luego ensamblar. Esto incluye la mandíbula, los cuernos, la parte frontal y la nuca. Cada parte está modelada con precisión para asegurar que, una vez impresa, se pueda ensamblar fácilmente sin comprometer la integridad del diseño. Además, los detalles del diseño permiten una impresión detallada que captura la esencia tanto orgánica como tecnológica del demonio Astaroth. Este diseño es ideal para un fanático de la mitología y el arte digital, y una vez impresa en 3D, ofrecerá una pieza visualmente impactante que se puede usar como máscara, adorno o incluso pieza de colección. description: One of the most mysterious objects in Steven Speilberg's Disclosure Day. Known simply as "The Device", it appears throughout the film as an object of immense but largely unexplained power. It is used to communicate, influence people, and later interact with technology, yet its true nature remains an enigma. 🎬 A recreation from memory I saw Disclosure Day and immediately wanted to model The Device. The challenge? Rather than waiting for reference material to appear, I wanted to see how close I could get while the movie was still fresh in my mind. 🛸 Accuracy and future updates From what I could determine: - The Device has a heptagonal-to-rectangular form - It features a series of unusual symbols - It has a metallic appearance I've recreated the symbols as I remember them from the film, but as better reference material becomes available I expect to refine and update the model. If future images reveal inaccuracies, I'll update the design where practical. 🖨️ Print notes - Single-colour print - No AMS required - Designed to print cleanly as a display piece For the most screen-accurate appearance, I recommend printing in a metallic or silk filament. I just used Matte PLA as it was all I had 👽 Why print it? - Movie prop replica - Sci-fi display piece - Conversation starter - Early fan recreation of an iconic object from the film 🚀 Getting in early I fully expect more versions of The Device to appear over the coming weeks as reference images become available. This is my attempt to recreate it before that happens. If you spotted details in the movie that I've missed, let me know in the comments. 🙌 If you print one - Share your make - Follow for future movie-inspired models - Boost if you'd like to support more fan recreations 😄

Footsteps of corporate enforcer mechs grow louder through the narrow corridor; they tracked the faint energy signature all the way to his hidden shop. Kael tightens his grip on the light blue handle, and feels the bone segments rearrange themselves to perfectly fit the shape of his palm. The last memory fragment flooding his mind is not the death of the researcher who hid this dagger, but the chorus of waking spores whispering softly through his nerves: “We are not the enemy. description: A non-flying display replica of the WIY Strila — a Ukrainian interceptor drone built as a slim "tail-sitter" quadcopter, with four motors on swept X-wings, a nose sensor, a side pitot boom and a red tail pull-ring. This is a decorative scale model only : it doesn't fly and has no electronics or functional parts. Designed from reference photos as a parametric model, and sized for easy desktop printing. ✨ Highlights Accurate detailing — 4-window ogive motor nacelles, panel screws, section seam lines, belly payload box, side fin, nose cameras and the red tail ring. Four propellers that actually spin — they snap onto the motor axles with no glue, so they stay free to turn. Glue-together build — clean flat and keyed joints, no screws or hardware of any kind. Easy to print — most parts lay flat; only the motor cones want a little support. 🖨️ Printing Files are sized as a desk-friendly display: ~310 mm long (about 180 mm across). Want the real-life full size? Just scale to 200% → 620 mm — or scale to taste. 17 printed parts: body in 3 sections, plus 4× wing, 4× motor, 4× propeller, the nose probe and the tail ring. Suggested colours: dark grey fuselage, black/dark motors, red tail ring (a single colour prints fine too). 🔧 Assembly Glue is the only thing you need (CA / super glue). Print, clean up any supports, then: Glue the three body sections into one fuselage. Slot each wing into the body, and a motor onto each wing tip. Peg in the nose probe and the tail ring. Snap the propellers onto the motor axles — do not glue these so they keep spinning. description: 民国空军礼仪剑，俗称鹦鹉剑、英武剑，亦被称作空军中正剑，是民国中央航空学校专属毕业纪念礼仪佩剑，为抗战时期中国空军飞行员、援华外籍飞行人员的专属荣誉信物，与陆军制式中正剑形制、定位截然不同。该剑造型典雅别致、英姿飒爽，受民国时期国力薄弱、工业条件有限影响，原版佩剑大多做工粗糙、无统一制式规格。本模型高度还原原版全套配饰与形制细节，完整复刻器物风貌，以此缅怀抗战空军先烈，致敬长空忠魂。 The Republic of China Air Force ceremonial sword, commonly known as the Parrot Sword, is also called the Air Force Zhengzhong Sword. It was an exclusive ceremonial commemorative sword for graduates of the Republic of China Central Aviation School, serving as a supreme honor token for Chinese Air Force pilots and foreign volunteer aviators during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, which is completely different from the standard army Zhengzhong Sword. Boasting an elegant and heroic shape, the original swords were mostly crudely made without unified specifications due to the weak national strength and limited industrial conditions at that time. This model highly restores the full set of accessories and original structural details of the authentic sword, inheriting the memory of heroes and paying tribute to the martyrs of the Republic of China Air Force. 本模型采用1:1真实比例还原。受常规打印设备成型尺寸限制，刀身与刀鞘无法一体式打印，模型已做分段切割处理，需后期拼接打磨组装。若你的打印设备支持30cm以上大尺寸成型，可直接下载完整STL文件一体打印。 This model is restored in a 1:1 real scale. description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours. Absolutely NO A.I. was used to make these models nor the images. Do not reupload my files somewhere else. I will upload them where I want. DO NOT SELL THEM! I made these models from scratch, and choose to upload them for free for the cosplay community for free. Remixes are welcome, especially as this can be improved, but please give attribution, and posted under the same CC BY-NC-SA license terms. The M1 Carbine was developed in 1941 to bridge the gap between a handgun and a full-power battle rifle. Weighing about 5 pounds, it was issued to officers, paratroopers, and support troops as a lightweight defensive arm. It became the most produced U.S. small arm of WWII, with over 6 million manufactured. Origins and Development In June 1940, the U.S. War Department requested a "light rifle". Standard issue rifles like the M1 Garand were too heavy and cumbersome for non-combatants, medics, and heavy weapons crews. Winchester Repeating Arms accepted the challenge, relying heavily on a short-stroke gas piston designed by David "Carbine" Williams. Formally adopted on October 22, 1941, the new platform fired the .30 Carbine cartridge. Wartime Production Due to massive wartime demand, the U.S. government brought in 10 primary contractors to manufacture the weapon. Many of these companies had never built firearms before, including the Rock-Ola Jukebox Company and IBM Corp . Key Variants M1 Carbine: The standard semi-automatic configuration fed by a 15-round box magazine. Early versions lacked bayonet lugs, which were added later in the war. M1A1 Carbine: Introduced for airborne troops, this variant featured a side-folding metal stock that reduced its overall size for easier jumping and carrying. M2 Carbine: Developed late in the war, this variant added a selective-fire switch allowing for fully automatic fire. Post-War Legacy After WWII, the M1 Carbine remained in service during the Korean and Vietnam Wars. Many surplus models were subsequently issued to allied police forces and armed forces in Asia. In the 1960s, the U.S. government released thousands to the public through the Civilian Marksmanship Program . Today, it is prized by military history collectors and reproduced by gunmakers.
